# OgreBot - User Guide

This guide explains every window of the new OgreBot: what each one is for, and what every option on it does.

Every page starts with a picture of the window, then goes through it one area at a time. The area being
described is outlined in **pink** in its picture.

> **:memo: Examples use made-up names**
>
> Every name in these pictures - Kannkor, Brutus, Mirelle, Tobbin - is made up. Nothing here shows a real
> character, account, guild or server.

## Where to start

- Installing the bot? Start with [Installing and first start](install.md): one download, sign in, and the bot
  fetches the rest.
- New to the bot? Read [The basics](basics.md) first. It covers the window buttons every window shares.
- Setting up a character: [OgreBot](ogrebot/index.md), then its [Settings](ogrebot/settings.md) and
  [Cast Stack](ogrebot/cast-stack.md) tabs.
- Running zones: the [Instance Controller](windows/ic.md).
- Sharing out loot: [SmartLoot](windows/smartloot.md).

## Help inside the game

Every window has a **?** in its title bar. Click it for a short explanation of that window. The
**Full documentation** button in that box opens this guide.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/install.md

# Installing and first start

This page takes you from nothing to a running bot: download one file, sign in, and let the bot fetch the rest. It
takes a few minutes. After that, the bot keeps itself up to date every time it loads.

## Before you start

- **InnerSpace** and **ISXEQ2**, installed and working. InnerSpace must run as 64-bit, which is its default.
- **Your OgreBot username and password.** They are the same as for OgreBot Classic. You got them in the
  **Welcome to ISXOgre** email when you subscribed. No subscription yet? See
  [How to Subscribe](../about/pricing.md#how-to-subscribe).
- **Your PC's clock set right.** Sign-in is refused when the clock is off by more than 10 minutes.
- **InnerSpace in a folder Windows lets you write to.** The bot saves its settings and downloads inside the
  InnerSpace folder. A folder under `Program Files` can stop it from saving.

## Step 1: Start one game session

Close every EverQuest 2 session first. Then start **one**, with an InnerSpace profile that loads nothing by itself,
such as InnerSpace's own **EverQuest 2 Client** profile.

> **:bulb: Why only one?**
>
> When the bot updates itself it reloads in every session on the PC. A profile that loads OgreBot Classic by itself
> also gets in the way of the first install.

## Step 2: Download ISXOgreX

Open the InnerSpace console (the **`~`** key) and paste this line:

```
httpget -file "${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/x64/Extensions/ISXDK35/ISXOgreX.dll" https://cluster1.ogregaming.com/eq2/download_isxogrex.php
```

Wait until the console says it succeeded.

> **:bulb: Or download it in your browser**
>
> [Download ISXOgreX.dll](https://cluster1.ogregaming.com/eq2/download_isxogrex.php) and save it into your
> InnerSpace folder, in `x64\Extensions\ISXDK35\`. The file must be named exactly `ISXOgreX.dll`.

This one file is all you download by hand. It fetches everything else itself.

## Step 3: Load it and sign in

In the console, type:

```
ext isxogrex
```

A window called **OgreX - Login** opens. Enter your OgreBot **Username** and **Password** and click **Login**. They
are in the **Welcome to ISXOgre** email you got when you subscribed, and they are the same as for OgreBot Classic.
Copy and paste them: they are case-sensitive. They are saved on this PC, so you only do this once. The console then says `authenticated`.

If sign-in fails, the console says why: see [If something goes wrong](#if-something-goes-wrong).

## Step 4: The first download

The bot now downloads the rest of itself: about 1,500 files, a little over 100 MB. The console counts them off as
they arrive: first how many files there are to get, then a line every few files saying how far it has got, for
example `patch: downloading 300 of 1544`. You do not have to watch it, and you can close the console while it works:
the welcome window below opens by itself when everything is in. When the new files are in, the extension reloads itself once. That is
normal. It signs in again by itself, and then the bot's windows open.

**The maps download afterwards.** The maps the bot uses to move and fly around zones are large, about 14 GB in all.
They download in the background after the bot has loaded, and the console says so:
`navmesh: downloading ... in the background - the bot is ready to use`. You can play while they download.

## Step 5: The welcome tour

When the download is done, the **Welcome to OgreBot** window opens and plays a short animation of an ogre smashing
its way in. It ends on **Start the tour**. Click it for a short tour of how every Ogre window works: resizing, the
right-click menu on the title bar, saving a window's place, and the settings. Click **Got it** at the end. You can
skip both: press and hold **Hold to skip** for 3 seconds during the animation, or close the tour.

Right after the tour, the **Migration Assistant** opens for a moment and closes itself. It adds an InnerSpace profile
called **Everquest 2 ISXOgreX** that loads the bot by itself next time. If you used OgreBot Classic on this PC, it also
copies your Classic settings into the new bot: see [Migration Assistant](windows/migrate.md).

## Step 6: Log in and open the bot

Log your character in to the world the usual way. Then type:

```
ogre
```

OgreBot starts, and its small window appears: see [OgreBot's small window](windows/ogremini.md). Click
**Show Main** for the big window.

**The first time on each character**, the bot asks to export your abilities: a box says there is no ability export and
offers **Run export now**. Click it. The bot needs the export to know what your character can cast, and it stays
paused until the export is done.

## Step 7: Save your characters

Open the **EQ2Chars** tab in the big OgreBot window and add each of your characters, with its game account and
password if you want the bot to log it in for you. See [EQ2Chars](ogrebot/eq2chars.md).

From then on, `ogre <name>` logs that character in from character select and starts the bot, for example
`ogre Brutus`. Until a character is on the list, `ogre <name>` only says it is not a known character.

## Next time

Start your session with the **Everquest 2 ISXOgreX** profile. The bot loads, signs in and updates by itself. Then
type `ogre <name>` at character select, or `ogre` once you are in the world.

## If something goes wrong

| The console says | What to do |
|---|---|
| `login failed - invalid credentials. Re-enter them in the login box.` | Your username or password is wrong. Type them again in the login window. They are case-sensitive. |
| `your OgreBot subscription is not active - adapter not loaded.` | Your account has no active OgreBot subscription. |
| `login failed - ... Sync this machine's clock ...` | Set your PC's clock right (Windows Settings, Time & language, **Sync now**), then type `ext isxogrex` again. |
| `login failed - ... too many machines or IPs for your subscription.` | Your account is signed in on more PCs than it allows. |
| `cannot reach the OgreGaming server. Retrying in ...` | The bot tries again by itself. If it keeps failing, check your internet connection and firewall. |
| No Ogre windows appear | See [No Ogre windows](no-ogre-windows.md). |

## Next steps

- [The basics](basics.md): the window buttons every Ogre window shares.
- [OgreBot](ogrebot/index.md): the main window, then its [Setup](ogrebot/setup.md) and
  [Cast Stack](ogrebot/cast-stack.md) tabs.

# The super secret project

Where to even start! I guess a super brief history of how OgreBot became to be. I'd guess the basics of my story was the same as most people's here. A friend wanted me to play eq2 with them (they wanted me to make a bot, as I had done so for eq1). I said sure, but I was ONLY playing 1 toon. Pretty sure I made a troubadour. I was coding at low levels but it was hard back then. It logically only made sense, to have a second account for a priest. It's only 2 accounts, that's basically just 1 account.

Then I was killing slow... so may as well add some dps to the group... 3 accounts is barely more than the 2 I already have. It's only 1 more. Yes, you can absolutely hear the "justification" to myself about how this is all fine. The friend who got me into eq2, I'm pretty sure at this stage, is absolutely laughing his ass off, because he new this would happen, and he knew exactly what was coming next.

Well, if I'm already at 3, then I may as well just have my own group. Then there were 6.

Okay, fast forward almost 20 years or something now. Lax/Innerspace comes out with LGUI2 (it's what OgreCraft2's UI is done in). It provided a TON more options for dealing with GUIs, but LGUI2 isn't very friendly. I find it way over complicated, it was very new, so minimal documentation or examples. I made it work, but still didn't like it.

Then others, decided to bring in external GUIs. I thought this was an interesting idea, but the problem is, EVERYTHING is tied to my current GUI, that changing would be an absolute nightmare. It would basically be a rewrite of Ogrebot... and for what? To change the GUI?

Then a friend (don't tell him I called him that) and I were talking and joking... How long would it take, to rewrite Ogrebot from scratch, and make it work with a new GUI. With basically full parity (meaning, no loss of features). Our estimate was over a year. That assumes I focus the majority of my time there. That was absolutely not going to be worth it. Full stop, no thanks.

I didn't want to code untolds above tier 20, because Dominion of Pain sucks, so I was looking for a way to distract myself. I thought I'd look into these alternate GUIs to run some performance bench marks. If a new fancy GUI would be a net loss in performance, that's not worth it, at all. FPS (frames per second, not first person shooter) is way more important than having a fancy dancy GUI.

Did a bunch of research, and choose one. It is built using HTML (basically a webpage). This is fantastic, because HTML is likely the most common language ever (I didn't actually check to see if that's true, but almost every single website uses html). That means there's infinite amount of examples, and support etc etc.

I figured, okay, lets load this up, see how it works, do some performance tests, then go from there.

A WEEK LATER, I finally get it working. Like... me working on it every spare moment I have for an entire week. I was ready to bash my head into a wall.

Now that I've wasted a week, figured I should do some performance tests. I figured sink or swim new GUI. I created 3 identical GUIs. One in LGUI1, one in LGUI2, and one in this newGUI. They had something like 50 checkboxes, 50 labels etc.

I then had the same script monitor the fps while idle, then I started sending information to them every frame (this isn't realistic, but it's a good test). It was doing I think almost 200 changes to the GUI every frame. (a label that goes from 1, to 2, to 3, sliders going up like a progress bar etc). I figured put it under stress and see what happens.

Here's the results (higher numbers are better)

Static:

NewGUI: 45.7

LGUI1: 39.4

LGUI2: 33.2

Under extreme load:

NewGUI: 41.9

LGUI1: 36.7

LGUI2: 26.1

Well, that tells two stories. LGUI2 is bad on performance, is difficult to work with, and is in the garbage.

NewGUI is actually better than LGUI1 in performance, and looks better. How about that.

Okay, cool story, time to move on... ... ...

I started messing around to see what it looked like, and what it was capable of doing. Thought it would be nifty, but honestly, a rewrite of Ogrebot still was not worth it. Too time consuming.

But for a new project... maybe.

So I started a new extension, got things loaded up, but wasn't sure what new project to work on. I thought okay, I'll just re-create something of Ogre. I'll do OgreConsole, keep it simple, doesn't require any external things like isxeq2, it simply displays information.

Did that, was pretty nifty. But it was basically a listbox. I used 1 element. May as well do another window. Was curious how it could handle something like MCP. Being able to drag and resize, how it could handle right clicking with new windows, swapping buttons, frame in frame (static vs changing buttons), etc. This was going to be a good test.

It was.. overall.. pretty simple. It was HTML... webpages. Almost anything you want to do, has 25309235 examples available.

Okay, so the GUI works. How am I going to make it actually usable. I've always known that lavishscript is "slow" overall, and here I am using an extension written in c++ (which is very fast). Well, lets go down that road a little bit, and see if I can figure out how to do more stuff in c++, then start testing performance, to see where this goes. As you can tell, performance is likely the highest priority I have. I want more FPS, and never want to lose any FPS. Could I move any big number crunching, into c++. For example, there's HUNDREDS of checks for Ogrebot to find an ability it wants to cast from the caststack. I start down that road....

Okay, have a mock of that working, but the real test is having an actual cast stack. Well, what if we just made a little mock up of Ogrebot's GUI, then loaded the caststack in, and see how it goes.

Well, in order to have a usable caststack, you need an export, so gotta load that up too.

Here's where it became very obvious to me. Loading the export in lavishscript, you know when you load ogrebot, and it has that bed red message of "Loading..." on top of the GUI, most of that time is loading the export and pulling it apart (finding the highest ability etc). It's something like 2-5 seconds.

I have the export in c++, and did the same thing, had it pull out the highest abilities etc. I load it... it loads. Like.. instantly. Okay, I must have missed something... oh no. It's done.. instantly.

Pretty sure I pivoted, and started running tests. Just simple tests.

In lavishscript, doing ${Me.Name}, ${Me.Health}. Doing it both in lavish and in c++. Ran them a few hundred thousand times, turns out c++ does them 3 to 10 times faster (depending, string vs int etc). Everything, is just insanely faster in c++. Okay, how much can I do solely in c++?

Apparently, I started rewriting Ogrebot, in c++, as kind of a, lets see how this goes. Every time I ran performance tests, with the new GUI, and c++, it absolutely destroyed lavishscript and LGUI1 (that's what Ogrebot is currently in). Apparently I was going down this rabbit hole, that I said was not worth it at all.

I had to take a pause and started thinking. Okay, if I'm doing this, it's going to break *EVERYTHING*. Every single side script out there that touches my GUI. If I'm basically re-doing it in c++, that's going to break OgreBotAPI... breaking everything. I had to decide, am I okay with breaking everything? If I'm going to break things, then I may as well fix things too. For example, I'm sure you've all heard of the famous "ForWho". That decides who listens to the various commands. Almost everything has a forwho... but did you know, 27 things either did not have a forwho, or had it in the wrong spot? But i couldn't change it, because it would break things. GUESS WHAT! I'M ALREADY BREKAING THINGS!

I still have not told anyone except my "friend" that got me into this mess. He was sworn to secrecy, because I knew where he lives. Well.. I know he lives in USA.

At the time of writing this portion of this, I'm still a long ways away from having something for alpha testers. Most of the important subsystems are built. The caststack, campspot, mcp, ogreconsole, osa. 100% within c++, and all with this new fancy html GUI. It's super speedy! And as I have been going along, I have been trying to put together a list of "what do I think works well" and "what needs improved". There are some seriously cool QoL (quality of life) features. I'll document them as I get there, but most of them you will be able to find on your own.

So, what does this mean for the future of Ogre? It's changing with the times. It's getting a complete overhaul. A face lift (new GUI), and complete back end rewrites.

Here's the short "good and bad" about this.

The good:

New, modern GUI that is much easier to use, and more familiar for people.

FPS increase, although I'm not going to hold my breath until I get more and am able to use it in a zone etc.

Everything has it's own TLO and datatypes, and for scripters, this means you can LSTYPE things! (if you're not a scripter, this won't mean anything).

The bad:

Every single script/side script out there, will stop working immediately. While this is really unfortunate, it was the only way to do this project. I'm going to have documents that explain, with examples, of how scripts can be updated to a new format that will work (basically instead of calling the GUI this way, you do it this way).

I will also do my best to help people who have scripts, but got them from people who no longer play, and help you convert them.

People will need to "learn" a new GUI, but I honestly don't think this will be a big deal. It looks modern, but the same. Once you see it, you'll understand.

That's it for now. I would like to say, I have learnt my lesson.. by putting off doing untolds, I ended up with a much, much bigger project on my hands... but I have definitely not learned anything from this...

&lt;fast forward like 2 months&gt;

It's Oct 14th, 2026. I have said I am going to add some testers this week. So.. this is coming out for people to see and test, REAL soon.

Anyone who was paying attention to my clues I was giving, one of them was this, a common phrase I say:

`____ _______`

4 letter word, space, 7 letter word. Only 1 person got it. I think everyone got caught up, on the 4 letter word had to be "ogre", but it wasn't.

It was "full rewrite". One person did guess "ogre rewrite", which was half right, I suppose.

Which then leads to a question of "full rewrite of what?", and the answer to that, is "EVERYTHING".

Now, lets talk about what, everything means. Oh, it means everything. Every, single, thing.

From authentication, to ogrebot, to craft (yes, another rewrite), to mcp, etc etc. When you are rewriting things, you know what that means? UPGRADES! So many things, got upgrades. When in doubt, right click.

I took 20 years of Ogre content, and rewrote all of it. Was it worth it? I guess in the end, that depends on how you all think of it. So far, I am very pleased with it.

P.S. the writing of this, was done entirely by me, with no AI.

P.S.S. Of course, when I say "this", I mean this specific document only :)

# The basics

Every OgreBot window works the same way. This page covers what they all share.

## The title bar

![A title bar](assets/basics/titlebar.png)

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Title** | The window's name. Drag it to move the window. Double-click it to minimize or restore the window. |
| **▼ / ▲** | Minimizes the window: it rolls up to its title bar where it is, so you can get to the game or another window quickly. Click **▲** to restore it to exactly the size it had. Some windows keep a line showing while minimized - the Instance Controller keeps its run status and a Pause button. A window always opens at its normal size; being minimized is not remembered. A few windows do not have it: OgreBot's small toolbar, and the Effect Tracker, which has its own Shrink button. |
| **?** | Opens a short help box for this window. Its **Full documentation** button opens this guide. |
| **Lock** | Click it to lock the window, and again to unlock it. A locked window cannot be moved or resized, and the padlock is lit while it is locked. The lock is remembered for next time. It does not save the window's place: use **Save Position** for that. |
| **X** | Closes the window. |

Some windows put extra buttons in the title bar too, for example a gear for settings.

## The right-click menu

Right-click a window's title bar for this menu:

![The right-click menu](assets/basics/menu.png)

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Help** | The same as the **?** button. |
| **Save Position** | Remembers where the window is and how big it is. It opens there next time. Save it while it is minimized and it opens minimized every time; save it again while it is open to stop that. It is dimmed while the window is locked: unlock the window to save its position. |
| **Lock / Unlock** | Stops the window from being moved or resized, or allows it again. Like the padlock, it is remembered for next time. |
| **Minimize / Restore** | The same as the **▼ / ▲** button. |
| **Reset** | Puts the window back where it first opened, at its first size, turns off Lock and Pin to back, sets Console back to use default, and restores it if it was minimized. |
| **More** | A sub-menu of the items below. |
| **Scale + / Scale -** | Makes this window bigger or smaller. |
| **Scale: use default** | Goes back to the size set in Ogre Options. |
| **Pin to back / Unpin from back** | A pinned window always stays behind every window that is not pinned, even when you click it. Remembered for next time. |
| **When Console is open** | A sub-menu: what this window does when the InnerSpace console opens over it - **Use default**, **Slide below**, **Hide** or **Leave in place**. **Use default** follows the choice in Ogre Options (named in brackets); the other three are this window's own, whatever Ogre Options says. The ticked one is in force. Remembered for next time. |
| **Minimize all windows / Restore all windows** | Minimizes every Ogre window that is open, or - once they all are - restores them all. |
| **Match on all sessions** | Moves this window to the same place, size and scale, and minimizes or restores it, on every session on this PC that has it open. Locked windows move too and stay locked. Nothing is saved: use **Save Position** for that. |

## The help box

![The help box](assets/basics/help.png)

The help box sits next to the window it explains. You can move it and close it like any other window.

## Resizing

Drag the right edge, the bottom edge, or the bottom-right corner of a window to resize it.

# No Ogre windows

OgreBot loads and runs, but no Ogre windows appear in the game. Ogre's windows are drawn inside each game, unless you chose to have one separate program, `OgreUltralight.exe`, draw them for every game to save memory. When they cannot start, the InnerSpace console says why, and a window opens (at most once a day) with two choices: the steps on this page, or the other way of drawing them.

## Two ways of drawing Ogre's windows

- **Inside each game** (the default). Nothing extra runs.
- **In `OgreUltralight.exe`**, one program for every game on the PC. It uses about 150 MB less memory per game, but with many games running it can become the slow part. Tick **Draw Ogre windows in OgreUltralight.exe** in `ogre config` (Ogre tab), or type `ogre ui exe on` in the InnerSpace console. `ogre ui exe off`, or unticking it, goes back.

Either change takes effect when you restart the game, each box. Find what the console said below.

## "Windows Exploit Protection does not let EverQuest2.exe start other programs"

You chose `OgreUltralight.exe`, and a Windows security setting called Exploit Protection has a rule on `EverQuest2.exe` that stops it starting any other program. You may not have set this rule yourself. Other software can add it.

- **Draw the windows inside the game instead:** choose **Draw them in the game** in the window that opened, or type `ogre ui exe off`, then restart the game.
- **Or change the rule.** Close the game first.
  1. Open **Windows Security**.
  2. Open **App & browser control**, then **Exploit protection settings**.
  3. Open the **Program settings** tab.
  4. Find `EverQuest2.exe`. There can be more than one, one for each copy of the game. Do these steps for each one.
  5. Choose **Edit**, then find **Do not allow child processes**. Turn off **Override system settings** for it, then choose **Apply**.
  6. Start the game and load OgreBot.

  Windows may show slightly different names on your version.
- **Or let InnerSpace start it:** `ogre ui uplinkstart on` has the InnerSpace uplink start `OgreUltralight.exe` instead of the game. Restart the game after it; `ogre ui uplinkstart off` goes back.

## "Windows Smart App Control blocked OgreUltralight.exe" or "blocked Ogre's window files"

Smart App Control is a Windows 11 security setting that blocks programs and files that are not signed. Ogre's are not signed.

- **If it blocked `OgreUltralight.exe`:** draw the windows inside the game instead. Choose **Draw them in the game** in the window that opened, or type `ogre ui exe off`, then restart the game.
- **If it blocked Ogre's window files:** drawing them in `OgreUltralight.exe` will most likely be blocked too. Turning Smart App Control off is the fix: open **Windows Security**, then **App & browser control**, then **Smart App Control settings**, and choose **Off**. On some versions of Windows, Smart App Control cannot be turned back on without resetting Windows, so read what Windows says before you choose.

## "a file Ogre's windows need is missing" or "OgreUltralight.exe could not start - a file it needs is missing"

Ogre's windows need a few files beside them, among them Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime files, which the bot brings
with it. One of them is not there. Drawing the windows the other way will not help: both ways need the same files.

- **Restart the game.** Each time the bot loads it checks its files and downloads any that are missing.
- **If it comes back,** your antivirus may be removing the file. Look in its quarantine or history for a file from your
  InnerSpace folder's `x64\Extensions\ISXDK35\OgreUIRuntime\` folder, restore it, and allow that folder.
- When `OgreUltralight.exe` is the one that failed, Windows also shows its own box naming the missing file. That name
  helps if you send the files below.



## "Windows would not load Ogre's window files into the game" or "did not start inside the game"

Try the other way of drawing them: choose **Use OgreUltralight.exe** in the window that opened, or type `ogre ui exe on`, then restart the game. If that does not help either, send the files below.

## Still no windows?

Send these files to Kannkor, from your InnerSpace folder:

```
Scripts\OgreLogs\ui\ISXOgreUIHost.log
Scripts\OgreLogs\ui\OgreUltralight.log
```
