Fight setups that drive Balanced Synergy themselves (Sypheria the Shackled) tick this.* | off |



## Cast Stack (4 of 5)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Disabled** | The bot never casts abilities that move you up the hate list: not from the Cast Stack, not when a script or command asks for an ability, and not when it picks an HO ability. | off |
| **Only if you are not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while you are tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. | off |
| **Only if a fighter is not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while a fighter player is tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. A fighter on the ignore list (-ThreatFighterIgnoreList_Add) does not count, which is how a tank who must not hold the mob lets the others taunt off them. | off |
| **Disabled** | The bot never casts force-target (taunt) abilities: not from the Cast Stack, not when a script or command asks for an ability, and not when it picks an HO ability. | off |
| **Only if you are not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while you are tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. | off |
| **Only if a fighter is not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while a fighter player is tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. A fighter on the ignore list (-ThreatFighterIgnoreList_Add) does not count, which is how a tank who must not hold the mob lets the others taunt off them. | off |
| **Disabled** | The bot never casts hate-increasing abilities: not from the Cast Stack, not when a script or command asks for an ability, and not when it picks an HO ability. | off |
| **Only if you are not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while you are tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. | off |
| **Only if a fighter is not tanking** | The bot does not cast these abilities while a fighter player is tanking the mob, from the Cast Stack or for an HO. The ignore list is not used here. | off |
| **No Threat Position Decreases** | The bot never casts abilities that move you down the hate list: not from the Cast Stack, not when a script or command asks for an ability, and not when it picks an HO ability. | off |
| **No Threat Decrease** | The bot never casts hate-reducing abilities: not from the Cast Stack, not when a script or command asks for an ability, and not when it picks an HO ability. | off |



## Cast Stack (5 of 5)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Do not send pet to attack** | The bot stops sending your pet at the mob it is fighting, and stops re-aiming the pet when it drifts onto another mob. Your mercenary is handled separately (see Disable Merc Support).<br>*Encounter files can tick this during a fight.* | off |
| **Cure Curse in Reverse Order** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **X abilities to group cure** | While you cast something that is not a cure, cancel it when a group cure on your Cast Stack would cast right now (someone in your group has a detriment it removes, and it is ready), and cast that cure next. | off |
| **Disable Group/Raid Cures in CS** | The bot will not choose a group or raid cure when a script or command asks it for an ability, or when it picks an HO ability. The 'cure while stunned' feature on the Other tab also skips group cures. The normal Cast Stack rotation is NOT affected by this box.<br>*Despite 'in CS' (in Cast Stack) in the label, Cure entries on your Cast Stack still cast.* | off |
| **Disable Single Target Cures in CS** | The bot will not choose a player cure when a script or command asks it for an ability, or when it picks an HO ability. The 'cure while stunned' feature on the Other tab also skips single-target cures. The normal Cast Stack rotation is NOT affected by this box.<br>*Some encounter setups tick this expecting it to stop Cast Stack cures; it does not.* | off |
| **Enable Selective Single Target Cures** | Single-target Cure entries on your Cast Stack only cure the types ticked below (Arcane, Elemental, Noxious, Trauma). If none of the ticked types is one that cure removes, or nothing is ticked, that cure is not cast at all. Curse cures are not affected.<br>*While on, the bot also stops choosing player cures for script/command ability requests and HO picks.* | off |
| **Arcane** | With 'Enable Selective Single Target Cures' on, single-target cures may remove Arcane. | off |
| **Elemental** | With 'Enable Selective Single Target Cures' on, single-target cures may remove Elemental. | off |
| **Noxious** | With 'Enable Selective Single Target Cures' on, single-target cures may remove Noxious. | off |
| **Trauma** | With 'Enable Selective Single Target Cures' on, single-target cures may remove Trauma. | off |
| **Enable Selective Group Cures** | Group and raid Cure entries on your Cast Stack only count and cure the types ticked below. A group cure fires only when members have one of those types.<br>*While on, the bot also stops choosing group cures for script/command ability requests and HO picks.* | off |
| **Arcane** | With 'Enable Selective Group Cures' on, group cures count and cure Arcane. | off |
| **Elemental** | With 'Enable Selective Group Cures' on, group cures count and cure Elemental. | off |
| **Noxious** | With 'Enable Selective Group Cures' on, group cures count and cure Noxious. | off |
| **Trauma** | With 'Enable Selective Group Cures' on, group cures count and cure Trauma. | off |
| **X Abillties to Auto Cure Potions** | If you are casting when you need a cure potion (one of the types ticked below is on you and you have a ready potion for it), the bot cancels the cast and drinks the potion.<br>*It drinks whether or not 'Enable Auto Cure Potions' is ticked. It does not cancel a cure, a cast you started yourself, or anything while the cast stack or its cures are disabled.* | off |
| **Enable Auto Cure Potions** | When you are not casting and carry a ready 'Cure <type>' potion for a detrimental on you, the bot drinks it, checking about twice a second. Only the types ticked below are used. Potions only ever cure yourself. | off |
| **Arcane** | Allows automatic cure potions to be used for Arcane. | off |
| **Elemental** | Allows automatic cure potions to be used for Elemental. | off |
| **Noxious** | Allows automatic cure potions to be used for Noxious. | off |
| **Trauma** | Allows automatic cure potions to be used for Trauma. | off |



## Combat (1 of 2)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Allow Camp Spot** | Allows this character to use a camp spot. When on, the bot returns you to your camp spot when you stray from it. When off, a camp spot cannot even be set on this character, it never walks back to one, and it stays put for the Come2Me, Move2Area and Move2AreaNoTarget commands.<br>*Scripts and encounters can tick and untick this during a fight; it takes effect at once.* | off |
| **Dynamic Camp Spot** | Shows whether a camp spot is set: the bot ticks it when a spot is set and unticks it when the spot is cleared. Untick it yourself to stop the bot returning to the camp spot without deleting the spot.<br>*Setting a new spot ticks it again.* | off (not saved; the bot sets it) |
| **Auto Assist** | Switches assisting on. While it is ticked, the bot targets for the first available player on the Assist tab, or the player set by an assist command. Unticked, it does not assist at all.<br>*Auto Target, when it is on, takes over from assisting whatever this box says. 'ogre assist' still shows who you would assist while the box is off.* | off |
| **Dynamic Assist** | **Not built yet.** The assist command remembers who to assist on its own; this box is not used or updated. | off (not saved) |
| **Direct Assist Targeting** | Instead of targeting the player you assist (and fighting whatever they have targeted), the bot targets that player's target directly. If that player has no live target, your target is left alone. | off |
| **Dynamic Direct Assist Targeting** | Works the same as Direct Assist Targeting while it is ticked, and is never saved. The bot ticks it by itself when the game says your target is immune to area attacks cast through an assist, unless 'Do not automatically turn on DAT' is ticked. Untick it to stop. | off (not saved) |
| **Do not automatically turn on DAT** | When the game says your target is immune to area attacks cast through an assist, the bot normally ticks Dynamic Direct Assist Targeting so its area attacks go at the mob itself. Tick this to stop it doing that. When the bot ticks the box, area attacks wait 1 second while the target switches; when Direct Assist Targeting is already on, or this box is ticked, every area attack is held for 10 seconds instead. | off |
| **Face mob in combat** | While the bot is running and you are standing still, it turns you to face the mob you are fighting when you are more than 45 degrees off. It only does this within the 'Melee move when less' distance on the Setup tab (40 if blank). If you are on /follow it drops follow for a moment to turn. | off |
| **Ranged Attack** | When the mob is outside melee reach (or melee is off) and beyond your ranged minimum, the bot switches on ranged auto-attack.<br>*It never turns auto-attack on while you are invisible, stealthed or casting a stealth opener.* | off |
| **Melee Attack** | When the mob is within melee reach, the bot switches on melee auto-attack, and switches back from ranged to melee when the mob closes in.<br>*It never turns auto-attack on while you are invisible, stealthed or casting a stealth opener.* | off |
| **Move into Melee Range** | When the mob is farther away than your melee reach, the bot walks you into melee range. It does this even if you are tanking. It only acts within the 'Melee move when less' distance on the Setup tab (40 if blank), only when no camp spot is active, and only once the mob is at or below '% NPC HP to move into attack range'. | off |
| **Move behind mob** | When the mob is attacking someone else, the bot walks you round to its back, and backs you off if you are standing too close. The same distance, camp spot and health limits as 'Move into Melee Range' apply.<br>*If both this and 'Move in front of mob' are ticked, behind wins.* | off |
| **Move in front of mob** | When the mob is attacking someone else, the bot walks you round to its front, and backs you off if you are standing too close. The same distance, camp spot and health limits as 'Move into Melee Range' apply.<br>*Ignored when 'Move behind mob' is also ticked.* | off |
| **Disable LoS on Move behind** | Normally the bot will not move you behind, in front of, or up to the mob if a wall or obstacle is in the way. Tick this to skip that line-of-sight check for all three moves. | off |
| **Turn Off Attack** | While auto-attack is on but you no longer have a valid mob to attack (it died, is gone, or is above the '% NPC HP to attack' threshold), the bot switches auto-attack off. It checks twice a second. | off |
| **Ignore NPC HP to move** | The combat moves (behind, in front, into melee range) ignore the '% NPC HP to move into attack range' setting on the Setup tab and start as soon as you have a mob you can attack. | off |
| **Interrupt Mode** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **Disable Bulwark of Order** | Fighters: the bot normally watches chat for a mob announcing a big hit and casts Bulwark of Order timed to meet it. Tick this to stop it answering new warnings. A Bulwark already counting down still goes out. | off |
| **Disable anti-fear (crouch and walk while feared)** | When you are feared, the bot crouches you and switches you to walking, so you do not run as far; when the fear ends it stands you up and switches you back to running - only what it changed (already walking or crouched stays that way). It works only while OgreBot is loaded; pausing OgreBot freezes it (nothing changes until you resume). Tick this to switch it off - anything it changed is put back at once. |  |
| **Disable Auto-Defensives** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **Enable CD T4 Weapons** | **Not built yet.**  | off |



## Combat (2 of 2)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **NPC Cast Monitoring** | The bot watches nearby mobs for the spells they start casting. Zone data and encounter files use this to react, for example with an interrupt. Off means no scanning and no reactions.<br>*When a zone or encounter asks for a watch, the bot ticks this for you. It never unticks it, so your own untick sticks.* | off |
| **Auto Complete Ascension Combos** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **Ascension Embargo and Combos** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **Show Surge messages** | **Not built yet.**  | off |
| **Disable Merc Support** | The bot stops sending your mercenary to attack the mob you are fighting (and stops pulling it back off other mobs). | off |
| **Cancel Invis After Combat** | When you are invisible, out of combat and have no mob left to attack, the bot cancels your invisibility. | off |
| **Enable Raid Setups** | In raid zones, the bot runs the encounter setups written for that zone's fights (setup, triggers and mechanics). When off, no setup starts, by itself or by hand. Unticking mid-fight stops everything the fight was doing straight away, and ticking it again carries on watching the same fight without running its setup again. If a setup did run, its clean-up still happens when the mob dies, whichever way this box is.<br>*If a setup already ran for a mob, its clean-up still runs when that mob dies, even after you untick this.* | off |
| **Enable Heroic Setups** | The same as 'Enable Raid Setups', but for every zone that is not a raid zone (heroic, solo and so on). Turn it off at any point in a fight to take over, and back on to carry on. | off |
| **Disable Auto Setups** | Stops encounter setups starting on their own, in both raid and heroic zones. A setup you start yourself, or one the Instance Controller asks for, still runs, and a fight already set up carries on. The zone's Enable Raid Setups or Enable Heroic Setups box must still be on for any setup to run. | off |
| **Auto Target when Hated** | When you have no target, or only something you can't fight (a mob's corpse, chest, shiny or NoKill NPC, but not a dead group or raid member, so you can res them), the bot looks about once a second for a mob within 30 meters (and roughly your height) that is attacking someone in your group, and targets it. It never does this while you are assisting someone (Auto Assist). | off |
| **Disable Mortal Coil Dispel** | Mages: the bot normally dispels the 'Mortal Coil' buff from named mobs in range with your dispel ability. Tick this to stop it.<br>*'No Dispels' on the Settings tab also stops it.* | off |
| **Wait for Recovery time** | Normally the bot picks the next ability the moment a cast lands, queuing it during the recovery time. Tick this to make it wait out each ability's recovery time (minus 0.2 seconds) first. Items are not affected. | off |
| **Use reduced stun checks** | The Cast Stack decides you are stunned when you cannot turn, or when your Mining ability is not ready. Tick this to drop the 'cannot turn' test, so being unable to turn alone no longer stops casting. | off |
| **Dynamic ignore stun checks** | While ticked, the Cast Stack skips its stun tests entirely and tries to cast even if you look stunned.<br>*Meant for encounter scripts, for fights where the game falsely reports a stun.* | off (not saved; clears on reload) |
| **DoV Raid Debuffs** | When chat says the Destiny of Velious (DoV) raid debuff is about to expire on a mob, the bot re-casts your archetype's DoV raid debuff on it. | off |
| **Allow moving to cast** | Lets the bot move you into range to cast the Destiny of Velious (DoV) raid debuff, when the request to cast it does not say otherwise. | off |
| **Enable PvP** | Lets the bot fight enemy players: when your target, or your target's target, is a player the game marks as an enemy, they become your kill target, and the Cast Stack, auto-attack and movement act on them as on a mob. Friendly players are never affected. | off |



## Tab Enables

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable Chat Events** | Turns on the Chat Events tab. When a chat line matches one of its rows, the bot does that row's actions: send a line to OgreConsole, play a sound, and/or run a command. When off, chat lines are not watched at all. | off |
| **Enable Spawn Events** | Turns on the Spawn Events tab. When something matching one of its rows appears nearby, the bot does that row's actions (OgreConsole line, sound, command). | off |
| **Enable Despawn Event** | Turns on the Despawn Events tab. When something matching one of its rows disappears, the bot does that row's actions (OgreConsole line, sound, command). | off |
| **Enable Crowd Control** | Mez the adds that are hitting your group, using the Crowd Control tab's list. The mob your group is killing is never mezzed. A mez is renewed when it has 10 seconds or less left. | off |
| **Enable Announce Tab** | Turns on the Announce tab, so the bot announces the abilities listed there when you use them. | off |
| **Enable Consume Items** | Turns on the Consume Items tab, so the bot automatically uses the items listed there (following that tab's zone and combat rules). When off, the consume-items command also does nothing. | off |
| **Enable Aliases** | Turns on your custom aliases from the Aliases tab (names starting with *), so commands and Cast Stack targets can use them. When off, custom aliases resolve to nobody. The built-in @ slots such as @Tank are not affected. | off (the Cast Stack target dropdown treats a never-saved box as on) |
| **Enable Ability Tracker** | Turns on the Ability Tracker tab. About twice a second the bot reads the cooldowns of the abilities listed there and shares them, for example with the OgreMCP cooldown buttons. | off |
| **Enable Ability Embargo** | Turns on ability embargoes. While it is ticked, casting an ability on the Ability Embargo tab tells your other characters to hold off it, and the Cast Stack skips an ability that a command or another character has embargoed (-AbilityEmbargo) until the time is up. While it is off, nothing is sent, and embargoes are still kept but not followed, so ticking it later honours any that are still running. | off |
| **Enable Tag Embargo** | Turns on Embargo tags (see the Tags tab). While it is ticked, the Cast Stack skips an ability whose Embargo tag is on, and casting an ability that carries an Embargo tag turns that tag on. While it is off, this character neither follows Embargo tags nor turns them on. Tags sent by your other characters are still kept, so ticking it later honours any that are still running. | off |
| **Enable Tag Allow** | Turns on Allow tags (see the Tags tab). While it is ticked, an ability with an Allow tag only fires while that tag is on, and casting an ability that carries an Allow tag turns that tag on. While it is off, an Allow tag does not hold an ability back and casting does not turn one on. Tags sent by your other characters are still kept, so ticking it later honours any that are still running. | off |
| **Enable Item Embargo** | Turns on item embargoes. While it is ticked, the Cast Stack skips an item that a command or another character has embargoed (-ItemEmbargo, by the item's LinkID) until the time is up, and using an item on the Item Embargo tab's list tells your other characters to hold off it. While it is off, nothing is sent, and embargoes are still kept but not followed, so ticking it later honours any that are still running. | off |



## Pop up windows

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Accept Loot** | Lets the bot answer loot windows, using the choices on the Loot tab (for example lotto accept or decline, and free-for-all accept). When off, loot windows are left for you. | off |
| **Loot Corpses/Chests** | The bot loots corpses and chests, and picks up shinies, that are already within reach, unless you are in combat with something to attack. Shinies wait until you are out of combat. It does not walk to them. It also turns on a fix for mobs that get stuck in a 'dead but not lootable' state, by using the Loot action on them.<br>*Shinies can be switched off on the Loot tab.* | off |
| **Do not loot Corpses** | When looting is on, corpses are skipped. Chests and shinies are still looted. This also applies to the Instance Controller, which otherwise walks the group to the corpses around each named to loot them. | off |

| **Loot InCombat** | Lets the bot loot corpses and chests within reach while you are in combat with something to attack. It is separate from 'Loot Corpses/Chests', which covers every other moment, so tick both to loot at all times. Shinies always wait until you are out of combat. | off |
| **Move to loot-bugged mobs** | Off unless you tick it. The Instance Controller turns it on for its runs (a Startup Options row). Needs 'Loot Corpses/Chests'. When the mob you have targeted is stuck in the 'dead but not lootable' state and is too far away to loot, but no more than 40 m away, the bot moves you to it so the fix can use the Loot action on it, then moves you back to where you were. Only a character that has that mob targeted moves. The move takes priority over the camp spot: the camp spot does not pull you back until you are back. It gives up after 20 seconds getting there or 20 seconds getting back, and a zone with no navigation mesh is skipped. |  |
| **Accept Invites** | Accepts group and raid invites from characters on your EQ2Chars list. With the Other tab's option for anyone in range also on, it accepts invites from any nearby player. | off |
| **Accept No Choice Rewards** | When a reward window appears that offers only one reward and nothing to choose, the bot accepts it. New quest offers and reward windows with choices are left alone. | off |
| **Accept Res** | When someone offers you a resurrect, the bot waits the time set in 'Wait __ 10ths/second to accept RES' on the Setup tab, then accepts, but only if you are still dead and the window is still open. | off |
| **Accept Zone-In Confirmation** | Accepts the 'Do you wish to enter and apply the associated lockout?' prompt when you zone into an instance. | off |
| **Accept Raid Ready Checks** | Accepts raid ready checks automatically. | off |
| **Accept Dungeon is Ready** | Accepts dungeon finder 'Dungeon: ... is ready' pop-ups and Battle for Felwithe match prompts. It also accepts group-option votes started by characters on your EQ2Chars list. | off |
| **Do not auto accept quests** | By default the bot accepts every quest offered to you. Tick this to stop that. The accept-quest command also respects it.<br>*The Get Quest tool ticks this for itself while it runs and puts it back afterwards.* | off (so quests ARE auto-accepted) |
| **Do not auto accept trades from trusted toons** | By default, when one of the characters on your EQ2Chars list accepts a trade with you, the bot accepts it too. Tick this to stop that. Trades with anyone else are never auto accepted. | off (so trades from your own characters ARE auto-accepted) |
| **Do not auto-repair with Mender bots** | By default, when a repair bot (a Mender bot) is put down within 8 m of you while you are out of combat, the bot repairs your gear at it. Tick this to stop that. That includes a Mender bot the Instance Controller summons with 'Summon Mender bot to sell': it still sells, it just does not repair first. The repair command still works. | off (so a nearby repair bot IS used) |

# Setup

Setup holds the numbers that tune when the bot fights: how hurt a mob must be before you attack it, move to it or send your pet, how much health and power you keep before using attacks, and how many mobs an area attack needs. It also names who the Force Follow command follows. The right-hand column controls how tells and guild chat reach OgreConsole. Blank boxes use the default shown in each description.

## Setup

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **% NPC HP to attack** | The bot only attacks a mob once its health is at or below this percent. It covers Cast Stack attacks (CA and Debuff types), moving into combat position, Turn Off Attack and Cancel Invis After Combat.<br>*A Cast Stack entry with its own 'NPC HP' condition ignores this box.* | blank (counts as 100 - any health) |
| **% NPC HP to move into attack range** | The move options on Settings (move behind, in front, or into melee range) only start once the mob's health is at or below this percent. Once movement has started for a fight, it carries on until there is nothing left to attack.<br>*'Ignore NPC HP to move' on Settings skips this check.* | blank (counts as 100 - any health) |
| **% NPC HP for pet to attack** | Your pet and your mercenary are only sent in once the mob's health is at or below this percent.<br>*'Do not send pet to attack' on Settings stops the pet entirely.* | blank (counts as 100 - any health) |
| **% Power req. to use CAs** | The Cast Stack uses no attack abilities (CA and Debuff types) while your power is below this percent.<br>*A Cast Stack entry with its own 'My MP' condition ignores this box.* | blank (0 - no limit) |
| **% Health req. to use CAs** | The Cast Stack uses no attack abilities (CA and Debuff types) while your health is below this percent.<br>*A Cast Stack entry with its own 'My HP' condition ignores this box.* | blank (0 - no limit) |
| **Wait __ 10ths/second to accept RES** | When someone offers you a resurrection and 'Accept Res' on Settings is ticked, the bot waits this long before accepting, in tenths of a second (10 = 1 second). It then accepts only if you are still dead and the offer is still open. | blank (accepts straight away) |
| **Targets for Smart AEs** | How many mobs must be in range before the bot uses a point-blank or targeted area attack, while 'AE Smart CAs' on the Settings tab is ticked.<br>*A Cast Stack entry's own '# of mobs' overrides this.* | blank (counts as 2) |
| **Targets for Smart Encounters** | How many mobs the linked encounter must have before the bot uses an encounter-wide attack, while 'Encounter Smart CAs' on the Settings tab is ticked. A single mob never qualifies.<br>*A Cast Stack entry's own '# of mobs' overrides this; a '# of mobs' of 1 always allows it.* | blank (counts as 2) |
| **Melee move when less (40)** | The move options on Settings only move you when the mob is closer than this distance. 'Face mob in combat' only turns you toward mobs within this distance too. | blank (counts as 40) |
| **Auto Follow:** | Who Auto Follow follows: a group member's name, or an alias such as @Tank (your custom * aliases are listed while Enable Aliases on Settings is ticked). With 'Auto Follow Mode' on Settings ticked, the bot starts the game's own /follow on them whenever you are out of combat with nothing to attack, not already following anyone, and they are alive and closer than 'Auto Follow within'. The `-forcefollow` command starts it straight away.<br>*The list shows your group and raid members, the built-in @ aliases that name somebody right now, and your custom * aliases while Enable Aliases is ticked.* | empty |
| **Auto Follow within (35):** | Auto Follow only starts while the person is closer than this, measured flat (height left out). Blank means 35. 0 never starts it on its own; `-forcefollow` ignores this distance. | blank (35) |



## OgreConsole

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Only send tells from characters NOT in EQ2Chars** | Every tell this character receives is shown in OgreConsole on all your sessions. Tick this to send only tells from strangers, meaning characters not in your EQ2Chars list. | off (every tell is sent) |
| **Broadcast guild talk through OgreConsole** | Guild and officer chat that this character sees is sent to OgreConsole on all your sessions, as 'name -> <Guild>: text'.<br>*Tick it on one character per guild, or each line arrives once for every character that has it on.* | off |
| **Play annoying noise when receiving a tell from a stranger** | When a broadcast tell from a stranger (someone not in the receiving character's EQ2Chars list) reaches this session, a loud alarm sound plays.<br>*It is read on the session that plays the sound, not on the character that got the tell.* | off |
| **Do not show OgreConsole when you get a tell from a friend** | Normally OgreConsole opens when a broadcast tell arrives. Tick this so it only opens for tells from strangers, not from characters in EQ2Chars.<br>*The 'never auto open OgreConsole' option still wins over this.* | off (opens for every tell) |



## Good to know

- All the percentage boxes compare the MOB's health (or yours) to the number: 'at or below' for the mob boxes, 'at or above' for your own health and power.
- 'Attack NPC with 100% HP' on the Settings tab switches off the attack and pet mob-health boxes in one go. 'Ignore NPC HP to move' on Settings does the same for the move box.
- Auto Follow starts only out of combat with nothing to attack, and only when you are not already following someone. Once the game's /follow is running, the bot leaves it to the game.
- The OgreConsole boxes about sound and opening the console are read on the session that RECEIVES the broadcast tell, not on the character that got the tell.

# Status

Status shows what this bot is holding, ignoring or set to right now, grouped by topic: whether it is paused, why it is or is not assisting, whether Auto Target is suppressed, No Move and the camp spot, who it is following, which fighters are not being counted, and what is disabled in the Cast Stack. Anything out of the ordinary is highlighted. Nothing on this tab is saved. When something is holding up another tab, that tab gets an amber dot in the tab list, which you can see from any tab, and a Held line beside its title. Hover the dot to see why. If a player or a script set the hold, the Held line has a Release button. Holds the bot sets itself end on their own.

## Good to know

- The tab updates about twice a second while the OgreBot window is open.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/ability-embargo.md

# Ability Embargo

The tab is for abilities that only one of your characters should use at a time. When this character casts an ability on the list, it tells your other characters not to cast that same ability for a set time (the Duration, or the ability's own duration if left blank). It works while 'Enable Ability Embargo' is ticked on the Settings tab, on the character that casts it and on the ones that should hold off. To build the list, click an ability on the left, set the options in the form under the Ability Embargo List, then press Add. Click a row on the right to change it, double-click a row to switch it off, drag a row to move it, and use the X to remove it.

## Ability Embargo

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one to put it in the form under the Ability Embargo List, or double-click it to add it straight to the list with no options. The search box above filters it. | your abilities |



## Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Globally Mute messages** | Sends every embargo from this tab without showing it in OgreConsole, as if every row had Hide from OgreConsole ticked. Nothing is stopped: the embargo still goes out, over IRC too if the row has IRC ticked.<br>*Some Instance Controller setups tick it for you.* | off |
| **Ability Embargo List** | The abilities that are embargoed when you cast them, each with its Duration and options. When you cast an ability on this list, the other characters hold off that ability for its Duration. Click a row to load it into the form below and change it, double-click to switch it off, drag to reorder, X to remove. | empty |



## Add form (under the list)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Ability name** | The ability for the new row. Clicking an ability on the left fills it in, or you can type and pick from the suggestions. |  |
| **Duration** | How many seconds your other characters should hold off. Leave it blank to use the ability's own duration. | blank |
| **Add** | Seconds added to the duration, for example to hold off a little longer than the ability's own duration. | blank |
| **Subtract** | Seconds taken off the duration, for example so the next character is ready just before the first one's runs out. | blank |
| **IRC** | Also sends the embargo over IRC, to characters on other computers. | off |
| **Group** | Sends the embargo only to characters in this character's group. | off |
| **Me** | Stops only this character from recasting the ability for the duration. Nothing is sent to anyone else. | off |
| **Incl. caster** | Adds who cast it and the ability's name to the end of the embargo line, so anyone reading OgreConsole or IRC can see where it came from. | off |
| **Hide from OgreConsole** | Sends the embargo without showing it in OgreConsole. It still reaches your other characters. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the ability in the form, with the Duration and ticks you set, to the Ability Embargo List. Pressing Enter in a box does the same. After you click a row it becomes Update and saves your changes to that row instead (Cancel backs out). |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks every option in the form. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next Add. The Duration box is left as it is. |  |



## Good to know

- Nothing is sent unless 'Enable Ability Embargo' (Settings tab) is ticked on the character that casts the ability. The characters that should hold off need it ticked too, or they ignore the embargo.
- A row is matched by the ability, whatever its rank, and the embargo is sent by name, so a character with a different rank of it holds off too.
- An instant ability sends when it is cast. An ability with a cast time sends when the cast bar shows it, so a cast that never started sends nothing. If something makes it instant, so there is no cast bar, it sends once the ability is seen on cooldown, up to 3 seconds later. Casting a listed ability by hand counts too, if it shows on the cast bar.
- If a row has no Duration and the ability has none of its own (some last until cancelled), nothing is sent and the console says so. Give the row a Duration.
- The embargo is sent with the -AbilityEmbargo command, so you can watch it go out in OgreConsole (unless Hide from OgreConsole or Globally Mute is ticked). The character that cast the ability gets it too, as in the old bot. You can also send one yourself: -AbilityEmbargo takes an ability name or an ID.
- Loading a profile clears every ability and item embargo still running on that character.

# Ability Research

The game's Knowledge window can research one ability upgrade at a time, and each one takes days. This tab keeps a priority list of the abilities you want researched and which tiers you want. When it runs, the bot opens the Knowledge window, claims any finished research, and starts the first row on your list that the game offers at a tier you ticked. It runs by itself when your profile loads and 30 seconds after a 'Research of ... has been completed' message, unless 'Do not check Research on load' is ticked on the Settings tab. The left list shows what the game offers right now: press Preview to fill it. Click an ability there, tick the tiers you want, and press Add. On the right, drag rows to set priority (top first), click a row to change it, double-click to switch it off, and use the X to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Sort by Name** | Sorts the left list A to Z. When unticked it is sorted by level, highest first. Display only - it changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*It sits beside the search box, which only appears once the list has entries.* | off |
| **Full Research list** | What the game's research window is offering right now. Each row reads like '[097] Kick IV (Adept)': the level, the ability, and the tier researching it would give. Click one to put it in the form on the right, or double-click to add it straight to your list with no tiers ticked.<br>*The label shows '(press Preview)' while empty and '(N available)' once filled.* | empty until Preview, Claim + start next or a profile load fills it |
| **Research List** | Your research priorities, top first. Each row shows the ability's level, its name and the tiers you want (J, A, E, M, G, Anc). Drag to reorder, click to change, double-click to switch a row off, X to remove.<br>*A switched-off row is skipped.* | empty |



## Full Research list (left)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search ... abilities** | Type to filter the left list. Display only. |



## Research List (right)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Preview** | Opens the Knowledge window, fills the left list with what is on offer, and reports in the console what it would claim and start. It claims and starts nothing, then closes the window. |
| **Claim + start next** | Does it for real: claims any finished research, then, if nothing is being researched, starts the first enabled row on your list that the game offers at a tier you ticked. Research takes days.<br>*Posts 'Researching ...' (or 'NO RESEARCH STARTED...') to OgreConsole.* |
| **Clear list** | Removes every row from your Research List after asking you to confirm. Your abilities are not touched. |



## Add form (under the list)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Ability name** | The ability for the new row. Clicking an ability on the left fills it in, or you can type and pick from the suggestions. It must be the full name with its rank, for example 'Kick IV'. |  |
| **Journeyman** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Journeyman. | off |
| **Adept** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Adept. | off |
| **Expert** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Expert. | off |
| **Master** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Master. | off |
| **Grandmaster** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Grandmaster. | off |
| **Ancient** | Research this ability when the upgrade on offer is to Ancient. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the ability in the form, with the tiers you ticked, to the bottom of your Research List. After you click a row it becomes Update and saves your changes to that row instead (Cancel backs out). |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks all six tiers in the form. Otherwise the ticks carry over to the next Add. |  |



## Good to know

- A tier tick means 'research it TO this tier', and only the tiers you tick. Ticking Expert and Ancient researches upgrades to Expert or Ancient but skips Master and Grandmaster, for example because you craft those yourself.
- A row with no tier ticked is never researched. Double-clicking an ability on the left adds it with no tiers, so click the row afterwards and tick some.
- Rows match the ability's full name, rank included, so 'Kick IV' is not 'Kick V'. The number in brackets on each row is its level. '[--]' means the ability is not in this character's ability export, usually because it is out of date or from another character. 'Clear list' empties the list so you can start again.
- A row the game offers that is not in this character's ability export is reported to OgreConsole and passed over, and the next row gets its turn.
- If nothing on your list can be started, the bot posts 'NO RESEARCH STARTED. Review Ability Research Tab' to OgreConsole.
- The tier ticks stay ticked after Add, so you can add several abilities with the same tiers. 'Clear Options' unticks them.

# Ability Tracker

Ability Tracker watches the cooldowns of a short list of your abilities and shares them with all your characters. Its main use is the OgreMCP window: a button that casts a tracked ability turns red and counts down its cooldown, based on whichever of your characters has the longest wait for it. It only runs while 'Enable Ability Tracker' is ticked on the Settings tab. To add an ability, click it in the Full Ability list and press Add, or double-click it. On the right, double-click a row to switch it off, or use the X to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one to select it for the Add button below, or double-click it to add it to the Ability Tracker List straight away. | your abilities |
| **Ability Tracker List** | The abilities whose cooldowns are tracked, shown A to Z. Twice a second the bot reads how long each has left and shares it with your other characters, and the OgreMCP window shows it on matching buttons. Double-click a row to switch it off, X to remove.<br>*Needs 'Enable Ability Tracker' on the Settings tab.* | empty |

## Full Ability list (left)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search ... abilities** | Type to filter the ability list. Display only. |
| **Add** | Adds the ability you clicked in the list above to the Ability Tracker List. It is greyed out until you click one, and the name you picked is shown beside it. |

## Good to know

- Nothing happens until 'Enable Ability Tracker' is ticked on the Settings tab.
- An MCP button only lights up if its cast command names the ability without its rank, for example 'Kick' and not 'Kick VII'. The tracker matches on the plain name.
- Keep the list short. Every ability on it is checked twice a second and sent to your other characters.
- An ability this character does not have (not in its ability export) is skipped without a message.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/aliases.md

# Aliases

An alias is a nickname for one character, so your setup can say `*MainTank` instead of a real name. Type the alias and who it is for, then Add. The bot puts a star in front, so 'MainTank' becomes `*MainTank`, and you use that in a Cast Stack target or in a command's 'for who'. 'For' can be a character name or a class word (a class, subclass or archetype such as Fury or Priest). The bot checks you first, then your group, then your raid, and picks the first character that fits. Aliases only work while 'Enable Aliases' on the Settings tab is ticked.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Aliases** | Your aliases, in the order they are tried. Drag to reorder, double-click to switch one off, x to delete. The colour shows whether the alias is used on the Cast Stack and whether this row is the one that wins right now. | empty |



## Add an alias

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Alias (e.g. RaidMT)** | The nickname. The bot adds a star in front, so you use it as `*RaidMT`. | empty |
| **For (player / class / role)** | Who the alias means: a character name, or a class word such as a class, subclass or archetype. The first match wins: you, then your group, then your raid.<br>*An alias with an empty For never points at anyone.* | empty |
| **No-Raid** | Only look in your own group for this alias, never the rest of the raid. | off |
| **Add Alias** | Adds the alias to the end of the list. The same alias name can be added again with a different For, as a backup.<br>*An exact repeat (same alias, same For) is refused with a console message. Press Save to keep it.* |  |
| **Display Aliases** | Prints every alias, and the character each one points to right now, in the console. |  |
| **Team Groups…** | Opens the Team Groups window. A team group is one word (`*Team:Name`) that selects many characters and is shared by every session. |  |



## Good to know

- The alias list is drawn by its own code. Each row shows the alias, an arrow, and who it is for; NR means 'no raid'. Drag a row to reorder, double-click a row to switch it off, and the x deletes it (after a confirm).
- Several rows can share one alias name. The first row, from the top, that finds a character in your group or raid wins, so later rows are backups. Drag rows to choose which one is tried first.
- The name colour tells you two things. Green: used on the Cast Stack, and this row is the one the alias points to now. Yellow: used on the Cast Stack, but a different row (or nobody) wins right now. Orange: not used on the Cast Stack, but this row wins. Red: not used on the Cast Stack, and this row does not win.
- With 'Enable Aliases' (Settings tab) off, no alias resolves: every row shows yellow or red and a line above the list says so.
- Adding, removing or switching an alias off takes effect at once, but it is only kept if you press Save at the top.
- An alias picks ONE character. To aim at several characters with one word, use Team Groups (the button under the list) instead.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/announce.md

# Announce

Announce says something, or runs a command, whenever one of your abilities goes off. Each row is an ability, where to send it (Group, Raid, a tell to the target, an in-game command or a console command) and the text. In the text, *Target* becomes the name of whoever the ability was cast on and *Ability* becomes the ability's name. Nothing is announced unless 'Enable Announce Tab' on the Settings tab is ticked.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one to choose it for the next announce; its name appears next to the Add button. |  |
| **Announces** | Your announce rows, shown as ability, destination and text. Every switched-on row whose ability matches goes out, at any rank.<br>*Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off.* | empty |



## Announce

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Announce To** | Where the text goes. Group: group chat. Raid: raid chat. Tell To Target: a tell to the player the ability was cast on. In-Game Command: runs the text as a game command, so it must start with /. Execute In Console: runs the text as a console command. | Group |
| **Text to announce** | What to say or run. *Target* becomes the target's name and *Ability* the ability's name. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds a row for the ability you clicked, with this destination and text. When you are editing a row it says Update and saves your changes to that row instead. |  |



## Good to know

- To add a row: click an ability in the Full Ability list (its name shows next to Add), pick 'Announce To', type the text, then press Add or Enter.
- Click a saved row to load it back into the form; the button then says Update, and Cancel leaves it unchanged. Double-click a row to switch it off, and the x removes it. The list is shown A to Z.
- Instant abilities announce when the bot casts them. Abilities with a cast time announce when they appear on your cast bar, which includes casts you make by hand.
- For a cast you made by hand the bot does not know the target, so a row that uses *Target* or 'Tell To Target' is skipped for it.
- *Target* and *Ability* work in capitals or small letters. A text that contains NULL or ${ once they are filled in is not sent.
- A 'Tell To Target' row only goes out when the target is a player in your zone. A tell to an NPC, a pet or a mercenary is skipped.
- 'In-Game Command' text must start with / (for example `/shout *Ability* is up!`). 'Execute In Console' text must NOT start with /; it runs as a console command, for example an `oc` line.
- Group rows only go out while you are grouped, Raid rows only while you are in a raid.
- Only abilities are listed, not items.

# Ascension

The Ascension tab has one option. Etherflash normally teleports you to your target when it lands. With 'Etherflash - Prevent Port' ticked, the bot targets you yourself just before the cast finishes, so the damage still lands but you do not move. About a second after the cast ends it lets go, and your normal target comes back.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Etherflash - Prevent Port** | When the bot casts Etherflash, it switches your target to yourself once the cast is over 90% done, so the teleport takes you nowhere. About a second after the cast ends, your normal target returns.<br>*Only for Etherflash casts made by the bot, any rank.* | off |

## Good to know

- It only works when the bot casts Etherflash (for example from the Cast Stack). If you press Etherflash yourself, nothing changes.
- If nothing else is choosing your target (no assist, no auto-target), the bot puts back the target you had before the cast.

# Assist

Assist tells the bot whose fight to join. Pick people (or aliases such as @Tank) from the dropdown and they go into the Assist order list. While the bot is running, it uses the FIRST person on the list who is in your group or raid and in your zone: it targets that player, so your attacks go at whatever they are fighting. With 'Direct Assist Targeting' on Settings ticked, it targets that player's target directly instead. Drag names to change the priority, double-click a name to switch it off, and click x to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Choose whom to assist** | Pick a group or raid member, or an alias such as @Tank, to add them to the bottom of the Assist order list. The dropdown then resets; a name already on the list is not added twice.<br>*The choices are refreshed every time you open the dropdown.* | n/a (it adds a name, it stores nothing itself) |
| **Only assist within (meters)** | The bot only assists players within this many meters of you. A player further away is skipped, the same as a player in another zone: the bot tries the next name on the list, and if nobody is close enough your target is left alone. Leave it blank for 100. 0 means no limit. |  |
| **Assist order — drag to set priority, double-click to disable** | The people to assist, in priority order. The bot uses the first one who is in your group or raid, in this zone and within range, and ignores the rest until that person is gone.<br>*Disabled names stay in place (struck through) and are skipped.* | empty |



## Assist

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Drag a row** | Drag a row up or down to change who is assisted first. |
| **Double-click a row** | Switches that name off or back on. A switched-off name is struck through and skipped, but keeps its place. |
| **x (remove)** | Removes that name from the list. |



## Good to know

- The list is used whenever the bot is running and Auto Target is off, even if 'Auto Assist' on Settings is unticked. To stop assisting, disable or remove the names here.
- When 'Enable Auto Target' is ticked on the Auto Target tab, this list is ignored completely.
- An assist set by the `-assist` command takes priority over this list until it is turned off.
- Someone in your group but in another zone is skipped, and the next name down is used.
- Aliases are looked up each time, so @Tank follows whoever is your tank right now. An alias that points at nobody is skipped.
- Changes take effect straight away. Press Save at the top to keep them after a reload.
- Type `ogre assist` to see who the bot is assisting right now and why.

# Auto-Hunt

Auto-Hunt is a simple grinding mode. The bot looks for a mob near you, targets it and opens the fight with the first ready ability from your Pull Abilities list; your Cast Stack then fights as usual. Pick a saved path under Path and it walks that path between pulls; with none picked it pulls what comes within the scan radius. This tab is marked not finished. To switch it on, tick Auto Hunt or use the OgreConsole command `-autohunt` with hunt or off. It only runs while OgreBot is open with a profile loaded and the bot is not paused.

## Auto-Hunt

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto Hunt** | Ticked, Auto-Hunt runs on this character: scan, camp, prebuff, pull, and walk the path picked below between pulls. Switching it on tells the rest of your group to follow you (OgreFollow, through OgreConsole); switching it off leaves them following. It pulls nothing while you fly, and pulls again once you land. The same switch as the OgreConsole command `-autohunt` (hunt or off). It never loads ticked: a profile always starts with it off. | off |



## Auto Hunt Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Scan radius (box)** | How far around you the bot looks for a mob to pull, and for mobs attacking your group. Leave it blank to use the longest reach among your pull abilities (35 if none has a reach on file). A pull is only used on a mob it can reach. | empty (the longest pull reach) |
| **Check Aggro** | While anyone in your group (or raid) is in combat, the bot stops pulling and holds still. Your normal combat settings handle the fight. | off |
| **Check HP @** | While anyone in your group (or raid) has less health than the % in the box beside it, the bot stops pulling and holds still.<br>*A group member who is not in the zone counts as low health. A blank box never stops the hunt.* | off |
| **Check HP @ (box)** | The health % used by Check HP @. Only used while Check HP @ is ticked. | empty (never stops the hunt) |
| **Check Mana @** | While anyone in your group (or raid) has less power than the % in the box beside it, the bot stops pulling and holds still. | off |
| **Check Mana @ (box)** | The power % used by Check Mana @. Only used while Check Mana @ is ticked. | empty (never stops the hunt) |
| **Check if any group members dead** | While anyone in your group (or raid) is dead, the bot stops pulling and holds still.<br>*A group member who is not in the zone also counts as dead, so the hunt waits for them to arrive.* | off |



## Ignore mobs by con

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Gray** | The bot never pulls gray-con mobs.<br>*A gray mob already attacking your group is still fought.* | off |
| **Green** | The bot never pulls green-con mobs. | off |
| **Blue** | The bot never pulls blue-con mobs. | off |
| **White (even)** | The bot never pulls white-con (even) mobs. | off |
| **Yellow** | The bot never pulls yellow-con mobs. | off |
| **Orange** | The bot never pulls orange-con mobs. | off |
| **Red** | The bot never pulls red-con mobs. | off |
| **Non-Aggro** | The bot only pulls mobs that would attack you on sight. Mobs that leave you alone are skipped. | off |
| **Named** | The bot never pulls named mobs.<br>*Even when unticked, normal mobs in range are pulled before named ones.* | off |



## Pull Abilities

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **First ready one is used; drag order = priority** | Your pull list. When the bot has a mob targeted and you are out of combat, it uses the first entry from the top that is ready. Type in the box above to find one of your abilities or items; picking it adds it. Drag rows to change the order, double-click a row to switch it off or on.<br>*With an empty list the bot targets mobs but never pulls them.* | empty |



## Behaviour

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Campspot** | When the bot finds a mob to pull, the whole group camps at your spot and holds there for the fight. A new pull from the same spot sends nothing. When no mob has been in reach for 1.5 seconds (3 with Delay After Combat), the group is let go and follows you again; turning Auto Hunt off or pausing the bot lets it go too.<br>*It switches 'Allow Camp Spot' on for each toon. The rest of the group is let go with a full LetsGo. A toon more than 125 from your spot is not pulled in: it stands where it is until the group moves on, and one line in the console names it. Only toons on this PC are reached (OgreConsole).* | off |
| **CS-JO-JI** | Like Campspot, and the casters stay at the camp while the rest of the group may leave it to fight. Campspot wins if both are ticked. | off |
| **Prebuff** | Before each pull, the bot targets you, turns auto-attack on and waits 3 seconds, so your normal buffs have time to go out. Then it targets the mob.<br>*It does not cast buffs itself; your Cast Stack does that.* | off |
| **Ignore Collision** | Normally the bot skips mobs it cannot see (a wall or hill in the way). Tick this to let it pull those too.<br>*It looks from your eye height to the mob's, the same check your pull ability must pass to be cast.* | off |
| **Delay After Combat** | With Campspot or CS-JO-JI, the group waits 3 seconds with no mob in reach before it is let go to follow you again, instead of 1.5. | off |
| **Pause on Exquisite Chest drop** | While an Exquisite chest is lying within 50 of you, the bot stops pulling and holds still, so you can deal with it.<br>*It carries on by itself once the chest is gone.* | off |



## Path

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Walk this path** | Which of this zone's saved paths Auto-Hunt walks between pulls. It stops for each pull and carries on at the same point. A walk that ended or could not start stays ended: pick the path again to walk it. Choose (none) to hunt where you stand. The list is the zone you are in: another zone has its own.<br>*A name saved for another zone gets one line here, and the bot hunts where it stands.* | (none) |
| **Edit** | Opens the picked path in the Paths window, where you add, insert, drag and remove its points: `ogre paths <path>`. With (none) picked, the window opens with no path selected. A picked path this zone does not have gets one line. |  |



## Good to know

- The Auto Hunt box and `-autohunt` in OgreConsole (hunt / off) are one switch. It is not saved with your profile, so Auto-Hunt starts off every time the bot is loaded fresh.
- A mob that is already attacking your group is targeted before any new pull, whatever its con. The con, Non-Aggro and Named filters only decide which NEW mob to pull. With 'Check Aggro' ticked the bot instead holds still and leaves that fight to your normal combat settings.
- 'Check if any group members dead' and 'Check HP @' also count a group member who is not in the zone. The hunt waits until they arrive.
- Pulls only happen while you are out of combat, and only if at least one entry in the pull list is ready to use. With an empty list the bot targets a mob and just waits, and one line in the console says so.
- If the Scan radius box is blank, the bot looks 35 around you.
- A mob it picks stays picked until a different answer has held for 0.3 seconds, so a mob that blinks out of sight for a moment does not stop and start the hunt.
- Auto-Hunt only walks: it never flies a path, whatever the Nav window's fly setting, and a toon in the air lands first. A point no walking route reaches ends the walk with a line naming it. It stops walking for each pull, for a tripped safety check, for anything that attacks it and while it is dead, then carries on at the same point. A path that ends, is ended by a zone, or cannot start is not tried again until you pick it again in the list or send `-autohunt hunt`; the bot hunts where it stands.
- Auto-Hunt pulls nothing while you fly: no pull, no target, no camp and no safety hold, and a pull it was working ends. One line in the console says so as you take off. Its own walk lands first and then pulls; a walk you started yourself flies on.
- The group: switching Auto Hunt on makes the rest of your group follow you. With Campspot or CS-JO-JI ticked, each pull camps everyone at your spot (not where each toon happens to stand), nothing more goes out during the fight, and when no mob has been in reach for 1.5 seconds they are let go and follow you again. Only a pull more than 5 from the held spot sends the spot again. Death holds everything as it is; a zone forgets the camp without sending anything.
- A walk with no hunting is the Start button of the `ogre paths` window. Hunting does not end a walk you started, and that walk waits while the bot works a pull, but never in the air.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/cancel-on-cast.md

# Cancel On Cast

Some casts spoil a buff you keep up, so that buff needs to be cancelled and cast again fresh. Each row here says: when you cast THIS, cancel THESE buffs. The Cast Stack then puts them back. To build a row, click what you cast in list 1 and one or more buffs in list 2 (click a buff again to unpick it), then press Add. The row appears in Cancels setup, for example 'Armored -> Battle Tactics, Call of Shielding'. It only runs inside instances unless you tick the overland box. It waits while you are in combat, and it waits while the bot is paused.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **1. When you cast this  (ability or item)** | Pick the cast that should trigger the cancel. Abilities and items are both listed; items start with 'Item:'. Click one to select it. It is highlighted until you press Add. | your abilities and items |
| **2. ...cancel these  (pick several)** | Pick the buffs to cancel when that cast happens. Click as many as you like, and click one again to unpick it. Only buffs that last until cancelled are listed. | your until-cancelled buffs |
| **Cancels setup** | Your rows: the cast, then the buffs it cancels. After that cast, each buff still up is cancelled one at a time, once a second, until it is gone. Drag to reorder, double-click to switch a row off, X to remove.<br>*A 'C' on a row means it may cancel during combat. Tick 'In combat' beside Add when you make the row.* | empty |

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Also run in overland zones (by default this only runs inside instances)** | Lets the cancels happen in overland zones too. When unticked they only happen inside instances. | off |

## Build a row

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add** | Adds a row with your picks from lists 1 and 2 to Cancels setup. Tick 'In combat' beside it first to let that row cancel during a fight. It is greyed out until both lists have a pick (hover it to see which is missing). When several buffs are picked it reads 'Add (3)'. |

## Good to know

- While you are in combat the cancel is held until combat ends, however long the fight lasts. The 30-second limit below only starts counting once it is out of combat.
- Every cast the bot makes counts. A cast you make by hand counts only if it shows a cast bar, so an instant cast by hand is missed. Ranks do not matter: a row for 'Armored' fires on 'Armored IV' too.
- List 2 only shows buffs that last until cancelled. Timed buffs run out on their own, so they are left out.
- A buff on several people is cancelled once per second until it is gone everywhere. The bot gives up after 30 seconds or 12 tries (time held in combat does not count).
- Scripts can fire a row without casting anything: -CancelOnCast <who> "Armored" acts as if you had just cast Armored.

# Chat Events

Chat Events watches the game's incoming text for words you choose. When a line contains your text, the bot can run a console command, post a line to OgreConsole, play a 'Ding' sound, or any mix of the three. Nothing happens until you tick "Enable Chat Events" on the Settings tab. You build the events with the boxes at the top, and they appear in the Configured Events list below. Click a row to edit it, double-click it to switch it off or on, drag it to reorder, and use the X to delete it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured Events** | Your chat events. Each row shows the text it watches for, its command, and OC or Ding if ticked. Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag a row to reorder, and click X to delete it.<br>*A switched-off row is kept but never fires. The order does not change anything; every active row is checked.* | empty |



## Add an event

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Text to watch for** | The text to look for in incoming game text. An event fires whenever a line contains this text, in any case.<br>*Required. An event with no text cannot be added.* | empty |
| **Code to execute (leave blank for nothing)** | A console command to run when the text is seen. It runs exactly as if you typed it into the InnerSpace console. Leave it blank if you only want the OC line or the Ding. | empty |
| **OC - on success, send a message to OgreConsole** | When the text is seen, a line goes to OgreConsole saying which character saw it, the text it matched and the full line. | off |
| **Ding - on success, play a 'Ding'** | When the text is seen, a 'Ding' sound plays on this PC. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the event to the list below. Pressing Enter in either text box does the same. While you are editing a row this button reads Update and saves your changes to that row. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks OC and Ding. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next event you add. |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while editing a row. Stops editing without changing the row. |  |



## Good to know

- Nothing here works until "Enable Chat Events" is ticked on the Settings tab.
- The match ignores upper and lower case and can be anywhere in the line. Short text like "a" or "the" matches almost every line.
- An event with no command, no OC and no Ding is ignored, and the console prints a warning about it.
- The OC and Ding ticks stay ticked for the next event you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Changes take effect within about a second. Press Save at the top to keep them for next time.
- Chat Events keep working while OgreBot is paused.

# Codex Inspect

Codex Inspect uploads the gear of the people in your group or raid to the EQ2Codex.com website, so you can see it there. You need an EQ2Codex API token first: press Setup API Token and paste the one from your eq2codex.com account. Opening the tab fills the left list (Roster) with your raid, or your group, or just you when solo. Each name shows how long until it can be inspected again, or 'ready'. Double-click names to move them into the right list (To Inspect), or press Queue All, then press Inspect Queued Now. The bot inspects each name in turn and uploads it. Names that upload leave the right list; names that fail stay there in red, marked FAIL.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Refresh from Group/Raid** | Reads your raid or group again and redraws the Roster. Opening the tab does this too. |  |
| **Roster (double-click to queue)** | Everyone in your raid, or your group, or just you when solo. Each name shows '(cd: ...)' with the time until it can be inspected again, or 'ready'. Double-click a name to add it to the To Inspect list.<br>*A name already in the To Inspect list is not added twice.* | empty until the tab is opened |
| **Queue All** | Adds every name in the Roster to the To Inspect list. |  |
| **To Inspect (double-click to remove)** | The names waiting to be inspected and uploaded. Double-click a name to take it out. Names leave on their own as they upload; failed ones stay in red, marked FAIL. | empty |
| **Clear Queue** | Empties the To Inspect list. It does not stop a run that has already started. |  |
| **Inspect Queued Now** | Starts a run: the bot inspects each name in the To Inspect list, one about every 3 seconds, and uploads their gear to eq2codex.com.<br>*Greyed out while a run is going. Names inspected in the last 5 minutes are skipped.* |  |
| **Reset Raid Force** | Clears your active group/raid on the eq2codex.com website, including the gear and adornments uploaded for it. Nothing on your PC changes.<br>*Greyed out while a run is going.* |  |

## Top of tab

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Visit EQ2Codex.com** | Opens eq2codex.com in your web browser. |
| **Wiki** | Opens the EQ2Codex help pages in your web browser. |
| **Setup API Token** | Opens the EQ2Codex API Token window, where you paste your token from eq2codex.com. The token is kept on this PC, outside your profile, and is never shown back to you.<br>*The same window opens from the Codex Toons tab. One token serves both.* |
| **View my Group/Raid** | Opens your active group/raid page on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |

## Good to know

- Nothing uploads until an API token is saved with Setup API Token. The line under the buttons says 'NOT configured' until then.
- A name inspected in the last 5 minutes is skipped. The Roster shows the time left for each name.
- The bot waits about 3 seconds between people, so a full raid takes a few minutes. Inspect Queued Now and Reset Raid Force are greyed out while a run is going.
- The inspect window pops open and closes for each person. That is normal.
- A FAIL row stays in the To Inspect list so you can see who failed. Press Inspect Queued Now again to retry them, or double-click to remove them.
- A '409' failure in the console means another uploader's account has already claimed that character.
- The To Inspect list is not saved in your profile. Closing OgreBot with its X stops a run in progress; the names not yet done stay in the list for next time you open it, until the bot is unloaded.

# Codex Toons

Codex Toons uploads a snapshot of your own character (gear and stats) to the EQ2Codex.com website. Press Setup API Token once to paste your token from eq2codex.com, then press Upload My Toon Snapshot whenever you want your page updated. The result, good or bad, is posted in OgreConsole. You can also have it upload by itself every time the bot camps you out. For your group or raid members, use the Codex Inspect tab instead.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Visit EQ2Codex.com** | Opens eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **Wiki** | Opens the EQ2Codex help pages in your web browser. |  |
| **Setup API Token** | Opens the EQ2Codex API Token window, where you paste your token from eq2codex.com. The token is kept on this PC, outside your profile, and is never shown back to you.<br>*Same window and same token as on the Codex Inspect tab.* |  |
| **Upload My Toon Snapshot** | Inspects your own character and uploads your gear and stats to eq2codex.com. OgreConsole reports whether it worked. |  |
| **(idle)** | The upload status: whether a token is set, and whether an upload is running. | (idle) |
| **View My Characters** | Opens your characters page on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **View My Group/Raids** | Opens your saved groups and raids on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **Auto-upload my toon snapshot to Codex when I camp (-camp / logout)** | When the bot camps you out, it first starts an upload of your toon snapshot. The camp does not wait for the upload.<br>*Only camps done by the bot count, not a /camp you type yourself.* | off |



## Good to know

- Nothing uploads until an API token is saved with Setup API Token. The same token is used by Codex Inspect.
- You must be in the world. The inspect window pops open on yourself for a moment while the bot reads your gear.
- If another upload is already running (for example a Codex Inspect run), the snapshot is refused and OgreConsole says so. Try again when it is done.
- The auto-upload on camp only happens when the bot does the camping (for example the camp command, or the Instance Controller's end-of-list camp). Typing /camp yourself does not upload.

# Consume Items

Consume Items keeps you using items such as potions and temporary buffs. While the bot is running and 'Enable Consume Items' is ticked on the Settings tab, it checks the list about once a second. It uses the first item that is in your bags and ready, then waits before using that item again for as long as its effect lasts (10 minutes if the bot cannot read the duration). The list order is the priority. By default it only works inside instances; the two boxes at the top also allow guild halls and overland zones. To build the list, click an item in the Full Item List (your registered items from the Items tab), tick 'In-combat' if it should only be used in combat, and press Add. On the Consume Item List, drag rows to change the order, click a row to edit it, double-click a row to switch it off or on, and use the x to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Item List** | Your registered items from the Items tab. Click one to pick it for the Add form, or double-click it to add it straight away with no options. | your registered items |
| **Consume Item List** | The items the bot uses, in priority order: each check it uses the first one that is in your bags, ready, and not waiting out its effect. 'IC' on a row means in combat only.<br>*Drag to reorder, click to edit, double-click to switch off or on, x to remove.* | empty |

## Where it works

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Allow in Guild Halls** | Lets the list be used automatically in a guild hall. Without it, nothing is used there. | off |
| **Allow in Overland zones** | Lets the list be used automatically outside instances, in overland and city zones. Without it, items are only used inside instances. | off |

## Item lists

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **In-combat** | The item being added is only used while you are in combat. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the item picked on the left to the end of the list, with the In-combat option as ticked. When you are editing a row, it reads Update and saves your change. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks In-combat. It otherwise stays ticked for the next Add. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing happens unless 'Enable Consume Items' is ticked on the Settings tab. Pausing the bot also stops it.
- The Full Item List only shows items registered on the Items tab. If it is empty, register your consumables there first.
- Double-clicking an item on the left adds it straight away, without the In-combat option. To set it, click once, tick In-combat, then press Add.
- Nothing is used while you are moving or dead. In combat, the bot waits at least 5 seconds between uses.
- The wait for each item's effect is kept only while the session runs. After a reload the bot may use an item again straight away.
- The OgreConsole command `-ConsumeItems_ProcessList_AP` runs the list on demand (add `-all` to use every eligible item, not just the first). It ignores the zone boxes and the pause, but still needs 'Enable Consume Items'.
- To see what it picks and when, tick ConsumeItemsDebug on the Debug tab.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/crowd-control.md

# Crowd Control

With Enable Crowd Control ticked on the Settings tab, the bot mezzes (or roots) the extra mobs that are attacking your group, using the abilities in the Priority Order list, top first. It never mezzes the mob your group is killing, and it renews a mez when it has 10 seconds or less left.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | Your abilities, with a search box. Click one and press Add (or double-click it) to put it in the Priority Order list. | filled from your ability export |
| **Priority Order** | The mez abilities to use, top first. The bot uses the first one that is ready and can reach the add. Double-click a row to turn it off without removing it.<br>*Drag to reorder, double-click to switch a row off, x to remove. Clicking a row loads it back into the form.* | empty |

## Crowd Control

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Allow Epics as Valid Targets** | Off: the bot never mezzes an epic mob. On: epic mobs can be mezzed like any other add. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the ability you clicked on the left to the bottom of the Priority Order list. Next to it you see the picked ability, or 'click an ability on the left' until you pick one. |  |

## Good to know

- Only mobs within 30 metres that are attacking someone in your group or raid are mezzed. A mob that is just standing nearby is left alone.
- The mob your group is killing is never mezzed: your own target, and the target of the person you assist.
- To cast a mez the bot briefly targets the add, then gives you your target back. It also turns auto-attack off first, because a swing would break the mez.
- The bot only knows about its own mezzes. It does not see a mez another player put on a mob.
- Nothing is mezzed in a city unless Allow City Casting is ticked, or while an encounter has told the group to stop attacking.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/despawn-event.md

# Despawn Event

Despawn Event is the opposite of Spawn Events: it fires when something whose name contains your text disappears. The bot can then run a console command, post a line to OgreConsole, play a 'Ding' sound, or any mix of the three. Nothing happens until you tick "Enable Despawn Event" on the Settings tab. Build events with the boxes at the top; they appear in the Configured Events list below.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured Events** | Your despawn events. Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag a row to reorder, and click X to delete it.<br>*A switched-off row is kept but never fires.* | empty |



## Add an event

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Actor to watch for** | Part or all of the name to watch for. The event fires when something with a matching name disappears. Upper and lower case must match exactly.<br>*Required. An event with no name cannot be added.* | empty |
| **Code to execute (leave blank for nothing)** | A console command to run when a match disappears. It runs exactly as if you typed it into the InnerSpace console. Leave it blank if you only want the OC line or the Ding. | empty |
| **OC - on success, send a message to OgreConsole** | When a match disappears, a line goes to OgreConsole saying which character saw it, the text it matched and the full name. | off |
| **Ding - on success, play a 'Ding'** | When a match disappears, a 'Ding' sound plays on this PC. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the event to the list below. Pressing Enter in either text box does the same. While you are editing a row this button reads Update and saves your changes to that row. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks OC and Ding. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next event you add. |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while editing a row. Stops editing without changing the row. |  |



## Good to know

- Nothing here works until "Enable Despawn Event" is ticked on the Settings tab.
- The name match is case-sensitive: "vindicator" does not match "a Vindicator". Part of the name is enough.
- Something leaving your view can count as disappearing, not only a mob that dies or despawns.
- An event with no command, no OC and no Ding is ignored, and the console prints a warning about it.
- The OC and Ding ticks stay ticked for the next event you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Despawn events keep working while OgreBot is paused.
