# NPC Cast Monitoring

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Two tabs. **Monitor** writes down every spell a mob casts, with its name and spell number. **Watch list** watches the mobs listed for your current zone, and when one starts a listed spell, the bot can interrupt it or run your commands.
>
> **Monitor**
>
> - **Start** / **Stop** - turns the log on and off. It keeps running while you fight, zone or die, until you press Stop or close the window (closing it is the same as `ogre end npccast`).
> - **my target + its target** - logs your target and your target's target. These are the only spells that come with a **name**, because the name is read off your cast bars. Target the mob, or target the tank the mob is attacking.
> - **+ named NPCs nearby** / **+ every NPC nearby** - also logs other casters within 100 metres. Their spells show a spell number but no name, unless you have seen that spell on your cast bar before.
> - **Copy** - puts the whole list on your clipboard, ready to paste.
> - **Clear** - empties the list for this zone.
> - Each zone has its own list, saved to the file named under it. Send that file, or paste the copied list, to whoever asked for it.
>
> **Watch list**
>
> - **Add the spell my target is casting** - press it while your target's cast bar is up.
> - **Add by hand** - type a mob name and a spell number.
> - **interrupt** - the bot interrupts that spell with an interrupt you have ready.
> - **label** / **commands** - opens a small editor under the spell. Type, then **Save** or **Cancel**.
> - **remove** / **remove mob** - stop watching a spell or a whole mob here.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - The Watch list only works when **NPC Cast Monitoring** is ticked on OgreBot's Settings tab. While it is off, a red bar tells you when a button cannot do anything. Interrupts and commands also need OgreBot open and not paused. The Monitor needs none of that.
> - **Scan radius** takes 5 to 500. Leave it empty to use the default.
> - Your changes go in your own list, so updates never remove them. **Reset my edits** deletes them all for this zone, with no undo.

**Open it:** Type `ogre npccast` (also `ogre npccastmonitoring`, `ogre npccast panel` or `ogre npccast config`). If the window is already open, this does nothing. `ogre npccast status` prints the watch status in the console instead. `ogre end npccast` (or the window's X) stops the Monitor and closes the window.

## What it is for

This window has two tabs. **Monitor** writes down every spell a mob casts, with the spell's name and its ability id, so you can copy the list or send the file to whoever asked for it. It only records; it never makes the bot do anything. **Watch list** watches the mobs listed for the zone you are in, found by their exact name. When a watched mob starts casting one of the listed spells, the bot can interrupt it, run your own commands, or both. Each zone has a shipped list that comes with the bot, and your own list on top of it. Everything you change on the Watch list goes into your own list, so a bot update never removes it. The window opens on the Monitor tab.

## Header and tabs

The top line shows the zone and a count. On the Monitor tab the count is how many spells are in the log. On the Watch list tab it is how many mobs and spells are listed and how many mobs are being watched right now.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Monitor** | Shows the Monitor tab: the log of what mobs cast. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*The window always opens on this tab.* | shown |
| **Watch list** | Shows the Watch list tab: the mobs and spells watched in this zone, and what the bot does about them. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does. |  |



## Monitor: what to log, Start and Stop

Pick whose spells to log, then press Start. One of the three buttons is always lit. Your target and your target's target are logged in every choice.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **my target + its target** | Logs the spells of your target and of your target's target. Players are left out. These are the only spells that come with a name, because the name is read off your cast bars. Target the mob, or target the tank the mob is attacking.<br>*Your choice is not saved. After you restart the game it is back to this one.* | on |
| **+ named NPCs nearby** | Also logs every named NPC within 100 meters of you. Their spells show the ability id but no name, unless that spell was once named from your cast bars.<br>*Changing this while the Monitor runs takes effect at once.* | off |
| **+ every NPC nearby** | Also logs every NPC within 100 meters of you, named or not. Their spells show the ability id but no name, unless that spell was once named from your cast bars. | off |
| **Start / Stop** | Start begins logging and the button turns into a red Stop. It checks four times a second and keeps going while you fight, zone or die, until you press Stop. Stop saves the log and stops; the list stays on screen.<br>*Closing the window stops it too (and saves the log), the same as `ogre end npccast`. It runs while OgreBot is closed or paused, and with NPC Cast Monitoring unticked.* |  |



## Monitor: the log

One row per mob and spell, in the order they were first seen. A grey bar above the log says what your last button press did. With either of the 'nearby' choices, a second grey bar explains why some spells have no name.

## Monitor: Copy, Clear and the file

Under the log: whether the Monitor is running ('monitoring') or 'stopped', the two buttons, and the file the log is saved to.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Copy** | Puts the whole log on your clipboard as text, ready to paste: a line with the zone name, a line naming the columns, then one line per row (mob \| spell \| ability id \| cast time \| seen). The grey bar says how many lines were copied.<br>*Greyed out while the log is empty.* |
| **Clear** | Empties the log for this zone, and its saved file too. Spell names already learned are kept.<br>*No confirmation and no undo. Greyed out while the log is empty.* |



## Watch list tab

The Watch list always shows the zone you are in right now. Everything below is on this tab.

## Watch list: header

On this tab the zone name is the name of the zone's list file. The counts on the right say how many mobs and spells are listed and how many mobs are being watched right now.

## Watch list: adding spells

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Add the spell my target is casting** | Target a mob while its cast bar is up and press this. The mob's name and the spell it is casting are added to your list for this zone. The result shows in a green (worked) or red (did not work) bar under the buttons.<br>*The spell is added with no label and no action, so nothing happens yet. Tick interrupt or add commands afterwards.* |  |
| **mob name (box)** | The name of the mob to add, exactly as the game shows it. Capital letters do not matter.<br>*This box is not cleared after adding (the number and label boxes are), so you can add several spells for the same mob.* | empty |
| **ability id (box)** | The spell's number (its ability id). Anything that is not a digit is removed. Cleared after adding. | empty |
| **label (optional) (box)** | A name you give the spell so you know what it is. Only shown in this window. Cleared after adding. | empty |
| **Add by hand** | Adds the typed mob and spell number to your list for this zone. Nothing happens if the mob name or the number is empty.<br>*If that mob already has that spell in your list, nothing changes (the label is not updated).* |  |



## Watch list: zone settings and files

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Scan radius (box)** | How far away (in meters) mobs are watched in this zone. The grey number is the value in use when the box is empty. | empty (50) |
| **Set** | Saves the scan radius into your list for this zone. It must be from 5 to 500. An empty box or 0 removes your value, so the shipped value (or 50) is used again.<br>*A number outside 5-500 is refused: a red bar says so and nothing is saved. Check the footer's 'scanning to' number for the value in use.* |  |
| **scan players instead of NPCs** | When ticked, this zone watches players instead of NPCs. Saved into your list for this zone at once.<br>*Only useful for testing in a guild hall with other players casting.* | off |
| **Reload** | Reads the lists for the zone you are in again from disk. Use it after you edit a list file by hand. |  |
| **Import Classic custom** | Copies the converted custom lists from OgreBot Classic into your own list folder. A zone you already have your own list for is skipped, never overwritten. The console says how many files were copied and skipped.<br>*This works even when NPC Cast Monitoring is turned off.* |  |
| **Reset my edits** | Deletes your own list for this zone, so only the shipped list is left. Everything you added, removed or changed in this zone is gone, including the scan radius and the players setting.<br>*There is no confirmation and no undo.* |  |



## Watch list: messages

Bars under the buttons tell you what happened. Green or red is the result of your last capture or edit: when something you pressed could not be done (monitoring is off, no zone is loaded, a scan radius out of range, a list file that cannot be read or written), a red bar says why. Other red bars are problems with a list file. Grey bars are notes.

## Watch list: the list

One block per mob. Under each mob is one row per spell. A yellow 'yours' tag means the mob or spell comes from your own list. 'radius N' is a distance set just for that mob. 'watch only' means the mob has no spells listed. A long list of commands is cut short on its row; hold the mouse over it to read all of it.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Mob name / arrow** | Click to fold a mob's spells away or show them again. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*Folds are forgotten when the window is reopened.* | open |
| **remove mob** | Stops watching this mob in this zone. A mob from your own list is deleted from it. A mob from the shipped list is switched off in your list, so it stays off after updates.<br>*No confirmation. To get a shipped mob back, use Reset my edits (which undoes all your edits in this zone).* |  |
| **interrupt** | When ticked and this mob starts casting this spell, the bot targets that mob and casts an interrupt spell that is ready right now. Saved at once.<br>*Nothing is cast if you have no interrupt ready, or while OgreBot is closed or paused.* | as the list says |
| **label** | Opens a small editor right under this spell's row, with a box holding its current name. Type a new name and press Save. Cancel closes the editor without saving.<br>*Saving an empty box removes the name you gave it. A spell from the shipped list then shows its shipped name again.* |  |
| **commands** | Opens a small editor right under this spell's row, with the commands the bot runs each time this mob starts this spell, one per line. The row shows how many commands are set and what they are.<br>*Commands only run while OgreBot is open and not paused.* |  |



## Watch list: editing a label or commands

Pressing label or commands opens this editor under the spell's row.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Editor box** | The name or the command lines you are editing. What you type is kept while the list refreshes. Only one editor is open at a time; opening another one drops what you had not saved.<br>*Pressing Enter does not save. Use the Save button.* |
| **Save** | Saves the editor's text into your own list for this zone and closes the editor. For commands, empty lines are skipped, and saving an empty box removes your commands; a spell from the shipped list then uses its shipped commands again. |
| **Cancel** | Closes the editor. Nothing is saved. |
| **remove** | Removes this spell from the mob. A spell from your own list is deleted. A shipped spell is switched off in your list.<br>*Removing the last spell of a mob you added removes that mob too. A mob from the shipped list stays watched.* |



## Watch list: footer

Shows how far the bot scans and for what (NPCs or players), and where the shipped list and your own list for this zone are stored on disk.

## What the window shows

- Monitor header: the zone the log belongs to - the same name the Watch list tab shows - and 'N spell(s) logged', the number of rows in the log.
- Monitor log columns: Mob, Spell (its name, or a grey '(no name yet)'), Ability ID, Cast time (seconds, from the latest cast) and Seen (how many times that mob cast it). One cast counts once, even though the Monitor sees it several times while the cast bar is up. Casting the same spell again counts again.
- Monitor grey bars: the result of your last Start, Stop, Copy or Clear. With either 'nearby' choice, a second bar says that casts from mobs that are not your target (or your target's target) only get an ability id.
- Monitor footer: 'monitoring' in green while it runs, 'stopped' when it does not, and 'saved to' the log file for this zone.
- Zone name (both tabs): the file name used for the zone, for example Castle_Vacrul_Caverns_of_the_Forsaken_Heroic_II. '(no zone)' when nothing is loaded.
- 'N mob(s) · N ability entr(ies) · watching N': how many mobs and spells are listed, and how many mobs the scan is watching right now.
- Green bar: your last capture worked (or that spell was already in your list). Red bar: your last capture or edit did not work, with the reason (no target, not casting, monitoring off, radius out of range, and so on).
- Red 'OFF' bar: NPC Cast Monitoring is turned off on OgreBot's Settings tab. The list is empty and nothing is watched.
- Grey 'OgreBot is closed' bar: mobs are still watched, but nothing is interrupted and no commands run until OgreBot is open.
- Grey 'Per-cast logging is off' bar: shows until you tick NPCCastDebug on OgreBot's Debug tab.
- Red file bars: the shipped list or your list for this zone cannot be read, your file uses the old 'nomerge' spelling, or some spell numbers in it are not valid and were skipped.
- Grey 'REPLACES' bar: your file is set to replace the shipped list instead of adding to it.
- Mob tags: 'yours' = from your list, 'radius N' = a distance set just for that mob, 'watch only' = no spells listed.
- Spell rows: the spell number, its label ('(no label)' if none), the interrupt box, how many commands it runs, and a 'yours' tag when it comes from your list.
- Watch list footer: 'scanning to N for NPCs/players' is the widest distance in use (the zone radius or the biggest per-mob radius). 'shipped:' and 'yours:' are the two list files for this zone.

## Good to know

- The Monitor and the Watch list are separate. The Monitor only writes down what mobs cast; it never interrupts or runs anything, and it needs neither the NPC Cast Monitoring checkbox nor OgreBot open.
- Spell names in the Monitor only come from your cast bars (your target and your target's target), and only when the cast lasts longer than about a quarter of a second. Once a spell's name is known, it shows for that spell everywhere, in every zone and next time too.
- Each zone keeps its own Monitor log. Zone while it runs and the old zone's log is saved and the new zone's saved log comes back. Send the file named under the log, or paste what Copy gives you.
- Closing the window stops the Monitor, the same as `ogre end npccast`. Stop (or `ogre npccast monitor off`) stops it and keeps the window open. The console can also start it: `ogre npccast monitor`, `ogre npccast monitor named` or `ogre npccast monitor all`; it then runs without the window until you stop it.
- The Watch list is switched by the 'NPC Cast Monitoring' checkbox on OgreBot's 'Settings' tab. While it is off, the list is empty and capturing, reloading, adding, removing and editing are refused with a red bar saying so. Only Import still works.
- Entering a zone that has a list (shipped or yours) ticks that checkbox for you, once per zone. If you untick it, it stays off until you next enter a zone that has a list, or your profile is loaded again.
- A watched mob starting a spell that is not listed (or a 'watch only' mob) does not interrupt or run anything. It only lets encounter scripts know the mob is casting.
- Interrupts and commands only happen while OgreBot is open and not paused.
- Reset my edits deletes all your Watch list edits for this zone at once, with no confirmation.
- The Watch list only covers the zone you are standing in. To edit another zone's list, go there or edit its file.
- With NPC Cast Monitoring off, an empty Watch list says so and asks you to turn it on - adding needs it on.

# Tag Timers

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Shows every Embargo and Allow tag on this character right now, so you can see why an ability is being held back or let through.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - Tick **Show Tag Timers window** on the Tags tab to have it open with the profile, or use `ogre tags` to open it once.
> - Drag the edges to resize it, like any other Ogre window.
>
> **What each column means**
>
> - **Tag**: the tag's name.
> - **Type**: Embargo holds an ability back, Allow lets it through.
> - **From**: the character who set the tag. Two characters holding one tag show as two lines.
> - **Sent to**: who the tag went to: all, group, raid, me, or a character's name.
> - **Time left**: counts down. A tag coupled to a buff says "while <buff> is up" and ends when the buff does.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - **unknown** means the tag came from a command or a script that did not name anyone.
> - The window only shows tags. It changes nothing.

**Open it:** Tick **Show Tag Timers window** on the [Tags tab](../ogrebot/tags.md) to have it open with the profile, or type `ogre tags`. `ogre end tags` closes it.

## What it is for

Shows every Embargo and Allow tag on this character right now, so you can see why an ability is being held back or let through. It only shows tags: it changes nothing.

## The list

One line per holder. Two characters holding the same tag show as two lines, and the tag stays on until the last of them lets go. The lines stay sorted by tag name, so they do not jump about as the clocks run.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Tag** | The tag's name. |
| **Type** | Embargo holds an ability back, Allow lets it through. |
| **From** | The character who set the tag. **unknown** means a command or a script armed it without naming anyone. |
| **Sent to** | Who the tag went to: all, group, raid, me, or a character's name. |
| **Time left** | Counts down. A tag coupled to a buff says while that buff is up, and ends when the buff does. |

# Effect Tracker

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Records what effects are called and what they say they do, into a shared per-zone data set for encounter writers.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Player** - record the detrimentals that land on you.
> - **NPC** - record the effects on NPCs that are fighting.
> - **Merge zone** - combine every character's capture file for the zone you are in into one. It works with Player and NPC off too.
> - **Search** and click a row to read everything recorded for an effect.
> - **Right-click a row** to copy its coding details.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Both start off in every new session. The window opens shrunk; click **Expand**.
> - Each effect is examined once, ever, so a zone you ran before may show nothing new.
> - It switches itself off while one of the old OgreBot recorder scripts runs.

**Open it:** Type `ogre effecttracker` (or `ogre oet`). `ogre effecttracker on` turns on the player capture and `ogre effecttracker npc on` the NPC capture; both also open the window. `ogre effecttracker off` turns both off. `ogre end effecttracker` (or the window's X) turns both off and closes the window.

## What it is for

Effect Tracker records what effects are called and what they say they do. With Player on, it records every detrimental that lands on you. With NPC on, it records the effects on NPCs that are fighting. It opens each new effect's examine window, copies its text, and closes it again. Each effect is only looked at once, ever, and the results go into a shared per-zone data set that encounter writers use. This window turns the capture on and off and lets you browse what was captured in the zone you are in.

## Header

The green line shows the zone, your character, how many effects are waiting to be examined, and the name of the last effect captured.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Shrink / Expand** | Shrink folds the window down to a small title bar with just an Expand button, so it is out of your way. Expand brings it back to the size it was before you shrank it (940 by 600 the first time, because the window opens shrunk). Display only - the capture keeps running while shrunk.<br>*The window always opens shrunk. Click Expand to see the list.* | shrunk (the window opens small) |

## Turning the capture on and off

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Player: off / Player: ON** | Turns on (or off) recording of the detrimentals that land on you. When turned on it also looks at the detrimentals already on you.<br>*Effects already recorded before (by any of your characters) are skipped, so a zone you have done before may capture nothing new. It is not saved: it starts off again in every new session. Turning off the last of Player and NPC saves what was captured straight away.* | off |
| **NPC: off / NPC: ON** | Turns on (or off) recording of the effects on NPCs and named NPCs that have a target (are fighting). Up to 10 effects per NPC.<br>*It only captures during combat, because that is when NPCs carry the effects.* | off |
| **Merge zone** | Combines every character's capture file for the zone you are in into one merged file for the zone. Your own latest captures are saved first, so they are included. The console says how many records were added and updated.<br>*It works whether Player or NPC is on or not. Outside a zone it says 'not in a zone' and does nothing.* |  |

## Browsing what was captured

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Player dets (N)** | Shows the detrimentals your character has recorded in this zone. The number is how many there are. Display only. | selected |
| **NPC effects (N)** | Shows the NPC effects recorded in this zone (shared by all your characters). Display only. |  |
| **search name / icon key / effect text / actor (box)** | Shows only the effects whose name, description, icon key, effect text or mob names contain what you type. Capital letters do not matter. It searches after you stop typing or press Enter. Display only. | empty |
| **Clear** | Empties the search box and shows everything again. Display only. |  |
| **descriptions (server reads)** | When ticked, the tracker also asks the game server for each new effect's description, one effect at a time. When unticked, names and effect text are still captured from the examine window; only the description is missing.<br>*It is not saved: it is ticked again in every new session. The footer shows how many server reads were used.* | on |

## The list

One row per captured effect: its name, its icon key (two numbers), how many lines of text it has, '+desc' if it has a description, 'on <mob>' for NPC effects, any crowd control it causes in yellow, and a red note if the capture failed.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click a row** | Opens the row to show everything recorded for that effect: icon numbers, duration, counters, the description, each line of effect text, and the mobs it was seen with (named mobs are starred). Click it again to close it. Display only.<br>*Dragging across text selects it for copying instead of opening the row.* |
| **Right-click a row > Copy coding details** | Copies the effect's name, icon numbers, duration, the mob it was on, and all its text to the Windows clipboard, ready to paste into an encounter file or a note.<br>*If another program is holding the clipboard, the console says it could not copy.* |

## Footer

Record count (and 'showing N of M' when there are more than 250 matches; the file still has them all), how many effects were captured this session, how many effects are already known and will never be examined again, how many examine windows were opened, any timeouts or windows that were not ours, and how many server reads were used.

## What the window shows

- Header line: zone file name, your character, 'N/8 examining' while effects wait to be read, and 'last:' the last effect captured.
- Red 'Disarmed' bar: one of the old OgreBot recorder or effect tracker scripts is running. They use the same examine window, so the tracker switches itself off and refuses to turn on until they stop.
- Row name in red with '[examine timed out]' (or another reason): the capture failed. An 'Unknown_...' name means the effect could not be named. These are tried again later in the session, up to a limit.
- Yellow brackets such as [Stun Root]: crowd control found in the effect text (Stifle, Stun, Fear, Mez, Root).
- Open row, first line: main and backdrop icon numbers, the key, maxDuration (-1 means it lasts until removed), increments (counters), the actor type and the capture result.
- Open row, bottom: the mobs that were around when it landed. A star marks named mobs.
- Coloured text: some effect lines carry the game's own colour, and the window shows it the same way.
- Empty list: 'Nothing captured for this zone yet' (turn Player or NPC on and fight), 'Armed, and nothing captured yet', or 'Nothing matches' for a search.

## Good to know

- Player and NPC are not saved: both start off in every new session. Turning either on opens this window (shrunk) so you can always see it is running.
- Closing the window turns Player and NPC off (what was captured is saved), the same as `ogre end effecttracker`.
- An effect is examined only once, ever, across all your characters. A zone you already ran may show nothing new; that is normal.
- Starting one of the old OgreBot recorder scripts switches Effect Tracker off. Turn it back on after the script stops.
- While the tracker is working, you will see effect examine windows flash open and close. That is how it reads them.
- The list only shows the zone you are in, and only after capture has been turned on (or Merge zone pressed) this session.

The window opens shrunk. Click **Expand**:

![Shrunk](../assets/effecttracker/shrunk.png)

### NPC effects, searched

![NPC effects](../assets/effecttracker/npc.png)

### Blocked by an old recorder script

![Blocked](../assets/effecttracker/blocked.png)

![Right-click menu](../assets/effecttracker/rightclick.png)

# Hide Effects

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Hides clutter (guild buffs, pets, always-on class buffs) from your character's effects window, using lists of effect names.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Run** - check the effects on you and hide every one on a list for your class.
> - **List hidden**, **Clear all**, **Un-hide id** - see what the game is hiding, or show it again.
> - **Add** / **remove** - change the names in a group.
> - **Reset my edits** - undo every Add and remove you made, in all groups.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Nothing is hidden until you press **Run**. Effects that land later need another Run.
> - Removing a name does not un-hide it; use **Clear all** or **Un-hide id**.
> - Plain `ogre hideeffects` runs the hide; `ogre hideeffects panel` opens this window.

**Open it:** Type `ogre hideeffects panel`. If the window is already open, this does nothing. Plain `ogre hideeffects` does not open the window: it runs the hide straight away (the same as the Run button). `ogre end hideeffects` (or the window's X) stops a run and closes the window; effects already hidden stay hidden.

## What it is for

Hide Effects clears clutter out of your character's effects window. It keeps lists of effect names that nobody needs to see (guild buffs, pets, always-on class buffs and so on). When you press Run, it looks at every effect on your character and tells the game to hide the ones whose name is on a list that applies to you. The lists are split into groups: some apply to everyone, some only to one class or archetype. Your own additions and removals are kept in a separate file, so bot updates never undo them.

## Header

Shows the character, class and archetype the lists are matched against. 'run in progress…' appears on the right while a run is working.

## Buttons

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Run** | Checks every effect on your character, one at a time, and hides each one whose name is on a list that applies to your class. A list name also matches the same name with a rank after it (for example 'Aspect of Genius' also hides 'Aspect of Genius IV'). The console says what it checked and what it hid.<br>*It only runs when you press it; it does not keep hiding new effects afterwards. If you zone or log out while it is still checking names, the run is dropped - press Run again. Pressing it again during a run only says a run is already going.* |  |
| **List hidden** | Asks the game to print the list of effects it is hiding. The list appears in your EQ2 chat window, with the id of each one. |  |
| **Clear all** | Tells the game to show every hidden effect again.<br>*No confirmation. Press Run to hide them again.* |  |
| **effect id (box)** | The id of one hidden effect, as shown by List hidden. Anything that is not a digit is removed. | empty |
| **Un-hide id** | Tells the game to show that one hidden effect again. Nothing happens if the box is empty. |  |
| **Reload list** | Reads all the hide lists from disk again. Use it after editing a list file by hand. |  |
| **Reset my edits** | Deletes the file that holds your Add and remove changes, so every group loses those changes at once. A list file you put in your own custom folder by hand is not touched.<br>*No confirmation and no undo.* |  |

## The lists

One block per group, with the groups that apply to you first. The tag says what kind of group it is (general, ascension, subclass or archetype) and whether it 'applies' to you or is for an 'other class' (greyed out). A yellow 'custom file' tag means the group comes from a file in your own folder. The number on the right is how many names are in it.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Group name / arrow** | Click to fold a group away or open it again. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does. | open |
| **remove** | Takes this name off the group, so Run no longer hides it. Saved at once in your own file.<br>*It does not show the effect again if it is already hidden. Use Clear all or Un-hide id for that.* |  |
| **add a name to <group> (box)** | Type the name of an effect to add to this group. Capital letters do not matter. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed name to this group and saves it at once in your own file. Nothing happens if the box is empty.<br>*The name is not checked against the game, so a typo is saved and simply never matches.* |  |

## Footer

Left: how many groups and names apply to your character. Right: the last run - how many effects it checked, how many were on your lists, how many it hid, how many effect names it had to look up, and how many it could not read in time ('not ready', in red). The note in brackets says how the run went, for example 'running' while it hides and 'done' when it has finished.

## What the window shows

- Header: character name - class (archetype). '(no character)' before a character is loaded.
- 'run in progress…': a run is still checking names or hiding effects.
- Grey 'Not in world' bar: you can still edit the lists, but Run needs a character in the world.
- Group tag 'applies' (green): this group is used for your character. 'other class' (grey): it is not, but you can still edit it.
- 'custom file' (yellow): the group comes from a list file in your own save folder.
- Footer 'last run': scanned = effects checked, matched = on your lists, hid = hidden, name reads = names looked up, not ready = names the game never supplied in time.
- The window keeps itself up to date: the 'run in progress' marker, the footer and the 'Not in world' bar change on their own as a run goes and when you zone, within about a second.

## Good to know

- Nothing is hidden until you press Run (or type `ogre hideeffects`). New effects that land later are not hidden until you run it again.
- Removing a name from a list does not un-hide it. Use Clear all or Un-hide id.
- If one effect name is in two applying groups, the first group (general, then ascension, then your class, then your archetype) is the one credited.
- Reset my edits undoes all your Add/remove changes in every group at once (a list file you added by hand stays).

### More groups, folded

Groups for other classes are listed after yours, greyed out:

# Radar

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> A live map of what is around you. You are the ringed dot in the middle; the cyan wedge is the way you face. Click any dot to target it.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **zoom / dim / height** - how far you see, how solid the background is, and hiding other floors. Zoom and height are saved as soon as you let go of the slider.
> - **types** - pick which kinds of things are drawn (saved at once).
> - **verify** - check the radar's list against the game; the answer is in the console.
> - **Gear** - colours, rotation, labels, full screen, click-through, name lists, and **Save**.
> - **auto-hide** (clean mode) - no title bar, controls fade; point at the top-left corner to get them back.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Zoom, height and the types save themselves. Dim and the gear settings only stick if you press **Save**.
> - Stuck behind click-through? `ogre radar settings` or `ogre radar click off`.
> - A line under the title tells you when no data has come in for a while, and who a clicked dot targeted.
> - The X (or `ogre end radar`) turns the radar off. `ogre radar` does nothing if it is already open.

**Open it:** Type `ogre radar` in the console. `ogre end radar` (or the X on its title bar) turns it off again. The OgreBot Load tab boxes "Radar on" / "Radar off" do the same when a profile loads.

## What it is for

A live map of everything around you: mobs, players, pets, corpses, chests, doors and more, each drawn as a coloured dot around you in the middle. Click a dot to target it. It only shows things; it never moves or fights for you, and it keeps working while OgreBot is paused. The title bar reads Ogre Radar. Your look (zoom, colours, lists, and so on) is saved to one file shared by every character on this PC.

## Toolbar

The strip across the top. The zoom, dim and height sliders change only what you see; they do not change what the bot reads.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **zoom** | How far the radar reaches, in game units from you to the nearer edge of the window. Drag left to zoom in, right to see further (10 to 400). Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*Saved as soon as you let go of the slider (2026-11-15) - no Save needed.* | 100 (the radar radius) |
| **dim** | How solid the radar's background is. 100% is a solid panel, 0% is see-through so only the dots are drawn over the game. The same setting as background in the settings.<br>*Only kept for good if you press Save in the settings.* | 94% |
| **height** | Hides things more than this many units above or below you, so in a tower or a building you see your own floor. Shows ±N when on. Either end of the slider means off.<br>*Saved as soon as you let go of the slider (2026-11-15) - no Save needed.* | off |
| **types** | Opens the Radar Types window, where you pick which kinds of things are drawn. Press again to close it. |  |
| **verify** | Checks the bot's list of nearby things against a fresh read of the game and prints the result in the console. If the list had gone wrong it is rebuilt.<br>*The answer is in the console, not on the radar.* |  |
| **⚙ (gear, in the toolbar)** | Opens and closes the settings drawer over the radar. |  |
| **⚙ (gear, in the title bar)** | The same as the toolbar gear: opens and closes the settings drawer. |  |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Turns the radar off and closes it and the Radar Types window. Same as `ogre end radar`. |  |



## The scope

You are the white dot with the cyan ring in the middle; the cyan wedge shows which way you face. The rings mark a third, two thirds and all of the zoom distance. In the top right of the toolbar is the zone name.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click a dot** | Targets that actor. It works while OgreBot is paused, and it takes priority over the bot's own targeting for that click.<br>*Dots stay clickable even when click-through is on. For 4 seconds the line at the top of the radar says what you targeted (name, level, distance, health, type), whether or not the readout is switched on.* |



## Settings - Display

Open with either gear. The drawer covers the radar; Close (at the bottom) or the gear puts it away. While it is open the radar always takes the mouse, even if click-through is on.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **colour by: type** | Colours each dot by what it is (npc, named, player, pet...), using the Colours - by type list. | on |
| **colour by: con** | Colours each dot by its con colour (grey, green, blue, white, yellow, orange, red) using the Colours - by con list. Things with no con keep their type colour. | off |
| **rotation (heading-up / north-up)** | heading-up turns the map with you, so straight ahead is always up. north-up keeps north at the top and turns the facing wedge instead. | heading-up |
| **labels** | Writes each dot's name beside it. | on |
| **grid** | The outline, range rings and crosshair. Off leaves only the dots. | on |
| **updates: −** | Reads the game one time fewer per second. |  |
| **updates (slider)** | How many times a second the radar re-reads the game, 1 to 30. More gives fresher positions but costs more game time. This is the only setting in the drawer that costs anything.<br>*Not saved by Save: it goes back to 5 when the extension reloads.* | 5 / sec |
| **updates: +** | Reads the game one time more per second (up to 30). |  |
| **chunk: − / +** | Steps through off, 25, 50, 100, 150, 250, 400. When more actors are around than this number, one update is spread over several game frames, which smooths out the worst frame but makes positions a little older.<br>*Not saved by Save. With 100 things or fewer around, the default 100 does nothing, so there is no need to turn it off. The hint next to it says the same.* | 100 /frame |
| **glide** | Slides dots smoothly between updates instead of letting them jump. Costs the game nothing. | on |
| **blip size** | Size of each dot, 4 to 18 pixels. Named mobs are drawn 3 pixels bigger. | 8px |
| **label size** | Size of the name text, 7 to 20 pixels. | 9.5px |
| **background** | The same setting as dim on the toolbar: 0% is fully see-through (the radar is still clickable), 100% solid. | 94% |
| **auto-hide** | Turns clean mode on or off. In clean mode the title bar is removed and the toolbar fades out; hover the top-left corner of the radar to bring the controls back. See Clean mode below. | off |
| **click-through** | When ON, your mouse clicks go through the radar to the game, except on the dots and the toolbar, which still work.<br>*If you get stuck, `ogre radar click off` gives the mouse back and `ogre radar settings` opens this drawer.* | off |



## Settings - Full screen

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full screen: on / off** | Stretches the radar over the whole game screen, minus the offsets below. Turning it on also turns click-through on, so you can still play. Turning it off puts the window back where it was. | off |
| **offsets px: top / right / bottom / left** | Pixels to leave free at each edge of the screen when full screen is on (for example to keep your hot bars clear).<br>*Typing a number does nothing until you press apply.* | 0 |
| **apply** | Re-fits the full-screen radar using the offsets you typed.<br>*Only does something while full screen is on.* |  |



## Settings - Colours

One row per kind of thing (by type) and one per con colour. Click a swatch to open the colour picker above the list.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Swatch (coloured dot)** | Opens the colour picker for that row. The picker's heading uses the row's own name (named, craft, nokill...). |
| **#hex box** | Type a colour as # plus six hex digits (for example #ff8a3d). It applies as soon as the text is a valid colour.<br>*Anything else is ignored.* |
| **Picker: #hex box** | The picked colour as text; type a colour here to set it. |
| **Picker: R / G / B sliders** | Mix the colour from red, green and blue (0 to 255). The dots change as you drag. |
| **Picker: preset swatches** | Click one to use that colour. |
| **Picker: done** | Closes the picker. The colour you picked stays. |



## Settings - Lists

Each entry is part of a name and is matched without caring about capitals: 'darkpaw' matches 'a Darkpaw brute'. Saved lists are kept when you press Save. Temporary lists are never saved; they last until the game's UI reloads.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **whitelist ON / off (saved)** | When ON, only things whose name matches an entry are drawn.<br>*An empty whitelist is ignored rather than hiding everything.* | off |
| **blacklist ON / off (saved)** | When ON, things whose name matches an entry are hidden. | off |
| **whitelist ON / off (temporary)** | Same as the saved whitelist, for this session only. | off |
| **blacklist ON / off (temporary)** | Same as the saved blacklist, for this session only. | off |
| **name fragment, then Enter or Add (placeholder)** | Type part of a name. Enter does the same as Add. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed text to that list (skipped if it is already there). |  |
| **✕ (remove entry)** | Removes that entry from the list. |  |



## Settings - Debug, Save and Reset

The report buttons print to the console, not the radar. They are for tracking down problems.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **readout (shown / hidden)** | Shows a line at the top of the radar: how many things are drawn out of how many were read, and what the radar costs the game (time per frame and share of the CPU).<br>*Messages for you use the same line and show even when the readout is hidden: "no data for N s" when the radar has had nothing from the game for over 3 seconds, and what a clicked dot targeted.* | hidden |
| **verify cache** | Same as the verify button on the toolbar. |  |
| **perf** | Prints the radar's cost report to the console. |  |
| **status** | Prints the radar's current settings and state to the console. |  |
| **ui dump** | Prints the radar window's own drawing numbers to the console. |  |
| **dump** | Prints the first 10 things from the last update (name, type, distance, level, health, con, position) to the console. |  |
| **fields: full** | Reads everything the radar can show, including level, health and con. The lit button is the one in use. | full |
| **fields: lean** | Stops reading level, health and con: fewer game reads, but those three stop updating on the radar.<br>*Not saved. It goes back to full when the extension reloads.* |  |
| **reset perf** | Zeroes the radar's cost counters so the next perf report starts from now. |  |
| **force a scan** | Makes the radar re-read the game once, right away. |  |
| **Save** | Saves the radar's look and lists (everything in this drawer except updates and chunk, plus zoom, dim and height) to OgreSave\EQ2\Radar.json. The next time the radar opens it starts this way. One file for every character on this PC.<br>*The grey text next to Close confirms the save.* |  |
| **Reset all** | Puts every setting in the drawer back to the defaults, including zoom, dim, height, colours, the type choices and the saved lists (they are emptied). Nothing is written until you press Save.<br>*Close and reopen the radar without saving to get your saved settings back.* |  |
| **Close** | Closes the drawer. Unsaved changes stay in effect until the radar closes. |  |



## Clean mode (auto-hide)

With auto-hide on, the radar becomes a clean overlay: the title bar is gone (so no X, lock or ?) and the toolbar fades out. The space stays reserved at the top. A faint corner mark in the top-left shows where to point.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Hot corner (top-left)** | Point the mouse at the top-left corner of the radar (about 130 by 24 pixels) and the toolbar comes back. Move away and it fades again after a moment.<br>*The controls stay up while the settings drawer is open.* |
| **? (beside the gear)** | Opens this help. It only appears in clean mode, because the title bar and its ? are gone. |



## What the window shows

- Your character: the white dot with the cyan ring in the middle. The cyan wedge is the way you face.
- Dot colours (colour by type, the default): npc orange, named orange and bigger with a glow, nokill (guards, merchants) grey, special yellow, players blue, pets light green, your pet bright green, mercenaries teal, corpses dark grey, craft (crafting stations) purple, resources (harvest nodes) teal-green, chests amber, doors brown, anything else grey. Every colour can be changed in the settings.
- Dot shapes: players and mercenaries are rounded squares; everything else is round. Named mobs are 3 pixels bigger with an orange glow.
- Faded dots: corpses and anything at 0% health.
- Your target: its dot turns white with a white halo and its name goes white and bold.
- Rings: a third, two thirds and all of the zoom distance, measured to the nearer edge of the window. A tall window sees further up and down than sideways.
- Top right of the toolbar: the zone you are in.
- Only the 250 nearest things are drawn.

## Good to know

- Zoom, dim, height and every setting in the drawer are only kept for good if you press Save. Close and reopen the radar without saving and they go back to what you last saved (if you have never saved, your changes last until the game's UI reloads). Exception: choices in the Radar Types window save themselves. Only the type choice is saved - your other changes still wait for Save.
- updates and chunk are not saved at all; they return to 5 per second and 100 when the extension reloads.
- In clean mode there is no title bar and no X. Use the hot corner to get the controls back, or type `ogre end radar` to close it.
- If the radar stops you clicking the game, turn click-through on. If you then cannot reach the radar's settings, type `ogre radar settings`; `ogre radar click off` gives the mouse back, and `ogre radar uireset` puts every radar setting back to default (like Reset all - not saved until you press Save).
- Full screen turns click-through on for you.
- `ogre radar` when the radar is already open does nothing and prints nothing.

# Radar Types

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Picks which kinds of things the Radar draws. A lit button is shown; a dim one is hidden.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **The top row**: **[all]**, **quest** (quest only), **qst npc** (quest NPCs) and **no name**. **The grid** under it: one button per type.
> - **Click a type** (npc, named, pc, pet, corpse, chest, door...) to show or hide it.
> - **other** covers anything not in the list.
> - **quest** (quest only) narrows **npc**, **named** and **nokill** to the ones that update one of your quests - a mob to kill or an object to click. Every other type (pc, special, chest...) follows its own button.
> - **qst npc** always shows NPCs with a feather (or a quest update / complete icon) - the ones the quest helper hails - even with **nokill** off or **quest** on.
> - **no name** shows or hides actors with no name - mostly junk, sometimes not.
> - **name** (bottom right) turns name cutting on and off: lit cuts every name on the radar to the number beside it (5 to start). Change the number in the box; it is kept while cutting is off.
> - **[all]** shows everything; when everything is on it reads **[none]** and hides everything.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Each click is saved straight away. Only the type choice is saved (with the radar's zoom and height, which save themselves too) - other radar changes still wait for **Save**.
> - The dot on each button is that type's colour on the radar (change it under the radar's gear).
> - Open and close it with **types** on the radar.

**Open it:** Press **types** on the Radar's toolbar (open the radar first with `ogre radar`). Press types again, or the X, to close it.

## What it is for

Picks which kinds of things the Radar draws: mobs, named, players, pets, corpses, chests, doors and so on. Each button is one kind; lit means shown. Your choices are saved as soon as you click, so they are still there the next time you open the radar. It changes only what the radar shows, never what the bot does.

## Type buttons

The coloured dot on each button is the colour that kind is drawn in on the radar (change it in the radar's settings, Colours - by type).

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **[all] / [none]** | If anything is hidden, [all] shows every kind again. If everything is already shown, the button reads [none] and hides every kind, so you can then turn on just the ones you want. |  |
| **npc** | Mobs you can fight. | shown |
| **named** | Named mobs. | shown |
| **nokill** | NPCs you cannot attack, such as guards and merchants. | shown |
| **special** | Objects the game marks as special, usually things you can click. | shown |
| **pc** | Other players. | shown |
| **pet** | Pets that are not yours (your own pet is mypet). | shown |
| **mypet** | Your own pet. | shown |
| **merc** | Mercenaries. | shown |
| **corpse** | Corpses. | shown |
| **craft** | Crafting stations (forges, sewing tables and the like). | shown |
| **resource** | Harvest nodes. | shown |
| **chest** | Treasure chests. | shown |
| **door** | Doors. | shown |
| **other** | Anything that is none of the kinds above. | shown |
| **quest** | Narrows npc, named and nokill to the ones that update one of your quests - a mob to kill or an object to click. Every other type follows its own button. Saved like a type click. | off |
| **qst npc** | Always shows quest NPCs - a feather, or a quest update / complete icon, over a no-kill NPC (the ones the quest helper hails) - even with nokill off or quest on. The radar looks for them every 2 seconds, only while this is on. | off |
| **no name** | Actors with no name - mostly junk, sometimes not. Lit shows them, dim hides them. Saved like a type click. | shown |
| **name** | The button turns name cutting on and off; while lit, every name on the radar is cut to the number in the box (5 to start). The number is kept while cutting is off. Saved like a type click. | off, 5 |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes this window only. The radar keeps running. |  |



## What the window shows

- A lit button means that kind is drawn on the radar; a dim one means it is hidden.
- The top row holds the four switches ([all], quest, qst npc, no name); the grid under it holds one button per type.

## Good to know

- Every click saves your type choice straight away. Only the type choice: any other change you made on the radar and did not save yet (zoom, dim, colours...) still waits for the radar's Save.
- You never appear on the radar as a dot you can hide; you are always the marker in the middle.
- Closing the radar (its X or `ogre end radar`) closes this window too.

## Beside the radar

![Radar Types next to the radar, with doors, resources, craft and special turned off](../assets/eq2radarfilters/with-radar.png)

# Nav

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> The stop button for navigation. It pops up whenever the bot walks or flies your character somewhere, and closes when the trip ends.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **STOP** - end the trip where you are. Safe to press at any time.
> - **Pause / Resume** - hold the trip and keep the route; Resume carries on from here.
> - The X (or `ogre end nav`) stops the trip and closes the window. To keep it out of the way, move or resize it.
> - Watch the progress bar, waypoint count and distance left. **Waiting for mesh** means the zone's map is still loading; the trip starts by itself when it is ready.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Pausing OgreBot does not stop a trip - use STOP (or `ogre nav stop`).
> - While nav is paused nothing else will move your character until you Resume or STOP.
> - `ogre nav -nopanel` stops it popping up; `ogre nav panel` opens it by hand.

**Open it:** It opens by itself whenever your character starts a navigation trip, whoever started it (you, Instance Controller, the travel router...), and closes when the trip ends. To open it by hand type `ogre nav panel`. `ogre nav -nopanel` stops it popping up; `ogre nav -panel` turns that back on and opens it.

## What it is for

The stop button for navigation. While the bot walks or flies your character somewhere along the navigation map, this small window shows how far along it is and gives you a big STOP and a Pause. Navigation keeps going while OgreBot is paused, so this window is how you stop it.

## Status

The top line is the state (Moving in green, Failed in red, Arrived highlighted, Stopped plain) and why. The bar and the line under it show the waypoint you are on out of the whole route, and the distance still to go. The next line names the navigation map loaded for this zone. A red note appears when the trip is paused, nav is switched off, or OgreBot is paused.

## Buttons

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **STOP** | Ends the trip right where you are. The route is thrown away. It is safe to press at any time: if something else has since taken over moving your character, STOP leaves that alone.<br>*Greyed out when no trip is running.* |
| **Pause / Resume** | Pause stops walking but keeps the route, so Resume carries on from where you stopped without planning again. While paused, nav still holds the character: follow or the camp spot will not move it until you Resume or STOP.<br>*Greyed out when no trip is running. Turns yellow and reads Resume while paused.* |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Stops the trip and closes the window, the same as `ogre end nav`. Nothing hides the window while a trip goes on: move it or size it where you want it. |



## What the window shows

- State word: Moving, Planning (the route is being worked out, a little at a time so the game never freezes; the character waits until it is ready), Landing (coming down from flight), Waiting for mesh (the navigation map for this zone is still downloading; the trip starts by itself when it is ready), Arrived, Stopped (something ended the trip on purpose: you pressed STOP, or the bot that started the walk ended it), Failed (navigation could not get there, for example stuck or no route), or Idle.
- Reason, next to the state: why the trip is doing what it does, for example 'navmesh route', 'waiting for the navmesh', 'stuck', or 'OgreBot closed'.
- Bar and 'waypoint X of Y - N u to go': how far along the route you are, and the distance left in game units. 'waiting for the navmesh to land' while the map is still coming; 'no route' when idle.
- 'mesh <zone> - N polys': the navigation map in use. 'no mesh loaded yet (loads on the first trip in a zone)' is normal before your first trip in a zone.
- Red notes: 'Paused here. The route is kept - Resume carries on from this point.' / 'Nav is switched OFF - `ogre nav -on`' / 'OgreBot is paused. This trip keeps going; STOP ends it.'

## Good to know

- Pausing OgreBot does NOT stop a navigation trip. Use STOP here, or type `ogre nav stop`. `ogre end nav` (or the X) stops the trip and closes this window.
- The window closes itself as soon as a trip ends, so you rarely see Arrived, Stopped or Failed in it. The console says how the trip ended.
- While nav is paused it keeps control of your character, so nothing else (follow, camp spot) will move it until you Resume or STOP.

## Points of interest and paths

A point of interest is a name you give a spot in a zone. A path is a saved list of spots to walk in order. Both are kept in the [Points of Interest and Paths window](paths.md): type `ogre paths`.

- A point of interest's name works wherever a location does in that zone: `oc !c -NavTo igw:${Me.Name} bell`, `oc !c -ChangeCampSpot igw:${Me.Name} bell`, and `-TravelMesh` to reach it from another zone.
- `oc !c -Path igw:${Me.Name} <name>` walks a saved path, and `oc !c -PathStop igw:${Me.Name}` stops it. It runs while OgreBot is paused, waits through a fight or a death, and zoning ends it.
- The [Auto-Hunt tab](../ogrebot/auto-hunt.md) picks a path to walk between pulls.

## Other states

OgreBot paused while a trip runs:

![OgreBot paused](../assets/nav/botpaused.png)

Waiting for the zone's navigation map:

![Waiting for the navmesh](../assets/nav/waiting.png)

Opened by hand with no trip running:

![Idle](../assets/nav/idle.png)

# Travel Helper

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Lists where a travel map can take you, then sends your group to the one you pick.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Fast Travel, Wizard Spire, Druid Rings, Bell** - this character opens that map (standing by the spire, ring or bell for those three), reads every destination and lists them. The map closes again.
> - **Not near a spire, ring or bell?** The list is every destination Ogre knows for that network, and the window says so. Pick one and your group travels as usual - this character does not need to be there. A character whose own map does not offer it says so in its console.
> - **Open Travel Map** - lists the travel map you already have open, and leaves it open.
> - **Double-click a destination**, or select it and press **Travel** - everyone in the Master Control Panel's For Who window travels there. Each opens their own map and clicks that exact destination.
> - **Filter** - type part of a name to shorten the list. **Enter** picks the destination when only one is left.
> - **Keep list open after travelling** - leave this window up after you pick.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - If the For Who window was never set, everyone travels.
> - Spire, ring and bell travel needs that object within reach of every character you send - but not of the character who picks.
> - With Open Travel Map, everyone you send must have their own map open too.

**Open it:** Type `ogre travel`. Add a method to open it straight on that list: `ogre travel fast`, `ogre travel spire`, `ogre travel druid`, `ogre travel bell` or `ogre travel map`. A Master Control Panel button migrated from the old bot's Travel Helper opens it too. `ogre end travel` (or the window's X) stops a list that is being read, closes the map it opened, and closes the window.

## What it is for

The Travel Helper sends your group somewhere without anyone typing a zone name. Pick how to travel and this character opens that travel map, reads every destination it offers and lists them here. Double-click one and every character in the For Who window travels there: each opens its own map and clicks that exact destination. It is the old bot's Travel Helper window, rebuilt.

## Choosing how to travel

Each button makes this character open that kind of travel map and list it. The map closes again once it has been read, except for Open Travel Map.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Fast Travel** | Opens the Fast Travel map and lists its destinations. Works anywhere you can fast travel from. |
| **Wizard Spire** | Clicks the wizard spire next to you and lists where it goes. You must be standing by a spire.<br>*Nothing is cast: it uses the spire in the world, the same as the old bot.* |
| **Druid Rings** | Clicks the druid ring next to you, or in a guild hall the portal druid, and lists where it goes. |
| **Bell** | Clicks the bell or globe next to you and lists where it goes. |
| **Open Travel Map** | Lists the travel map you already have open, and leaves it open.<br>*Everyone you send to must have their own travel map open too - this one opens nothing for them.* |

## Picking a destination

The list shows every destination the map offers, in the map's order. Type in the filter box to narrow it.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Filter destinations** | Shows only the destinations whose name contains what you type. Enter picks the destination when only one is left (or the selected one). |
| **Destination list** | Click a destination to select it. Double-click it to travel there. Away from a spire, ring or bell, it lists every destination Ogre knows for that network (from its travel data) and says so: each character you send picks it on its own map. |
| **Travel** | Sends everyone in the For Who window to the selected destination.<br>*Each character opens its own map and clicks exactly that destination - the whole name, not part of it.* |
| **Keep list open after travelling** | Leaves this window open after you send the group. Off, it closes once you pick. |

## What the window shows

- Sends to: who a pick goes to and how, read from the Master Control Panel's For Who window.
- Opening the map and reading it...: this character is opening the map. The buttons are greyed out until it finishes.
- Could not list: why the map could not be read, for example nothing to click is in reach.
- The line under Sends to: what the last pick sent, and to whom.

## Good to know

- The For Who window decides who travels. If it was never set, everyone travels.
- Wizard Spire, Druid Rings and Bell need the spire, ring or bell within reach of every character you send. Anyone too far away stays where they are.
- Picking a destination with several drop-off points or instances uses the same choice as the travel commands: the last one offered.

# Points of Interest and Paths

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Names spots in the zone you are in, and saves walks through them. They are kept on this PC, for every toon.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Add** - save a point of interest at x, y, z. Leave those blank to use where you stand. **My Loc** fills them in for you.
> - **Remove / Rename** - change a point of interest of your own.
> - **New / Delete** - make or drop a path. A zone can hold as many as you like.
> - **Add / Insert / Remove / Clear** under the point list - build the path. Add goes on the end, Insert goes above the selected point. A point is a point of interest or x,y,z.
> - **Drag a point** to move it in the list.
> - **Nav / Camp spot** - how the toon walks that path. **Loop** starts it over after the last point.
> - **Start / Stop** - walk the path on this box.
> - **Import** - bring this zone's old AutoHunt path across from OgreBot Classic.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - A point of interest's name works wherever a location does in this zone: `-ChangeCampSpot`, `-TravelMesh`.
> - A shipped point of interest cannot be removed or renamed. Adding your own of that name overrides it.
> - Start stops with a line if a point cannot be found, before anything moves. Zoning ends a walk.
> - The first time you enter a zone with an old AutoHunt path, it comes across by itself as a path called Default. Nothing you already have is overwritten, and what you delete does not come back unless you press **Import**.
> - The Auto-Hunt tab picks one of these paths to walk between pulls, and its **Edit** button opens that path here. So does `ogre paths <path>`.
> - A walk under way keeps the points it had when it started. Stop and Start walks the new order.

**Open it:** Type `ogre paths`. To open it on one path, type `ogre paths <path>` or press **Edit** beside the path picker on the Auto-Hunt tab of OgreBot. `ogre end paths` or the window's X closes it. A path being walked goes on.

## What it is for

This window holds the named spots and the saved walks of the zone you are in. A point of interest is a name for a spot: the name then works wherever a location does in this zone, such as `-ChangeCampSpot`, `-NavTo` and `-TravelMesh`. A path is a list of points that a toon walks in order, and a zone can hold as many paths as you like. Both are kept on this PC, for every toon, and everything here also has a command for scripts.

## Zone and Import

The top line names the zone everything below belongs to. While you are zoning, or while the travel data loads, it says why the lists are empty.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Import** | Brings this zone's saved Auto-Hunt route across from OgreBot Classic, even if that was done before. A name or path already here is never overwritten.<br>*This also happens by itself, once, the first time you enter a zone that has an old route.* |



## Points of interest

Click a row to fill in the name, the x, y, z boxes and the path's Point box.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Name (box)** | The name of the point of interest to add. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number, because it would then read as a location. |
| **x / y / z (boxes)** | Where the point of interest is. Leave all three blank to use where you stand. |
| **My Loc** | Fills x, y and z from where you stand, so you can change them before you add. |
| **Add** | Saves the point of interest in this zone. A name you already have moves to the new spot. A name the bot ships with is overridden by yours, and it stays yours until you remove it. |
| **Remove** | Removes the selected point of interest of yours. If it was overriding a shipped one, the shipped one is back.<br>*Greyed out for a shipped point of interest.* |
| **New name (box)** | The new name for Rename. |
| **Rename** | Renames the selected point of interest of yours. A name another point of interest here holds is refused, and a path that used the old name does not follow it.<br>*Greyed out for a shipped point of interest.* |



## Paths

Click a path to select it. Its points show in the list under these buttons.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **New path name (box)** | The name of the path to make. |  |
| **New** | Makes an empty path in this zone. It walks by Nav and does not loop until you change it. A name already here is refused, so a slip cannot empty a path. |  |
| **Delete** | Deletes the selected path.<br>*No confirmation.* |  |
| **Walk by Nav / Camp spot** | How the toon walks this path. Nav goes to each point on the navigation map. Camp spot moves the camp spot to each point and lets the leash bring the toon. | Nav |
| **Loop** | Starts the path over at the first point after the last, until something stops it. A path of one point goes there and finishes, and so does a loop whose points are all where you stand. | off |
| **Start** | Walks the selected path on this box, in place of any walk under way. Every point is checked first: one that cannot be found stops it with a line, before anything moves.<br>*It runs while OgreBot is paused, and OgreBot must be open.* |  |
| **Stop** | Stops the walk on this box. The toon stands where it is. |  |



## Points of the path

The selected path's points, in the order they are walked. Drag a row to move that point: a line shows where it lands, the points between shift one place, and a plain click still selects the row.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Point: a name, or x,y,z (box)** | The point to add: the name of a point of interest, or x,y,z. A name is looked for when the path starts, so its point of interest can come later. |
| **Add** | Adds the point to the end of the selected path. |
| **Insert** | Puts the point in above the selected point, which moves down one. The new point is then the selected row.<br>*Greyed out until a point is selected.* |
| **Remove** | Removes the selected point. A path that passes the same point twice keeps the other one. |
| **Clear** | Takes every point off the selected path. The path stays, with its Walk by and Loop settings.<br>*No confirmation.* |



## What the window shows

- 'shipped' or 'yours' beside a point of interest: shipped ones come with the bot and cannot be removed or renamed.
- 'at an actor' in place of a location: a shipped point of interest that names an actor, not a spot. It has no location of its own, so a path or a location verb cannot use it.
- Green text: the path being walked and the point it is walking to, with a line under the lists saying the same. After an edit the line still reads the walk, and no row is green if the list no longer holds that point at that place.
- The last line of the window: the last thing the bot said about a point of interest or a path, a refusal included.

## Good to know

- Everything here is for the zone you are in. Another zone has its own points of interest and paths.
- Zoning ends a walk, with a line. So does a point the toon cannot get to, and closing OgreBot.
- A walk waits while something else has the toon and goes on from the same point: a fight, a death until a res or a revive in the same zone, a pull of Auto-Hunt, a movement block, the Pause of the Nav window. The last line of this window says what it is waiting for.
- The first time you enter a zone that has an old OgreBot Classic route, it comes across by itself as a path called Default, and one line says how many points came and which did not. What you delete afterwards does not come back unless you press Import.
- A camp spot walk needs 'Allow Camp Spot' on for that toon. A walk that finishes leaves the camp spot at its last point, and the camp spot you had before does not come back. Stop clears the camp spot, and the toon stands where it is.
- The Auto-Hunt tab picks one of these paths to walk between pulls, and it only walks: it never flies one. Start here walks a path with no hunting, and that walk may fly. Hunting does not end that walk, and the walk waits while Auto-Hunt works a pull. Auto-Hunt pulls nothing in the air, so a walk that flies is never held for one.
- A walk under way keeps the points it had when it started. Change the path as you like: Stop and Start walks the new order, and so does the next pick on the Auto-Hunt tab.
- A move or an insert is refused with a line if another box changed the list since you saw it, so a point never lands in the wrong place.
- A path or a point of interest saved on one box shows on every other box on this PC within a second or so.

### For scripts

The same things have commands: `OgreBotAPI.POI` for points of interest and `OgreBotAPI.Paths` for paths. In OgreConsole, `-POI_Add` saves a point of interest, `-Path` walks a path and `-PathStop` stops it. The verbs that change a path take a for-who first: paths are shared by every box on the PC, so name one box and one line changes the path once. `OgreBotAPI.Paths:InsertPoint` and `MovePoint` take a place counted from 1. `ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open` opens this window, on a path if you name one (`ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open[North Loop]`): any panel or script that wants a path edited calls that.

### A zone with no points of interest yet

![Empty](../assets/paths/empty.png)

# Safe Fall Trainer

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Trains Safe Fall for you: mount, fly up, dismount, fall, land, remount, repeat. Every landing is a skill-up chance.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Flight time** - how long each climb lasts, in ticks (10 ticks = 1 second, 5 to 600).
> - **Start** - target yourself, mount up and begin. It is dimmed, and does nothing, while a run is going or you are not in the world.
> - **Stop** - end training where you are.
> - Watch the phase, rounds, falls trained and ramps as it runs. "started at" is the flight time this run began with.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Clear your target to stop it; any target (even a mob) keeps it going.
> - Every 100 rounds the flight grows by half a second, up to 25 seconds.
> - Zoning ends the run. Do not mix it with follow, nav or a camp spot.

**Open it:** Type `ogre safefall panel`. `ogre safefall on` (or `ogre safefall on 45` for a 4.5 second flight) starts training without the window, `ogre safefall off` stops it, `ogre end safefall` (or the window's X) stops it and closes the window, and a bare `ogre safefall` prints its status in the console.

## What it is for

Trains your Safe Fall skill for you. It targets you, mounts up, then repeats: fly straight up for the flight time, dismount so you fall, wait until you land, remount, and go again. Every landing is a Safe Fall skill-up chance. Every 100 rounds the flight gets half a second longer so the falls get higher. It runs until you stop it, untarget yourself, or leave the world.

## Start, Stop and flight time

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Start** | Starts training with the flight time in the box: targets you, mounts up, waits 7 seconds, then begins the climb-and-fall loop.<br>*Dimmed, and does nothing, while training runs or while you are not in the world. To change the flight time, press Stop first.* |  |
| **Stop** | Stops training and stops the climb. You stay wherever you are (mounted or not).<br>*Dimmed, and does nothing, when nothing is running.* |  |
| **Flight time (… ticks)** | How long each climb lasts, in ticks: 1 tick is 0.1 second, so 30 is 3 seconds (shown to the right). Allowed 5 to 600.<br>*A number outside 5 to 600 turns the box red and Start refuses. The box follows the running value until you type in it; empty it to hand it back.* | 30 ticks (3.0 s) |



## Status

Read-only. It updates four times a second.

## What the window shows

- Pill next to SAFE FALL: 'running' (green), 'idle', or 'not in world' (red).
- Phase: what it is doing now - starting, flying up, stopping climb, dismounting, falling (1/2), falling (2/2), landed, remounting, idle.
- Round: how many rounds since the last flight-time increase, out of 100.
- Falls trained: completed climb-and-fall rounds since you pressed Start.
- Ramps taken: how many times the flight time has grown this run.
- In world / Target / Flying: yes or no. Target means you have something targeted (training stops when you have nothing targeted). Flying means you are flying on your mount.
- Deadline: the current flight time in milliseconds. It never goes above 25000 (25 seconds), even if the ticks keep growing.
- The long line: flight ticks and seconds, the flight time this run started at ('not started yet' before the first Start), the ramp rule, ramps so far and falls so far.
- The note box: the last thing that happened, for example 'dismounted - falling', 'self-target lost', 'left the world'.

## Good to know

- The quickest way to stop is to clear your target: training ends as soon as you have nothing targeted. Clicking a mob does not stop it - any target keeps it going.
- Zoning, camping or going to character select ends the run; it does not pick up again afterwards.
- It does not check whether something else is moving your character. Do not run it together with other movement (follow, nav, camp spot).
- Typing `ogre safefall on` while training is running starts over from round 0 (the Start button is dimmed then, so it cannot do this by accident).
- `ogre safefall panel` when the window is already open does nothing and prints nothing.
- Closing the window stops training, the same as `ogre end safefall`. Stop stops it and keeps the window open.

## Before you start

![Idle, before Start](../assets/safefall/idle.png)

A flight time outside 5 to 600 ticks turns the box red:

![A bad flight time](../assets/safefall/badticks.png)
