# Auto-Login

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Builds auto-login profiles: which character goes into which session. Start makes your sessions match the profile and loads OgreBot on each character once it is in the world.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Profiles** - click one to open it. **+ New** starts a blank one; **Import** copies your old OgreBot profiles.
> - **Character rows** - pick the PC (ThisUplink, or another PC), the session (is1, is2, or any) and the character.
> - **Other PCs** - add another PC's uplink name so a row can put characters on it. Start connects to it and logs those characters in there.
> - **Settings** - the game to launch and the pauses between launches and logins (in tenths of a second).
> - **ISBoxer character sets** - if you launch with ISBoxer, pick the set for each PC. Start launches them first, then logs your characters into the sessions they opened, and launches only a session that is still missing. Leave a PC empty if it doesn't use ISBoxer.
> - **Save** the profile, **Delete** the one selected in the list, or make a **Desktop shortcut** that runs it.
> - **Start** runs the profile as it is in this window. Tick **Dry run** to only list what it would do.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Saving over an existing profile needs **Overwrite** ticked.
> - Start never saves. Changes you have not saved are used for that one run only: close the window and the saved profile is as it was.
> - No passwords are stored; characters must be in your saved account list - on another PC, in that PC's list.
> - Another PC needs Ogre installed. One that can't be reached has its rows skipped.

**Open it:** Type `ogre autologin`. `ogre end autologin` closes it.

## What it is for

Auto-Login builds **profiles**: a named list of which character goes into which InnerSpace session. Press **Start** and InnerSpace itself (the uplink, not the game window) makes your sessions match the profile: characters already in the right place are left alone, a wrong character is camped out, missing sessions are launched, and each character is logged in with a pause between logins. Once a character is in the world, OgreBot is loaded for it. Profiles hold no account names or passwords; those come from your saved account list when the profile runs, so a profile is safe to share.

## Profiles list

Your saved profiles, in name order. The number after a name is how many characters it has. A red name with a warning sign is a profile file that could not be read.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Click a profile** | Opens that profile on the right so you can check it, change it, start it or delete it.<br>*Clicking a red (broken) profile only shows why it could not be read, in the log at the bottom.* |  |
| **+ New** | Clears the right side for a brand new profile: no name, one character row (ThisUplink, any), and the default settings.<br>*Nothing is saved until you click Save.* |  |
| **Import** | Copies your auto-login profiles from the old OgreBot into this window. It reads the old bot's AutoLoginProfiles.xml and AutoLoginSettings.xml (in Scripts\EQ2OgreCommon\OgreAutoLogin) and writes one new profile per old one. The log shows how many were written, skipped or failed.<br>*The old bot's timing settings are copied into every imported profile. Characters not in your saved account list are counted as warnings but still imported.* |  |
| **Overwrite on import** | When ticked, Import replaces a profile you already have with the same name. When not ticked, those are skipped and your existing profile is kept. | off |

## Profile name

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Profile name** | The name of the profile. Save uses it. The file on disk is named after it, with anything that is not a letter or number turned into an underscore.<br>*Spaces are fine. Renaming a saved profile and clicking Save moves it to the new name.* | empty |

## Character assignments

One row per character. Each field is pick-or-type: click it for a list, or type anything. Typing narrows the list.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Uplink** | Which PC this character is logged in on. ThisUplink means "whichever PC runs the profile". To put a character on another PC, add that PC to Other PCs below and pick it here: Start connects to that PC, launches and logs in its sessions there.<br>*The list offers ThisUplink plus the PCs in Other PCs (this PC itself is ThisUplink). That PC logs the character in with its own saved account list, and it needs Ogre installed.* | ThisUplink |
| **Session** | Which InnerSpace session the character must be in: is1, is2 and so on. "any" means any session is fine: if the character is already in the world somewhere it is left alone, otherwise a free session is used or a new one is launched.<br>*The list offers any and is1 to is24. Left empty, it saves as any.* | any |
| **Character** | The character to log in. The list shows the characters in your saved account list.<br>*A character that is not in your saved account list gets a warning when the profile runs, because its account cannot be looked up.* | empty |
| **x (remove row)** | Removes that character row. If it was the last row, a fresh empty row takes its place.<br>*Not saved until you click Save.* |  |
| **+ Add row** | Adds another character row (Uplink ThisUplink, Session any, Character empty). |  |

## Other PCs (uplinks)

The other PCs a character row can name, by their InnerSpace uplink name. It is the same list as OgreBot's Uplink Info tab and the MCP's Connect button. When a profile has rows on another PC, Start connects to that PC if it is not connected yet, checks that its uplink answers, then launches, logs in and loads OgreBot on its sessions from this PC. A PC that cannot be reached has its rows skipped and the rest of the profile still runs.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Uplink name** | Type the InnerSpace uplink name of another PC (in InnerSpace on that PC: its Remote name). | empty |
| **+ Add** | Adds the typed name to the list. The log says whether it was added.<br>*The list is saved at once, for every profile on this PC.* |  |
| **x (remove PC)** | Takes that PC off the list.<br>*Rows that name it keep the name; Start still tries to connect to it.* |  |

## Settings

Times are in tenths of a second: 150 means 15 seconds. The editor scrolls; these are below the character rows.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Game** | The InnerSpace game entry used when a new session has to be launched. The list comes from the games set up in InnerSpace.<br>*Left empty, it saves as Everquest 2.* | Everquest 2 |
| **Game profile** | The InnerSpace game profile used when a new session has to be launched. The list shows the profiles of the game chosen above. | everquest 2 default profile |
| **ISBoxer character sets** | If you launch with ISBoxer, the character set to launch on each PC: one line for this PC (ThisUplink) and one for each other PC the rows name. Start launches every PC's set first (another PC's on that PC), then logs your characters into the sessions they opened, and launches only a session that is still missing.<br>*Each list shows that PC's sets from ISBoxer. Leave a line empty for a PC that does not use ISBoxer. A PC whose last row is removed keeps no set.* | empty (no ISBoxer) |
| **Wait after load** | After new sessions are launched, how long to wait for them to load before logging anyone in. Only used when a session had to be launched. | 150 (15 seconds) |
| **Wait between launches** | The pause after each new session is launched, before the next one. | 50 (5 seconds) |
| **Login stagger - base** | The pause between one character's login and the next, so the server is not hit with every login at once. | 300 (30 seconds) |
| **Login stagger - random** | A random extra pause, up to this much, added to the base pause for each login. 0 turns the random part off. | 150 (up to 15 seconds) |

## Save, Delete, Shortcut and Start

At the opening window size these buttons are below the fold: scroll the right side down to reach Start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Overwrite** | Must be ticked to save over a profile that is already saved. Without it, Save refuses and says a profile with that name already exists.<br>*This includes saving changes to the profile you just opened. It is not remembered: it is off each time the window opens.* | off |
| **Save** | Saves the profile. The log says whether it worked, and the list on the left updates.<br>*A profile needs a name. A row with no character is dropped when saving; a blank Uplink saves as ThisUplink and a blank Session as any. Settings this window does not show (such as loginOnly or sessionAppearMaxDs, set by hand in the file) are kept.* |  |
| **Delete** | Asks for confirmation, then deletes the profile you selected in the list.<br>*It deletes the selected saved profile, even if you have typed a different name in the box. A new profile that was never saved cannot be deleted.* |  |
| **Delete (in the confirm box)** | Deletes the profile file and clears the right side to a new blank profile. This cannot be undone. |  |
| **Cancel (in the confirm box)** | Closes the confirm box without deleting anything. |  |
| **Desktop shortcut** | Puts a shortcut on your Windows desktop that runs this saved profile through InnerSpace, the same as pressing Start. The log shows where it was made.<br>*Save the profile first. A shortcut with the same name is replaced; if something else already has that name, a numbered copy like "Raid_Night (1)" is made instead.* |  |
| **Dry run** | When ticked, Start only works out and lists what it would do (who stays, who gets camped, which sessions it would launch, who it would log in). Nothing is actually done.<br>*Off means Start really does it. Tick it the first time you try a new profile.* | off |
| **Start** | Runs the selected profile, as it is saved, in InnerSpace. Characters already where they belong are left alone; a wrong character in a session is camped first; missing sessions are launched; then each character logs in, with the stagger pause between logins. Each character gets OgreBot loaded as soon as it is in the world. Progress appears in the log below as it happens.<br>*Start runs the profile as last SAVED, not what is on screen. Click Save first if you changed anything, or if the profile is new.* |  |

## Window

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes the window. A run that has already started keeps going in InnerSpace.<br>*Unsaved changes are lost.* |

## What the window shows

- Profiles (left): every saved profile, in name order. The number in brackets is how many characters it has. Green outline = the one open on the right. Red with a warning sign = a profile file that could not be read.
- The note under the name is a reminder that profiles hold no usernames or passwords.
- The log (bottom): green lines are things that worked, red lines are problems. During a Start it shows the run as it happens, between "run output" and "run complete" lines.
- The log stops following a run if nothing new appears for 90 seconds, or after 10 minutes.

## Good to know

- Saving changes to an existing profile needs Overwrite ticked, even if it is the profile you just opened.
- Start runs the SAVED profile. Save first if you changed anything.
- Rows on another PC are run from this PC: it connects to that PC and drives its sessions there. That PC needs Ogre installed and the characters in its own saved account list - passwords never leave the PC they are saved on.
- Profiles are saved as files in Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\AutoLogin\Profiles. They hold no passwords, so they are safe to copy or share.
- Characters must be in your saved account list so their account can be found when the profile runs.
- Opening the window again while it is open does nothing, so the profile you are editing stays.

![The settings and the Start button](../assets/autologin/window-lower.png)

The right side scrolls. At the size the window opens at, **Start** is below the fold.

Click a field for its list, or type: typing narrows the list, and you may type a value that is not in it.

# Persona

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Say which profile file each class uses on this PC, for example all rangers use `master_ranger.json`. A new character in a class with no rule starts from the class sample.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Server** narrows the rules to one server. Blank means every server. A short form like `ior` works.
> - **Pick a file** on a row sets the rule for that class. **All** is the rule for every class, on every server.
> - **Clear** forgets a rule.
> - **Characters that override a rule** lists those whose own setting beats a rule shown here. **Clear** puts one back on the rules.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - A change applies the next time that class loads.
> - One character's own setting is on the **Persona** tab in OgreBot.
> - `ogre end persona` closes this window.

**Open it:** Type `ogre persona`, or press Open Persona window on OgreBot's Persona tab. If the window is already open, this does nothing. `ogre end persona` (or the window's X) closes it.


## What it is for

A persona is one character in one class. This window says which profile file a class uses on this PC, for example all rangers use `master_ranger.json`. A rule can cover every server or one server. A character with no rule and no setting of its own starts from the sample profile for its class. One character's own setting, which beats these rules, is on the Persona tab in OgreBot.

## Which rules are shown

The Server box says which rules the rows below are for.


| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Server** | Blank shows and sets the rules for every server. A server name shows and sets the rules for that server only. A short form like `ior` works. |
| **Show** | Shows the rules for the server in the box, and reads the routing file again. Enter in the box does the same. |



## Rules

One row for All and one for each of the 26 classes. Each says which file it uses now.


| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Pick a file** | Sets the rule for this class to a profile file from your Main profiles folder. The All row is the rule for every class that has no rule of its own, and it has no server form. |
| **Clear** | Forgets this rule. |



## Characters that override a rule

A character listed here has its own setting for a class that has a rule shown above, so the rule does not reach it.


| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Clear** | Forgets this character's own setting, so it follows the rules again. |



## What the window shows

- A row with no rule says what happens instead: another rule that still applies, or that it starts from the class sample.
- The footer shows what the last button did.
- **missing** beside a file: the rule names a profile file that is no longer in the Main profiles folder. A character the rule is for can't open OgreBot until you pick another file or **Clear** the rule.

## Good to know

- A change applies the next time that class loads. A character already on that class is not changed until then.
- With every server shown, a character with its own setting counts as overriding the All rule too.
- A character's own setting wins over any rule here. It is set on the Persona tab in OgreBot.
- Every character on this PC shares these rules (OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/Profiles/Routing.json).

## Profile not found

When OgreBot can't open for a character because one of these rules names a profile file that isn't there any more, a small **Profile not found** window opens.

![The Profile not found window](../assets/routefix/window.png)

It says which rule it is (for one character, for every character of a class, or for every character), which file is missing, and which profile the character will use instead.

- **Fix it and open OgreBot** removes just that rule, then opens OgreBot the way you asked for it. No file is deleted.
- **Open the Persona window** opens this window, so you can pick a different file yourself.
- **Not now** closes it. OgreBot stays closed.

If the next rule also names a missing file, the window comes back for that one.

# Inventory Manager

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Tidies your bags: deposit to depots, sell, destroy, transmute or salvage (TSE), restock from depots, trade to players, and fill your quiver.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Run tab** - Look shows in the console what a mode would do; Run starts it. While something runs, Run becomes Queue.
> - **Sell list / Destroy list** - double-click a left row to add it; click a right row, then right-click it to remove it.
> - **TSE, Depot, Restock** - saved options for those modes. Depot saves only when you press Save.
> - **Trade** - queue items for nearby players, then Run the queue.
> - **Stop** stops the work; **Close** only closes the window. The X (or `ogre end im`) does both.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - The bag boxes on the Destroy list and TSE tabs decide which bags those runs touch.
> - Restock on the Run tab always uses the profile named Default.
> - Quiver refills with the ammo already in your quiver first, then the name on the Quiver tab.

**Open it:** Type `ogre im` (or `ogre inventorymanager`). Any `ogre im` command that starts work (for example `ogre im sell` or `ogre im -depot -sell -end`) also opens it. `ogre end im` stops the work and closes it.

## What it is for

The Inventory Manager (IM) tidies your bags. It can deposit into house and guild-hall depots, sell to a merchant, destroy junk, transmute or salvage gear (TSE), top up supplies from the depots (Restock), hand items to other players (Trade), and fill your quiver. The Run tab starts any of these; the other tabs hold each one's saved list or options. Every button sends the same `ogre im ...` command you could type yourself, and the log strip at the bottom shows one line per thing IM actually did.

## Header, tabs and the log settings

The tabs only change what you see. The dot and word on the right say whether IM is working and on what.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Run / Sell list / Destroy list / TSE / Depot / Restock / Trade / Quiver** | Switches the page. Opening Sell list or Destroy list also rebuilds that tab's left-hand list (the merchant's items, or your bags). Otherwise display only.<br>*Switching to Sell list does not walk to or open a merchant - it only reads a merchant window that is already open.* | Run |
| **Log** | Shows or hides the row of activity-log settings under the header. Display only. | hidden |
| **Always** | The activity log strip is always on screen. Saved. | on (this is the starting choice) |
| **Only while running** | The log strip appears only while a mode is working, and hides again when it is idle. Saved.<br>*Showing and hiding the strip makes the whole window taller and shorter by the strip's height.* | off |
| **Never** | Hides the log strip for good. Saved. Use the Log button to get the setting back. | off |
| **Clear it** | Empties the activity log. |  |



## Run tab - the modes

One row per mode. Look prints what the mode would do in the console and changes nothing. Run starts it. While anything is running, every Run turns into Queue and every Look greys out (see the second picture).

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Run (depot)** | Deposits into your house or guild-hall depots using the line saved on the Depot tab.<br>*Greyed out if nothing is saved on the Depot tab. There is no Look for depot.* |
| **Look (sell)** | Lists in the console which items on your sell list the open merchant would buy. Sells nothing.<br>*Needs a merchant window already open.* |
| **Run (sell)** | Sells every item on your sell list to a merchant, then closes the merchant window. If no merchant window is open, it opens one that is within reach first.<br>*Stand next to a merchant. Bags marked NO SALE in the game are never offered.* |
| **Look (destroy)** | Lists in the console what the destroy run would destroy. Destroys nothing. |
| **Run (destroy)** | Destroys every item on your destroy list found in the bags ticked on the Destroy list tab. Destroyed items do not come back.<br>*Use Look first. It only touches the bags ticked on the Destroy list tab (bags 1 and 2 to start with).* |
| **Run (tse)** | Transmutes, salvages and/or extracts items using the options saved on the TSE tab.<br>*There is no Look for TSE.* |
| **Look (restock)** | Lists in the console what the Default restock profile still needs and which depots are in reach. Pulls nothing.<br>*Always the profile named Default. To look at another profile use Preview on the Restock tab.* |
| **Run (restock)** | Pulls items from your depots until you hold the target amount of each row in the Default profile. It never buys anything; a shortfall is reported.<br>*Always the Default profile. Use 'Run this profile' on the Restock tab for another one.* |
| **Look (trade)** | Walks the trade queue in the console: who is in reach and what would go in the first trade window. Hands nothing over. |
| **Run (trade)** | Hands each queued item to the player it names, one entry at a time. The other player must be nearby and accept the trade. |
| **Run (quiver)** | Fills your equipped quiver or pouch with ammo from your bags, then from the Ammo Depot. |
| **Queue (any mode, while something runs)** | Adds that mode to the waiting line. Queued modes run one after another, in the order you clicked, when the current one finishes. A dot or ×2 beside the mode name shows it is waiting.<br>*Look buttons stay greyed out until everything has finished.* |



## Run tab - Right now

Read-only. Window says whether IM counts its window as open. Doing names the running mode (or idle). Detail shows that mode's current step. Queued (only when something is waiting) lists the modes still to come, in order.

## Sell list tab

Left: what the open merchant would buy from you (green = already on your sell list, xN = how many stacks). Right: your saved sell list. It fills by itself when you open a merchant window while this tab is showing.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **type to filter… (left)** | Hides left-hand rows whose name does not contain the text. Not case-sensitive. Display only. | empty |
| **Double-click a left row** | Adds that item to the sell list (or destroy list on the Destroy tab) and saves it. The row turns green.<br>*Adding an item that is already there does nothing.* |  |
| **type to filter… (right)** | Hides right-hand rows whose name does not contain the text. Display only. | empty |
| **Click a right row, then right-click it** | Removes that item from the list and saves it.<br>*Right-clicking a row that is not selected only selects it, so a stray right-click never removes anything.* |  |
| **Re-open merchant** | Reads the merchant again and refills the left list. If no merchant window is open it opens one within reach first (your last one, your target, or the nearest). Either way it then closes the merchant window.<br>*It closes the merchant window even if you opened it yourself. If no merchant is within reach it says so in the console and the list is left as it was.* |  |



## Destroy list tab

Same two lists as the Sell tab: left is what is in your bags, right is your saved destroy list. Double-click and right-click work the same way.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **1 2 3 4 5 6** | Which of your six bags the destroy list works with: the left list shows their items, and Run destroy (and Look) only touch these bags. Saved. The list rebuilds as you tick.<br>*The same boxes decide the left list and the run, so they always agree.* | 1 and 2 on |
| **Overseer** | Also use items in your Overseer bag, for the list and the run. Saved. | off |
| **Harvest** | Also use items in your Harvest bag, for the list and the run. Saved. | off |
| **Shared TS** | Also use items in your Shared Tradeskill bag, for the list and the run. Saved. | off |
| **Refresh** | Re-reads your bags and rebuilds the left list. |  |



## TSE tab

Everything here is saved, and a plain `ogre im tse` (or Run tse) uses it. Options typed on the command line still win for that one run.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Transmute** | TSE transmutes the items it picks. Ticking it unticks Salvage and Salvage + Transmute. | on |
| **Salvage** | TSE salvages the items it picks. Ticking it unticks the other two. | off |
| **Salvage + Transmute** | TSE salvages or transmutes each item, whichever applies. Ticking it unticks the other two. | off |
| **Extract (overlay)** | Also extracts, on top of whichever of the three above is ticked. | off |
| **No tier, Handcrafted, Treasured, Legendary, Fabled, Mastercrafted, Mythical, Celestial, Masters, Spell scrolls, Unknown tier** | Which item tiers TSE may use. An item of an unticked tier is left alone. Each box saves as you click.<br>*Treasured also covers Uncommon; Mastercrafted also covers Mastercrafted Legendary and Mastercrafted Fabled. Unknown tier is for a tier the bot has never seen (a new expansion).* | Treasured, Legendary and Fabled on; the rest off |
| **from** | Lowest item level TSE will use. Saved when you leave the box or press Enter.<br>*If 'from' is above 'to', nothing qualifies and a warning shows beside the boxes.* | 1 |
| **to** | Highest item level TSE will use. Saved when you leave the box or press Enter. | 200 |
| **Only at or below** | When ticked, TSE only uses an item whose resolve is at or below the number beside it. When unticked, resolve is not checked at all. | off |
| **Resolve number** | The highest resolve TSE may use when 'Only at or below' is ticked. Saved when you leave the box or press Enter; you can set it before ticking the box.<br>*With the box ticked, 0 means nothing qualifies.* | 0 |
| **Bags 1 2 3 4 5 6** | Which of your six bags TSE looks in. TSE's own set - separate from the Destroy tab's. Saved. | 1 and 2 on |
| **Overseer / Harvest** | Lets TSE also use items in your Overseer bag or your Harvest bag. Each box is for its own bag. | off |
| **Shared TS** | Lets TSE also look in your Shared Tradeskill bag. That bag holds crafting materials, so it rarely has anything TSE can use. | off |



## Depot tab

This builds the depot line a plain `ogre im depot` (and Run depot, and the -depot step of a chain) uses. Nothing is sent until you press Save; the line under 'The line this sends' shows what Save will store.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Nearest** | Use whichever size of each depot is in reach. Ticking it unticks Small and Large. | on |
| **Small** | Use the regular-size depots. Can be on together with Large (it visits both). Unticks Nearest. | off |
| **Large** | Use the large depots. Can be on together with Small. Unticks Nearest. | off |
| **everything, all tiers** | Ticks every depot with All (including Ammo). Unticking it unticks every depot.<br>*This includes the Ammo Depot, so a depot run would put your arrows back in the depot.* | off |
| **Depot name (Harvesting Supply Depot, Scroll Depot, ... Ammo Depot)** | Includes that depot. Ticking a depot with no tier beside it turns on its All.<br>*Ammo is off by default because `ogre quiver` pulls ammo out of that depot.* | every depot on with All except Ammo Depot (off) |
| **All (beside a depot)** | Uses that depot's own Deposit All button: everything the depot accepts. Ticking it clears that depot's single tiers. | on for every depot except Ammo |
| **Tier boxes (Common, Treasured, Legendary, Fabled, Rare, (Lesser), ...)** | Deposit only these tiers into that depot, using the depot's own buttons. Each depot has its own set. Ticking one turns off All for that depot. | off |
| **Commons, Rares, Manas, Infusions, Powders, Fragments** | Deposits these harvested/refined items one at a time by name, into a ticked depot that takes them. This is how you say, for example, 'fragments but not powders'.<br>*They only go into depots that are ticked above.* | off |
| **Arrows, Shurikens** | Deposits arrows or shurikens one at a time by name into the Ammo Depot.<br>*Only works when Ammo Depot is ticked.* | off |
| **Back to saved** | Throws away your unsaved ticks and shows the saved line again. |  |
| **Save** | Saves the line shown above. From now on Run depot, `ogre im depot` and the -depot chain step use it.<br>*Greyed out when no depot is ticked, no container size is ticked, or a ticked depot has nothing it could take (no tier, no All, and no item box that depot accepts - a red note says which).* |  |



## Restock tab

A profile is a list of items with a target amount. Rows that do not apply to this character (by For who) are dimmed. Changes save as you make them.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Profile** | Which profile this tab shows and edits. The number is how many rows it has. Display only. | the first profile (Default) |
| **Preview** | Lists in the console what this profile still needs and which depots are in reach. Pulls nothing. |  |
| **Run this profile** | Pulls items from your depots until you hold each row's target (only the rows meant for this character). Never buys.<br>*Greyed out while IM is running something.* |  |
| **Target** | How many of that item to hold. Saved when you leave the box or press Enter. 0 removes the row. |  |
| **For who** | Which characters this row is for: all, a name, @Scout1, a class word such as priests, *Team:Name and so on. Saved when you leave the box or press Enter. Other characters skip the row. | all |
| **▾ (beside For who)** | Opens a short list to pick from: All, Fighter, Mage, Priest, Scout, G1 to G4. Picking one fills the box and saves it. |  |
| **× (Drop)** | Removes that row from the profile and saves. |  |
| **item name…** | The exact name of the item for a new row. | empty |
| **From examine** | Fills the name in from the item examine window you have open. |  |
| **Amount (next to item name)** | The target for the new row. | 1 |
| **for who: all** | Who the new row is for: all, a name, or a class such as fighter. Empty means all. | empty (all) |
| **▾ (beside for who: all)** | The same short list. Picking one fills the box; nothing is saved until you press Add. |  |
| **Add** | Adds the row to the profile shown and saves, for the characters in the for who box. If the item is already there, its target is replaced. |  |



## Trade tab

A list of hand-overs: which item, how many, to whom. The list lives only until the game or the bot is restarted.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Preview** | Walks the list in the console: whether each player is in reach and what would go in the first trade window. Hands nothing over.<br>*Greyed out when the list is empty.* |  |
| **Run the queue** | Opens a trade with each named player in turn and hands over the item. They must be nearby and accept.<br>*Greyed out when the list is empty or IM is already running.* |  |
| **Clear** | Empties the whole list. |  |
| **× (Drop)** | Removes that one entry. The entries below it move up a number. |  |
| **player…** | Who gets the item. | empty |
| **qty or all** | How many to hand over. Empty or 'all' means every one you have. | empty (all) |
| **item name…** | The item to hand over. | empty |
| **From examine** | Fills the name in from the item examine window you have open. |  |
| **Queue it** | Adds the entry to the end of the list. Needs a player and an item. |  |



## Quiver tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Arrows (bow) / Bolts (crossbow) / Throwing (shuriken)** | The ammo name to refill with. Filling the quiver uses the ammo already in your quiver first, then this name, then the built-in name shown in grey. | empty (built-in name) |
| **Examine** | Sets that kind of ammo to the item in the examine window you have open. |  |
| **Fill the quiver** | Fills your equipped quiver or pouch with ammo from your bags first, then from the Ammo Depot. The kind of ammo follows your ranged weapon and what is already in the quiver. |  |



## Button row and closing

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Stop** | Stops whatever IM is doing: the running mode, the whole waiting line, and any depot pull still going. The window stays open.<br>*Greyed out when nothing is running.* |
| **Run <tab> / Queue <tab>** | Starts the mode for the tab you are on - the same as that mode's Run on the Run tab (or Queue while something is running).<br>*On the Restock tab this runs the Default profile, not the one you picked - use 'Run this profile' for that. Not shown on the Run tab.* |
| **Help in console** | Prints the list of `ogre im` commands in the console. |
| **Close** | Closes the window. A mode that is running keeps running. Cancels a pending -end, and closes a merchant window IM left open.<br>*To stop the work and close, use `ogre end im`.* |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Stops the work and closes the window, the same as `ogre end im`. Also cancels a pending -end and closes a merchant window IM left open. |



## What the window shows

- Status dot and word (top right): grey and 'idle' when nothing runs; green and the mode's name while one runs.
- Yellow '-end is armed' notice: this window will close itself a moment after all the work finishes (started with `-end`, e.g. `ogre im -depot -sell -end`).
- Run tab, mode row highlighted with a dot: that mode is running now; its 'What it does' text is replaced by what it is doing.
- Run tab, dot or ×N after a mode name: that mode is waiting in the queue (N times).
- Sell and Destroy lists: green on the left = already on your list; xN = how many stacks of it there are.
- Restock rows in dim grey: not meant for this character (For who does not match).
- Activity log: one line per thing actually done - a stack sold, an item destroyed or transmuted, a depot emptied - plus a 'finished' line per mode. The coloured word is which mode did it.

## Good to know

- Restock's Look and Run on the Run tab (and 'Run restock' at the bottom) always use the profile named Default. Use the buttons on the Restock tab for another profile.
- Quiver refills with the ammo already in your quiver first, then the name on the Quiver tab.
- The Close button does not stop a running mode. The X (or `ogre end im`) stops it and closes the window; Stop stops it and keeps the window.
- The Depot tab saves nothing until you press Save.
- The trade list is not saved; it is lost when the game or bot restarts.

Every Run becomes **Queue** and the Look buttons grey out. Here TSE is running, sell and depot are waiting (Right now > Queued), and `-end` will close the window when all three are done.

# TaskRunner Lists

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Builds the lists TaskRunner works through: which characters it logs in, in what order, and which timed chores each one does. Run a list with `ogre taskrunner -list <list>` (`run <list>` works too).
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Run** - starts the selected list on this session (save first). The bar shows what it is doing: which character, which chore, and the last result. **Stop** stops it and leaves the character where it is.
> - **List** - click the box and type to find a list (they are in alphabetical order). Type a name that is not a list yet and pick **+ New list** (or press Enter) to make it.
> - **New / Duplicate / Rename / Delete** act on the selected list. Duplicate copies the members, their order and the run mode.
> - **Click a character** on the left to add it to the selected list. Use the **search** box to find a character or account. In **By account**, right-click an account and pick **Add all toons** (or open it and press **Add all**) to add the whole account - anyone already in the list is skipped.
> - **Drag a member row** up or down to change the order the list runs in.
> - **Chore buttons** on a row turn a chore on or off for that character. The **Everyone in** row does it for the whole list.
> - **When run** - **Keep looping** (stays running and picks chores up as they come due - leave it overnight) or **One pass** (does what is due now, then stops).
> - **Stagger start** - each session waits before its first login (is2 30 seconds, is3 60 seconds, and so on). Leave it on when one command starts lists on every session, or the server turns some logins away.
> - **Chore options** - one row per chore. **Guild hall first** travels to the guild hall unless the character is already in one or in a house. **Harvest depot after** puts all harvests into the nearest harvest depot afterwards. **Destroy list after depot** then destroys the items on your IM destroy list - the excess the depot would not take. It only runs with Harvest depot after on, and only when the depot finished. **Bushels** (Plant): the harvest gives a bushel - leave it packed, take the latest reward (a new expansion is picked up on its own), or a chosen reward number. A bushel is lore, so the plant is never harvested while one is still in the bags - with "leave it packed" that character skips the plant until you unpack it. (Pack Pony always loads OgreBot first - it reads its answers from your profile.)
> - **Save** writes your changes (what you set by hand in your own TaskRunner files is kept). **Discard** throws them away and reads the files again.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Never run two lists that share a character on two sessions at once.
> - A character's chores are the same in every list they are in.
> - **Overseer** never logs a character in by itself: it runs when the character is logged in for another chore (the pack pony). Its status says "next login" while it waits.
> - A character in a raid is never logged out: the run stops and leaves everyone where they are.
> - A character that cannot do a chore at all (no Pack Pony) is marked with an error and skipped until you clear it: `ogre taskrunner clear <name>`.
> - Closing the window loses unsaved changes without asking.
> - Closing the window also stops a run in progress, the same as `ogre end taskrunner`. `ogre taskrunner stop` stops it and leaves the window open.

**Open it:** Type `ogre taskrunner panel` (or `ogre tr panel`). `ogre taskrunner gui` and `ogre taskrunner config` also open it.

## What it is for

TaskRunner logs your characters in one after another and does their timed chores, such as the Artisan's Pack Pony and the Goblin House Plant. This window builds the named lists it works through. Pick characters from the ones you have a stored login for, put them in a list, and choose which chores each one does. Then press Run, or type `ogre taskrunner run <list>`, to run the list on this session. Nothing is written until you press Save.

## Header

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Refresh roster** | Reads your stored logins again, so characters you have added since the window opened show up on the left.<br>*Your unsaved list edits are kept.* |



## Lists

The box at the top picks the list you are editing. The buttons beside it act on that list.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **List: (box)** | Click the box and type to find a list. Lists are in alphabetical order, each with how many characters it holds. Pick one to edit it. Type a name that is not a list yet and pick + New list, or press Enter, to make it. | the first list |
| **New** | Opens a name box under the row. Type the new list's name and press OK. The list starts empty.<br>*One word, no spaces or quotes, up to 40 characters: you type it after `ogre taskrunner run`. A name that is already used (in any letter case) is refused with a red message.* |  |
| **Duplicate** | Copies the selected list to a new name: its members, their order and its run mode. The name box opens with a free name filled in. The copy becomes the selected list. |  |
| **Rename** | Opens the name box with the selected list's name, to rename it. |  |
| **Name box (OK / Cancel)** | Shown by New, Duplicate and Rename. Enter does the same as OK, Escape the same as Cancel. |  |
| **Delete** | Deletes the selected list. The characters keep their chore choices.<br>*No confirmation, but nothing is written until Save; Discard brings it back.* |  |



## Run and Stop

At the right of the list row. While a list runs, the status here says which character and which chore it is on, and the footer shows the last result.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Run <list>** | Starts the selected list on this session, using its When run choice and the Stagger start option.<br>*Run uses the saved lists: with unsaved changes it refuses and tells you to save first.* |
| **Stop** | Shown while a list runs. Stops the run and leaves the character where it is. |



## Run options

One row for the whole run, then one row per chore. These are for every list, and Save writes them like everything else.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Stagger start (30s per session)** | Each session waits before its first login: is1 at once, is2 after 30 seconds, is3 after 60, and so on. Leave it on when one command starts lists on every session, or the server turns some logins away.<br>*`nostagger` or `stagger` after `ogre taskrunner run <list>` overrides this for that run.* | on |
| **Guild hall first** | The chore only runs in a guild hall or a house. A character that logged out anywhere else travels to the guild hall first. | on for Pack Pony, off for the others |
| **Harvest depot after** | Afterwards, puts all harvests into the nearest harvest depot. Needs a depot near where the chore runs. | on for Pack Pony, off for the others |
| **Destroy list after depot** | After the harvest depot, destroys the items on your IM destroy list: the excess the depot would not take. It only runs with Harvest depot after on, and only when the depot finished. | off |
| **Bushels: <choice>** | Only on the Plant row. The harvest gives a bushel: leave it packed, take the latest reward (a new expansion is picked up on its own), or take a chosen reward number.<br>*A bushel is lore, so the plant is never harvested while one is still in the bags. With Do not unpack that character skips the plant until you unpack it.* | latest reward |



## Your characters (left side)

Every character you have a stored login for, with its account and server. 'in 2' means the character is already in two lists; those rows are dimmed.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **All toons** | Shows every character in one alphabetical list. Display only. | on |
| **By account** | Groups the characters under their accounts. Display only. | off |
| **search characters or accounts...** | Narrows the left side to characters or accounts whose name contains the text. | empty |
| **Click a character** | Adds that character to the end of the selected list. A character new to TaskRunner starts with every chore turned on.<br>*A character already in the list gets a red 'already in' message. With no list yet you are told to make one first.* |  |
| **Click an account (By account view)** | Opens the account to show its characters. Click again to close it. Display only. | all closed |
| **Add all** | Adds every character on that account to the selected list. Characters already in it are skipped. Right-clicking an account does the same, from any account, open or not.<br>*The button is only shown on an opened account.* |  |



## How the list runs, and chores for everyone

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Keep looping** | When this list runs, it keeps going: it does everything due, then waits and picks up chores as they come due again. For leaving it on overnight.<br>*A list that has never chosen lights what the general TaskRunner setting says (shipped: Keep looping). Typing `ogre taskrunner run <list> once` or `... loop` overrides the choice for that run.* |
| **One pass** | When this list runs, it does what is due right now for each character, then stops. |
| **<chore> (Everyone in <list>: row)** | Gives that chore to every character in the list. If everyone already has it (lit up), a click takes it away from everyone instead. 'partial' means only some have it.<br>*The message line says how many characters actually changed.* |
| **Clear errors (N)** | Shown when characters in this list have chores in error. Clears every error in the list, and those chores run again when next due. |



## List members (right side)

The characters in the selected list, in the order they are logged in.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **<chore> (on a character row)** | Turns that chore on (lit up) or off for just this character.<br>*A character's chores are the same in every list they are in.* | on for a newly added character |
| **Drag a row** | Moves the character to a new place in the login order. Press on the row itself, not on one of its buttons. |  |
| **! and ↺ (beside a chore)** | A red ! means that chore failed for this character. Click it to read why. The arrow beside it clears the error, and the chore runs again when next due.<br>*A character that cannot do a chore at all stays in error until you clear it. `ogre taskrunner clear <name>` does the same.* |  |
| **Remove** | Takes the character out of this list. Their chore choices are kept in case you add them again. |  |
| **Tidy** | Forgets the chore choices of characters that are no longer in any list. The button sits at the top right of this side.<br>*Nothing is written until Save.* |  |



## Warnings, messages, Save and Discard

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Save / Save *** | Writes your lists and chore choices to OgreSave/EQ2/TaskRunner/custom/lists.json, and TaskRunner starts using them straight away. Only what differs from your other TaskRunner files is written, and anything you set by hand for a character there (a chore's own timer, or switching the character off) is kept. 'Save *' means there are unsaved changes.<br>*Greyed out when nothing changed. If a list is running right now, the new lists are used when that batch ends.* |
| **Discard** | Throws away every unsaved change and reads the lists again from the files on disk (so a hand edit made while the window was open shows up). |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes the window and stops a run in progress (the same as `ogre end taskrunner`). Unsaved changes are lost: opening it again reads the saved lists.<br>*There is no 'unsaved changes' prompt.* |



## What the window shows

- List box: the selected list, with how many lists you have beside it. In its drop-down, each list shows how many characters it holds.
- Left side: your characters with account and server. 'in N' = in N lists already (row dimmed). A yellow 'dup' = that name is on more than one account, and TaskRunner cannot tell which one you mean.
- Right side heading: the list name, how many characters, and 'run order' - characters are logged in top to bottom.
- Character row badges: yellow 'also in N' = the character is in other lists too (hover to see which). Red 'no login' = there is no stored login for that name, so TaskRunner cannot log it in.
- Chore buttons: lit up (the theme colour, green by default) = the character does that chore, plain = it does not. Each button shows the chore's name; Pack Pony, Overseer and Plant are the shipped ones.
- Beside a chore that is on: the time until it can run again, or 'due'. Overseer never logs a character in by itself, so it can wait at 'next login' until another chore does.
- Yellow warnings above the footer: a character in two lists, an empty list, a character with no stored login, or a character with every chore turned off. They fold into one line; click it to open or close them.
- The message line: green for what your last click did, red when it was refused and why.
- Minimized: one line with what the run is doing, a Stop or Run button, and Expand.

## Good to know

- Never run two lists that share a character on two sessions at the same time. The window warns you, but nothing stops it.
- Chore choices belong to the character, not the list: turning a chore off for Kannkor in one list turns it off in every list Kannkor is in.
- Nothing is saved until you press Save. Closing the window loses unsaved changes without asking. Typing the open command again while the window is open does nothing (your edits stay).
- The left side only lists characters with a stored login. If it is empty, set up your logins first, then press Refresh roster.

## By account

![Characters grouped by account](../assets/trlists/accounts.png)

Click **By account**, then click an account to open it. **Add all** puts every character on that account into the selected list.

## Before your first list

![No lists yet](../assets/trlists/empty.png)

Type a name in the List box and press Enter (or use **New**), then click characters on the left to fill it.

# Watcher

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Two small alert tools. **Find** tells you when a named creature or NPC shows up in your zone. **Track Shiny** tells you when a shiny of one colour appears near you. When one turns up it drops a waypoint and tells your other sessions.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Add** a name to watch, or add the **-rorr** preset (the four epic ability researchers).
> - **Click the idle pill** next to Find or Track Shiny to turn it on or off.
> - **Scan now** checks the zone once for every name on the list and writes what it finds in Hits (no waypoint).
> - **Colour**: click the shiny colour to track. Purple is chosen to start with.
> - **Clear log** empties the Hits list.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Names must match exactly: "Wanderer" will not find "The Wanderer". Find is silent in a guild hall.
> - Closing the window stops both tools, the same as `ogre end watcher`. To stop only one, click its pill, or type `ogre end find` / `ogre end trackshiny`.
> - Open this window with `ogre watcher`.

**Open it:** Type `ogre watcher`. `ogre find -panel` and `ogre trackshiny -panel` open the same window.

## What it is for

The Watcher has two small tools in one window. **Find** watches for named creatures or NPCs: when one on your list appears in your zone, you get a message, an alarm sound, an in-game waypoint on it, and every other session is told. **Track Shiny** looks for a shiny (a harvestable collectible) of one colour anywhere in your zone and does the same when a new one shows up, with a ding on every session instead of the alarm. Neither needs the window to be open, but closing it with the X ends both.

## Header

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Clear log** | Empties the Hits list below. It does not change the watch list or turn anything off. |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Ends the Watcher (the same as `ogre end watcher`): Find and Track Shiny both stop, and the window closes.<br>*To stop only one, click its pill, or type `ogre end find` or `ogre end trackshiny`. The window stays open.* |



## Find - the watch list

Names must match the whole name exactly (capital letters do not matter). "Wanderer" will not match "The Wanderer".

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **idle / armed (pill next to Find)** | Turns Find on or off. When you turn it on it also checks the zone once for anything already on your list. While on, a listed name that appears gets a message, a waypoint, a note to your other sessions and an alarm sound; one that leaves gets a DISAPPEARED line and the same alarm. The alarm plays on the session that saw it.<br>*With an empty list it stays idle and the console says "nothing to watch - add a name first". The on/off choice is remembered after a restart.* | idle |
| **Actor name (exact)... (placeholder)** | Type a creature or NPC name to watch. Pressing Enter does the same as Add. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed name to the watch list. It does not turn Find on.<br>*A name already on the list is not added twice.* |  |
| **+ -rorr preset** | Adds the four Renewal of Ro researchers (the NPCs that upgrade your epic abilities): The Wanderer, Filowen Curetouch, Angrus Silentfang and Balkot Stonefury.<br>*Only names not already on the list are added. It does not turn Find on.* |  |
| **Scan now** | Checks the zone once, right now, for every name on the list. Each one found is added to Hits as a FOUND line with its location.<br>*Works even while Find is idle. A scan result is a Hits line only: no waypoint and no message to other sessions. It also works in a guild hall.* |  |
| **Clear list** | Removes every name from the watch list and turns Find off.<br>*No confirmation.* |  |



## Find - names and hits

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **x (remove name)** | Removes that one name from the watch list.<br>*Removing the last name turns Find off.* |



## Track Shiny

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **idle / armed (pill next to Track Shiny)** | Turns Track Shiny on or off. While on, it looks through the whole zone every half second for a shiny of the chosen colour, nearest first. When it finds a new one it adds a line to Hits, puts a waypoint on it and tells your other sessions, and every session dings. The same shiny is only reported once. The on/off choice is remembered after a restart. | idle |
| **Colour (White / Green / Purple / Red / BlueShimmer / Blue buttons)** | Which shiny colour to look for. Click a colour; the lit one is in use.<br>*Changing the colour clears Last seen. It does not turn tracking on.* | Purple |



## What the window shows

- Hits: the latest 50 alerts, newest at the bottom. FOUND = seen by a scan. APPEARED = a listed name just showed up. Both are green. DISAPPEARED = it left (grey). "Purple shiny!" = a shiny of that colour was found (yellow). The number after Hits is how many lines there are.
- The pills: green 'armed' means that tool is on; grey 'idle' means it is off.
- polls every 500 ms: how often Track Shiny looks around. It can be changed with `ogre trackshiny -interval <ms>` (250 to 30000).
- Last seen: the name and location of the last shiny found.
- The footer is a fixed reminder of how names and shinies are matched.

## Good to know

- Find names must match exactly. "Wanderer" does not find "The Wanderer".
- Find alerts are silenced while you are in a guild hall. Scan now still works there.
- Closing the window with the X stops Find and Track Shiny, the same as `ogre end watcher`. To stop only one, click its pill, or type `ogre end find` / `ogre end trackshiny`. Opening the window while it is already open does nothing.
- The watch list, colour and on/off choices are saved and come back after a restart. The Hits list is not saved.
- Typing `ogre find <name>` in the console REPLACES the whole watch list with that name and turns Find on. Use the Add box to add a name instead.

## First open

![Nothing watched yet](../assets/watcher/empty.png)

With an empty list both tools are idle. Add a name (or the **-rorr** preset), then click the **idle** pill next to Find to turn it on.

# Ability Export

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Makes the ability file OgreBot needs to cast your abilities, by reading your knowledge book one ability at a time.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Choose what to include**: passives, ascension abilities, a minimum tier or level range, or just a few named abilities.
> - **Merge** into the file you have, write a **Fresh file**, or add **Only abilities I don't have yet** (much faster).
> - **Tradeskill export instead** makes the files Ogre Craft uses.
> - **Run export** starts it. This window steps aside while it runs (`ogre export` brings it back); the small Exporting Abilities window shows progress and can stop it.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - A full export takes a while. OgreBot reloads your abilities when it finishes, unless it was a dry run or you ticked **Don't reload OgreBot when finished**.
> - `ogre export -start` runs with the options set here, without opening this window.
> - Your choices are saved as you make them.
> - If none of the abilities in **Just these abilities** is found, nothing is exported and the top line says so.

**Open it:** Type `ogre export` (or `ogre abilityexport`); typing it again while the window is open does nothing, except while an export runs: then it brings this window back, and the export keeps going. `ogre export -start` runs an export straight away with the options set in this window, without opening it. `ogre export -default -start` does the same with the default options. `ogre end export` (or the window's X) stops a running export and closes the window.

## What it is for

OgreBot needs a list of your character's abilities to cast them. This window makes that list: it reads your knowledge book, one ability at a time, and writes the file OgreBot loads. You pick what to include, then press Run export. While it runs, this window steps aside and the small Exporting Abilities window shows progress. When it finishes, OgreBot reloads your abilities and cast stack from the new file (unless you turn that off).

## Top row

The yellow text left of the buttons is the result of the last thing you did (for example 'Export finished.', 'Export stopped - nothing was written.' or 'Options reset to defaults.').

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Help** | Shows or hides a short explanation under every option. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*The explanations are the same plain-language text as this page.* | off |
| **Reset** | Puts every option back to its default and saves that straight away. |  |
| **Run export / Run (dry run) / Run cache action / Running…** | Starts the export with the options shown. The label tells you what will happen: 'Run (dry run)' when nothing will be written, 'Run cache action' when you picked a cache action that does not export. While the export runs this window steps aside; the small Exporting Abilities window shows the progress and has the Stop button.<br>*Greyed out while the red 'can't run' box is showing, and while an export is already running.* |  |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes this window, and stops an export that is running (the same as `ogre end export`). |  |



## What to export

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Include passive abilities** | Adds your passive abilities to the file. They are left out unless you tick this.<br>*Has no effect on a tradeskill export.* | off |
| **Tradeskill export instead** | Exports ONLY your tradeskill abilities, for Ogre Craft, instead of your combat abilities. It writes up to three files (your crafting class, plus tinkering and adorning if you have them) into the EQ2OgreCraft TSExports folder.<br>*It opens and closes the Examine window once per ability - leave the game window alone while it runs.* | off |
| **Skip ascension abilities** | Leaves your ascension abilities out of the file.<br>*Cannot be ticked together with 'Ascension abilities ONLY' - the window refuses to run.* | off |
| **Ascension abilities ONLY** | Exports nothing but your ascension abilities. | off |
| **Include effect descriptions** | Keeps each ability's effect text in the file. Untick for a smaller file. OgreBot works out what an ability does either way. | on |



## Minimum tier

Pick one. Only abilities at or above the chosen tier are exported.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **All tiers** | Exports every tier. | selected |
| **Journeyman+** | Leaves out Apprentice abilities. |  |
| **Adept+** | Keeps Adept and higher. |  |
| **Expert+** | Keeps Expert and higher. |  |
| **Master+** | Keeps Master and higher. |  |
| **Grandmaster+** | Keeps Grandmaster and higher. |  |
| **Ancient** | Keeps only Ancient abilities.<br>*The old bot never actually filtered on Ancient; this one does.* |  |



## Level range

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Minimum level** | Skips abilities whose class level is below this number. 0 means no minimum.<br>*AA and ascension abilities count as level 0, so any minimum above 0 drops all of them (the window warns you).* | 0 |
| **Maximum level** | Skips abilities whose class level is above this number. 999 means no maximum.<br>*Must be a whole number and not below the minimum, or the window refuses to run.* | 999 |



## Export file

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Merge into existing export** | Starts from the file you already have and adds or updates abilities in it. Abilities not rescanned this time are kept.<br>*On a tradeskill export, only the recorded highest tradeskill level carries over - the ability list is rebuilt from this run.* | selected |
| **Fresh file (replace)** | Ignores the file you already have and writes a brand-new one from this run only. |  |
| **Only abilities I don't have yet** | Merges, but skips every ability already in your file without looking it up again. The quick way to add newly learned abilities.<br>*Abilities already in the file are not refreshed.* |  |
| **Dry run (do not write)** | Does the whole scan but writes nothing, and OgreBot is not reloaded.<br>*The category cache (below) is still updated.* | off |
| **Don't reload OgreBot when finished** | Normally, when an export finishes, OgreBot reloads your abilities and cast stack from the new file. Tick this to leave them as they are. | off |



## Category cache

The cache only makes exports faster: it remembers which abilities an export would throw away anyway, so they are not looked up again. It never changes what ends up in the file. Leave it on Normal unless something is wrong.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Normal (load + use + record)** | Uses the shared cache and adds anything new it learns. | selected |
| **Consolidate, then export** | Folds the cache notes your other sessions left into the main cache first, then exports as normal. Normally only the first session (is1) does this. |  |
| **Consolidate only (no export)** | Folds the other sessions' cache notes into the main cache and stops. No export runs.<br>*Run it after your other characters have exported.* |  |
| **Clear the cache (no export)** | Empties the cache and stops. No export runs. The next normal export rebuilds it.<br>*Only needed if the cache has gone bad.* |  |



## Just these abilities

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Ability names or IDs** | Leave blank to export everything. Otherwise type ability names (spelled as in your knowledge book) or ability ID numbers, separated by commas or new lines, and only those are exported. With 'Merge' the rest of your file is kept as it was.<br>*Names that are not found are listed on the console. If none of them is in your knowledge book, nothing is exported and the window's top row says so.* | empty |



## What the window shows

- Grey text next to each option (like -passive) is the matching script word, for the command at the bottom. Display only.
- Yellow 'Heads up' box: things worth knowing about the options you picked. You can still run.
- Red 'These options can't run' box: something must be fixed first. Run export is greyed out until it is.
- Green command line: the same export as a one-line script command (ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities[...]). Display only.
- Saves to: where the file will be written - normally OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityExports/V3_<name>_<class>_<server>_AbilityExport.json. For a tradeskill export it shows the folder instead ('up to 3 files in').
- Footer: a reminder that `ogre export -start` skips this window.

## Good to know

- A full export looks up every ability one at a time and takes a while. 'Only abilities I don't have yet' is much faster.
- Every option change is saved as you make it, so the window opens the same way next time.
- `ogre export -start` uses the options set in this window. `ogre export -default` (without -start) shows the defaults here without saving them - they are saved as soon as you change an option or press Run export.
- Stopping an export (Stop, or closing the small progress window) writes nothing - the old file is untouched, and this window's top row says 'Export stopped - nothing was written.'
- If none of the abilities in 'Just these abilities' is in your knowledge book, nothing is exported and the top row says so. Names that are not found are listed on the console.
- Typing `ogre export` while this window is open does nothing.
- Options file: OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityExports/export-gui.json. Delete it to go back to defaults.

### While an export runs

Pressing Run export hides this window and opens the small **Exporting Abilities** window (see its own page). When the export ends, this window comes back with the result in the top row.

# Exporting Abilities

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Shows the progress of an ability export. It opens by itself when an export starts and closes by itself when it ends.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Watch progress**: the ability being read, how many of your abilities have been looked at, and how many were kept or skipped.
> - **Stop** ends the export; the Ability Export window comes back if it was open. Closing this window ends the export and closes the Ability Export window too, the same as `ogre end export`.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Stopping writes nothing - your old ability file is left as it was.
> - On a tradeskill export the Examine window opens and closes for each ability. Leave the game window alone until it finishes.

**Open it:** Opens by itself when an ability export starts - from Run export in the Ability Export window, or `ogre export -start`. It closes by itself shortly after the export ends.

## What it is for

A small progress window for an ability export. It shows which ability is being read, how far through the list the export is, and how many abilities were kept or skipped. It is the only way to see (and stop) an export while it runs - the big Ability Export window steps aside until the export ends.

## Progress

Top line: the ability being read right now. It says '(cached)' for an ability the export already knows it would skip, so it is not looked up again, and 'Complete' on the last frame.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Stop** | Stops the export. Nothing is written - your old file stays as it was - and OgreBot does not reload its abilities. If the big Ability Export window stepped aside for the export, it comes back. |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closing this window stops the export, like Stop, and closes the Ability Export window too (the same as `ogre end export`).<br>*The window closes itself about a second and a half after a finished export - that does not stop anything.* |



## What the window shows

- Top line: the ability being read, '(cached)' for one the export skips without a lookup, 'Starting…' before the first one, and 'Complete' at the end.
- n / total: abilities looked at so far out of all the abilities in your knowledge book.
- The bar: the same progress as a percentage.
- added · skipped: how many abilities this run kept for the file, and how many it passed over (passives, wrong tier or level, not in your selection, and so on). With 'Only abilities I don't have yet', the ones already in your file count as skipped - they stay in the file.

## Good to know

- The count is every ability in your knowledge book, not just the ones that end up in the file - most exports skip a lot of them.
- On a tradeskill export the game's Examine window flickers open and shut for each tradeskill ability. Leave the game window alone until it finishes.
- When the export finishes, OgreBot reloads your abilities and cast stack from the new file (unless you ticked 'Don't reload OgreBot when finished' or ran a dry run).
