# OgreBotAPI.Overseer

## Methods

### `AddAgents`

`OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AddAgents[fw, destroy=TRUE]`

Adds every Overseer agent card in your bags and Overseer bag to your agent collection, one card per pulse, and prints a count of added, duplicate, converted and destroyed cards when done. With destroy TRUE a duplicate is converted when that gives items and destroyed otherwise (one whose item details do not load in time is left); with FALSE duplicates are kept, and a second call while a pass runs is refused with a console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `destroy` | bool | `TRUE` | TRUE converts or destroys duplicate cards; FALSE keeps them (any word that is not a yes word counts as FALSE) |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AddAgents[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Overseer_AddAgentsToCollection`

### `AutoAddQuests`

`OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AutoAddQuests[fw]`

Uses every Overseer mission scroll in your bags and Overseer bag - the same add pass the daily run does, on its own. It is refused with a console warning while the daily run or another add pass is going.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AutoAddQuests[igw:${Me.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Overseer_AutoAddOverseerQuests`

### `BuyMissions`

`OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions[fw, flag...]`

Queues an Overseer mission buy run at the merchant, started on the next pulse; with no flags it uses this character's own Overseer Buy tab, and flags such as -season 3, -colour Blue, -num 2, -amount 5, -replenishonly, -noscribe or -destroy override it, each as its own argument (a first word that is not a flag gets one line and starts nothing, a later unknown word is skipped). It needs OgreBot open with a profile loaded and is refused with a console warning when a buy run is already going, and a second call before the next pulse replaces the first.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `flag...` | string |  | Option flags for the run, one per argument, with a flag's value as the next argument (-season, 3); none uses this character's Overseer Buy tab |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions[igw:${Me.Name},-replenishonly]
```

### `CheckQuests`

`OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests[fw]`

Starts the daily Overseer run now instead of waiting for the bot to start it; the run then works through its steps on the pulse. It is refused with a console warning when a run or an add-missions pass is already going or when 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked, and with OgreBot closed it runs on the default options.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests[igw:${Me.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Overseer_CheckQuests`

# OgreBotAPI.Paths

## Members

### `Count`

`${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Count}`

How many saved paths the zone you are in has. It reads 0 in a zone with none, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.

**Returns:** int: the current zone's saved paths.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Count}
```

### `Running`

`${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Running}`

TRUE while a path is being walked on this character, a Paths:Start walk or AutoHunt's. It is FALSE again once the walk finishes, is stopped or ends at a zone.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a walk is in flight on this character.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Running}
```

## Methods

### `AddPoint`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:AddPoint[fw, name, point]`

Adds a point to the end of a saved path of the zone you are in, and a new name makes the path, walked by nav with no loop. A POI name is not looked up here, so its POI can come later: Paths:Start checks every point.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. |
| `point` | string |  | A POI name, or x,y,z. A script that writes x,y,z without quotes gets the same point. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:AddPoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,bell]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_AddPath`, `OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_AddPoint`

### `Clear`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:Clear[fw, name]`

Takes every point off a saved path of the zone you are in. The path stays, with its mover and its loop setting.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:Clear[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_ClearPoints`

### `Delete`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:Delete[fw, name]`

Deletes a saved path of the zone you are in. An unknown name prints one line and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:Delete[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]
```

### `InsertPoint`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:InsertPoint[fw, name, at, point]`

Puts a point into a saved path of the zone you are in at a place in the list, and the point at that place and the ones after it move down one. An unknown path, a place outside the list or a point that cannot be one prints one line and changes nothing, and a walk under way keeps the points it had at its Start.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. It must exist: a place is a place in a list, so this never makes a path. |
| `at` | number |  | The place the point takes, counted from 1. One past the last point puts it on the end. |
| `point` | string |  | A POI name, or x,y,z. A script that writes x,y,z without quotes gets the same point. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:InsertPoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,2,bell]
```

### `MovePoint`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:MovePoint[fw, name, from, to]`

Moves a point of a saved path of the zone you are in to another place in the list, and the points between shift one place. An unknown path or a place outside the list prints one line and changes nothing, and a walk under way keeps the points it had at its Start.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. |
| `from` | number |  | The place of the point to move, counted from 1. |
| `to` | number |  | The place it ends at, counted from 1. Moving a point to the place it holds changes nothing. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:MovePoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,5,2]
```

### `RemovePoint`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:RemovePoint[fw, name, point]`

Takes the first point of that text off a saved path of the zone you are in, so a path that passes a point twice keeps the later one. An unknown path or point prints one line and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it. |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. |
| `point` | string |  | The point as the path holds it, in any case: a POI name, or x,y,z. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:RemovePoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,bell]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_RemovePoint`

### `Start`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:Start[fw, name]`

Walks a saved path of the zone you are in, point by point, by the path's own mover, in place of any walk under way and through a pause of OgreBot; a point that does not resolve stops it before anything moves, and OgreBot must be open. It waits while something else has the character (a fight, a death, an AutoHunt pull, a movement block) and goes on from the same point, and one line says when it finishes, cannot reach a point, or ends at a zone or OgreBot closing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `name` | string |  | The path's name, in any case. A path of one point goes there and finishes, looping or not. A path walked by camp spot leaves the camp spot at its last point when it finishes, and no earlier camp spot comes back. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:Start[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]
```

### `Stop`

`OgreBotAPI.Paths:Stop[fw]`

Stops the path being walked, a Paths:Start walk or AutoHunt's: the character stands where it is, and a walk by camp spot has its camp spot cleared. With no walk it prints one line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Paths:Stop[${Me.Name}]
```

# OgreBotAPI.POI

## Members

### `Count`

`${OgreBotAPI.POI.Count}`

How many points of interest the current zone has, shipped and your own together. It reads 0 in a zone with none, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.

**Returns:** int: the current zone's total. A POI of yours that overrides a shipped one counts once.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.POI.Count}
```

### `Loc`

`${OgreBotAPI.POI.Loc[name]}`

Where a point of interest of the current zone is, shipped or your own. It reads empty for an unknown name, for a POI that names only an actor, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The POI's name, in any case. |

**Returns:** string: x,y,z to two decimals, or empty when there is no such location.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.POI.Loc[bell]}
```

## Methods

### `Add`

`OgreBotAPI.POI:Add[name, x, y, z, sender]`

Saves a named point of interest in the zone you are in, where you stand or at x,y,z, for every character on this PC. A shipped name is overridden, a name of your own moves to the new spot, and a refusal prints one line and saves nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The name, in any case. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number. |
| `x` | float |  | X of the spot. Leave x, y and z out to use where you stand. With any of them given all three are needed, and 0,0,0 is refused. |
| `y` | float |  | Y (height) of the spot. |
| `z` | float |  | Z of the spot. |
| `sender` | string |  | Leave this out in a script. The -POI_Add row fills it with the box that sent the line, and every other box does nothing. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.POI:Add["Quest giver",100,20,-250]
```

### `Remove`

`OgreBotAPI.POI:Remove[name]`

Removes a point of interest of your own from the zone you are in, and a shipped POI it was overriding is back. A shipped POI cannot be removed: that and an unknown name print one line and change nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The POI's name, in any case. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.POI:Remove["Quest giver"]
```

### `Rename`

`OgreBotAPI.POI:Rename[old, new]`

Renames a point of interest of your own in the zone you are in. A shipped POI, an unknown name and a new name that another POI here holds each print one line and change nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `old` | string |  | The POI's name now, in any case. |
| `new` | string |  | The new name. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.POI:Rename["Quest giver","Quest giver east"]
```

# OgreBotAPI.Position

## Members

### `ActorModelSize`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.ActorModelSize[nameOrId]}`

Returns an actor's model size: its collision radius times its collision scale. Returns 0 when the argument is blank or the actor cannot be found.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nameOrId` | string |  | the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:&lt;owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it) |

**Returns:** float: the actor's collision radius times its collision scale; 0 when it is not found.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.ActorModelSize[${Target.ID}]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GetActorModelSize`

### `AtAngle`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngle[angle,actorNameOrId,dist=3]}`

Returns the point at angle degrees around an actor, measured from the actor's heading, dist plus your model size plus the actor's model size away, at the actor's height plus 0.5. Returns "" when the actor cannot be found; it only computes a point and moves nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | int |  | whole degrees around the actor from its heading: 0 is directly behind it and 180 directly in front, 90 and -90 its two sides (a fraction is dropped) |
| `actorNameOrId` | string |  | the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:&lt;owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it) |
| `dist` | float | `3` | the gap between the two bodies, before the model sizes are added |

**Returns:** string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when the actor is not found.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngle[90,${Target.ID},5]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.PointAtAngle`

### `AtAngleNoTargetSize`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngleNoTargetSize[angle,actorNameOrId,dist=3]}`

Same as Position.AtAngle, but the distance adds only your own model size, not the actor's. Returns "" when the actor cannot be found.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angle` | int |  | whole degrees around the actor from its heading: 0 is directly behind it and 180 directly in front, 90 and -90 its two sides (a fraction is dropped) |
| `actorNameOrId` | string |  | the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:&lt;owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it) |
| `dist` | float | `3` | the distance before your model size is added |

**Returns:** string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when the actor is not found.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngleNoTargetSize[180,${Target.ID},3]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.PointAtAngleNoSize`

### `DistanceToActor`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.DistanceToActor[nameOrId=Target]}`

Returns your distance to an actor as the game reports it (the actor's Distance), using your current target when no actor is given. Returns -1 when the actor cannot be found or you are not in the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nameOrId` | string | `Target` | the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:&lt;owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it); blank = your current target |

**Returns:** float: the distance to the actor; -1 when it is not found or you are not in the world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.DistanceToActor[${Target.ID}]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GameDistanceToActor`

### `FarthestActorFrom`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestActorFrom[anchorNameOrId,actorName,minDist=20]}`

Returns the id of the actor named exactly actorName (any case) that is farthest, in straight-line 3D distance, from an anchor actor, as long as it is more than minDist away. Returns 0 when the anchor or no actor of that name is found, or when even the farthest one is not past minDist.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchorNameOrId` | string |  | the actor to measure from: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:&lt;owner>, a class word or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it) |
| `actorName` | string |  | the full name of the actors to choose among (whole-name match, any case) |
| `minDist` | float | `20` | the winner must be farther than this from the anchor, or the answer is 0 |

**Returns:** int64: the chosen actor's id; 0 when there is none.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestActorFrom[${Target.ID},"a void tentacle",20]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestActorFrom`, `OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestActorFrom_ref`

### `FarthestGroupDistance`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestGroupDistance}`

Returns the distance to the farthest other member of your group. Returns 0 when you are solo or not in the world.

**Returns:** float: the largest distance from you to another group member; 0 when there is none.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestGroupDistance}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestGroupDistance`, `Obj_OgreUtilities.GroupWithinDistance`

### `MyModelSize`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.MyModelSize}`

Returns your model size: your collision radius times your collision scale, the body edge the bot adds to its distances.

**Returns:** float: your collision radius times your collision scale.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.MyModelSize}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GetMyModelSize`

### `Toward`

`${OgreBotAPI.Position.Toward[fx,fy,fz,tx,ty,tz,dist=15]}`

Returns the point dist away from the first point in the direction of the second, measured flat (x and z only), with the second point's y. It does not stop at the second point when dist is longer than the gap, and returns "" when fewer than six coordinates are given.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fx` | float |  | the starting point's x |
| `fy` | float |  | the starting point's y (not used in the result) |
| `fz` | float |  | the starting point's z |
| `tx` | float |  | the point to head toward, x |
| `ty` | float |  | the point to head toward, y (becomes the result's y) |
| `tz` | float |  | the point to head toward, z |
| `dist` | float | `15` | how far from the starting point to go |

**Returns:** string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when fewer than six coordinates are given.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.Toward[${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Me.Z},${Target.X},${Target.Y},${Target.Z},10]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.PointTowardDist`

# OgreBotAPI.Quest

## Members

### `ActorHas`

`${OgreBotAPI.Quest.ActorHas[actorId]}`

Whether the actor with this id is within a distance of 10 and offers a quest or has a quest update or hand-in for you. With no id it prints a console line and answers FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actorId` | int64 |  | the actor id to check; required |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when that actor is within 10 and has a quest offer, update or hand-in; FALSE otherwise.

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ActorHasQuest`

### `Have`

`${OgreBotAPI.Quest.Have[name]}`

Whether a quest with this exact name, in any case, is in your active quest journal. No name, or not being in the world, answers FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the full quest name to look for; case does not matter |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the quest is in your active journal; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Quest.Have["Feathers For Sethis"]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.HaveQuest`, `Obj_OgreIH.Check_Quest_Exists`

## Methods

### `Accept`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:Accept[fw, questName=""]`

Clicks Accept on an offered new quest window, never a quest reward window, and does nothing when none is offered. It accepts whether or not the Settings Do not auto accept quests box is ticked, since that box stops only the automatic accept; given a name, a group leader with auto share on shares that quest two seconds later.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `questName` | string | `""` | the quest to share after accepting; blank accepts with no share |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Quest:Accept[${Me.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AcceptQuest`, `Obj_OgreUtilities:AcceptQuest`

### `CheckKunarkAscending`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:CheckKunarkAscending[fw]`

Opens and closes the quest journal, then prints which Kunark Ascending prerequisite quests you have not completed: the languages, the heritage quest, the signature line and an Epic 1.0 quest. It runs in turn on the action queue and ends with a completed line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:CheckKunarkAscendingRequirements`

### `CompareUpdate`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:CompareUpdate[fw, questName, sender]`

Reads your own steps for a quest and asks other characters to compare theirs; a character on a different step says so in its own console and you get a tally. The character that runs it asks, the for-who is who is asked, and all or blank asks the rest of your group.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): which characters are asked; all or blank is your group but you |
| `questName` | string |  | the quest to compare; a missing one prints a console line |
| `sender` | character name |  | the character that asks; the -CompareQuest console line fills it. Leave it out in a script: the character running it asks, and any other name makes the call do nothing |

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:CompareQuestUpdate`

### `Delete`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:Delete[fw, questName]`

Deletes one quest from your own journal straight away and prints the result. There is no group leader check, and a quest that is not in the journal or has moved in it is not deleted.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

### `ShareQuestWhenAble`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuestWhenAble[fw, questName, zoneName]`

Shares one quest once the group has gathered (waiting up to 5 minutes), but only while you are in zoneName - leaving that zone first stops the share with a console line. With all only the group leader shares.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `questName` | string |  | the exact quest name, any case |
| `zoneName` | string |  | the zone the share is for; blank means the zone you are in now |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuestWhenAble[all,"Feathers For Sethis","${Zone.Name}"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ShareQuestWhenAble`

### `ShowMissionInfo`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowMissionInfo[fw]`

Prints the hot zone mission rotation for this server to the console: what is current, what comes next and the time until it changes. It runs on every addressed character, with no group leader check.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowMissionInfo[${Me.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:DisplayEtherealMissionInfo`

### `ShowWiki`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowWiki[fw, name=""]`

Opens the EverQuest 2 wiki page for a quest in your web browser; a blank name uses the quest selected in the quest journal, and with none selected a console line says so and nothing opens. A blank for-who means is1 here, not all.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `name` | string | `""` | the quest to look up; blank uses the quest selected in the journal |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowWiki[${Me.Name},"Feathers For Sethis"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ShowWikiForQuest`

### `SpewMissionTimers`

`OgreBotAPI.Quest:SpewMissionTimers[fw, ...searches]`

Opens the quest journal on its Mission Timers tab and sends one oc line per mission whose name contains a search word, with the time to reset and whether it is completed. With no search word it prints a reminder and nothing else, and it closes the journal when done.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `...searches` | string |  | one or more words; a mission matches when its name contains any of them, in any case |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Quest:SpewMissionTimers[${Me.Name},Weekly,Daily]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Spew_MissionTimerInfo`

# OgreBotAPI.Roster

## Members

### `ArchetypeOf`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.ArchetypeOf[class]}`

The archetype of a subclass name, in lower case: fighter, priest, mage or scout. An actor ID is also accepted and that actor's class is used; a class tier name such as warrior, or anything unknown, reads an empty string.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | string |  | A subclass name such as templar (any case), or an actor ID. |

**Returns:** string - fighter, priest, mage or scout, empty when unknown.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.ArchetypeOf[${Target.ID}]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `ClassInfo.Archetype`, `GetArchetypeFromClass`, `GetInfoOb.Archetype`

### `BaseClassOf`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.BaseClassOf[class]}`

The class tier of a subclass name, in lower case: templar reads cleric, berserker reads warrior. An actor ID is also accepted and that actor's class is used; anything that is not a subclass reads an empty string.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | string |  | A subclass name such as berserker (any case), or an actor ID. |

**Returns:** string - the class tier (warrior, cleric, bard and so on), empty when unknown.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.BaseClassOf[berserker]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.GetBaseClass`, `GetInfoOb.GetClass`, `OgreBotAPI.Get_BaseClass`

### `CountGroupBy`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountGroupBy[mode,search]}`

Counts the members of your group, you included, that match mode and search. Only player characters count: a member whose type reads as anything else (a corpse, for example) is skipped; with no mode it matches by Class, and a mode word the list does not know matches nobody.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `Class` | How to match: All (everyone; search ignored), Class (exact subclass, e.g. templar), RawClass or ParentClass (class tier, e.g. cleric), Archetype, NotArchetype, Role (tank, priest, enchanter, bard, dps), Cursed (search ignored), KraletusCharmers (coercers and troubadors, search ignored). Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody. |
| `search` | string |  | The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case. |

**Returns:** int - number of matching group members, 0 when none match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountGroupBy[Archetype,priest]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.CountGroupBy`, `GetInfoOb.CountGroupBy_`, `CheckGroupSetup`

### `CountRaidBy`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountRaidBy[mode,search]}`

Counts the members of your raid, you included, that match mode and search; in a raid every member counts, corpses too. When you are not in a raid it answers exactly as CountGroupBy does.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `Class` | How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody. |
| `search` | string |  | The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case. |

**Returns:** int - number of matching raid members (group members when not in a raid).

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountRaidBy[Role,priest]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.CountRaidBy`, `GetInfoOb.CountRaidBy_`

### `Flagged`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.Flagged[n=1]}`

TRUE when flag number n is set on this character. Flags are kept by this session only, are set with Roster:Flag, and can be read anywhere, even outside the world; flag 24 is the same state as Marked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int | `1` | The flag number to check. |

**Returns:** bool - TRUE when flag n is set.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.Flagged[2]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.FlaggedToon`, `GetInfoOb:ToonFlagged`, `OgreBotAPI.ToonFlagged`

### `GroupIDBy`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDBy[mode,search,rank=1]}`

The actor ID of the rank-th group member, you included, that matches mode and search, with matches sorted alphabetically by name. Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped); reads 0 when nobody matches or rank is past the last match.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `Class` | How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody. |
| `search` | string |  | The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case. |
| `rank` | int | `1` | Which match to return, counting from 1 in name order. |

**Returns:** int64 - the member's actor ID, 0 when there is no such match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDBy[Class,templar,1]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.GetGroupIDBy`, `GetInfoOb.GetGroupIDBy_`

### `GroupIDPreferred`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDPreferred[search,rank=1]}`

The actor ID of the rank-th group member, you included, whose archetype or role matches search, ordered by how useful that class is to spare (for dps the order is flipped so pure damage classes come first). Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped), a member matching any of the listed pools counts, ties go to the pool listed first and then to name, and it reads 0 when nobody matches.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string |  | One or more archetypes or roles separated by \|, for example scout, dps or scout\|mage. |
| `rank` | int | `1` | Which match to return, counting from 1 in preferred order. |

**Returns:** int64 - the member's actor ID, 0 when there is no such match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDPreferred[scout|mage,1]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.GetGroupIDPreferred_`, `OgreBotAPI.GetGroupIDPreferred`

### `GroupNameBy`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNameBy[mode,search,rank=1]}`

The name of the rank-th group member, you included, that matches mode and search, with matches sorted alphabetically by name. Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped), as in GroupIDBy, so the same rank names the same member in both; reads an empty string when nobody matches or rank is past the last match.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `Class` | How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody. |
| `search` | string |  | The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case. |
| `rank` | int | `1` | Which match to return, counting from 1 in name order. |

**Returns:** string - the member's name, empty when there is no such match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNameBy[Class,templar,1]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.GetGroupInformation`, `GetInfoOb.GetGroupNameBy_`, `OgreBotAPI.GetGroupNameBy`

### `GroupNamePreferred`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNamePreferred[search,rank=1]}`

The name of the rank-th group member, you included, whose archetype or role matches search, in the same preferred order as GroupIDPreferred, so the same rank names the same member in both (a corpse is skipped). search can list several pools with \|; reads an empty string when nobody matches.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string |  | One or more archetypes or roles separated by \|, for example scout, dps or scout\|mage. |
| `rank` | int | `1` | Which match to return, counting from 1 in preferred order. |

**Returns:** string - the member's name, empty when there is no such match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNamePreferred[dps,1]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.GetGroupNamePreferred_`, `OgreBotAPI.GetGroupNamePreferred`

### `GroupSize`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupSize}`


### `InCombat`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InCombat}`

TRUE when anyone in your group is in combat mode, you included, so a solo character reads its own; it checks your group only, never the rest of a raid, and a member in another zone counts as out of combat. Reads NULL when you are not in the world; for your character alone, hated included, use ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.InCombat}.

**Returns:** bool - TRUE when any member of your group, you included, is in combat mode; FALSE when nobody is.

### `InEQ2Chars`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InEQ2Chars[speaker,fullAccountOnly=FALSE]}`

TRUE when speaker is on the list the chat commands trust: every character saved in your account list, on any account (characters not yet assigned to one included), and the name OgreIRCSession, matched in any case. With fullAccountOnly TRUE it is TRUE only when that character also has complete account details saved, the kind a login needs; it works outside the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speaker` | string |  | The character name to look up. |

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.InEQ2Chars`

### `InZone`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InZone[within=0]}`

TRUE when every other member of your group is in this zone and alive, and, when within is above 0, no farther away than within. Solo reads TRUE, outside the world reads FALSE; it checks your group only, never the rest of a raid.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

### `NearestOfClass`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.NearestOfClass[class,range=50,scope=auto,includeMe=TRUE]}`

The actor ID of a group or raid member of the given class who is within range, or 0 when there is none. A match is the subclass, its class tier or its archetype (warrior finds a berserker, fighter finds any fighter); you are checked first and returned with no distance test when includeMe is TRUE, then the closest member in range wins.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | string |  | A subclass, class tier or archetype name, any case. Empty reads 0. |
| `range` | float | `50` | The farthest a member may be. Members whose distance reads 0 are never matched. |
| `scope` | string | `auto` | auto (your raid when in one, else your group), raid, or any other word for your group. |
| `includeMe` | bool | `TRUE` | TRUE to answer with your own ID when your class matches. |

**Returns:** int64 - the matching member's actor ID, 0 when none is in range.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.NearestOfClass[priest,30,auto,FALSE]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.Class`

### `SortGroupByID`

`${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortGroupByID[mode,search,exclude]}`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `search` | string |  | The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case. |
| `exclude` | string |  | A character name to leave out of the ordering, any case. Empty leaves nobody out. |

**Returns:** int - your 1-based position among the matches, 0 when you are not one of them.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortGroupByID[Archetype,scout]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb:Get_GroupIDs`, `GetInfoOb.SortGroupByIDBy_`, `OgreBotAPI.SortGroupByIDBy`

## Methods

### `CheckMemberLevel`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:CheckMemberLevel[fw, onlyNonMembers=FALSE]`

Each selected character prints "&lt;name> Membership level: &lt;level>" on the InnerSpace console, using the game's subscription level. With onlyNonMembers TRUE, characters whose level reads Member print nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `onlyNonMembers` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE to print only for characters that are not Member. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:CheckMemberLevel[all,TRUE]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:CheckMemberLevel`

### `Disband`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:Disband[fw]`

Each selected character sends the game's /disband, which takes it out of its group. It needs the character in the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:Disband[${Me.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Disband`

### `Flag`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:Flag[fw, n=1]`

Sets flag number n on each selected character. When the flag was not already set, a line saying so goes to OgreConsole; setting a flag that is already set is silent, a number outside 1 to 24 is refused with a console line, and it works outside the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `n` | int | `1` | The flag number to set, 1 to 24. Flag 24 is the same state as Mark. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:Flag[${Me.Name},2]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:FlagToon`, `GetInfoOb:FlagToon`

### `FlagNextPerson`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:FlagNextPerson[fw, mark=1, via=any, search..., -GroupOnly]`

Finds the next character after you and tells that character, over IRC and over oc to every session on this PC, to set flag mark on itself. A group goes in actor id order, so every box agrees on who is next, and a raid in slot order; both wrap round, and nothing is sent when nobody passes.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `mark` | int | `1` | The flag number the next person sets. |
| `via` | string | `any` | any, archetype or baseclass: who may be next. Any other word means any. |
| `search...` | string |  | the archetypes or base classes to match; left out, your own |
| `-GroupOnly` | switch |  | use the group even when you are in a raid |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:FlagNextPerson[${Me.Name},3]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:FlagNextPerson`, `OgreBotAPI:FlagToonNextPerson`

### `Invite`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:Invite[fw, who]`

Each selected character sends a group invite to who; an alias such as @Healer1 is turned into that character's name first. Nobody already in your group or raid is invited (silently); a missing name, or one that is not plain letters, is refused with one line on the InnerSpace console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `who` | string |  | The character to invite, by name or alias; me means you, who are always skipped. Required. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:Invite[${Me.Name},${Target.Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Invite`

### `Inviter`

`OgreBotAPI.Roster:Inviter[fw, toon...]`

Each selected character invites a list of characters in order, about one second apart, skipping anyone already with it; names may also be split by spaces or commas. Put -r (or -ri, -raidinvite) before a name to raid-invite that one; -from, -i and -inviter are not supported here and skip the name after them with a warning, and starting a new list stops one that is still running.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `toon...` | string |  | The names (or aliases) to invite, in order, each optionally led by -r for a raid invite. Any other word starting with - is skipped. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Roster:Inviter[${Me.Name},${Target.Name}]
```

# OgreBotAPI.Session

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session.AtCharacterSelect}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.AtCharacterSelect`

`${OgreBotAPI.Session.CharacterName}`

This character's name. It returns "" when not in the world, for example at character select.

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.CurrentCharacter`

### `ReviveLocation`

`${OgreBotAPI.Session.ReviveLocation[option,exact]}`

While you are dead, finds the revive point named by option in the death window and returns its row number. It returns 0 when you are alive, not in the world, give no option, or no revive point matches.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | string |  | a row number, or a revive point name such as Entrance, compared case-insensitively with the text before the bracket; a row that is not a revive point is never chosen |
| `exact` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE: the name must match in full; FALSE: the name may be part of the revive point's name |

**Returns:** int: the row number (from 1) of the matching revive point; 0 when there is none

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session.ReviveLocation[Entrance,FALSE]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_ReviveLocation`

## Methods

### `CollectShiny`

Targets the nearest collectible shiny, by the Loot tab's own test (an actor named only a question mark or an exclamation mark, or a resource whose name has a question mark), and collects it if it is within 10 meters. Nothing happens when none is that close; this runs on demand and is separate from the Loot tab's own shiny collecting.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

# OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns

## Members

### `IsOpen`

`${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.IsOpen}`

Returns whether the Temp Adornments window is open on this session.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the Temp Adornments window is open; FALSE when it is not.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.IsOpen}
```

### `Profiles`

`${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.Profiles}`

Returns how many temporary-adornment profiles are saved - one profile file is shared by every character on this PC. The first read loads that file and, when there is none yet, creates it with the default profiles CBOC, Pot and HP plus any profiles saved by the classic Temp Adorns window.

**Returns:** int: the number of saved profiles; 0 when there are none or the profile file could not be read.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.Profiles}
```

## Methods

### `Apply`

`OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Apply[fw, profile]`

Queues putting a profile's temporary adornments on your gear: each listed piece gets its adornment from your bags, even a piece that already has it with time left; it skips only pieces with nothing equipped and adornments you do not carry. A blank or unknown profile name, or not being in the world, prints one console line and queues nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `profile` | string |  | the saved profile to apply, any case (CBOC, Pot and HP exist by default); a two-handed primary row in it is used for Primary when your primary weapon is a two-hander |

```text
OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Apply[igw:${Me.Name},CBOC]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ApplyTempAdorn`, `OgreBotAPI:PoP_TempAdorns`

### `Close`

`OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Close[fw]`

Closes the Temp Adornments window. Nothing happens when it is not open.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Close[${Me.Name}]
```

### `List`

`OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:List[fw]`

Prints every saved temporary-adornment profile to the console, one line each with its gear pieces and their adornments. Says so when there are no profiles.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:List[${Me.Name}]
```

### `Open`

`OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Open[fw]`

Opens the Temp Adornments window, where profiles are built, saved, deleted and applied. Works at character select too, and does nothing when the window is already open.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text
OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Open[${Me.Name}]
```

# OgreBotAPI.Travel

## Members

### `ZoneDoorValue`

`${OgreBotAPI.Travel.ZoneDoorValue[option]}`

Reads the row that ZoneDoor would pick for an option in the zone-door destination window that is open now, without clicking anything. It reads the window only when it is open and answers 0 otherwise.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | string |  | A row number, a destination name (the whole name in any case, with or without its instance number), or LAST_ENTRY for the last listed row. |

**Returns:** int: the 1-based row of that destination in the open window; 0 when no window is open, the option is empty, no row matches, or a row number is past the end of the list.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Travel.ZoneDoorValue[LAST_ENTRY]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Travel_Get_ZoneDoorValue`

## Methods

### `Bell`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:Bell[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]`

Double-clicks a bell within reach (15 units unless the travel data says otherwise), picks toWhere on its map, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when no bell is in reach or the destination is still missing after a second look.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `toWhere` | string |  | The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the bell offers. |
| `exact` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it. |
| `mzo` | string | `LAST_ENTRY` | When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Travel:Bell[${Me.Name},"Antonica"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:TravelBell`

### `Druid`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:Druid[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]`

Double-clicks a druid ring within reach, or in a guild hall talks to the guild hall druid, if there is one, and uses the ring that conversation brings up, then picks toWhere on its map, clicks the zone button and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when nothing opens or the destination is still missing after a second look.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `toWhere` | string |  | The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the ring offers. |
| `exact` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it. |
| `mzo` | string | `LAST_ENTRY` | When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Travel:Druid[${Me.Name},"Steamfont"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:TravelDruid`

### `Fast`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:Fast[fw, toWhere, flag...]`

Opens the game's fast travel map, picks toWhere, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when the map does not open or the destination is still missing after a second look.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `toWhere` | string |  | The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively as part of a label unless -em is given; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the map offers. |
| `flag...` | string |  | Optional switches in any order. -em (or -exactmatch) matches the whole label. -mto &lt;option> picks that number of sub-map location, counting from 1, the one whose description contains that text, Random, or Last; without it the last location is picked. -loc &lt;x,y,z> (or -mtl) picks the sub-map location nearest that point. -mzo &lt;option> picks the zone-door row: a number, a name, or LAST_ENTRY (the default). -report echoes the sub-map's locations instead of picking one. Unknown words are ignored. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Travel:Fast[${Me.Name},"Antonica",-mto,Random]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:FastTravel`, `call Obj_OgreUtilities.FastTravel`, `Obj_OgreUtilities.Obj_Travel`

### `Mesh`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh[fw, zone, poi=""]`

Plans a route from this zone to zone across the travel network (zone doors, bells, spires, druid rings, the travel map, guild hall amenities and travel items such as call-to-home), echoes its hops, then walks and travels it hop by hop. A trip asked for while zoning starts once the zone settles, a new route replaces the one in progress only when it can be planned, and the route ends when OgreBot ends; a bot you paused stays paused on arrival.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `zone` | string |  | The destination zone: its display name in any case, or its travel-data id. An empty zone echoes "no destination zone given", and an unknown one echoes a "did you mean" list. |
| `poi` | string | `""` | A named point inside the destination zone to walk to at the end. A point the zone does not declare gets a console line and the route still goes to the zone. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh[${Me.Name},"Antonica"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:TravelMesh`

### `MeshFeatures`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshFeatures[fw, flag="", on=""]`

With no flag, echoes the account travel features the route planner knows for this character (the Friends and Family unlocks) and starts a scan for any still unanswered. With a flag and a yes or no, saves your answer for this character, which the planner then trusts and never scans again; a flag with no answer prints an error and saves nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `flag` | string | `""` | The feature id to set: sod_friends_and_family or roc_friends_and_family, in any case. Empty lists every feature instead of setting one; an id that is not one of those prints a line naming them and saves nothing. |
| `on` | bool |  | TRUE when the character holds the feature, FALSE when it does not. Needed with a flag; a word that is not a yes or no word leaves the feature as it is. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshFeatures[${Me.Name},sod_friends_and_family,TRUE]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:TravelMeshFeatures`

### `MeshGroup`

`OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshGroup[fw, zone, poi=""]`

Starts the same route as Mesh on this character, then sends it to the rest of the group as a console command, and each member plans its own route from where it stands, staggered so the group does not move as one. Addressed to more than one character each plans its own route and nothing is sent, and when this character cannot plan the route nothing is sent.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|


# OgreBotAPI.Util

## Members

### `Between`

`${OgreBotAPI.Util.Between[v,lo,hi]}`

TRUE when v is from lo to hi with both ends included, compared as whole numbers, so decimals are cut off before comparing. If lo is greater than hi the answer is always FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v` | int64 | `0` | The number to test. |
| `lo` | int64 | `0` | The lowest allowed value, included. |
| `hi` | int64 | `0` | The highest allowed value, included. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when lo &lt;= v &lt;= hi; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Between[${Me.Level},50,60]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Between`

### `BetweenFloat`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

### `FileExists`


### `RoundToNearest`

`${OgreBotAPI.Util.RoundToNearest[value,step,incBy]}`

Rounds a whole number to the nearest multiple of step, then adds incBy; an exact half rounds up, so 45 with step 10 gives 50 and 44 gives 40. 0 and negative values are rounded the same way, and a step below 1 is used as 1.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | int | `0` | The number to round. Decimals are cut off; 0 and negatives are kept. |
| `step` | int | `1` | Round to a multiple of this, for example 10. Anything below 1 is used as 1. |
| `incBy` | int | `0` | Added to the rounded result. |

**Returns:** int: the rounded value plus incBy.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.RoundToNearest[${Me.Level},10,0]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.RoundNumToNearestValue`

### `CheckResearch`

`OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearch[fw, forceReport=FALSE]`

Queues a look at the research (Knowledge) window, opening it first when it is not up, and echoes "Research: &lt;name> --> &lt;progress>." to the console. Without forceReport it echoes only when the research reads Complete.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `forceReport` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE echoes the progress whatever it says; FALSE echoes only when it is Complete. |


### `CheckResearchMaterials`

`OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearchMaterials[fw]`

Queues a pass over every Advancement, Companion, Mount, Tradeskill, Upgrade and General Research Material in your bags: each is examined and the first choice in the window it opens is picked, or the windows are closed with a console line when it has no eligible research. With none in the bags it echoes that and does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |


*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Research_Material_Check`

### `DelayedAction`

`OgreBotAPI.Util:DelayedAction[fw, delay, command...]`

Runs a console command after a delay on each character the for-who picks at the time of the call; the timer is dropped if that character zones before it fires. Give the command as one quoted argument (escape any comma inside it), and note that a bare number for the delay is milliseconds.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `delay` | string |  | How long to wait: a bare whole number is milliseconds, or add a unit - 500ms, 10s, 1.5s, 2m, 1h. Anything else (30x, "30 s", -5) echoes an error and nothing is armed. |
| `command...` | string |  | The command to run, quoted as one argument, for example "eq2execute sit". If it arrives in several pieces they are joined back with commas and a warning is echoed; an empty command echoes an error and nothing is armed. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Util:DelayedAction[igw:${Me.Name},10s,"eq2execute sit"]
```

### `OnScreenTimer`

`OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimer[fw, time=30, slot=1, message="Timer:", minUpdate=1]`

Shows a message with a live countdown in one of the ten on-screen timer slots, opening the on-screen display if it is closed; the line is removed 5 seconds after the countdown ends. A slot below 1 uses slot 1 and one above 10 uses slot 10, and a slot that was set less than minUpdate seconds ago silently keeps its old timer.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `time` | float | `30` | Seconds to count down from. Decimals are cut off. |
| `slot` | int | `1` | Which timer line to use, 1 to 10. A number outside is moved to the nearest of them. |
| `message` | string | `"Timer:"` | The text shown before the countdown. Empty uses "Timer:". |
| `minUpdate` | int | `1` | Seconds after this call during which a new timer for the same slot is refused. 0 allows an immediate replacement. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimer[igw:${Me.Name},45,2,"Adds in:",1]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:OnScreenTimer`

### `OnScreenTimerReset`

`OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimerReset[fw, slot=1]`

Clears one on-screen timer slot; the line disappears within a second. It does not lift the minUpdate hold of the timer it clears, so a new timer for that slot inside that time is still refused.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `slot` | int | `1` | Which timer line to clear, 1 to 10. A number outside is moved to the nearest of them. |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimerReset[igw:${Me.Name},2]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:OnScreenTimerReset`

# OgreBotAPI.Vars

## Members

### `Bool`

`${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Bool[name]}`

Reads the script variable name as a yes/no: TRUE only when its whole value is 1, true, yes or on in any case. A missing variable, an empty value or any other text (2, enabled, a value with spaces around it) reads FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The variable name, case-sensitive. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the stored value is a yes word; FALSE otherwise, including when the variable is missing.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Bool[UseCampSpot]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_Variable_Bool`

### `Exists`

`${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Exists[name]}`

TRUE when a variable called name is in this session's script variable store, even if its value is empty. Use it to tell a missing variable from an empty one, since Get returns an empty string for both.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The variable name, case-sensitive. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the variable is stored; FALSE when it is missing or name is blank.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Exists[PullCount]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_VariableExists`

### `Get`

`${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Get[name]}`

The value stored under name in this session's script variable store (set with OgreBotAPI.Vars:Set), or an empty string when there is no such variable. Names ignore case, and the store lives in memory on this session only: it is not shared with other characters, not saved, and lasts until it is cleared or the extension is unloaded.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The variable name; case does not matter. |

**Returns:** string: the stored value; empty when the variable is missing or was set to an empty value.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Get[PullCount]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_Variable`, `OgreBotAPI.Variables`

### `GetInternal`

`${OgreBotAPI.Vars.GetInternal[name]}`

The value stored under name in the internal variable store (set with OgreBotAPI.Vars:SetInternal), or an empty string when there is no such variable. It is a separate store from Get and Set but lives the same way: in memory on this session only, not shared, not saved; names ignore case.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The internal variable name; case does not matter. |

**Returns:** string: the stored value; empty when the variable is missing or was set to an empty value.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.GetInternal[LastZone]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_InternalVariable`, `OgreBotAPI.InternalVariables`

### `InternalExists`

`${OgreBotAPI.Vars.InternalExists[name]}`

TRUE when a variable called name is in this session's internal variable store, even if its value is empty. It only looks at the internal store, not the one Get and Set use.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The internal variable name, case-sensitive. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the internal variable is stored; FALSE when it is missing or name is blank.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.InternalExists[LastZone]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_InternalVariableExists`

# OgreBotAPI.Windows

## Members

### `CastingWindowVisible`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.CastingWindowVisible}`

Whether the game's casting bar is on screen. Always FALSE while you are not in the world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the casting bar is visible; FALSE when it is hidden or you are not in the world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.CastingWindowVisible}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.IsCastingWindowVisible`

### `ReplyExists`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.ReplyExists[text]}`

Which reply of the open reply dialog (the window a clicked item or object opens) contains the text, in any case. It answers a number, not TRUE/FALSE, so test it with > 0; it does not look at the NPC conversation window.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string |  | Text to look for inside each reply. Matches anywhere in the reply, any case. |

**Returns:** int: the 1-based number of the first reply that contains the text; 0 when no reply dialog is open, nothing matches, or the text is empty.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.ReplyExists[Yes]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ReplyDialog_ReplyExists`

### `RewardID`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardID[num|name,windowId]}`

The number of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name the same way AcceptReward picks it. A number past the window's reward count, a name that matches no row, an empty selection, or no reward window all answer 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num\|name` | number or text |  | The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing. |
| `windowId` | int | `0` | The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up). |

**Returns:** int: the 1-based reward number; 0 when there is no reward window or nothing matches.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardID[2,0]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardID`

### `RewardLinkID`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardLinkID[num|name,windowId]}`

The LinkID of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name the same way AcceptReward picks it. Empty when there is no reward window, nothing matches, or the game has no LinkID for that row.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num\|name` | number or text |  | The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing. |
| `windowId` | int | `0` | The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up). |

**Returns:** string: that reward's LinkID; empty when there is no window or no match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardLinkID[1,0]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardLinkID`

### `RewardName`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardName[num|name,windowId]}`

The item name of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name. Empty when there is no reward window, nothing matches, or the row does not read.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num\|name` | number or text |  | The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing. |
| `windowId` | int | `0` | The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up). |

**Returns:** string: that reward's item name; empty when there is no window or no match.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardName[1,0]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardName`

### `RewardWindowID`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardWindowID}`

The id of the active reward window: the oldest reward window the bot saw open that is still up, or with none held, the one open now. It reads 0 when no reward window is up.

**Returns:** int64: the active reward window's id; 0 when none is open or you are not in the world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardWindowID}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.RewardWindow_Get_WindowID`

### `SelectOption`

`${OgreBotAPI.Windows.SelectOption[n]}`

Which option of the open select window matches, without clicking anything and without printing anything, so a script may read it as often as it likes. Options count from 1 (OldBot's numbers were one higher).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search...` | number or text |  | The option to find: a number is that option's position; text must match the option name exactly (any case). Add -substring as another argument to match text anywhere in the name. |

**Returns:** int: the 1-based option position; 0 when no select window is open, nothing matches, or no argument is given.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.SelectOption[1]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.Select_Window_GetOption`

## Methods

### `AcceptNoChoiceReward`

`OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptNoChoiceReward[fw, windowId=0]`

Presses Receive on a reward window that offers no choice. It refuses, with a console line, a window that offers a choice, a 'New Quest!' offer, or a window whose reward pack is not shown.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `windowId` | int | `0` | The reward window id. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up). |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptNoChoiceReward[${Me.Name},0]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AcceptNoChoiceReward`

### `AcceptReward`

`OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptReward[fw, num|name=0, windowId=0]`

Takes a reward from a reward window: on a choice window it accepts the reward you name, and on a single or no-choice window it presses Receive whatever you pass, but never on a 'New Quest!' offer. Each outcome, including no window or no match, prints a line to the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `num\|name` | number or text | `0` | The reward to take on a choice window: its number (1 = the first) or its item name (any case). Ignored on a single-reward window. |
| `windowId` | int | `0` | The reward window id. 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up). |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptReward[${Me.Name},1,0]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:AcceptReward`, `Obj_OgreIH:AcceptReward`

### `Choice`

`OgreBotAPI.Windows:Choice[fw, option=1]`

Clicks one of the choice window's buttons: 1 is the first button, 2 the second. Another number is clamped to the nearer of the two, with a console line saying which it chose; does nothing when no choice window is open.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `option` | int | `1` | Which button to click: 1 or 2 (below 1 is 1, above 2 is 2). |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Windows:Choice[${Me.Name},1]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ChoiceWindow`

### `Select`

`OgreBotAPI.Windows:Select[fw, search...]`

Picks an option in the open select window and then presses its OK. The match happens at once but the clicks are queued: the option first, then OK about 0.3 seconds later; each pick and each miss prints a line to the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `search...` | number or text |  | The option to pick: a number is its position (1 = the first real option); text must match the option name exactly, any case. Flags may come before or after it as their own arguments: -substring (match text anywhere in the name), -test (click the option but not OK), -reportonly (say which option matches, click nothing) and -spew (list the options). |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Windows:Select[${Me.Name},1]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Select_Window`

# OgreBotAPI.Zone

## Members

### `CityRestrictions`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CityRestrictions}`

TRUE in one of the bot's 17 city zones, such as The City of Freeport or Qeynos Province District, unless Allow City Casting is ticked. FALSE out of world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE in a listed city with Allow City Casting unticked; FALSE otherwise or out of world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CityRestrictions}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.CityRestrictions`

### `CleanName`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CleanName[name]}`

The same cleaned name as Name, made safe for file and setting names: spaces become underscores and the characters , [ ] : ' and ` are removed. Reads "" out of world when no name is passed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | `${Zone.Name}` | a zone name to clean; blank means the zone you are in |

**Returns:** string: the cleaned zone name with underscores for spaces; "" out of world when no name is given.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CleanName}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.CleanZoneName`, `Ogre_Instance_Controller.CleanZoneName`

### `InGuildHall`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InGuildHall}`

TRUE when the zone's short name contains guildhall, except the Island of Mara Estate (guildhall_mara). FALSE out of world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE in a guild hall; FALSE elsewhere or out of world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InGuildHall}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.InGuildHallZone`, `Obj_OgreUtilities.InGuildHallZone`, `OgreBotAPI.InGuildHallZone`

### `InHouse`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouse}`

TRUE when you look to be inside a house: not in a guild hall, and a Magic Door to the Guild Hall or a market bulletin board is in the zone. It is a guess from those two objects; FALSE out of world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when either object is in the zone and it is not a guild hall; FALSE otherwise or out of world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouse}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.InHouseZone`, `OgreBotAPI.InHouseZone`

### `InHouseAccess`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouseAccess}`

TRUE in one of the eight zones the bot treats as house-access zones: Antonica, Halas, the two Qeynos zones, Timorous Deep, Greater Faydark, Neriak and Freeport. This is the outdoor zone, not the house itself; FALSE out of world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the zone's short name is antonica, halas, qeynos_combined01, qeynos_combined02, exp04_rgn_timorous_deep, exp03_rgn_greater_faydark, neriak or freeport_combined; FALSE otherwise or out of world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouseAccess}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.InHouseAccessZone`, `OgreBotAPI.InHouseAccessZone`

### `InInstance`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InInstance}`

TRUE when the zone name contains a [ (instances are named like that, such as [Heroic] or [Solo]) and you are not in a guild hall. FALSE out of world.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE in an instance; FALSE in an open zone, a guild hall, or out of world.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InInstance}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `GetInfoOb.InAInstance`, `OgreBotAPI.InInstance`

### `Name`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name[name]}`

The zone name with colour codes and the trailing instance number removed. Every trailing digit and space is stripped, so a name that really ends in a number loses it; "" out of world when no name is passed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | `${Zone.Name}` | a zone name to clean; blank means the zone you are in |

**Returns:** string: the cleaned zone name; "" out of world when no name is given.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ZoneName`

### `ResetReady`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetReady}`

TRUE once the Zone Reuse table has been read at least once and no re-read is asked for or running. Wait for it after ResetUpdateInfo before reading ResetZoneData.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the table is in and not being re-read; FALSE before the first read or while a re-read is pending.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetReady}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_IsReady`

### `ResetUpdating`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetUpdating}`

TRUE while a Zone Reuse re-read is asked for or running.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a re-read is pending or running; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetUpdating}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_IsUpdating`

### `ResetZoneData`

`${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetZoneData[zone,field]}`

One zone's entry from the Zone Reuse window, as last read by ResetUpdateInfo. A zone that is not in the table reads FALSE, and an unknown field prints a console line and reads FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | text |  | the zone name exactly as the Zone Reuse window shows it, any case |
| `field` | text |  | blank reads TRUE when the zone has an entry; otherwise ZoneName, IsSet (TRUE when its timer state is known), Resettable, TimeLeft (seconds) or TextTimeLeft |

**Returns:** bool, int64 or string by field: TRUE/FALSE for blank, IsSet and Resettable; seconds for TimeLeft; text for ZoneName and TextTimeLeft. FALSE when the zone is not in the table.

```text
echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetZoneData["${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}",Resettable]}
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_Get_ZoneData`

## Methods

### `ChampionsResetter`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChampionsResetter[fw, zone]`

Resets one zone with your Champion's Zone Lockout Reset item: examines it, then picks the zone in the window it opens. Prints a console line when the item is not in your bags, is on cooldown, or does not list the zone.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `zone` | text |  | the zone name as the item's window lists it |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChampionsResetter[${Me.Name},"${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}"]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Champions_Zone_Resetter`

### `ChangeZoneTo`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChangeZoneTo[fw, toWho]`

When the group member is in another instance of your zone, sends the game's /zone_to_group_member_zone command for them on this character. A name that is not in your group or a different zone prints a console line; nothing happens when they share your instance.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `toWho` | character name |  | the group member whose instance to join |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChangeZoneTo[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ChangeZoneTo`, `Obj_OgreIH:ChangeZoneTo`

### `ForceReset`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ForceReset[fw, zone]`

Presses Force Reset in the Zone Reuse window for one named zone, which uses up one of your limited force-reset charges. A blank zone prints a console line and does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `zone` | text |  | the zone name as the Zone Reuse window shows it |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Zone:ForceReset[${Me.Name},"${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}"]
```

### `ResetAll`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ResetAll[fw, allowRaid=FALSE]`

Runs the game's reset_all_zone_timers command on each matching character. In a raid it does nothing unless allowRaid is TRUE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |
| `allowRaid` | bool | `FALSE` | TRUE to reset even while in a raid |

```text
OgreBotAPI.Zone:ResetAll[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:ZoneResetAll`

### `ResetUpdateInfo`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ResetUpdateInfo[fw]`

Asks the bot to re-read the Zone Reuse window, which it opens and closes to do so. Asking again while a re-read is pending does nothing extra; ResetUpdating and ResetReady follow it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text

```

### `ResetZone`

### `ShareQuestsForZone`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:ShareQuestsForZone[fw, zone=""]`

Shares, one at a time after the group has gathered, the Hot Zones missions in your journal that belong to this zone. It works only while you are in that zone, and with for-who all only the group leader shares.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

### `SpecialZoneSpecific`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:SpecialZoneSpecific[fw]`

The Special button: in zones with a known puzzle it clicks the puzzle object in reach (a clock, door, brazier, rope, zip line or orb) or hands the press to that zone's fight. Anywhere else it double-clicks the nearest interactable object of a special type.

### `Zone`

`OgreBotAPI.Zone:Zone[fw]`

Double-clicks the nearest zone exit on each matching character: an object named with exit, else with zone_, else the nearest door, else a NoKill NPC within 30 meters. Does nothing in a guild hall.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw` | for-who |  | [for-who](ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names |

```text

```

*Was (OldBot):* `OgreBotAPI:Zone`
