# ISXOgreEQ2

## Members

### `AbilityDetails`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails}`

The AbilityDetails sub-object: the Ability Details window, which opens through OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AbilityDetails, not through this object. :Close closes it (ogre end abilitydetails) and :UI is the window's own click channel, which does nothing without its one argument.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails](AbilityDetails.md)

**Returns:** object: the AbilityDetails sub-object; it always exists, has no members, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails}
```

### `AbilityEfficiency`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency}`

The AbilityEfficiency sub-object behind ogre ae: :Run with no argument writes a per-ability efficiency report from your ability export to OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityEfficiency/&lt;name>_&lt;class>_&lt;server>_AbilityEfficiency.txt, and :Run[-h] or :Run[help] prints the usage. Any other word is refused; it is a one-shot with no members.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency](AbilityEfficiency.md)

**Returns:** object: the AbilityEfficiency sub-object; it always exists, has no members, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency}
```

### `AbilityUpgrades`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades}`

The AbilityUpgrades sub-object behind ogre oau: :Run[minLevel] reports which Scroll Depot scrolls would upgrade an ability you know, from the given minimum scroll level (a default when left out), and :Run[-h] prints the usage. It only reports, buys nothing, and has no members.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades](AbilityUpgrades.md)

**Returns:** object: the AbilityUpgrades sub-object; it always exists, has no members, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades}
```

### `Analysis`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis}`

The Analysis sub-object behind ogre analysis: watches actors, records what changes and when, and scans a zone for actors that match. Its methods are :Open, :Close, :End, :Status, :Demo, :Rate, :Taps, :Monitor, :Scan, :Sessions, :Export, :Import and the panel's :UI, and it has no members.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis](Analysis.md)

**Returns:** object: the Analysis sub-object; it always exists, has no members, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis}
```

### `AntiAfk`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk}`

The AntiAfk sub-object behind ogre afk: :On[1\|0] starts a /who at random long intervals so the character is not idle (1 silent, 0 with messages, nothing keeps the current setting) and :Off stops it. :Invites[on\|off] is a separate switch that auto-accepts group invites from characters on your own accounts, :Help prints the usage, and it has no members.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk](AntiAfk.md)

**Returns:** object: the AntiAfk sub-object; it always exists, has no members, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk.

### `Auth`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth}`

**Returns:** object: the Auth sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth}
```

### `AutoLogin`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.AutoLogin}`

The auto-login settings window: :Open / :Close / :Toggle show it, and the window's own buttons save, delete or start login profiles and make desktop shortcuts for them. Echoing the object prints ISXOgreEQ2.AutoLogin.

### `BgRender`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender}`

The BgRender sub-object behind ogre bgrender: while this client is not the foreground window it skips the game's drawing except once a second and caps the background loop, so a background session uses much less CPU and GPU while the bot, the network and scripts keep running. It is off when the extension loads and never skips while you are logging in, zoning, camping or at character select.

All of it: [ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender](BgRender.md)

**Returns:** object: the BgRender sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender}
```

### `BuildHash`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BuildHash}`

The fingerprint of the ISXOgreEQ2 file this session loaded: the SHA-256 of its code section as 64 hex characters, the same value the session log's first adapter line shows. Two sessions that show the same value run the same build.

**Returns:** string: 64 hex characters, or NULL if the file could not be read

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BuildHash}
```

### `Chat`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat}`

# ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails

## Methods

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails:Close`

Closes the Ability Details window (the same as `ogre end abilitydetails`) and drops any clicks it had not acted on yet. The window is opened with OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AbilityDetails.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityDetails:Close
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency:Run[-h]`

Scores every ability in your loaded ability export as the damage in its description divided by cast plus recovery time (recast is not counted), writes one Name\|Value line per ability best first to Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityEfficiency/&lt;name>_&lt;subclass>_&lt;server>_AbilityEfficiency.txt and prints the top 20 (the same as `ogre ae`). With no export loaded it prints an error telling you to run `ogre export`, and any argument other than a help word is refused.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h` | switch |  | print the usage instead of running (-help, --help, ? and help work too) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityEfficiency:Run
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades

## Methods

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades:Run[minLevel]`

With a container window open it reads that one and leaves it open; otherwise it opens each Scroll Depot within 30 units in turn, reads it and closes it, and either way reports which spell scrolls upgrade an ability you already know, both in your console and to your other sessions through the Ogre console with your name in front (the same as `ogre oau`). It is queued, scribes or uses nothing, and is refused with a console line when you are not in the world, no ability export is loaded, a scan is already running or the level is not a whole number from 1 to 1000.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLevel` | int | `121` | ignore scrolls below this level (1 to 1000); -h prints the usage instead |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AbilityUpgrades:Run[125]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis

## Methods

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Close`

Closes the window and leaves everything running. :End stops it too.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Close
```

### `Demo`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Demo`

Fills the window with sample data and opens it, for looking at the layout. Nothing is saved.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Demo
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:End`

Turns the monitor and the taps off, drops a scan in progress, a + Cursor countdown and the spawn watch, and closes the window, the same as `ogre end analysis` and the window's X. What was recorded stays.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:End
```

### `Export`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Export[name]`

Saves the monitored actors and scan results to a file and says where.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The file name. Optional: with none it is session_ and the date and time. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Export["My Run"]
```

### `Import`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Import[name]`

Loads a saved session, replacing what is in memory and stopping live monitoring. With no name, or one that cannot be read, it prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | A session name from :Sessions, or a path; required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Import["My Run"]
```

### `Monitor`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Monitor[word,actor]`

The monitor: starts or stops sampling, empties or prints the list, or adds or removes an actor. With no word, or another word, it prints one warning listing the words.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | string |  | on and off start and stop sampling, clear empties the list, list prints it, add and remove take an actor; required. |
| `actor` | string |  | For add and remove: an actor id, or target or cursor for the actor you have targeted or are pointing at. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Monitor[add,target]
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Open`

Opens the Analysis window, the same as bare `ogre analysis`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Open
```

### `Rate`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Rate[ms]`

Sets how often monitored actors are sampled. A value outside 100 to 10000, or none, prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int |  | Milliseconds between samples, 100 to 10000; the default is 250; required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Rate[500]
```

### `Scan`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Scan[terms]`

Snapshots the actors that match, reusing the window's terms if you give none; with none there either it scans the whole zone. It refuses to start while a scan runs or out of the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terms` | string |  | Terms like Level>120: a member, then =, &lt; or >, then a value, one argument each; a term that does not read that way prints a warning and is skipped. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Scan["Level>120"]
```

### `Sessions`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Sessions`

Prints the names of the saved sessions to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Sessions
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Status`

Prints the monitor, taps, scan and sample counters to the console, with the last error if there is one.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Status
```

### `Taps`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Taps[state]`

Turns the passive event logs on or off and prints the status.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string |  | on or off. Optional: anything but off, or nothing, turns it on. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Analysis:Taps[on]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk

## Methods

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Help`

Prints the `ogre afk` usage lines to the console. It changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Help
```

### `Invites`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Invites[state]`

Turns automatic acceptance of group invites on or off: an invite is accepted from any name on your characters list (every account, auth-only names included), a switch separate from the keepalive that starts off at every load. A missing value is refused with a warning and nothing changes.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string |  | on, 1 or TRUE to accept; off, 0 or FALSE to stop |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Invites[on]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Off`

Stops the keepalive /who and prints "anti-AFK keepalive OFF" to the console (the same as `ogre end afk`). The group-invite switch set by AntiAfk:Invites is left as it is.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:On[silent]`

Starts the keepalive, which sends `/who all <your name>` to the game right away and then again after a random 10 to 15 minutes, only while you are in the world, until AntiAfk:Off or the extension unloads. Calling it while it is already on changes only the verbosity, and any other value is refused with an error and the usage.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `silent` | string |  | 1 or TRUE for silent; 0 or FALSE to also print "Ogre Anti AFK" to the console each time; leave out to keep the current setting (silent until changed) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.AntiAfk:On[1]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Auth

## Members

### `AccessLevel`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.AccessLevel}`

The access level text the Ogre login reported for this account. If the login did not send one, it reads a fixed default value.

**Returns:** string: the account's access level as text; a fixed default value when the login did not send one.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.AccessLevel}
```

### `AccessLevelNum`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.AccessLevelNum}`

The account's access level as a number, as the Ogre login reported it. It reads -1 when the login sent no number.

**Returns:** int: the account's access level number; -1 when the login sent no number.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.AccessLevelNum}
```

### `Authorized`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.Authorized}`

Whether this session's Ogre login was accepted. In normal use it reads TRUE, because the extension does not stay loaded without an accepted login.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when this session's Ogre login was accepted; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.Authorized}
```

### `RelayGroup`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.RelayGroup}`

The relay group this session sends its relays to right now - ogre_everquest2 unless the Relay Groups tab sets another. It is the same value the bot's own relays use, so it follows a change on that tab at once.

**Returns:** string: the current relay group name.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.RelayGroup}
```

### `Username`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.Username}`

The Ogre account username this session logged in with. Empty when the login sent no username.

**Returns:** string: the Ogre account username; empty when none was sent.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Auth.Username}
```

## Methods

### `Spew`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Auth:Spew`

Prints one line to the console with this session's Ogre username, whether its login was accepted, its access level text and number, and the relay group it sends to.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Auth:Spew
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender

## Members

### `Enabled`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Enabled}`

Whether background render skipping is turned on (ogre bgrender on). On does not mean it is skipping right now - see Skipping.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE after :On, FALSE after :Off and when the extension loads.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Enabled}
```

### `Held`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Held[name]}`

Whether a hold stops BgRender from skipping draws. With no name it asks whether any hold is in place; with a name, whether that one is.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `""` | the hold to ask about; leave it out to ask whether any hold is in place |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when that hold (or any hold) is in place.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Held[Crafting]}
```

### `Holds`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Holds}`

How many holds are in place. BgRender skips draws only while this is 0.

**Returns:** int: the number of distinct holds.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Holds}
```

### `Skipping`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Skipping}`

Whether BgRender is skipping draws at this moment: it is on, nothing holds it, your character is settled in the world, and this client is in the background (or Force is on).

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while draws are being skipped; FALSE while every frame is drawn.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender.Skipping}
```

## Methods

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Clear`

Removes every hold, whoever added it.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Clear
```

### `Draw`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Draw[ms]`

Sets how often a background client still draws one frame, so its window or thumbnail keeps updating. Values are held between 0 and 60000.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int | `1000` | milliseconds between background draws; 0 never draws while in the background |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Draw[1000]
```

### `Force`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Force[onoff]`

Treats this client as a background one even while it is the foreground window, so you can watch the effect on the window in front of you. For testing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onoff` | string | `off` | on or off (also TRUE / FALSE or 1 / 0) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Force[on]
```

### `Hold`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Hold[name]`

Adds a named hold: while any hold is in place every frame is drawn, as if BgRender were off. Use it around anything that needs the screen drawn and release the same name after; holding a name twice is one hold.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | your hold's name - any text; each caller releases only its own name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Hold[Crafting]
```

### `Hz`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Hz[n]`

Sets the most loops per second a background client runs while it is skipping draws, so a loop with no draw cannot spin a core. The bot runs once per loop, so a low value also slows the bot.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int | `100` | loops per second, held between 0 and 1000; 0 is no cap |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Hz[100]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Off`

Turns background render skipping off (`ogre end bgrender`): every frame is drawn again. The hook stays installed but does nothing until :On.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:On`

Turns background render skipping on and prints the status; while this client is the foreground window every frame is still drawn. The first time, it finds and hooks the game's draw function, and if that fails (for example after a game patch) it says why and stays off.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:On
```

### `Release`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Release[name]`

Removes the named hold; when no hold is left, BgRender may skip draws again. Releasing a name that is not held does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the hold to remove |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Release[Crafting]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Status`

Prints BgRender's state (`ogre bgrender`): on or off, the draw interval and loop cap, whether the draw hook is installed, whether it is skipping now and if not why (off, held, world not settled, foreground), the holds, and the last second's loop, draw and skip counts.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.BgRender:Status
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Chat

## Members

### `Hits`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Hits}`

Total times a filtered chat listener matched a line and ran, since the extension loaded. Listeners that receive every line are not counted here.

**Returns:** int64: filtered-listener matches since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Hits}
```

### `Lines`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Lines}`

Total lines handed to the extension's chat listeners since it loaded: every chat-channel line, game text line and announcement, injected lines included. A read-only counter that only goes up.

**Returns:** int64: lines passed to the chat listeners since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Lines}
```

### `Matchers`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Matchers}`

How many registered chat listeners are filtered - they run only when a line matches their pattern.

**Returns:** int: current filtered listener count

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Matchers}
```

### `RawSubs`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.RawSubs}`

How many registered chat listeners receive every line and do their own parsing.

**Returns:** int: current every-line listener count

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.RawSubs}
```

### `SeenAnnounce`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenAnnounce}`

Announcements received since the extension loaded (EQ2's announcement event).

**Returns:** int64: announcements received since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenAnnounce}
```

### `SeenChat`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenChat}`

Chat-channel lines received since the extension loaded (EQ2's incoming chat text event). Lines injected through OgreBotAPI.Comms:InjectChat are counted here too, once processed on the next pulse.

**Returns:** int64: chat-channel lines received since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenChat}
```

### `SeenText`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenText}`

Game text lines received since the extension loaded (EQ2's incoming text event: system messages, combat text and other text the game prints).

**Returns:** int64: game text lines received since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.SeenText}
```

### `Subscribers`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Subscribers}`

How many chat listeners are registered inside the extension right now: the every-line listeners plus the filtered ones (RawSubs + Matchers).

**Returns:** int: current listener count, RawSubs plus Matchers

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.Subscribers}
```

### `TellReceived`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.TellReceived}`

Tells addressed to you since the extension loaded. Each one also fires the OgreEvent_InGameTell event.

**Returns:** int64: tells received since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.TellReceived}
```

### `TellSent`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.TellSent}`

Tells you sent since the extension loaded. Each one also fires the OgreEvent_InGameTellSent event.

**Returns:** int64: tells sent since the extension loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Chat.TellSent}
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Class

## Members

### `Archetype`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Archetype}`

The local character's archetype in lowercase: fighter, priest, mage or scout. It is read from the game the first time it is asked for once in world and refreshed on every zone load; it is empty before any character has been read, and a ChangeValue override does not change it (only Is does).

**Returns:** string: fighter, priest, mage or scout; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Archetype}
```

### `AscensionClass`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.AscensionClass}`

The local character's ascension class: Thaumaturgist, Elementalist, Etherealist or Geomancer, in that capitalisation. Empty when the character has no ascension class or none of those names is found in the game's ascension label.

**Returns:** string: Thaumaturgist, Elementalist, Etherealist or Geomancer; empty when none is found

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.AscensionClass}
```

### `ClassTier`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.ClassTier}`

The local character's class grouping, the level between archetype and subclass, in lowercase: warrior, crusader, brawler, cleric, druid, shaman, shaper, sorcerer, enchanter, summoner, bard, rogue, predator or animalist. Empty before any character has been read.

**Returns:** string: the lowercase class grouping; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.ClassTier}
```

### `HasEpic2`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.HasEpic2}`

TRUE for a ranger who owns the ranger epic 2.0 ability, FALSE otherwise. The buff is hidden and kept up, so owning it is taken to mean it is on.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the character is a ranger who owns the epic 2.0 ability; FALSE otherwise

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.HasEpic2}
```

### `Is`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Is[name]}`

TRUE when name matches the local character's archetype, class grouping or class, case-insensitive, with an optional leading Is ignored, so Is[Scout], Is[predator] and Is[IsRanger] all answer TRUE for a ranger. A value forced with ChangeValue for that name wins over the real class, and no argument returns FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | An archetype, class grouping or class name, optionally prefixed with Is (fighter, crusader, paladin, IsPaladin) |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the name matches the character (or a ChangeValue override for it is TRUE); FALSE otherwise or when no name is given

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Is[templar]}
```

### `OnBGServer`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnBGServer}`

TRUE when the current server is the Battlegrounds server. The server name match is case-insensitive.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE on Battlegrounds; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnBGServer}
```

### `OnKaladimServer`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnKaladimServer}`

TRUE when the current server is Kaladim. Kaladim also counts as TLE, so OnTLEServer is TRUE there too.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE on Kaladim; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnKaladimServer}
```

### `OnTLEServer`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnTLEServer}`

TRUE when the current server is a Time Locked Expansion server: Kaladim, Varsoon, Fallen Gate, Stormhold, Deathtoll, Zarrakon or Wuoshi. The server is read with the class identity (first read and every zone load) and again by UpdateServer.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE on one of the listed TLE servers; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnTLEServer}
```

### `OnVarsoonServer`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnVarsoonServer}`

TRUE when the current server is Varsoon. Varsoon also counts as TLE, so OnTLEServer is TRUE there too.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE on Varsoon; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnVarsoonServer}
```

### `Ruleset`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Ruleset}`

The current server's ruleset as one word: Battlegrounds, TLE or Live. Any server not on the TLE or Battlegrounds list answers Live, including before the server has been read.

**Returns:** string: Battlegrounds, TLE or Live

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Ruleset}
```

### `Subclass`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Subclass}`

The local character's final class in lowercase, such as templar, ranger or shadowknight (one of the 26 classes). Empty before any character has been read.

**Returns:** string: the lowercase class name; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Subclass}
```

### `WaterBreathingAbility`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.WaterBreathingAbility}`

The name of the group water-breathing ability the bot uses for the local character's class: Water Spirit for a mystic, Abominus for a defiler. Every other class, channeler included, answers empty.

**Returns:** string: Water Spirit, Abominus, or empty for every other class

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.WaterBreathingAbility}
```

## Methods

### `ChangeValue`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Class:ChangeValue[member,value]`

Forces Is[member] to answer value for the local character, so ChangeValue[IsFighter,TRUE] makes a non-fighter run fighter logic, and auto removes the override so it reads what the game says again; it lasts across zones until set again or a different character is read. A missing argument, a member that is not an archetype, class or subclass, or a value that is not TRUE, FALSE or auto prints one line and stores nothing, the same line as OgreBotAPI.Roster:SetClassValue.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `member` | string |  | The class name to force, with or without a leading Is (IsFighter, fighter, IsTemplar): an archetype, class or subclass |
| `value` | string |  | TRUE or FALSE (also 1/0, yes/no, on/off) to force it, or auto to remove the override |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Class:ChangeValue[IsFighter,TRUE]
```

### `Update`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Class:Update`

Re-reads the local character's name, class, ascension class and server from the game right away; out of world the read is held and happens on the first Class read once in world. ChangeValue overrides survive for the same character but are dropped when a different character is read, and a console line says so whenever the identity changes.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Class:Update
```

### `UpdateServer`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Class:UpdateServer`

Re-reads the server name now and resets OnTLEServer, OnKaladimServer, OnVarsoonServer, OnBGServer and Ruleset from it. Class values are not touched.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Class:UpdateServer
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Codex

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:End`

Stops a running Codex inspect pass: drops the names still waiting, closes the inspect window and prints how many were not inspected - the same as ogre end codexinspect. Players already uploaded keep their cooldown; with no pass running it does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:End
```

### `Inspect`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Inspect[names,setting]`

Queues the named players to be inspected one at a time, 3 s apart, each one an inspect request to the game server (a server request), and each uploaded to Codex as an active raid member - the same as ogre codexinspect. A name inspected in the last 5 minutes (by default) is skipped, reset clears the active raid roster on Codex, status (or ?) or no argument prints the status line, and the console says how many were queued.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | string |  | a comma-separated list of player names, or reset, or status / ? |
| `setting` | string | `""` | optional; leave it out |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Inspect[status]
```

### `Toon`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Toon[word]`

Inspects your own character and uploads its snapshot to Codex - the same as ogre codextoon: it sends the game an inspect request for you (a server request), then uploads over the web and prints the result when the upload answers. With status (or ?) it only prints the Codex status line, and it refuses with a message when Codex is not set up, you are not in the world, or an upload is already running.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | string | `""` | status or ? prints the Codex status line instead of uploading; leave it out to upload |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Toon[status]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Collection

## Members

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Running}`

TRUE while an `ogre cm` collection run is in progress, from the depot or from your bags. Starting another while one runs is refused with a busy warning.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a collection run is going; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Running}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Status}`

Progress of the running collection run, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection}` returns.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "cm (done/total, n added)" for a depot run or "cm -inventory (done/total, n added)" for a bag scan.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Status}
```

## Methods

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Run[flags...]`

The engine behind `ogre cm`: opens the collectible depot within 10 m, turns Hide Grey on, then withdraws each listed piece one at a time, examines it and clicks the quest journal's Add button; the final result line goes to OgreConsole prefixed with your name. With -inventory it scans your bags instead and MAKES A SERVER CALL PER ITEM (`.ToItemInfo.IsCollectible` and `.AlreadyCollected`, waiting up to 5 s for each item's info), so it is slow.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string |  | none = the nearest depot whose name contains Collectible Depot, else a Personal Collectible Stash; -small = exactly Collectible Depot; -large = exactly Collectible Depot (Large) (a named depot that is not found refuses the call); -inventory (also 1 or -1) scans your bags instead; unknown words are ignored |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Run[-large]
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Stop`

Stops a running collection run, closes the depot window if it is open and prints "cm: stopped.". Does nothing when idle.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:End`

Closes the Content Builder window (the same as `ogre end contentbuilder` and the window's X). Changes that were not saved are kept and offered back the next time the window opens, and a run it started goes on.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:End
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:Open[tier,path]`

Opens the Content Builder window (the same as `ogre contentbuilder`), on a zone file when you name one. A window that is already open comes to the front, and asks before it opens that file over unsaved changes; without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tier` | string | `none` | The root the zone file is in: default or custom. Leave both out to open the window as it was. |
| `path` | string | `none` | The zone file's path inside that root, ending in .json. A path with spaces may be quoted or written as several words. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:Open[custom,"My_Zone.json"]
```

More: [developer/zone-files/builder.md](../../zone-files/builder.md)

# ISXOgreEQ2.Craft

## Members

### `Crafted`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Crafted}`

How many crafts the current queue has made: a writ or loop run crafts queue after queue, and this counts the one crafting now. Once nothing is running it reads the count from the last queue that ran, so a finished run does not drop to 0.

**Returns:** int: crafts made so far in the current queue, or in the last queue once idle; 0 before any run.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Crafted}
```

### `CraftTotal`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.CraftTotal}`

How many crafts the current queue plans to make: a writ or loop run crafts queue after queue, so this is one queue's total, not the whole run's. Once nothing is running it reads the total of the last queue that ran.

**Returns:** int: the planned craft count of the current queue, or of the last queue once idle; 0 before any run.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.CraftTotal}
```

### `Details`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Details}`

The whole crafting picture as one JSON string: running, paused, flow, stage, status, crafted, craftTotal, recipe, row, rows, lastError, and short (a list of name / need / have / fuel for what the latest resource count came up short on). recipe is "" and row / rows are 0 when no queue row is being crafted.

**Returns:** string: a JSON object with the fields listed above.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Details}
```

### `Flow`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Flow}`

Which crafting run is going: idle, queue, writs, autotinkering, lowlevelleveling or quest. It goes back to idle when the run finishes.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "queue", "writs", "autotinkering", "lowlevelleveling" or "quest".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Flow}
```

### `IsReady`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.IsReady}`

Whether the crafting engine has started up, which happens on its first pulse after the extension loads. It does not mean the recipe book has been read - see ScanActive and QueueUpdated.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE once the crafting engine has started; FALSE before that.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.IsReady}
```

### `LastError`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastError}`

The last refusal or failure the crafting engine reported, the same line the panel shows in red. It is cleared only when a run passes its start checks.

**Returns:** string: the last error or refusal text; "" when there has been none since the last good start.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastError}
```

### `LastScribedRecipeId`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeId}`

The recipe id of the recipe you scribed most recently, by this engine or by hand, filled in when the recipe book is read again after the game's "put in recipe book" message, so it lags the name briefly. If that name is not found in the re-read book the id keeps the previous recipe's, so it can disagree with LastScribedRecipeName.

**Returns:** int64: the last scribed recipe's id; 0 when none has been seen since the extension loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeId}
```

### `LastScribedRecipeName`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeName}`

The name of the recipe you scribed most recently, by this engine or by hand, taken from the game's "put in recipe book" message.

**Returns:** string: the last scribed recipe's name; "" when none has been seen since the extension loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeName}
```

### `Lite`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Lite}`

Whether craft lite is on - the reaction engine that casts the crafting reaction arts during a craft, also for crafts you start by hand. Opening the panel or starting any run turns it on.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when craft lite (crafting reactions) is on; FALSE when it is off.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Lite}
```

### `MissingResources`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.MissingResources}`

Whether the latest queue's resource count came up short of something it needs. It stays set after the run ends and resets when the next count starts; Details lists what is short.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the latest resource count was short; FALSE before any count and when nothing was short.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.MissingResources}
```

### `NavigationDetails`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}`

The most recent navigation request as a JSON string, the same payload OgreCraft_NavigationRequired passes: requestID, action, category, key, displayName, customNamedPoint, precision, zone, characterName, targetFound, and targetID / targetName / targetX / targetY / targetZ / targetDistance when the target was found. It keeps the last request after it is answered and is "" before the first one.

**Returns:** string: the last navigation request's JSON; "" when no request has been made since the extension loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}
```

### `Paused`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Paused}`

Whether the crafting pause is on. A pause turned on with no run going still reads TRUE but holds nothing, and the next start clears it.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the crafting pause is on; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Paused}
```

### `QueueUpdated`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.QueueUpdated}`

Whether every recipe add and queue load you asked for has landed in the setup queue. An add or load asked while the recipe book is still being read waits for the read, and this is FALSE until it lands.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when no add or queue load is waiting for the recipe book; FALSE while one waits.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.QueueUpdated}
```

### `Recipes`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Recipes}`

How many recipes the engine has indexed from your recipe book. It is 0 until the book has been read; a read starts when a run starts, when you scribe a recipe or on Scan, and also when the panel opens or craft lite turns on unless Do NOT load recipes on startup is ticked.

**Returns:** int: the number of recipes indexed by the last recipe-book read; 0 before the first read.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Recipes}
```

### `RecipesInQueue`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.RecipesInQueue}`

How many recipe rows are in the setup queue (the queue Start crafts). It counts rows, not the quantity to craft.

**Returns:** int: the number of rows in the setup queue; 0 when it is empty.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.RecipesInQueue}
```

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Running}`

Whether a crafting run is going: a setup-queue run, writs, auto tinkering, low level leveling or quest crafting. A paused run still counts as running.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while any crafting run is going (paused or not); FALSE when crafting is idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Running}
```

### `ScanActive`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.ScanActive}`

Whether the engine is reading your recipe book right now. Runs wait for the read to finish before they resolve any recipe.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while the recipe book is being read; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.ScanActive}
```

### `Setting`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Setting[id]}`

One crafting panel setting, read by its id, as the raw stored text. An id that has never been saved returns "" (the built-in default is not filled in), and a call with no id returns NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | The panel setting id, such as slider_craft_writcount or checkbox_craft_useevents. |

**Returns:** string: the stored value of that setting; "" when it is not set.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Setting[slider_craft_writcount]}
```

### `Stage`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Stage}`

One word for what crafting is doing right now, such as countingResources, findingStation, walking, crafting, findingWrit, turningIn, buyingBooks or disposing. It reads idle when nothing is running.

**Returns:** string: the current stage word; "idle" when no run is going.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Stage}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Status}`

The crafting engine's status line, the same text the panel shows, such as "idle", "crafting &lt;recipe>", "scanning recipes", "paused" or "waiting for your navigation script (...)". A refused start does not change it - the reason is in LastError.

**Returns:** string: the current status text; "idle" when nothing is running.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Status}
```

### `WaitingForNavigation`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.WaitingForNavigation}`

Whether the crafting engine is waiting for your script to move the character, after it fired OgreCraft_NavigationRequired. This happens only with the "use events" setting (checkbox_craft_useevents) on; the wait has no time limit and Stop ends it.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a navigation request is waiting for CompleteNavigation or DeferNavigation; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.WaitingForNavigation}
```

## Methods

### `AddLastScribedRecipe`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[qty]`

Adds the recipe you last scribed this session (by the bot or by hand) to the craft setup queue, waiting for the recipe book to be read first when needed. With nothing scribed yet it prints a warning and adds nothing; it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qty` | int |  | How many to craft; left out, 0 or less it is 1. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[2]
```

### `AddRecipe`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipe[nameOrID|lastknownrecipe, qty]`

Adds a recipe to the craft setup queue by full name, by part of a name that matches only one recipe (4 letters or more), by recipe ID, or lastknownrecipe for the recipe last scribed this session; a recipe already queued gets the quantity added. A recipe not in your book prints a warning and adds nothing, an add made before the book is read waits for it, and this is OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddRecipe without the for-who.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nameOrID\|lastknownrecipe` | string |  | The recipe name, its ID (plain digits), or lastknownrecipe. A name may also be passed as several arguments; they are joined with spaces. |
| `qty` | int |  | How many to craft. Read only when it is the last of two or more arguments and a whole number; left out it is 1, and 0 or less becomes 1. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipe["Tempered Iron",2]
```

### `AddRecipeListFromFile`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipeListFromFile[file]`

Adds the recipes of one of your saved craft queues to the setup queue (the panel's Load Queue replaces it instead), warning about any recipe not in this character's book. The name is a queue in your queues folder, any path is cut off and a .json or .xml ending dropped, a missing name or file prints a warning, and a queue that needs the recipe book waits for the book to be read.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string |  | The saved queue's name, with or without .json, as saved from the craft panel; a folder in front of it is ignored. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipeListFromFile["MyQueue.json"]
```

### `BuyAllTinkeringRecipes`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes[]`

Buys every tinkering recipe book you do not already know or carry from Fizza Cogsworth, then scribes the ones your skill allows when the Scribe recipes setting is on. It is refused unless you carry at least 3 platinum, are in Steamfont Mountains and are within 10 meters of her, and also while a crafting flow or merchant errand is running (the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes).

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes
```

### `Catalog`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Catalog[]`

Prints how much the craft data files loaded: devices, universal devices, merchant types, recipe book series, conversions and partial conversions. The files are loaded first if they were not yet.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Catalog
```

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Clear[]`

Empties the craft setup queue, whether or not a flow is running, and prints setup queue cleared. Each row it drops fires OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated as a removed row, as a remove does.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Clear
```

### `CompleteNavigation`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation[]`

Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event (sent only when the craft setting to use events for movement is on) to say your script has moved the character; craft then takes the nearest station or NPC of the same name within 100 m and checks the distance again. If no request is waiting it prints a warning, and it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:CompleteNavigation.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation
```

### `DeferNavigation`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation[]`

Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event to say your script will not move the character, so craft walks there with its own movement. If no request is waiting it prints a warning, and it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:DeferNavigation.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:End[]`

Closes the craft window and ends all of crafting: the running flow, craft's own movement, a merchant errand, a summoned station, and craft lite. It is the same as ogre end craft and the window's X; use Stop to stop a run and keep the window.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:End
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Help[]`

Prints the ogre craft console words and their arguments to the console. It changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Help
```

### `Lite`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Lite`

Turns craft lite on, so the crafting reactions are cast for you during crafting rounds, and prints a console line when the state changes; turned on in the world with the recipe book not yet read, it also starts reading the book unless the "Do NOT load recipes on startup" setting is ticked. Opening the panel and starting any crafting flow turn it on as well.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Lite
```

### `LiteOff`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:LiteOff`

Turns craft lite off, so no crafting reactions are cast, drops any reaction waiting to be cast, and prints a console line when the state changes. Starting any crafting flow turns it back on.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:LiteOff
```

### `Minimize`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Minimize[]`

Rolls the craft window up to its header while crafting carries on; Open brings it back. With the window not open it does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Minimize
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Open`

Opens the crafting panel, or brings back a minimized one, and turns craft lite on - the same as a bare `ogre craft`. A panel that cannot open prints why and leaves craft as it was, and with the "Do NOT load recipes on startup" setting ticked an unread recipe book stays unread.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Open
```

### `Pause`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Pause[on|off]`

Pauses or resumes crafting: off resumes, and on, any other word or no argument pauses. A craft already begun finishes and nothing new starts while paused, and a pause made with no flow running is dropped when the next flow starts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on\|off` | string | `on` | off resumes; on, any other word, or nothing pauses. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Pause[on]
```

### `Queue`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Queue[]`

Prints each row of the craft setup queue to the console as quantity, recipe name and recipe ID, or setup queue is empty. It changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Queue
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Reload`

Writes any setting changed in the last second, then reloads the craft settings from disk and the craft data files (devices, merchants, recipe books and reaction arts), printing what the data files loaded.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Reload
```

### `Save`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Save`

Writes changed craft settings to disk now instead of waiting for the automatic save, and prints settings saved or settings NOT saved (saved also when nothing had changed and nothing was written). It refuses to write over a settings file that could not be read.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Save
```

### `Scan`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Scan`

Re-reads your recipe book from the start, opening the book so the client lists every recipe, and restarts a scan already in progress. Out of the world it does nothing and prints nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Scan
```

### `ScribeRecipe`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:ScribeRecipe[name|all=all]`

Scribes recipe scrolls from your bags one at a time, then opens and closes the tradeskill book so the new recipes are listed. A name scribes only scrolls whose full item name matches it in any case (a name with a comma arrives whole), nothing matching prints a line, and a call while scribing adds the new scrolls to the run (the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:ScribeRecipe).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name\|all` | string | `all` | The scroll's full item name in any case, or all for every scribeable scroll in your bags. Left empty it scribes all. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:ScribeRecipe[all]
```

### `Set`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Set[key,value]`

Changes one craft setting by its key and prints the new value; it is saved by itself about a second later. Both arguments are required, and a key that is not a craft setting (any case is accepted) prints a warning and saves nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | The setting's key, the panel control's id such as checkbox_craft_scriberecipes. |
| `value` | string |  | The new value, stored as given (TRUE or FALSE for a checkbox). |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Set[checkbox_craft_scriberecipes,TRUE]
```

### `Start`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Start`

Starts crafting the setup queue, the same as `ogre craft start` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:Start (without the for-who). It is refused with a console line and LastError when you are not in the world, a run is already going, or the setup queue is empty, and a refused start changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Start
```

### `StartLLL`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartLLL`

Starts low level leveling, a loop that crafts low-level recipes round after round and stops when your tradeskill level is 9, or 19 or higher - the same as `ogre craft lll` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartLLL. It is refused when you are not in the world or a run is already going.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartLLL
```

### `StartQuest`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartQuest[]`

Crafts the recipe steps of the quest selected in your journal, one of each per pass, until no craftable step is left; it keeps to that quest even if you select another one mid-run. It is refused when no quest is selected, a crafting flow is already running, or you are not in the world, and is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartQuest.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartQuest
```

### `StartTinker`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartTinker`

Starts auto tinkering, a loop that crafts tinkering recipes round after round and ends when you have no tinkering skill or it is at its maximum - the same as `ogre craft tinker` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartTinker. It is refused when you are not in the world or a run is already going.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartTinker
```

### `StartWrits`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartWrits`

Starts a writs (rush order) run for as many writs as the writ count setting (default 10), the same as `ogre craft writs` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartWrits. It is refused below tradeskill level 20, when you are not in the world, or when a run is already going.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartWrits
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Status[]`

Prints the crafting state to the console: craft lite on or off, the flow, the status text, crafted of total, the number of recipes read from your book, and the last error when there is one. It changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Stop`

Stops the running crafting run and drops a pause, printing "craft: stopping (Craft:Stop)." to the console, while the panel stays open (End closes it). With no run going it drops a pause and prints that nothing is running, the same as `ogre craft stop`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats

## Members

### `Keys`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Keys}`

The keys of the loaded lists, comma separated - each key is also the flag that picks that list in Get and Plan (the shipped ones are cd, ka, mm, pop and vov). Re-reads the list files first if any changed on disk.

**Returns:** string: the loaded list keys joined with ", "; "" when none loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Keys}
```

### `Lists`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Lists}`

How many crafting-mats lists are loaded: the shipped ones plus your own from OgreSave/EQ2/CraftingMats/custom. Reading it first re-reads the list files if any changed on disk; any load warnings are in Warnings, and Get, Plan and Reload print them.

**Returns:** int: number of loaded lists; 0 when no list files were found

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Lists}
```

### `Warnings`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Warnings}`

The warnings the last load of the list files produced, such as an unreadable file; Get, Plan and Reload also print them each time they run. Re-reads the list files first if any changed on disk.

**Returns:** string: the warnings joined with " \| "; "" when the load was clean

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Warnings}
```

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:End`

Stops a depot withdraw that a crafting-mats run started (only that one) and closes the editor window; unsaved edits are kept for the next Open. This is what `ogre end craftingmats` and the window's X do.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:End
```

### `Get`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Get[flags...]`

Works out the mats for the chosen lists and categories, prints any list-file warnings and the plan, then starts pulling them from the Harvesting Supply Depot and buying any fuel at the Guild Fuel Merchant on the pulse after the call returns (the same as `ogre craftingmats -<flags>`). No flags pulls the Visions of Vetrovia signature line; nothing is pulled when not in world, when another depot errand is running, or when only unknown words were given, and the run stops if no depot is within 11 of you.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string |  | Any mix, dash optional, any case: a list key (-vov, -cd, -mm, -pop, -ka or your own list's key), -sig / -s, -daily / -d, -weekly / -w, -plan to print only, help. A list with no category uses its own signature line (daily + weekly for Kunark's Ascending), a category with no list uses Visions of Vetrovia, and unknown words are ignored with one warning. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Get[-vov,-daily,-weekly]
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Help`

Prints the `ogre craftingmats` usage to the console: the list and category flags, the defaults, the script calls and where to put your own lists so updates never overwrite them.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Help
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Open`

Opens the Crafting Mats list editor window, where you change a list and save it to your own custom file (the same as bare `ogre craftingmats`). Calling it while the window is open changes nothing, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning instead.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Open
```

### `Plan`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Plan[flags...]`

Prints any list-file warnings and the shopping list Get would use - the mats to pull from the depot and the fuel to buy - and touches neither the depot nor the merchant. Takes the same flags as Get; no flags plans the Visions of Vetrovia signature line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string |  | Any mix, dash optional, any case: a list key (-vov, -cd, -mm, -pop, -ka or your own list's key), -sig / -s, -daily / -d, -weekly / -w, -plan to print only, help. A list with no category uses its own signature line (daily + weekly for Kunark's Ascending), a category with no list uses Visions of Vetrovia, and unknown words are ignored with one warning. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Plan[-ka]
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Reload`

Re-reads every list file from disk now, prints any warnings the load produced, then "craftingmats: reloaded -" with the list count and keys. Rarely needed: the lists are re-read by themselves whenever a list file changes.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Reload
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer

## Members

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Running}`

TRUE while a house-to-guild-hall, guild-hall-to-house or small-to-large depot transfer is running. Only one transfer runs at a time; starting another is refused with a busy warning.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a depot transfer is running; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Running}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Status}`

The running transfer's current depot type, its place in the list and how many withdrawals have been made, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer}` returns.

**Returns:** string: "idle", or "&lt;type> (n/total, k pulled)" where type is harvest, ammo, adorn, food, lore, potion, collectible, fuel or scroll.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Status}
```

## Methods

### `GHToHouse`

`ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:GHToHouse[flags...]`

The engine behind `ogre ghtohouse`: must start in your guild hall, then withdraws each chosen guild hall depot and deposits it into the matching personal house depot, travelling back and forth until that depot is empty (at most 40 trips per type). If a house depot says it cannot hold any more, the rest goes back into the guild hall depot and that type is skipped; each house depot must be within 8 m of where you arrive in the house.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string |  | -all (the eight shared depot types, not scroll), or any of -harvest/-h, -ammo, -adorn, -food, -lore, -potion, -collect/-collectible/-c, -fuel, each with a -no twin (-noharvest/-nh, -nocollect/-nocollectible/-nc, -nofuel ...); read left to right so `-all -nofuel` is all but fuel; a bare word is the house owner to enter (default your own name); an unknown flag is warned about and ignored; at least one depot type must end up selected or the call is refused; -scroll adds the scroll depot, which -all does not include |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:GHToHouse[-harvest,-scroll]
```

### `HouseToGH`

`ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:HouseToGH[flags...]`

The engine behind `ogre housetogh`: empties the chosen personal house depots into the matching guild hall depots, travelling between the guild hall and the house as often as needed (at most 40 trips per depot type), and pulling Superior Rune items one at a time. Started in the guild hall it first deposits what you carry there; each guild hall depot must be within 11 m of where you arrive, and a missing door or depot stops the run with a console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string |  | -all (the eight shared depot types, not scroll), or any of -harvest/-h, -ammo, -adorn, -food, -lore, -potion, -collect/-collectible/-c, -fuel, each with a -no twin (-noharvest/-nh, -nocollect/-nocollectible/-nc, -nofuel ...); read left to right so `-all -nofuel` is all but fuel; a bare word is the house owner to enter (default your own name); an unknown flag is warned about and ignored; at least one depot type must end up selected or the call is refused; -scroll is warned about as unknown here (there is no house scroll depot) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:HouseToGH[-all,-nofuel]
```

### `SmallToLarge`

`ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:SmallToLarge[flags...]`

The engine behind `ogre smalldepottobigdepot`: in your guild hall, withdraws one depot type from "&lt;type> Depot" and deposits it into "&lt;type> Depot (Large)" (within 11 m), repeating until the small depot is empty. It is refused outside a guild hall or for an unknown type; with the do-not-deposit option it fills your bags once and stops.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string | `-harvest` | one depot type: -harvest, -adorn/-adornment, -ammo, -scroll/-spell, -collectible/-collectable, -food/-drink, -fuel, -lore/-legend or -potion/-poison/-totem (the last one given wins); TRUE, 1 or -donotdeposit only fills your bags, FALSE or 0 turns that off again; any other word refuses the call |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:SmallToLarge[-adorn]
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:Stop`

Stops the running depot transfer and prints "depot transfer: stopped."; does nothing when idle. You stay where the transfer had got to, and items already withdrawn stay in your bags.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Det

## Members

### `DetrimentalInfo`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo[mainIconID,backdropIconID,-actorID,-maxEffects,field]}`

One field of a detrimental effect matched by its icon pair: on you (no -actorID, or your own ID) it reads the bot's detrimental tracker, which refreshes about every 500 ms, and for any other actor it walks that actor's effect list live, the first 10 effects unless -maxEffects says otherwise. Numeric fields (exists, id, mainiconid, backdropiconid, currentincrements, duration, maxduration, iseffectinfoavailable) come back as a number - 0 when not found, duration in whole seconds, and always 0 for duration on another actor - while any other field name (Name, Description, Type...) reads the game's effect info, a server request, and the read is NULL out of the world or with fewer than two arguments.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mainIconID` | int |  | the effect's MainIconID |
| `backdropIconID` | int |  | the effect's BackDropIconID |
| `-actorID` | switch | `0 (you)` | -actorID &lt;id>: read this actor's effects instead of yours |
| `-maxEffects` | switch | `10` | -maxEffects &lt;n>: how many of another actor's effects to walk; 0 walks them all; not used for you |
| `field` | string | `exists` | the field to return; the last word that is not a switch wins. A read changes nothing: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel is the way to cancel |

**Returns:** int64 or string: exists is 1 or 0; id, icon ids, currentincrements, duration and maxduration are numbers (0 when not found); any other field is a string (empty when not found).

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo[176,313,-actorID,${Target.ID},currentincrements]}
```

### `DetrimentalInfo_JSON`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo_JSON[mainIconID,backdropIconID,-actorID,-maxEffects,-ExtraFields]}`

A detrimental effect as JSON (ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration, MaxDuration): with no icon pair (or 0,0) a JSON array of every detrimental on you (or of another actor's first effects with -actorID), and with an icon pair that one effect as an object, {} when not found. The switches are read in any position and the first two other arguments are the icon pair; Duration and MaxDuration are always 0 for another actor, and the read is NULL out of the world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mainIconID` | int | `0` | the effect's MainIconID; 0 with backdropIconID 0 lists every effect |
| `backdropIconID` | int | `0` | the effect's BackDropIconID; with fewer than two icon arguments there is no pair (0,0) |
| `-actorID` | switch | `0 (you)` | -actorID &lt;id>: read this actor's effects instead of yours |
| `-maxEffects` | switch | `10` | -maxEffects &lt;n>: how many of another actor's effects to walk; 0 walks them all; not used for you |
| `-ExtraFields` | switch | `off` | -ExtraFields: add Name, Description, Type, UsesRemaining, NumEffectStrings and EffectStrings to a matched effect (a server request); not applied to the whole list |

**Returns:** string: a JSON array (every effect) or a JSON object (one matched effect, {} when not found).

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo_JSON}
```

## Methods

### `DetrimentalCacheClear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCacheClear`

Empties the bot's detrimental tracker, so its next scan sees every detrimental still on you as new. That fires OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded again for each of them and echoes a +det line for each.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCacheClear
```

### `DetrimentalCancel`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel[mainIconID,backdropIconID]`

Cancels the detrimental effect on you with this icon pair, immediately, and echoes a cancel line to the console when it finds it. It says nothing when no such effect is on you; OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelDetrimental is the same cancel with a for-who and a not-found message.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mainIconID` | int |  | the effect's MainIconID |
| `backdropIconID` | int |  | the effect's BackDropIconID |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel[176,313]
```

### `Dump`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Dump[mode,-noinfo]`

The `ogre dets` console dump: lists every detrimental on you from the tracker (dets, the default), your maintained spells and their targets (m), or your target's effects (target), one line each. By default it also reads each detrimental's Name and Description, a server request per effect, which -noinfo skips; out of the world it only prints a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `dets` | dets (or det, d), m (or maintained), target (or t); -h, -help or ? as the first word prints usage |
| `-noinfo` | switch | `off` | skip the Name and Description reads; -info turns them back on |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Dump[dets,-noinfo]
```

### `Set_DetrimentalScanTime`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Set_DetrimentalScanTime[ms]`

Sets how often, in milliseconds, the bot's detrimental tracker rescans your detrimentals (500 by default); every reader of the tracker sees the change. A value outside 100 to 5000 is refused with a console warning and the interval stays as it was, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int |  | the scan interval in milliseconds, 100 to 5000 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Set_DetrimentalScanTime[250]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter

## Members

### `ActiveCount`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.ActiveCount}`

The number of encounters that are setting up or running right now.

**Returns:** int: encounters in setup or active; 0 when none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.ActiveCount}
```

### `Current`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Current}`

The encounters setting up or running right now, as a JSON array. Each entry has primary (the first named mob), state ("setup" or "active"), named (every named mob), expansion and zone.

**Returns:** string: a JSON array of the active encounters; "[]" when none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Current}
```

### `IsActive`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.IsActive[mob]}`

Whether any loaded encounter naming that mob is setting up or running. The mob name is matched ignoring case, whatever zone you are in.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mob` | string |  | The named mob's name. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when that mob's encounter is in setup or active; FALSE when it is not, when no encounter owns that name, or when no name is given.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.IsActive[${Target.Name}]}
```

### `Loaded`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Loaded}`

The number of encounter files loaded, across every zone. It changes when a reload or a zone-in picks up new or edited files.

**Returns:** int: the number of loaded encounters.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Loaded}
```

### `Sequences`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Sequences}`

Every live encounter sequence as a JSON array, so you can see which step a fight is waiting on. Each entry names its encounter and holds either its condition rules or the list it is running (setup, a trigger and so on) with the current step.

**Returns:** string: a JSON array of live sequences; "[]" when none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Sequences}
```

### `Validation`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Validation}`

The answer of the last Encounter:Validate, as JSON: ok (true when the file would load), errors and warnings (how many), fileErrors and ruleErrors (the errors split: a file error stops the file from loading, a rule error does not), and issues - one for each line it printed, with the list, the rule and the step it belongs to (counted from 1), the message, and whether it is only a warning. Empty until Encounter:Validate has run.

**Returns:** string: JSON, for example {"ok":true,"errors":0,"warnings":0,"fileErrors":0,"ruleErrors":0,"issues":[]}; "" before the first Encounter:Validate.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Validation}
```

More: [developer/zone-files/builder.md](../../zone-files/builder.md)

## Methods

### `Debug`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Debug[switch,value]`

Turns the console echo of encounter messages (comms) or step changes (steps) on or off, then prints both settings; with no switch it only prints them - the same as `ogre encounter debug`. Both are always written to the log; an unknown switch or a missing on/off prints a warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switch` | string | `""` | comms or steps; blank just prints the current settings. |
| `value` | string | `""` | on or off; needed when switch is given. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Debug[steps,on]
```

### `Fire`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Fire[mob]`

Sets up for an encounter on the next pulse: the fight of the named mob given, or with no name the nearest or engaged named in this zone; a setup already running is started again. It is OgreBotAPI.Bot:SetUpFor without the for-who, and it is ignored with a warning when Enable Raid Setups (raid zones) or Enable Heroic Setups (other zones) is off, or when no encounter owns that name.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mob` | string | `""` | The named mob whose encounter to set up; blank picks the nearest or engaged named in this zone. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Fire[${Target.Name}]
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Help`

Prints the `ogre encounter` words (reload, debug and sequences) with one line each to the console, the same as typing a bare `ogre encounter`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Help
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:List`

Prints this zone's encounter coding to the console: one line per fight with its named mobs, (DISABLED) when switched off, and its file. It always answers, even "No encounter coding for this zone", and is OgreBotAPI.Encounter:List without the for-who.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:List
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Reload`

Re-reads every encounter file from disk in the background and swaps the new set in when it is done, which ends every encounter setup and sequence in progress - the same as `ogre encounter reload`. It prints one line at once and a second with the loaded, scanned and error counts when the swap lands.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Reload
```

### `Sequences`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Sequences`

Prints the Sequences JSON to the console, or "(none live)" when nothing is running - the same as `ogre encounter sequences`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Sequences
```

### `Validate`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Validate[root,path]`

Checks one fight file by the same rules the game uses when it loads fight files, and changes nothing: a file on disk by its root and path (the same as `ogre encounter validate`), or the base64 text of a fight file's JSON. It prints whether the file would load and each problem, and keeps the answer for Encounter.Validation.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | string |  | The root the fight file is in: default or custom. With no path, this one argument is read as the base64 text of a fight file's JSON, checked as a new file of your own. |
| `path` | string | `none` | The fight file's path inside that root, ending in .json. A path with spaces may be quoted or written as several words. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Validate[custom,"My Zone/My Mob.json"]
```

More: [developer/zone-files/builder.md](../../zone-files/builder.md)

# ISXOgreEQ2.Events

## Members

### `Count`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Count}`

How many native game events the extension listens to, currently 14, numbered from 0 for the event argument of Received, Dispatched, Subscribers, EventName and NativeName.

**Returns:** int: the number of events (14 today)

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Count}
```

### `Dispatched`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dispatched[<event>]}`

How many arrivals of this game event have been handed out to the extension's features since it loaded, or the total for all events when the argument is left out. It trails Received only by what is still Pending, and an unknown event gives NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<event>` | string |  | The event's 0-based number or its name, such as ActorSpawned; leave it out for the total across all events |

**Returns:** int64: arrivals handed out for that event since load (or for all events); NULL for an unknown event

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dispatched[ActorSpawned]}
```

### `Dropped`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dropped}`

Total game events thrown away since the extension loaded, because more than 4096 were waiting at once (oldest dropped first) or the event was not recognised. It never resets.

**Returns:** int64: events dropped since load

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dropped}
```

### `EventName`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.EventName[<event>]}`

The extension's name for a game event, such as IncomingChatText, looked up by its 0-based number or its name. A missing or unknown event gives NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<event>` | string |  | The event's 0-based number (0 to Count minus 1) or its name |

**Returns:** string: the event's name; NULL for a missing or unknown event

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.EventName[0]}
```

### `NativeName`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.NativeName[<event>]}`

The ISXEQ2 event a game event is read from, such as EQ2_onIncomingChatText, which is also the name a script attaches its own atom to. A missing or unknown event gives NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<event>` | string |  | The event's 0-based number (0 to Count minus 1) or its name, such as IncomingChatText |

**Returns:** string: the ISXEQ2 event name; NULL for a missing or unknown event

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.NativeName[IncomingChatText]}
```

### `Pending`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Pending}`

How many received game events are waiting to be handed to the extension's features; they are handed out every pulse, so this is normally 0. At most 4096 can wait, and beyond that the oldest are dropped and counted in Dropped.

**Returns:** int: events waiting to be handed out right now

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Pending}
```

### `Received`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Received[<event>]}`

How many times this game event has arrived since the extension loaded, or the total for all events when the argument is left out. The event is its 0-based number or its name in any case (IncomingChatText, ActorSpawned and so on), and an unknown event gives NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<event>` | string |  | The event's 0-based number or its name, such as IncomingChatText; leave it out for the total across all events |

**Returns:** int64: arrivals of that event since load (or of all events); NULL for an unknown event

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Received[IncomingChatText]}
```

### `Stats`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Stats}`

One summary line, such as attached=yes events=14 pending=0 dropped=0 recv=5120 disp=5120, with recv and disp totalled across all events. Echoing ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events} prints the same line after the word Events.

**Returns:** string: the summary line

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Stats}
```

### `StatsJSON`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.StatsJSON}`

The full event table as one JSON object: attached, count, pending, dropped, and an events array giving each event's i, label, native, received, dispatched and subscribers.

**Returns:** string: a JSON object

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.StatsJSON}
```

### `Subscribers`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Subscribers[<event>]}`

How many of the extension's own features are listening to this game event (such as the chat and spawn handling behind OgreBotAPI.Events), or the total when the argument is left out. Atoms a script attaches to the ISXEQ2 event itself are not counted, and an unknown event gives NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<event>` | string |  | The event's 0-based number or its name, such as FinishedZoning; leave it out for the total across all events |

**Returns:** int: listeners on that event (or on all events); NULL for an unknown event

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Subscribers[FinishedZoning]}
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment

## Methods

### `Boost`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Boost[flag,count,...]`

Starts boosting the item already selected on the tradeskill window's Experiment tab, picking each queued stat and clicking Begin and the confirm dialog for every boost; it also turns on the crafting reaction handling. It refuses with a console line when you are not in the world, lack the Experiment AA, a run is already going or no stat is queued, and words it does not know are echoed and skipped.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag` | string |  | the stat to boost: -p, -pot or -potency for potency, -cb or -critbonus for crit bonus, or -&lt;stat> for any other stat label the game offers |
| `count` | int |  | how many boosts of that stat to queue |
| `...` | string |  | more flag, count pairs, run in the order given |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Boost[-p,3,-cb,2]
```

### `Items`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Items`

Lists the numbered item rows on the Experiment tab's item page to the console, briefly enlarging the tradeskill window to read them and then putting it back. It prints a warning instead when you are not in the world, lack the Experiment AA, a run is in progress or no list is showing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Items
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Run[row,flag,count,...]`

Boosts the item on row `row` of the Experiment item list (the numbers Items prints) with the same flags as Boost. A missing row, a row number out of range or no queued stat is refused with a console line and nothing starts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row` | int |  | the item row number from Experiment:Items, starting at 1 |
| `flag` | string |  | the stat to boost: -p, -pot or -potency, -cb or -critbonus, or -&lt;stat> for any other stat label |
| `count` | int |  | how many boosts of that stat to queue |
| `...` | string |  | more flag, count pairs, run in the order given |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Run[2,-p,5]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Status`

Prints the tradeskill experiment helper's state to the console: running or not, its last status, whether you have the Experiment AA, items done and skipped, boosts made, the last error and the usage lines. It is what a bare `ogre experiment` runs.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Stop`

Stops a running experiment and gives the tradeskill window back its size (the same as `ogre end experiment`). When nothing is running it only prints "experiment: not running" to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Stop
```
