# ISXOgreEQ2.Export

## Members

### `Busy`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Busy}`

TRUE from the moment an ability export starts until its file is written or the export is stopped. ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities returns at once and runs in the background, so poll this to know when it is done.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while an ability export is running; FALSE when none is.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Busy}
```

### `Processed`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Processed}`

How many abilities the running export has processed so far - the count its progress window shows. Reads 0 when no export is running.

**Returns:** int: abilities processed so far by the running export; 0 when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Processed}
```

### `Total`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Total}`

How many abilities the running export will process in all. Reads 0 when no export is running.

**Returns:** int: abilities the running export will process; 0 when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Total}
```

## Methods

### `Abilities`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities[flag...]`

Starts the ability export in the background and returns at once: it reads each ability's game info one ability at a time (a server request per ability) and writes OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityExports/V3_&lt;Name>_&lt;SubClass>_&lt;Server>_AbilityExport.json, the file OgreBotAPI.Abilities loads. With no flags it is the standard export (no passives, no tradeskill, merged into the existing file); a call while one is running is ignored with a console line, and when it finishes OgreBot reloads its abilities unless -noreloadbot or -nosave was given.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag...` | string |  | optional flags in any order: -passive (include passives), -tradeskill (tradeskill export to the crafting XML files), -nodesc, -minlevel &lt;n>, -maxlevel &lt;n>, -j / -a / -e / -m / -gm / -ancient (lowest tier to keep), -new (fresh file, no merge), -na (only abilities not already in the file), -nosave (dry run, nothing written), -noreloadbot; a word that starts with - and is none of these is refused with one line and nothing starts; any other word is an ability ID or name to export only those (a name is looked up by name, a server request) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities[-passive]
```

### `Config`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Config[word...]`

The `ogre export` command: with no words it opens the Ability Export options panel, or brings it back if a run hid it. -start runs the export now with the panel's current options and no panel (a server request per ability, as Abilities does; refused while one is running), -default uses the default options for this call only without saving them, stop stops a running export, and any other word is named on the console and nothing happens.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word...` | string |  | optional words, any order, case-insensitive, leading dash optional: -default, -start, stop |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Config[stop]
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Export:End`

Stops a running ability export (nothing is written, and abilities are not reloaded) and closes the export options window - the same as `ogre end export` or either window's X. When nothing is running and nothing is open it does nothing and says nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Export:End
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Game

## Members

### `Busy`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Game.Busy}`

Whether a login or camp started by ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Login or :Camp is still running. It goes FALSE when the flow finishes, times out or is aborted.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a login or camp is in progress; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Game.Busy}
```

### `State`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Game.State}`

The step the login or camp flow is on, as a short phrase such as login: wait for login screen or camp: wait for camp to complete. It reads idle when nothing is running.

**Returns:** string: the current login/camp step; idle when nothing is running.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Game.State}
```

## Methods

### `Abort`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Abort`

Stops a login or camp that ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Login or :Camp started, resumes the bot if the camp had paused it, and prints aborted. Does nothing when nothing is running.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Abort
```

### `Camp`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Camp[mode]`

Camps out the current character, pausing the bot first and retrying the camp once if it fails; a failed camp resumes the bot if it was running. It refuses with a console line when you are not in the world or are in combat, and with no word it camps to the login screen and then closes the InnerSpace session.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `""` | where to stop: charselect (or cs, select) camps to character select and stays; login (or loginscene, loginscreen) camps to the login screen and stays; empty or any other word camps to the login screen and closes the session |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Camp[charselect]
```

### `ConvertAccounts`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Game:ConvertAccounts[overwrite]`

Copies every account and character from the legacy OldBot file EQ2OgreCommon/DoNotShareWithOthers/EQ2Chars.xml into the account store OgreSavePrivate/EQ2/Accounts.json, and prints how many it wrote. If the store already holds data it refuses with a console line unless you pass overwrite; the XML file is left untouched.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overwrite` | string | `""` | overwrite, force or TRUE to replace an existing account store; anything else, or nothing, keeps it |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Game:ConvertAccounts
```

### `Login`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Login[character]`

Logs the named character in from the saved account store, on its only or default server unless -s,&lt;server> follows the name, and as whatever class it was unless -c,&lt;class> does: it fills the login screen, clicks Connect, picks the character at character select if it stops there (first 10 slots only), and when that list does not hold it enters the world on the first listed character the account can play and camps to the login screen to log in from there, waiting up to 180 s to reach the world. It runs over the next frames with progress on the console; it stops with a message when no name is given, the character is locked, every listed character is locked, you are already in as that character, or no saved login exists for it, and if you are in the world on another character it first camps that one (not in combat, bot paused for the camp).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `character` | string |  | the character to log in; its account, password and server come from the saved account store |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Game:Login[${Me.Name}]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest

## Methods

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Help`

Prints the `ogre getquest` usage lines (start, list, reload, status, stop) to the console, with the reminder that you must stand next to the NPC because it does not walk.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Help
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:List`

Prints every loaded quest row: the quest name, the NPC to hail, the wanted step and the zones it is for, with rows that were never checked against the live game marked [UNVERIFIED]. Prints a warning when no rows are loaded.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:List
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Reload`

Re-reads the quest rows from the shipped files (Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/GetQuest/default) and your own (Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/GetQuest/custom) and prints how many loaded. It is refused with a warning while a run is active.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Reload
```

### `Start`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Start`

For the zone you are in (`ogre getquest`), hails the configured NPC and takes its quest, then deletes it from your journal and takes it again until it lands on the wanted step or the row's attempt cap (50 by default) runs out; it never walks, so stand within 15 units of the NPC first. It runs on the bot's action queue and refuses with one line while already running, out of the world, or when no row exists for the zone; it turns on the Do Not Accept Quests setting at the start and puts it back when the run ends, and a round that fails (NPC out of range, no conversation) prints why and ends the run; only a wrong step takes another round.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Start
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Status`

Prints whether a quest reroll is running or idle, how many rows are loaded, your zone, the last result, and the session's run, success and failure counts.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Stop`

Aborts a running quest reroll, restores the Do Not Accept Quests setting and prints 'getquest: aborted (auto-accept restored).', and a round already under way stops at its next step. When nothing is running it prints 'getquest: not running.' instead.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.GetQuest:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite

## Methods

### `Interval`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Interval[ms]`

Sets how often the light harvester runs a pass, in milliseconds (250 to 10000, default 500), and prints the new value; it is not saved. A missing, non-numeric or out-of-range value is refused with a warning and nothing changes.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int |  | milliseconds between passes, 250 to 10000 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Interval[1000]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Off`

Turns the light harvester off (`ogre end hl`): no more scans or harvests from the next frame, and it prints 'harvestlite: off'. Your current target is left as it is.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:On`

Turns the light harvester on (`ogre hl`; it starts off and the switch is not saved): every 500 ms it double-clicks your target when that is a resource node within reach (5 units plus both model sizes), and when you have no target, are not moving or casting and have no loot window open it targets the nearest node in reach through the bot's targeting, paused or not. It never walks to a node, drops the node while you are in combat with something within 15 units targeting you, and prints 'harvestlite: ON'.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:On
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Status`

Prints the light harvester's state: on or off, the pass interval, the reach, threat and scan radius, its pass, scan, harvest, target and back-off counts, whether a combat back-off is holding, and what it last did.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HarvestLite:Status
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone

## Methods

### `Now`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Now`

Makes the next Rekindle Bond attempt happen right away instead of waiting out the 15 to 30 minute timer, or looks for a Heartstone now if none has been found yet. It is refused with a warning while the helper is off, and an attempt still does nothing unless you are within 6 units of the Heartstone.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Now
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Off`

Turns the Heartstone helper off (`ogre end heartstone`): no more scans or rekindles, and it prints 'heartstone: disabled'. This is not saved, so the helper is on again after the extension reloads.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:On`

Turns the Heartstone helper back on, prints 'heartstone: ENABLED' and looks again for a Heartstone within 200 units about 3 seconds later. The helper is on by default and works whether or not OgreBot is running: after each zone-in it looks for a Heartstone and, once found, uses Rekindle Bond on it at a random 15 to 30 minute interval, waiting while you are dead or camping out and skipping that turn when you are more than 6 units away.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:On
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Status`

Prints the guild-hall Heartstone helper's state (`ogre heartstone`): on or off, whether it has found a Heartstone in this zone, the 6-unit reach, the 15 to 30 minute wait, and its scan, attempt and rekindle counts.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Heartstone:Status
```


### `Reset`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Reset`

Removes your custom additions to the effect list.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Reset
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Run`

Runs the hide pass now: walks your effects and hides everything the list claims for your class, the same as bare `ogre hideeffects`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Run
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Status`

Prints what is loaded, what applies to this character and how the last run went to the console. It makes no server call.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HideEffects:Status
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs

## Members

### `Diag`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs.Diag}`

One diagnostic line about the on-screen HUD overlay: whether it is open, which HUD parts are switched on, whether you are in a raid, whether the group or raid part is the one showing, how many updates it has sent and whether the UI host is up. Reading it does one game read and changes nothing.

**Returns:** string: space-separated key=value pairs describing the HUD overlay's state.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs.Diag}
```

## Methods

### `Authorized`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Authorized[names]`

Replaces the list of character names the HUD's nearest-player alert ignores with one comma-separated list; names match in any case. No argument, or an empty one, clears the list (your group and raid never set the alert off anyway).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | string | `""` | character names separated by commas, no spaces |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Authorized["Bob,Alice"]
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Close`

Closes the on-screen HUD overlay and leaves the switched-on parts as they are. Setting a raid message line or switching a HUD part on later opens it again.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Close
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Open`

Opens the on-screen HUD overlay - a click-through layer that shows the nearest NPC, group or raid member distances and the raid message lines, for the parts that are switched on. If its files cannot be read or the UI host is not up it stays closed and only the log says why.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Open
```

### `Set`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Set[key,value]`

Sets one HUD overlay setting by key: a part on or off, a display option, or a position. Switching the npc, group, raid or raidopts part on opens the overlay if it is closed, switching one off never closes it, and an unknown key is ignored.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | parts (on/off): npc, group, raid, raidopts; options (on/off): hidename, hidecasting, grouphidename, grouphidecasting, raidonly; positions and spacing (numbers): npcx, npcy, groupx, groupy, groupinc, raidx, raidy, raidinc, raidspacer, raidgap, raidoptx, raidopty, raidoptinc; namewidth and groupnamewidth (1-40, the raid and group name column width). Case does not matter |
| `value` | string |  | 1, TRUE or on to switch on (anything else is off), or the number for a position key |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Set[group,TRUE]
```

### `SetOption`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:SetOption[slot,text,displaySecs,removeSecs,minUpdateSecs]`

Writes one raid message line on the HUD overlay, with an optional countdown after the text, and removes it after removeSecs; minUpdateSecs then makes the line ignore further writes for that long. A non-empty text opens the overlay if it is closed and empty text blanks the line; a slot outside 1-10 is ignored, and a call without a slot and text prints one usage line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | int |  | which raid message line, 1 to 10 |
| `text` | string |  | the text to show; empty blanks the line |
| `displaySecs` | int | `0` | seconds of countdown shown after the text; 0 shows no countdown |
| `removeSecs` | int | `30` | seconds until the line is removed; 0 or less means 30 |
| `minUpdateSecs` | int | `0` | seconds the line ignores further writes (an empty write still clears it); 0 or less means no lock |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:SetOption[1,"Next add in:",20,25]
```

### `Test`

`ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Test[on]`

TRUE loads five demo raid message lines (10 s countdown, gone after 15 s) at once, opening the overlay if it is closed; FALSE, or no argument, clears all ten lines if the demo was loaded. A second TRUE does nothing until a FALSE in between.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | bool | `FALSE` | 1, TRUE or on loads the demo lines; anything else clears them |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.HUDs:Test[TRUE]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.IC

## Members

### `FileArgs`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileArgs}`

The IC File Args text from the IC window (or set with IC:SetFileArgs or the -fileArgs option). A running zone also sees it in its values as options.fileArgs.

**Returns:** string: the IC File Args text; "" when none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileArgs}
```

### `FileOption`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileOption[n]}`

Whether IC File Option n (1, 2 or 3) is ticked in the IC window; what each one means is up to the zone file. Any n outside 1-3 reads NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int |  | which IC File Option, 1 to 3 |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when that option is ticked; FALSE when not; NULL for n outside 1-3.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileOption[1]}
```

### `FileOptionLabel`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileOptionLabel[n]}`

The text the IC window shows for IC File Option n: a label set with IC:SetFileOptionLabel, else the zone file's own label (the running file, else the one selected in the window), else "IC File Option n". Any n outside 1-3 reads NULL.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int |  | which IC File Option, 1 to 3 |

**Returns:** string: the option's label as shown; NULL for n outside 1-3.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileOptionLabel[2]}
```

### `Loaded`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Loaded}`

The number of zone files IC has loaded. It reads 0 until IC first reads its folders, which happens on Reload or the first IC call that needs them (reading this member does not load them).

**Returns:** int: how many zone files are loaded; 0 before the first load.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Loaded}
```

### `MaxWait`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.MaxWait}`

Max wait per zone, in seconds (default 3600, saved with the IC settings); 0 waits forever. A zone script still running past it is scored failed (the script itself is not ended) and a steps zone is stopped, and time spent with IC paused or staying in zone until a zone is ready does not count.

**Returns:** int: seconds a zone may run; 0 means no limit.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.MaxWait}
```

### `Note`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Note}`

Why the current or last run ended, such as "reported complete", a failure reason or "by user" after a stop. It is cleared when a new run starts.

**Returns:** string: the end reason of the last run; "" while a run is going or before any.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Note}
```

### `Paused`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Paused}`

Whether IC's own pause is on (set by Pause, the IC window, a halt at end of zone or a no-trade shiny). This is not OgreBot's pause.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while IC is paused; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Paused}
```

### `RunId`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.RunId}`

The id of the current or last run, a short hex text that is new each time a zone file starts. The run's values are also saved as OgreSave/EQ2/IC/runs/&lt;RunId>.json; each run start deletes the ones over 7 days old.

**Returns:** string: the current or last run's id; "" before any zone has started.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.RunId}
```

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Running}`

Whether a run is in flight: TRUE while IC is zoning in, launching a zone script or running a zone. FALSE when idle, done or failed.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a run is zoning in, launching or running; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Running}
```

### `RunState`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.RunState}`

Where the current or last run stands, as a word: idle, zoning in, launching, running, done or failed.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "zoning in", "launching", "running", "done" or "failed".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.RunState}
```

### `State`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.State}`

IC's whole state as JSON text: zone files loaded and skipped, its folders, both pauses, the run (state, id, zone, script, step, verdict, max wait), the list and the lockout table. A bare ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC} returns the same text.

**Returns:** string: IC's state as one JSON object.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.State}
```

### `Validation`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Validation}`

The answer of the last IC:Validate, as JSON: ok (true when the file would load), errors and warnings (how many), and issues - one for each line it printed, with the list and the step it belongs to (counted from 1), the message, and whether it is only a warning. Empty until IC:Validate has run.

**Returns:** string: JSON, for example {"ok":true,"errors":0,"warnings":0,"issues":[]}; "" before the first IC:Validate.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Validation}
```

More: [developer/zone-files/builder.md](../../zone-files/builder.md)

### `Value`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Value[key]}`

The run's values that IC publishes for the zone file to read (zone, options, run, list, group and more): bare, the whole document as JSON text; with a key, one dotted key such as zone.fullName or run.completed.1 (arrays count from 1, keys are case-sensitive). True/false values read TRUE or FALSE, objects and arrays read as JSON text, an absent key reads NULL and a key that holds empty text reads empty.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | a dotted key into the values, such as zone.fullName or options.fileArgs; leave it off for the whole document |

**Returns:** string: the whole values document as JSON, or one value as text; NULL before any run, for an absent key, or for a key that holds empty text.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Value[zone.fullName]}
```

### `Verdict`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Verdict}`

The run's verdict: idle (nothing has run), pending (a run is in flight), completed, completedWithFailures (a steps zone ended but a step did not do its job) or failed. A skipped zone and a stopped zone script run read completed, while a stopped steps zone or a stopped zone-in reads failed.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "pending", "completed", "completedWithFailures" or "failed".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Verdict}
```

### `Zone`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Zone}`

The full zone name (with its difficulty) of the current or last run. It is set when a zone file starts, so while IC is still zoning in it names the last zone.

**Returns:** string: the run's full zone name; "" before any zone has started.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Zone}
```

### `ZoneEnd`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.ZoneEnd}`

Where a script zone's zone end stands after it called IC:ZoneEnd: none (not asked), busy (calling the group to the guild hall or staying in the zone), halted (halt at end of zone, waiting for Resume), zoneOut (zone out now), calledGH (the group is in the guild hall, so do not zone out) or ghFailed (the call failed; end the zone as usual). It goes back to none when a new run starts or the run is stopped.

**Returns:** string: "none", "busy", "halted", "zoneOut", "calledGH" or "ghFailed".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.ZoneEnd}
```

## Methods

### `Check`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Check[zone]`

Prints which zone files claim a zone (exact or prefix match) and whether the zone is available according to the lockout table; no zone means the one you are in. When the table is out of date it asks for a fresh read and says to ask again shortly, except while IC is paused, you are out of the world or a read is already pending, when it only says the table is not fresh.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string |  | the zone name to check; leave it off for your current zone |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Check["${Zone.Name}"]
```

### `Complete`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Complete[note]`

For a zone run by a script: marks the run completed, so it is scored COMPLETED when the script exits, while a script that exits without calling this is scored FAILED. It does not end the run, prints nothing, does nothing when no run is in flight, and a steps zone, which completes itself, refuses it with one line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | string |  | optional text kept as the run's note; empty gives "reported complete" |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Complete["all nameds killed"]
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:End`

Closes IC out, the same as the IC window's X and `ogre end ic`: the window closes, IC's pause clears, and a running zone and list stop as with Stop. Unlike Stop it does not cancel end-of-list actions already under way and says nothing when nothing is running.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:End
```

### `Fail`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Fail[reason]`

Ends the current run at once as FAILED with the reason, printed on the console; a zone script keeps running, a steps zone stops at its current step without its exit steps, and a zone-in stops its route. Does nothing when no run is in flight.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string |  | why it failed; empty gives "the script reported failure", or on a steps zone "IC:Fail was called with no reason" |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Fail["group member missing"]
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:List[filter]`

Prints every loaded zone file (folder, path, zone, difficulties, and [delegates] for one that hands off to another file or a script) and a count. A filter keeps only files whose zone or path contains it, any case, with its words joined by a space.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string |  | text to match in the zone name or file path; leave it off to list all |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:List[Zobboz]
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Open`

Opens the IC window, the same as `ogre ic`. Already open does nothing, and it warns when the UI host is not available.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Open
```

### `Options`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Options[switches...]`

Sets IC options by switch: -&lt;option> turns a tick-box on and -&lt;option>=off turns it off (on, off, true, false, 1, 0, yes or no, any case), while -afterWipe=, -maxWait=, -fileArgs= and -stopAfterZone take values. No argument prints every option and its state; changes are saved and reported in one line, and switches that could not be set are listed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switches...` | string |  | one or more option switches, each starting with - |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Options[-loop,-skipShinies=off,-maxWait=5400]
```

### `Pause`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Pause`

Turns on IC's own pause, which stops IC moving the zone and the list along while OgreBot, and any fight already under way, keep going. Prints "IC PAUSED" when it changes, and time paused does not count against the max wait.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Pause
```

### `Queue`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Queue[action,args...]`

Edits the IC list: add,&lt;tier>,&lt;path>, add,&lt;tier>,&lt;zone name> or add,&lt;zone name> adds a zone file, startat,&lt;row>,&lt;N> makes that row start at step N (N of 1 or less clears it), and clear empties the list. No action, or any other word, prints the list, and add or startat without their arguments is refused.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string |  | add, startat or clear; anything else or nothing prints the list |
| `args...` | string |  | the action's arguments: a tier and path or a zone name for add, a row and step number for startat |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Queue[add,default,"Rage of Cthurath/_04_Zon_Zobboz_The_Graftwerk.json"]
```

### `Refresh`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Refresh`

Marks IC's cached zone lockout table out of date, so the next check reads it from the game again. Prints "lock table invalidated - it re-seeds on the next check".

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Refresh
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Reload`

Re-reads every zone file from IC's folders and prints "N zone(s) from M file(s) - X skipped, Y warning(s)". Same as the IC window's Reload and `ogre ic reload`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Reload
```

### `Resume`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Resume`

Clears IC's own pause and prints "IC resumed" when it changes. It is also how you go on after a halt at end of zone or a pause for a no-trade shiny.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Resume
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Run[tier,relPath]`

Starts one zone file (not the list): when you are not in its zone and the travel data knows the way, IC first takes the group there, then a zone that hands off to a script launches it with no arguments (the script reads ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Value}) and a steps zone runs its own steps. It refuses with a console line when you are not in the world, a run is already in flight, IC is paused, OgreBot has no profile loaded, or the file is missing, not valid or disabled.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tier` | string |  | which zone file folder: default (the shipped files) or custom (your own, under OgreSave/EQ2/IC/custom) |
| `relPath` | string |  | the zone file's path inside that folder; further arguments are joined to it with a space |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Run[default,"Rage of Cthurath/_04_Zon_Zobboz_The_Graftwerk.json"]
```

### `RunList`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:RunList[row]`

Starts the queued list from a row (1-based, default the top); a row the queue does not have, or one that is not a number, prints "no row N (the queue has M)" and starts nothing. It refuses with a console line when you are not in the world, a run or the end-of-list actions are still going, or the queue is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row` | int | `1` | the list row to start at, counting from 1 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:RunList[2]
```

### `SetFileArgs`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetFileArgs[text]`

Sets the IC File Args text and saves it; no argument clears it. Only the first argument is used, so quote text that holds commas.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string |  | the new IC File Args text; empty clears it |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetFileArgs["fast loot"]
```

### `SetFileOptionLabel`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetFileOptionLabel[n,text]`

Sets the text the IC window shows for IC File Option n (1-3); empty text goes back to the zone file's own label or "IC File Option n". The label is cleared when the next zone starts, and n outside 1-3 prints a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int |  | which IC File Option, 1 to 3 |
| `text` | string |  | the label to show; empty restores the default |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetFileOptionLabel[1,"Kill the optional named"]
```

### `SetMaxWait`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetMaxWait[seconds]`

Sets Max wait per zone in seconds and saves it; 0 waits forever. A fraction rounds up, a number below 0 becomes 1 and a huge one is held at the largest value, while text that is not a number (or no argument) changes nothing, each with a console line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | number |  | seconds a zone may run; 0 means no limit |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetMaxWait[5400]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Status`

Prints IC's report on the console: zone files loaded and their folders, both pauses, the lockout table, the run, its verdict and max wait, the current step, the list and the options that are on. Same as `ogre ic status`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Stop`

Stops the run and the list where they stand and clears IC's pause: a zone script is no longer tracked but is NOT ended, and a steps zone stops at its current step without running its exit steps. With nothing running it cancels end-of-list actions still under way, or prints "nothing is running" (same as the IC window's End and `ogre ic stop`).

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Stop
```

### `Validate`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Validate[tier,path]`

Checks one zone file by the same rules the Instance Controller uses when it loads zone files, and changes nothing: a file on disk by its tier and path (the same as `ogre ic validate`), or the base64 text of a zone file's JSON. It prints whether the file would load and each problem, and keeps the answer for IC.Validation.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tier` | string |  | The root the zone file is in: default or custom. With no path, this one argument is read as the base64 text of a zone file's JSON. |
| `path` | string | `none` | The zone file's path inside that root, ending in .json. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Validate[custom,"My_Zone.json"]
```

More: [developer/zone-files/builder.md](../../zone-files/builder.md)

### `Value`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Value[key]`

Prints the run's values on the console: no key prints the whole document and the path of its saved copy, a dotted key prints one value, "" (empty) for empty text, or "NULL (absent)". Before any run it prints "no values - nothing has run yet"; a script reads values with ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.Value[key]} instead.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | a dotted key such as zone.fullName; leave it off to print the whole document |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Value[zone.fullName]
```

### `Wipe`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Wipe`

Declares a wipe now: a steps zone that is running its enter or steps list stops and runs its wipe recovery. Out of the world, or with no such zone running, it prints why and does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:Wipe
```

### `ZoneEnd`

`ISXOgreEQ2.IC:ZoneEnd`

Called by a zone script where it would zone out: IC runs the zone end a steps zone gets (halt at end of zone, then Call to GH after each zone or Stay in zone until a zone is ready, as ticked), and the script then reads ${ISXOgreEQ2.IC.ZoneEnd} until it is not busy or halted. With no zone script running, or on a steps zone, it prints a warning and does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.IC:ZoneEnd
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps

## Members

### `Busy`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps.Busy}`

TRUE while an inventory flow started through this object (Overflow, MoveBag or Trade) is running. Only one of the three runs at a time, and starting another while one runs is refused with a busy warning.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while an overflow, bag move or trade flow is running; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps.Busy}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps.Status}`

One line naming the running inventory flow and its progress, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps}` returns.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "overflow (N popped)", "mbc (done/total)" or "trade (done/total)".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps.Status}
```

## Methods

### `MoveBag`

`ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:MoveBag[from,to]`

The engine behind `ogre mbc`: moves every item in carried bag `from` into bag `to`, one item every 0.2 s, where a bag's number is its inventory slot (1-6). It is refused with a console warning when a number is missing or out of range, both are the same bag, a slot holds no bag, the source bag is empty, or another inventory flow is running.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | int |  | bag number (1-6) to empty |
| `to` | int |  | bag number (1-6) to move the items into |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:MoveBag[2,3]
```

### `Overflow`

`ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Overflow`

The engine behind `ogre overflow`: pops items out of the overflow window into your bags, one every 0.2 s, until the game says the overflow is empty or has no room, only one bag slot is left free, or 300 items have been popped. It returns at once and the work runs on later frames; it is refused with a console warning when another inventory flow is running or you are not in the world.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Overflow
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Stop`

Drops whichever overflow, bag move or trade flow is running, without printing anything; does nothing when idle. An open trade window is left as it is.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Stop
```

### `Trade`

`ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Trade[count]`

The engine behind `ogre trade`: opens a trade with your current target, adds up to `count` whole stacks from your bags of the item you have EXAMINED (exact name, any case), then accepts. You need a target and an open examine window; when nothing is examined or no stack matches, the run rejects the trade it opened and ends with a console line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | int | `12` | most stacks to hand over; missing, not a whole number, or 0 or less uses 12 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.InvOps:Trade[4]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Lag

## Methods

### `Budget`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Budget[first,second]`

Sets the two frame budgets the reports count against and saves them, then prints them. A first budget of 1 ms or less, or a second that is not above it, is not taken; with either value missing it prints one warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first` | float |  | The first budget in ms. |
| `second` | float |  | The second budget in ms, above the first. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Budget[33,50]
```

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Clear`

Clears the recorded frames; recording carries on.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Clear
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Close`

Closes the Lag window, the same as `ogre end lag`. The ledger keeps recording; :Off stops it.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Close
```

### `Dump`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Dump[seconds]`

Writes the recorded frames to the dump file and says where.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | float |  | How far back to dump. Optional: everything recorded when left out. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Dump[120]
```

### `Minutes`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Minutes[minutes]`

Sets how many minutes of frames the ledger holds, saves it, and starts the ledger empty. With no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | int |  | Minutes to hold, held between 1 and 60. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Minutes[10]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Off`

Turns the ledger off and saves it: nothing is recorded, and the frames already recorded are kept.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:On`

Turns the ledger on and saves it: every frame is recorded.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:On
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Open`

Opens the Lag window, the same as bare `ogre lag`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Open
```

### `Overhead`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Overhead`

Prints what the ledger itself costs per frame to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Overhead
```

### `Report`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Report[seconds]`

Prints the report for the last stretch of frames to the console: frame rate, stability, and what cost the most.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | float |  | How far back to look. Optional: 60 when left out. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Lag:Report[30]
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/MCP.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.MCP

## Members

### `ForWho`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.ForWho}`

The for-who text MCP buttons and bound keys use on this session, from the For Who picker or MCP:SetForWho. A button with its own for-who still uses its own.

**Returns:** string: the for-who text in force on this session; all when nothing has been picked (everyone).

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.ForWho}
```

### `IrcConnected`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.IrcConnected}`

Whether this session last heard that the IRC link is up. It starts FALSE on a new session and stays FALSE until the IRC hub reports in; while FALSE, MCP buttons that send over IRC go through OgreConsole instead.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the IRC hub last reported the link connected; FALSE when it reported it down or has not reported yet.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.IrcConnected}
```

## Methods

### `AddBind`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:AddBind[key,buttonId,name,event]`

Links a keyboard key or mouse button (an InnerSpace key name such as G600-G9) to an MCP button, so pressing it runs MCP:Fire on that button. The bind is saved to Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCPBinds.json, armed at once, and every EQ2 session on this PC picks it up; a bind with the same name is replaced, and a button id that has no command yet only prints a note.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | The InnerSpace key name to bind, such as G600-G9 or F13. |
| `buttonId` | string |  | The MCP button to run, as MCP:Buttons lists it. |
| `name` | string | `MCP_<key>_<buttonId> with every other character turned into _` | A name for the bind, used by MCP:RemoveBind. |
| `event` | string | `press` | release fires when the key is let go; anything else fires on press. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:AddBind[G600-G9,static:0_0,G9Heal,press]
```

### `Buttons`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Buttons`

Prints every configured MCP button to the console with its id, label, page and command, so you can find the id to give MCP:Fire or MCP:AddBind. With no saved layout it prints a line saying there are no buttons yet.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Buttons
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Close`

Closes the Master Control Panel together with its For Who, Build command and Assign keys windows. It also cancels a key test that is still waiting for a press.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Close
```

### `Fire`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Fire[buttonId]`

Runs an MCP button by its id, exactly as clicking it would: the button's command is read from the saved layout at that moment and sent with the button's own for-who, or this session's For Who when the button has none. A missing id, no saved layout, or a button with no command prints one console line and sends nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buttonId` | string |  | The button's id as MCP:Buttons lists it: btn:&lt;id> (follows the button when it moves), static:&lt;row>_&lt;col> or page:&lt;page>:&lt;row>_&lt;col>. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Fire[static:0_0]
```

### `FixHoistOrder`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:FixHoistOrder`

Repairs buttons that an older MCP:Migrate wrote with some arguments in the wrong order, touching only the affected buttons and writing OgreMCP.json.bak first. It runs once per file (a second call prints that it is already done), prints how many buttons were fixed or need checking by hand, and has every EQ2 session on this PC reload when anything changed.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:FixHoistOrder
```

### `ListBinds`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ListBinds`

Prints every saved key bind to the console: its name, key, press or release, the button it runs, and whether it is disabled.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ListBinds
```

### `Migrate`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Migrate[overwrite]`

Converts the old OgreBot MCP buttons (Scripts/EQ2OgreBot/MCP/MCPCustomSettings.xml) into the new panel's Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCP.json and prints a summary; button types with no command equivalent come across as label only. It refuses to replace an existing OgreMCP.json unless you pass overwrite, and on success every EQ2 session on this PC reloads the panel.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overwrite` | string | `off - an existing file is kept` | The word overwrite (or 1, TRUE, yes, on) replaces an existing OgreMCP.json, discarding its current layout. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Migrate
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Open`

Opens the Master Control Panel (MCP), the window of buttons that send commands to your characters, with its saved layout; the same as `ogre mcp`, and alt+backtick toggles it. Calling it while the panel is already open does nothing; if the in-game UI host is not running or a panel file cannot be read, nothing opens and one console line says which, and a missing command catalog opens the builder empty with a line.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Open
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Reload`

Re-reads Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCP.json and updates an open panel to match, which is how a change saved on one session shows up on the others. It is skipped when the file is exactly what this session just saved, or when the file is not valid JSON.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Reload
```

### `ReloadBinds`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ReloadBinds`

Re-reads Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCPBinds.json, removes this session's live key binds and arms the saved ones again. Adding or removing a bind on any session runs this on every EQ2 session on the PC.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ReloadBinds
```

### `RemoveBind`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:RemoveBind[name]`

Removes a saved key bind by name, disarms it and tells every EQ2 session on this PC to drop it. An unknown name prints a console line and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The bind's name as MCP:ListBinds shows it. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:RemoveBind[G9Heal]
```

### `Send`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Send[message,-tab,tab,-rg,group,-cfw,who]`

With arguments it sends message exactly as ISXOgreX.Console:Send does (a leading !c or !ci makes it a command, anything else is a chat line). With no arguments it sends the button just clicked on this session, once, through the same route a click uses, and otherwise the console input box line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | `the button just clicked, or the input box line` | The literal line to send; a leading !c or !ci makes it a command. Leave out every argument for the button just clicked, or the console input box line. |
| `-tab` | switch | `(none)` | Also show the line in the console tab named by the next argument; may be given more than once. |
| `tab` | string | `(none)` | The console tab name that follows -tab. |
| `-rg` | switch | `(none)` | Send to the relay group named by the next argument instead of the bot's own relay group. |
| `group` | string | `the bot's relay group` | The relay group name that follows -rg. |
| `-cfw` | switch | `(none)` | Give the command a for-who, used by its commands whose own for-who is left as auto. |
| `who` | for-who | `everyone` | [for-who](../ogrebotapi/ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names - the value that follows -cfw. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Send["!c -pause","-cfw","igw:${Me.Name}"]
```

### `SetForWho`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:SetForWho[value]`

Sets the For Who that MCP buttons and bound keys use on this session only, held in memory (not saved, not shared, back to everyone after a restart). With a value it sets that as a custom For Who and shows it in the picker (spaces are removed; all or an empty value clears it back to everyone); with no value it takes the choice the For Who picker just made.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | string | `(none) - the picker's choice` | The for-who text to use, such as igw:&lt;name> or several names joined with \|. Leave it out to take the For Who picker's current choice. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:SetForWho[igw:${Me.Name}]
```

### `Toggle`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Toggle`

Opens the Master Control Panel when it is closed and closes it when it is open. This is what alt+backtick runs.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Toggle
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/MerchantCraft.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft

## Methods

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Help`

Prints the `ogre mc` usage lines to the console and does nothing else. It is what `ogre mc help` runs.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Help
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:List`

Reads the recipes your TARGETED merchant sells and prints them numbered, for use with Start["#n"]. It is refused with a console warning when a run is already going, you are not in the world, the target is not a merchant within 9 m, or you lack the Summon Crafting Stations ability.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:List
```

### `Start`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Start[words...]`

The engine behind `ogre mc <recipe> [count]`: for each round it buys the recipe from your targeted merchant (only if you do not know it), scribes it, summons the crafting station it needs, empties the craft engine's setup queue and crafts it 3 times. It has the same refusals as List and also refuses with no recipe or while a craft run is going; on a recipe not yet cached it MAKES A SERVER CALL (`.ToRecipeInfo`, to learn the crafting device), and only when the craft panel's "Allow recipe-info server call" option is on, which it is by default.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `words...` | string |  | a partial recipe name (one or more words, first match wins) or "#n" for row n of List's numbering, then an optional trailing whole number = rounds (1 to 999, default 1; each round is 3 crafts) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Start[ferrite,bracelet,4]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Status`

Prints the merchant-craft state (running or idle, the current recipe and round, how many recipes the last scan found) and then the usage lines to the console. It is what bare `ogre mc` and `ogre mc status` run.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Stop`

Abandons the merchant-craft run and prints "mc: stopped.", or "mc: nothing is running." when idle. It does not stop a craft queue the run already started, and a summoned station stays.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Stop
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/MerchantOps.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps

## Members

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Running}`

TRUE while a buyfuel or buycrate run is in progress. Only one runs at a time; starting another is refused with a busy warning.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a fuel or crate purchase run is going; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Running}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Status}`

One line naming the running merchant run and its progress, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps}` returns.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "buyfuel '&lt;fuel>' (round n)" or "buycrate (done/total)".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Status}
```

## Methods

### `BuyCrate`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyCrate[flags...]`

The engine behind `ogre buycrate`: targets and opens this zone's crate merchant (who must be nearby), buys one of each chosen heroic and raid crate, accepts the purchase prompt and closes the merchant. Only exp17_dun_fordel_midst and exp18_rgn_svarni_expanse have one (Svarni sells no heroic crate), and anywhere else, or when nothing matches the flags, the call is refused with a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags...` | string | `-all` | -r/-raid for the raid crate, -h/-heroic for the heroic crate, -all for both; read left to right, so `-raid -all` buys both and `-all -raid` only the raid crate; unknown words are ignored |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyCrate[-h]
```

### `BuyFuel`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyFuel[amount]`

The engine behind `ogre buyfuel`: at the guild hall Fuel Depot (within 11 m) it counts how much of the fuel you have EXAMINED the depot holds, buys the shortfall from the merchant titled Guild Fuel Merchant and deposits it, repeating for at most 10 rounds. It is refused when nothing is examined, a run is already going or you are not in the world, and stops with a console warning when the depot is missing, too far or does not open.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | int | `90000` | how much of the fuel the depot should end up holding; missing, not a whole number, or 0 or less uses 90000 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyFuel[20000]
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:Stop`

Stops a running buyfuel or buycrate and prints "merchant: stopped."; does nothing when idle. Open depot or merchant windows are left as they are.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:Stop
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Migrate.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate

## Methods

### `Cancel`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Cancel[task]`

Backs out of a pending overwrite confirmation for one task, putting its row back to its normal state. It does nothing when that task is not waiting for a confirmation or the name is unknown.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string |  | the task whose confirmation to cancel: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Cancel[profiles]
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Close`

Closes the Migration Assistant window and cancels its pending auto-close. Nothing that has already run is undone.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Close
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Open`

Opens the Migration Assistant window (the same as `ogre migrate`), listing each migration task with its status and a re-run button. Before it opens it silently runs any task whose old file exists and whose new file does not, and when the window is already up it does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Open
```

### `RequestRerun`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:RequestRerun[task]`

Puts one task's row in the Migration Assistant into its overwrite confirmation state, the same as clicking its re-run button; it reads and writes no files. It only does so when that task's old source data exists, otherwise nothing changes.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string |  | the task to ask about: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:RequestRerun[accounts]
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Run[task,overwrite]`

Runs one migration task now, copying old OgreBot data into the new store (your old XML files are kept); the isprofile task instead asks InnerSpace to add its game profile and ignores overwrite. Without overwrite a task whose new file already exists is not rewritten and its row asks you to confirm instead, an unknown task name does nothing, and the result shows in the Migration Assistant window and the log.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string |  | the task to run: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile |
| `overwrite` | string |  | the word overwrite (any case) to replace data that already exists; anything else, or leaving it out, keeps existing data |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Run[irc]
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Nav.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Nav

## Members

### `NavActive`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavActive}`

TRUE while a nav trip is in progress - planning its route, waiting for this zone's navmesh, or moving. A paused trip still counts as in progress.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a trip is planning, waiting for its navmesh or moving; FALSE when idle or once the last trip has ended (Arrived, Stopped, Failed).

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavActive}
```

### `NavDistance`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavDistance}`

Straight-line distance from the character to the trip's destination, refreshed every pulse while it moves, on foot or flying. It is -1 when idle, while a trip is still planning or waiting for its navmesh, and after a trip ends.

**Returns:** float: distance in game units to the destination; -1 when no trip is moving.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavDistance}
```

### `NavMeshOn`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshOn}`

TRUE unless nav has been switched off with Nav:Set[mesh,off] or `ogre nav -off`. While it is off, new trips are refused; the switch is not saved and starts TRUE each time the extension loads.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when nav is allowed to move this character; FALSE when it is switched off.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshOn}
```

### `NavMeshPolys`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshPolys}`

How many walkable polygons the loaded navmesh has. It is 0 when no mesh is loaded in this zone yet.

**Returns:** int: polygon count of the loaded mesh; 0 when none is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshPolys}
```

### `NavMeshTiles`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshTiles}`

How many tiles the loaded navmesh has. It is 0 when no mesh is loaded in this zone yet.

**Returns:** int: tile count of the loaded mesh; 0 when none is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshTiles}
```

### `NavMeshZone`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshZone}`

Name of the navmesh that is loaded - the zone's short name in lower case, or the base zone's name when this zone is a copy that uses it. It is "" until a mesh is loaded in this zone (see NavOnMap).

**Returns:** string: the loaded mesh's zone name; "" when none is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshZone}
```

### `NavOnMap`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMap}`

TRUE when a navmesh is loaded right now, so nav can plan a route without waiting. The mesh loads on the first trip or route request in a zone and is set aside on every zone change, so this reads FALSE after zoning until something asks for a route.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when a navmesh is loaded; FALSE when none is loaded yet in this zone.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMap}
```

### `NavOnMesh`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMesh}`

TRUE while the current trip is driven over a navmesh route. It is FALSE when idle, while a trip still waits for its navmesh or plans its first route, and once a trip ends.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while a trip is driven over a navmesh route; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMesh}
```

### `NavReason`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavReason}`

Plain words about the trip: while it plans or moves, what the plan is doing; once it has ended or while it waits for a navmesh, why. It is empty before the first trip, and reads "already there" when a trip was asked for the spot the character already stands on.

**Returns:** string: the plan in force, or why the last trip ended; "" before any trip.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavReason}
```

### `NavState`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavState}`

The trip's state as one word; Arrived, Stopped and Failed stay until the next trip starts, and a paused trip still reads Moving. Stopped means somebody ended the trip on purpose, Failed means nav gave up - NavReason says why.

**Returns:** string: a state word such as Idle, Planning, WaitingForMesh, Moving, Arrived, Stopped or Failed.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavState}
```

### `NavWaypoint`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoint}`

The waypoint on the current route the character is heading for, counted from 1 (the first point after the start) up to NavWaypoints on the last leg. It is 0 when no route is being walked, a finished trip included.

**Returns:** int: the waypoint being walked to, 1 to NavWaypoints; 0 when no route is being walked.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoint}
```

### `NavWaypoints`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoints}`

How many waypoints the current route has after its start point, so NavWaypoint reaches it on the last leg. It is 0 when no route is being walked, a finished trip included.

**Returns:** int: number of waypoints after the start; 0 when no route is being walked.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoints}
```

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:End`

Ends the trip under way and closes the nav window, the same as `ogre end nav`, `ogre nav end` or the window's X. It prints "nav: stopped (...)" only when a trip was under way.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:End
```

### `Flags`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Flags[flag...]`

Runs the `ogre nav -<flag> ...` line: -loc x,y,z (or -to) starts a trip and applies -precision, -nodoors/-doors and -reset with it (it ignores -set, -on/-off and -panel/-nopanel on the same line), while a line without -loc takes -set key value, -reset [key], -on/-off, -panel/-nopanel, -stop, -status or -help. With no flag it prints a warning and a bad or unknown flag prints an error naming it; -precision and -nodoors stay in force after the trip.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag...` | string |  | The flags and their values, one per argument; a -loc point may be one "x,y,z" argument or three. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Flags[-loc,${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Math.Calc[${Me.Z}+30]},-precision,3]
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Help`

Prints the `ogre nav` command help to the console, one line at a time. This is bare `ogre nav` or `ogre nav help`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Help
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Open`

Opens the nav panel (trip state with Stop and Pause buttons) now; if the window cannot open it prints "nav panel: &lt;reason>". This is `ogre nav panel`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Open
```

### `Set`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Set[key,value]`

Changes one nav setting for this session (not saved) and prints "nav: &lt;key> = &lt;value>"; an unknown key, or a value the setting refuses, prints an error and changes nothing. The key is case-insensitive, and `mesh` (alias `on`) never refuses: a yes word switches nav on and any other value switches it off.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | The setting's name, such as arrive, finalarrive, doors or avoid. |
| `value` | string |  | The new value - a number for distances and counts, on or off for switches. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Set[arrive,4]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Status`

Prints what nav is doing to the console - state, reason, paused, waypoint progress, the loaded mesh and every setting changed from its default. This is `ogre nav status`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Stop`

Ends the trip under way (NavState becomes Stopped) and prints "nav: stopped"; the nav panel stays open. With no trip under way it changes nothing but still prints the line - this is `ogre nav stop`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Stop
```

### `To`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:To[x,y,z]`

Starts a trip that moves the character to the point, replacing any trip already under way; it returns at once and the route is planned over the next frames (watch NavState). A missing value, or one that is not a number, prints an error and starts nothing, and a refusal (not in world, movement held by another system, no navmesh) prints "nav: &lt;reason>".

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | float |  | X of the destination. |
| `y` | float |  | Y of the destination - Y is up in EQ2. |
| `z` | float |  | Z of the destination. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:To[${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Math.Calc[${Me.Z}+30]}]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast

## Methods

### `Capture`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Capture`

Asks for the cast your target is casting right now to be captured, the window's Capture button.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Capture
```

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Clear`

Empties your script watch list. Watches from zone data and encounters stay.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Clear
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:End`

Stops the Monitor and closes the window, the same as `ogre end npccast` and the window's X. The watch list is left alone.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:End
```

### `Import`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Import`

Copies the shipped OldBot conversions into your own NPC cast data, never overwriting a file you have.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Import
```

### `Monitor`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Monitor[word]`

The Monitor: starts it on a set of mobs, stops it, or acts on its rows. No word starts it on your target, and any word it does not know prints its status.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | string |  | target, named, all or on start it; off or stop stop it; copy and clear act on its rows; status prints its state. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Monitor[named]
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Open`

Opens the NPC Cast Monitoring window, the same as bare `ogre npccast`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Open
```

### `Radius`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Radius[n]`

Sets the scan radius for the script watch list. With no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Radius[80]
```

### `Reload`

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Reload
```

### `Status`

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Status
```

### `Unwatch`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Unwatch[name]`

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Unwatch["Ancient Guardian"]
```

### `Watch`

`ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Watch[name]`

Adds a mob to your script watch list. With no name it prints one warning and changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Watch["Ancient Guardian"]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot

## Members

### `Character`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Character}`

The character whose OgreBot profile is loaded.

**Returns:** string: the character name; empty when nothing is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Character}
```

### `Count`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Count}`

How many single control values the loaded profile holds (checkboxes, text boxes, combo boxes). List sections such as the Cast Stack are not counted.

**Returns:** int: the number of stored control values; 0 when nothing is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Count}
```

### `Dirty`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Dirty}`

TRUE when the loaded profile has changes that are not saved to disk yet. Only Save writes them; closing OgreBot, Reload, or loading another profile drops them.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when there are unsaved changes; FALSE when there are none or nothing is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Dirty}
```

### `IsReady`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.IsReady}`

TRUE when OgreBot is up: its main window or mini toolbar is open AND a profile is loaded - the check the bot's own features use before they act, and what ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.IsReady} reads too.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when a window is open and a profile is loaded; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.IsReady}
```

### `Loaded`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Loaded}`

TRUE while an OgreBot profile is loaded for this session. Closing OgreBot unloads the profile, so this goes FALSE on close.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when a profile is loaded; FALSE when none is.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Loaded}
```

### `PanelVisible`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.PanelVisible}`

TRUE when the OgreBot main window or the mini toolbar is open, whether or not a profile is loaded. Use IsReady to ask whether the bot can run.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when either window is open; FALSE when both are closed.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.PanelVisible}
```

### `Profile`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Profile}`

The name of the loaded OgreBot profile, in the spelling stored in the profile file.

**Returns:** string: the profile name; empty when nothing is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Profile}
```

### `Value`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Value[id]}`

The stored value of one OgreBot window control, read from the loaded profile in memory (unsaved changes included). The id must match exactly; OgreBotAPI.Options.Value is the case-insensitive version.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | the control id (the same id the profile saves it under), for example checkbox_settings_enablealiases |

**Returns:** string: the control's value as text; empty when the id is not stored, no id is given, or nothing is loaded.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Value[checkbox_settings_enablealiases]}
```

## Methods

### `Alias`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Alias[verb,arg1,arg2,arg3,arg4]`

Edits the loaded profile's custom aliases in memory (Save keeps them) and refreshes the Aliases tab and Target list; names get a leading * if they lack one, and add refuses only the same name with the same For. Verbs are display (print what each alias resolves to now), add or edit (name,For,NoRaid), del (name), delat or toggle (index), editat (index,name,For,NoRaid) and move (from,to) with 0-based indexes, it does nothing with no profile loaded, and OgreBotAPI.ForWho:AddAlias and RemoveAlias use this same editor.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verb` | string |  | display, add, edit, del, delat, editat, toggle or move |
| `arg1` | string |  | the alias name (add, edit, del) or a 0-based row index (delat, editat, toggle, move) |
| `arg2` | string |  | the For value (add, edit; an empty one on edit clears it), the new name (editat) or the target index (move) |
| `arg3` | string |  | No-Raid as a yes/no word (add, edit) or the For value (editat) |
| `arg4` | bool |  | editat only: No-Raid |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Alias[add,Healer,${Group[1].Name},FALSE]
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Close`

Closes OgreBot entirely: both windows close, the profile is unloaded (unsaved changes are dropped with a warning in the console), travel routes stop, and follow and camp spots are cleared unless OgreBotAPI.Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot is on. It is the same close as the X on either window, `ogre end bot` and OgreBotAPI.Bot:End.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Close
```

### `CreateProfile`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:CreateProfile[name]`

Makes a new profile from the current settings, unsaved changes included, writes it to disk and switches to it. It fails with a console line when the name is already used (case does not matter).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the new profile's name; a b64: prefix marks a base64 name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:CreateProfile[Solo]
```

### `DeleteProfile`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:DeleteProfile[name]`

Deletes a named profile from the character's profile file on disk. It refuses, with a console line, the loaded profile, the default profile, the last remaining profile and a name that does not exist.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:DeleteProfile[Solo]
```

### `Dump`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Dump[path]`

Writes every stored control value of the loaded profile (unsaved changes included) to a JSON file and prints the count and path. List sections such as the Cast Stack are not included, and the file is overwritten each time.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | the file to write |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Dump["${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/ogrebot_values.json"]
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:List[section,op,arg1,arg2]`

Edits one list section of the loaded profile (the Cast Stack or any other ordered list tab) in memory; Save keeps it, and a Cast Stack edit reaches the running cast stack at once. Ops are add (entry), insert or update (index,entry), del or toggle (index) and move (from,to), with 0-based indexes and each entry as base64-encoded JSON; it does not refresh the open window and does nothing with no profile loaded.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | string |  | the profile section name, for example CastStack |
| `op` | string |  | add, insert, update, del, move or toggle |
| `arg1` | string |  | the base64 JSON entry (add) or a 0-based row index (every other op) |
| `arg2` | string |  | the base64 JSON entry (insert, update) or the target index (move) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:List[CastStack,toggle,0]
```

### `LoadProfile`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:LoadProfile[name]`

Switches to another named profile of the loaded character and refreshes the cast stack and window; if OgreBot is not open it opens it with that profile. Unsaved changes to the current profile are dropped, with one warning line unless you named the profile already loaded, a name that is not found prints a line and keeps the current profile, and OgreBotAPI.Options:LoadProfile calls this.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:LoadProfile[Raid]
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Open[character,profile]`

Loads the character's profile from disk and opens the OgreBot main window and mini toolbar with it, then scans gear and inventory for the Items tab. Calling it while OgreBot is open loads the profile again and drops unsaved changes with one warning line; unlike the `ogre` command it leaves the pause state as it was, and a failed load (no character, profile not found) prints a line and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `character` | string | `${Me.Name}` | the character whose profile to load |
| `profile` | string | `the character's default profile` | the profile name to load |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Open[${Me.Name},Group]
```

### `OpenMini`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:OpenMini`

Opens the OgreBot mini toolbar on its own, without loading a profile, and prints a line. If the mini toolbar is already open it does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:OpenMini
```

### `RefreshTargets`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:RefreshTargets`

Re-reads which aliases and targets resolve right now and sends them to the OgreBot window's Target dropdown. It does nothing when the main window is closed.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:RefreshTargets
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Reload`

Reads the loaded profile again from disk, dropping unsaved changes with one warning line, and refreshes the cast stack and the open window. It does nothing when no profile is loaded; OgreBotAPI.Bot:Reload is a different call that restarts the whole bot.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Reload
```

### `ReloadKeyBinds`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadKeyBinds`

Reads the shared key binds file again (forward, backward and the other movement keys) and prints the new forward and backward keys. Another EQ2 session on this PC sends it after a key is changed.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadKeyBinds
```

### `ReloadUi`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadUi`

Reloads the in-game window pages from disk, then reopens the OgreBot main window and mini toolbar if they were open, with the same profile and settings. Nothing in the bot is reloaded or reset; this is what `ogre ui reload` runs.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadUi
```

### `Research`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Research[mode]`

Runs the Ability Research check: it opens the Knowledge window and, with go or run, claims finished research and starts the next ability from the saved priority list, then closes the window. With no mode or any other word it only reads the window and says what it would do (trace also logs each window read), and a call while a check is running is ignored.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `preview` | go or run for the real run, trace for a logged preview; anything else is a preview |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Research[go]
```

### `Save`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Save`

Writes the loaded profile's changes to disk and prints each file it wrote. With nothing loaded or nothing changed it prints that and writes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Save
```

### `SaveProfileAs`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SaveProfileAs[name]`

Overwrites another profile with the current settings, unsaved changes included, and switches to it. It fails with a console line when that profile does not exist or is the loaded one.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the profile to overwrite; a b64: prefix marks a base64 name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SaveProfileAs[Solo]
```

### `ScanItems`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ScanItems`

Asks for a scan of equipped gear, inventory and adornments on the next pulse, to fill the Items tab's source list. The request is dropped when no profile is loaded or the in-game UI is not ready, and opening OgreBot already runs one.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ScanItems
```

### `SetDefault`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SetDefault[name]`

Makes a named profile the one this character loads by default, and writes that to the profile file at once. It fails with a console line when nothing is loaded or the profile does not exist.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SetDefault[Group]
```

### `UplinkConnect`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkConnect`

Connects this PC's uplink to every PC on the Uplink Info list except this one, spaced out, and prints how many it did (or that there is nothing to do). A second connect or disconnect from the same session within 3 seconds is ignored and only written to the log.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkConnect
```

### `UplinkDisconnect`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkDisconnect`

Disconnects this PC's uplink from every PC on the Uplink Info list except this one, and prints how many it did (or that there is nothing to do). A second connect or disconnect from the same session within 3 seconds is ignored and only written to the log.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkDisconnect
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.OSA

## Methods

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Close`

Closes the On-Screen Assistant window and stops its NPC scan, including an open that is still being retried. It does not untick the Enable On-Screen Assistant setting, so the window opens again only when that setting is next switched on (or at the next load while it is ticked).

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Close
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Open`

Opens the On-Screen Assistant (OSA) window, the same as `ogre osa`: a live list of the NPCs around you, named NPCs first and then by distance, up to 35 rows, refreshed about 5 times a second within the Settings scan radius (50 until a value is set, at most 200). It does nothing while the window is already up, and it does not tick the Enable On-Screen Assistant setting, which opens and closes the window by itself whenever it changes.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Open
```

### `Target`

`ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Target[id]`

Targets the actor with the given ID at once by sending the `target <id>` command, which is what clicking a row in the OSA window does. A call with no ID prints a line and targets nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | int |  | ID of the actor to target |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Target[${Target.Target.ID}]
```
