# ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer

## Methods

### `BuyMissions`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissions[flag...]`

Starts a run that buys Overseer missions at the merchant on this session, using this character's Overseer Buy tab with any flags overriding it: -season N, -colour C, -num N, -amount N (at most 20), -replenishonly, -scribe or -noscribe, -destroy or -nodestroy, -gettogh or -nogettogh (go to the guild hall when done); unknown words are skipped. Refused with a console line when OgreBot is not open with a profile, a buy run is already going, or the first argument is not a -flag - the same run OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions queues with a for-who.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag...` | string |  | Optional flags, one per argument, each value as its own argument after its flag; none uses the Overseer Buy tab as saved |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissions[-season,2,-amount,5]
```

### `BuyMissionsStatus`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStatus`

Prints whether the Overseer mission buy run is idle or, if running, the phase it is in.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStatus
```

### `BuyMissionsStop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStop`

Aborts the Overseer mission buy run in progress and prints the reason. Prints "nothing running." when idle; same as `ogre end buyoverseermissions`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStop
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Run`

Starts a manual Overseer run on this session now, skipping the 60-minute throttle; it uses OgreBot's Overseer tab when OgreBot is open, and the defaults (complete finished quests, add bag missions, start mishaps and new quests, take rewards) when it is not. Refused with a console line when any argument is passed, a run is already going, a bag-mission add is busy, or 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked - the same run as OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests and `ogre overseer`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Run
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Status`

Prints the Overseer run's current phase, whether it is running, and how many quests it has started and completed. When idle after a run it also prints roughly how many seconds until the next automatic run is allowed.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Stop`

Ends the Overseer run in progress on this session and prints "run aborted", or prints "nothing to stop" when idle. Same as `ogre end overseer`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Stop
```


# ISXOgreEQ2.Paths

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:End`

Closes the Points of Interest and Paths window, which is what `ogre end paths` and the window's X do. A path being walked goes on.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:End
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open[path]`

Opens the Points of Interest and Paths window (the same as `ogre paths`), on a saved path of the zone you are in when you name one: this is the one way to open it, from a panel, a button or a script. A window already open comes to the front on that path, a path this zone does not have prints one line and the window opens with nothing picked, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | `none (nothing picked)` | The path to open on, in any case. A name with spaces may be quoted or written as several words. Leave it out to open the window with nothing picked. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open["North Loop"]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Perf

## Methods

### `Measure`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Measure[seconds,nothreads]`

Measures the frame rate and what uses each frame for a number of seconds, then prints a report to the console and the log file - the same as ogre perf. The capture starts on the next frame; if one is already running, or a word other than a number or nothreads is given, it prints a line and measures nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | int | `10` | how long to measure, 3 to 120 (values outside are clamped) |
| `nothreads` | string | `""` | the word nothreads turns off the per-thread breakdown; it may come before or after the seconds |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Measure[30]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Status`

Prints one console line saying whether a measurement is idle, about to start, or running with the seconds done and left - the same as ogre perf status.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Stop`

Ends a running measurement early and prints the report for what was measured, or cancels one that has not started yet - the same as ogre perf stop. With nothing running it prints that nothing is being measured.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:End`

Stops the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler if it runs and always closes its panel, keeping the history. This is what `ogre end potcb` and the panel's X do.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:End
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Help`

Prints the `ogre potcb` usage to the console: open, on / off, status, reset and interval.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Help
```

### `Interval`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Interval[ms]`

Sets how often the sampler reads Potency, Crit Bonus and Fervor, held between 50 and 10000 ms (a negative is 50), and prints the new value. With no value it prints the current interval; a value that is not a number keeps the interval in force and says so.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int |  | Sampling interval in milliseconds, 50 to 10000 (the sampler starts at 200). Optional: leave it out to print the current interval. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Interval[500]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Off`

Stops the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler and closes its panel, keeping the recorded history. If it was not sampling it prints "potcb: not running." and leaves the panel open.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:On`

Starts the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler, which reads the three stats every interval (default 200 ms) while you are in world, and prints one line saying so. Does nothing if it is already sampling, and does not open the panel.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:On
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Open`

Opens the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor tracker panel, starting the sampler first if it was stopped (the same as bare `ogre potcb`). If the panel is already up it stays as it is, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning while sampling still starts.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Open
```

### `Reset`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Reset`

Clears every recorded Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor figure and the sampled time, then prints "potcb: history cleared". The sampler stays on or off as it was.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Reset
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Status`

Prints every Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor figure to the console: running or stopped and time sampled, then per stat the current value and peak, the in-combat min / avg / max, time at cap, time at peak and combat time by tenth of the peak, and the overall min / avg / max. It also warns when readings were skipped because a stat showed no number.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Status
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget

## Methods

### `Ceiling`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Ceiling[us]`

Sets the shared frame ceiling and saves it; below 0 reads as 0. With no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us` | float |  | The ceiling in microseconds; 0 means none. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Ceiling[4000]
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Close`

Closes the Pulse Budget window, the same as `ogre end pulse`. The budget keeps running.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Close
```

### `JobTest`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:JobTest[state]`

A test mode for this session only: every pulse job pauses at every checkpoint, so state that does not survive a frame shows up at once. It is never saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string |  | on or 1 turns it on; any other word turns it off. Required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:JobTest[on]
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Off`

Turns the shared frame ceiling off and saves it. Each section still keeps its own slice.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:On`

Turns the shared frame ceiling on, resets the counters and saves it.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:On
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Open`

Opens the Pulse Budget window, the same as bare `ogre pulse`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Open
```

### `Report`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Report`

Prints the per-section table to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Report
```

### `Reset`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Reset`

Resets the counters.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Reset
```

### `Slice`

`ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Slice[section,us]`

Sets how long a resumable section may run per frame and saves it; a slice paces the work and never skips any of it. A missing section or value prints one warning, and a section nothing matches prints another.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | string |  | The section's name, or its number from :Report. |
| `us` | float |  | Microseconds per frame; 0 lets it run to completion. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Slice[3,200]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper

## Methods

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Help`

Prints the `ogre quest` usage lines (start, stop, status, list, reload) to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Help
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:List`

Prints what the loaded reply table holds: the total rule count, the rules that apply in every zone, the rules in each zone's own list, and the counts of ignored objects and chat captures. A zone that has its own list does not also use the every-zone rules.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:List
```

### `Off`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Off`

Stops the quest helper and prints its hail, object-click and reply counts, which add up across every run this session. When it is not running it prints 'questhelper: not running.' instead.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Off
```

### `On`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:On[option1]`

Starts the quest helper (`ogre quest`), which runs until QuestHelper:Off and about every half second answers an open NPC conversation from its reply table (or takes the only reply), otherwise hails a non-attackable NPC within 10 units that has a quest to give, update or complete, otherwise double-clicks an interactable object within 5 units that is not on its ignore list and is not a way out of the zone (a name with the word zone, teleporter or exit), logging every hail and click with its zone. It does nothing while you are moving, out of the world or in a guild hall, the hail goes through the bot's queued Hail action, and it prints one line when it starts (or says it is already running).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option1` | int | `none` | Optional. 1 = always click reply 1 and ignore the reply table; leave it out to use the table. Any other value is refused with one line and nothing starts. Calling On again while it runs switches this mode. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:On[1]
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Reload`

Re-reads the reply table from the shipped files (Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/QuestHelper/default) and your own (Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/QuestHelper/custom), warns about each file that fails to load, and prints the rule count. If no file loads at all, the table already in use is kept and the line says so instead of a loaded count.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Reload
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Status`

Prints the quest helper's state to the console: running or stopped, whether it always takes reply 1, your zone, what it last did, how long since it last acted, its hail, object-click and reply counts for this run (they start from 0 at each start), and how many reply rules are loaded.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Status
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Queue.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Queue

## Members

### `Blocking`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Blocking}`

Why the most urgent waiting entry cannot start yet, as a line like seq=5 CastAbility prio=100 age=900ms: resource busy: CastBar, or starved by a higher-priority haltQueue entry. Empty when nothing is waiting or the next entry is free to start.

**Returns:** string: the reason line; empty when nothing is held up

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Blocking}
```

### `Count`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Count}`

Number of entries in the action queue, running plus waiting.

**Returns:** int: entries running plus waiting; 0 when the queue is empty

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Count}
```

### `Enqueue`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Enqueue[priority,kind,arg0,arg1,ttlstart,ttlmax]}`

Adds an entry exactly like ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add and returns its seq, the id you pass to Status, IsDone and Remove. Reading the member is what adds the entry, so every read queues another one, and an unknown kind (ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices included) or a flow name that is not registered adds nothing and returns 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | int | `100` | Higher runs first; 0 means the default 100 |
| `kind` | string |  | What to do, any case: CastAbility, CastItem, ClickCastBar, RawCommand, Movement or Flow. ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices are not kinds here; OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbIDQueued queues an apply-verb |
| `arg0` | string |  | Depends on kind: RawCommand the console command, CastAbility the ability id or name, CastItem the item name, ClickCastBar the actor id, Movement x,y,z with an optional precision, Flow the flow name |
| `arg1` | string |  | Depends on kind: CastAbility the target name (empty = current target), CastItem the equip slot (empty = the bag item by name), ClickCastBar the wait in tenths of a second (empty = 4 seconds), Flow its arguments |
| `ttlstart` | int | `0` | Milliseconds the entry may wait to start before it is dropped with status Expired; 0 = no limit |
| `ttlmax` | int | `0` | Milliseconds the entry may run before it is stopped with status Aborted; 0 = no limit |

**Returns:** int64: the new entry's seq (1 and up); 0 when the kind is unknown

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Enqueue[100,RawCommand,"echo queued"]}
```

### `Entry`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Entry[index]}`

One queue entry as a readable line, such as seq=12 prio=100 RawCommand waiting age=40ms arg0=echo hi, where seq is the entry's id. The index counts from 1, running entries first and then waiting ones, each sorted by priority then by the order they were added.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | int |  | Position in the queue counting from 1: running entries first, then waiting ones, highest priority first |

**Returns:** string: the entry line; empty when the index is 0, past the end or missing

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Entry[1]}
```

### `EntryJSON`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.EntryJSON[index]}`

One queue entry as a JSON object with seq, priority, kind, status (running or waiting), holds, haltQueue, haltCastStack, ageMs, blocked, arg0, arg1 and label. Same index as Entry, counting from 1, so a loop from 1 to Count reads the whole queue.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | int |  | Position in the queue counting from 1: running entries first, then waiting ones, highest priority first |

**Returns:** string: the entry as a JSON object; {} when the index is 0, past the end or missing

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.EntryJSON[1]}
```

### `InFlight`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.InFlight}`

Whether any queue entry is running right now.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when at least one entry is running; FALSE when none is

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.InFlight}
```

### `IsDone`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.IsDone[seq]}`

Whether the queue entry with that seq has finished in any way (Done, Failed, Expired, Aborted or Removed), so a wait loop never hangs on a failed entry; read Status for how it ended. A seq that finished and has since been forgotten also reads TRUE, while a seq never issued reads FALSE.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seq` | int64 |  | The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the entry has finished, however it ended; FALSE while it is waiting or running, or when the seq was never issued

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.IsDone[1]}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Status[seq]}`

The state of the queue entry with that seq. Unknown means the seq was never issued or finished too long ago to remember (only the most recent 256 are kept).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seq` | int64 |  | The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew |

**Returns:** string: Pending, InFlight, Done, Failed, Expired, Aborted, Removed or Unknown

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Status[1]}
```

## Methods

### `Add`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add[priority,kind,arg0,arg1,ttlstart,ttlmax]`

Adds an action to the priority queue, which runs it on its turn once the cast bar or movement it needs is free (highest priority first, even while OgreBot is paused), and prints an Add seq=N line to the console. Waiting and running entries are dropped on a zone change or when OgreBot ends, a Flow lives as its registered flow does, with that flow's holds and halts, and a flow name that is not registered gets one line; use the Enqueue member instead when you need the seq back.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | int | `100` | Higher runs first; 0 means the default 100 |
| `kind` | string |  | What to do, any case: CastAbility, CastItem, ClickCastBar, RawCommand, Movement or Flow. ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices are not kinds here; OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbIDQueued queues an apply-verb |
| `arg0` | string |  | Depends on kind: RawCommand the console command, CastAbility the ability id or name, CastItem the item name, ClickCastBar the actor id, Movement x,y,z with an optional precision, Flow the flow name |
| `arg1` | string |  | Depends on kind: CastAbility the target name (empty = current target), CastItem the equip slot (empty = the bag item by name), ClickCastBar the wait in tenths of a second (empty = 4 seconds), Flow its arguments |
| `ttlstart` | int | `0` | Milliseconds the entry may wait to start before it is dropped with status Expired; 0 = no limit |
| `ttlmax` | int | `0` | Milliseconds the entry may run before it is stopped with status Aborted; 0 = no limit. For a Flow it can only shorten the flow's own limit |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add[100,RawCommand,"echo queued"]
```

### `Remove`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Remove[seq]`

Removes the waiting queue entry with that seq (its Status becomes Removed) and prints the result to the console. A running entry is not removed, and an unknown or missing seq only prints that there is no such entry.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seq` | int64 |  | The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Remove[1]
```

### `Spew`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Spew`

Prints every queue entry to the console, running entries then waiting ones, one line each starting with its seq, then a line on how to remove one. Prints empty - 0 entries when the queue is empty.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Spew
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver

## Members

### `Running`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Running}`

TRUE while a quiver refill is moving ammo out of your bags, or while the ammo depot pull it started is still running. A depot errand started by something else does not count.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while either half of a quiver refill runs; FALSE when idle.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Running}
```

### `Status`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Status}`

Progress of a quiver refill: the bag half with its count, then the ammo depot pull while that runs.

**Returns:** string: "idle", "filling from bags (done/total)", "arming the depot pull" or "pulling ammo from the depot".

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Status}
```

## Methods

### `Refill`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Refill`

The engine behind `ogre quiver` and the quiver step of the Inventory Manager chain: moves matching ammo from your bags into the equipped quiver or pouch (1 s apart, 2 s in combat), then, in a guild hall, tops it up from the ammo depot, warning and stopping when no ammo container is equipped or the ammo kind cannot be told. To tell arrows, bolts or thrown ammo it makes ONE SERVER CALL (the equipped ranged weapon's `.ToItemInfo.SubType`, only when that item's info is already available), then falls back to what is in the container, then to the container's name.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Refill
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Stop`

Stops both halves of a quiver refill, the bag moves and the ammo depot pull it started, and prints "quiver: stopped.". Prints nothing when neither half is running; it is the same stop `ogre end quiver` uses.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Stop
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Radar.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Radar

## Methods

### `Budget`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Budget[n,ms]`

The read budget: how many actors a pulse may read their slow fields, and how old a slow field may get. With no argument it prints both; an age out of range is refused, but the actor count is still written.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int |  | Actors per pulse, 0-5000. Optional. |
| `ms` | int |  | The oldest a slow field may get, 0-600000 ms. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Budget[60,3000]
```

### `Cap`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Cap[n]`

Draws only the nearest n blips, where 0 means no cap; it bounds what is drawn, not what is read. With no argument it prints the cap, and out of range is refused.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int |  | The cap, 0-5000. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Cap[200]
```

### `CfgPath`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:CfgPath`

# ISXOgreEQ2.Refine

## Methods

### `Bags`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Bags[bags...]`

Sets which carried bags (1 to 6) a refine run scans - bags 1 and 2 by default - and echoes the new list. A missing list is refused with a console line, anything that is not bag numbers, all or none prints the usage line and changes nothing, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bags...` | string |  | bag numbers 1 to 6, as separate arguments or one list such as 1,2,5; each digit is one bag, so 12 means bags 1 and 2; or all / none |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Bags[1,2,3]
```

### `Plan`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Plan`

A dry run: scans the selected bags with the current settings and prints each item a run would refine (bag, slot, quantity, name) and why the others were skipped. Nothing is refined, and out of the world it only prints a warning.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Plan
```

### `Rare`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rare[value]`

Turns refining of Rare resources on or off (off by default) and echoes the new setting. A missing value is refused with a console line, a value that is not on or off prints the usage line, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | string |  | on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rare[off]
```

### `Raw`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Raw[value]`

Turns refining of Raw resources on or off (on by default) and echoes the new setting. A missing value is refused with a console line, a value that is not on or off prints the usage line, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | string |  | on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Raw[on]
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Reload`

Re-reads the refiner's resource list now: the shipped files under Ogre/EQ2/Refine/default plus your own under OgreSave/EQ2/Refine/custom. It echoes how many resources loaded, and a warning for any file it could not read or when no files were found.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Reload
```

### `Rewards`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rewards[value]`

When on, every reward window that appears while a refine run is in progress is accepted automatically - including ones unrelated to refining, such as a quest reward. Off by default; a missing value is refused with a console line, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | string |  | on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rewards[off]
```

### `Start`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Start`

Starts one background pass over the selected carried bags: for each Raw or Rare resource on the refiner's list (provisioner resources skipped) it uses your Refine ability, refines the item until the stack is gone or a try limit is reached, and answers the refine confirm window itself while the run lasts. It refuses with a console line when a run is already going, you are not in the world, the resource list is empty, you lack the Refine ability, or Raw and Rare are both off.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Start
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Status`

Prints the refiner's state to the console: how many resources its list holds, whether Raw and Rare are on, which bags it scans, whether reward windows are auto-accepted, and the progress of a run in flight, then the usage line. The same as `ogre refine` or `ogre refine status`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Stop`

Stops a refine run in progress, the same as `ogre end refine`. When nothing is running it prints "refine: not running." to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames

## Methods

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Reload`

Re-reads both replenish name files now, warning in the console about any problem it finds, then prints the same report as ReplenishNames:Show. A changed file is picked up on its next use anyway, so this is only needed to see the result straight away.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Reload
```

### `Show`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Show`

Prints the fallback potion, food and drink names the replenish options use when nothing better is set, plus where the shipped file and your own file (OgreSave/EQ2/Replenish/custom/replenish-names.json) live. The files are re-read first when either has changed since the last read.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Show
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler

## Members

### `Active`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Active[key]}`

Whether a timer with this key still has a fire pending. Keys ignore case; a one-shot timer reads FALSE once it has fired.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key) |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when a fire is still pending for this key; FALSE when there is no such timer.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Active[MyTimerEvent]}
```

### `Count`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Count}`

How many keyed timers are pending in the scheduler. The encounter engine's timers live in the same table, so they count too.

**Returns:** int: number of pending keyed timers.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Count}
```

### `Remaining`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Remaining[key]}`

Milliseconds until the next fire of the timer with this key. Reads 0 when there is no such timer or it is due now.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key) |

**Returns:** int64: milliseconds to the next fire; 0 when there is no such timer or it is due.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Remaining[MyTimerEvent]}
```

## Methods

### `Cancel`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Cancel[key]`

Stops the timer with this key before it fires again. Keys ignore case, and a key with no timer does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key) |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Cancel[MyTimerEvent]
```

### `ClearNonPersistent`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:ClearNonPersistent`

Cancels every script and encounter timer that was not armed with -persistent, and leaves the bot's own pending delayed casts and actions. Finishing a zone clears every non-persistent timer, the bot's included.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:ClearNonPersistent
```

### `FireEvent`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEvent[delay,eventName,payload,-persistent,-key]`

Fires the LavishScript event eventName once after the delay, always with exactly one argument (the payload, or an empty string). Arming a key that is already pending replaces that timer, and unless -persistent is given the timer is dropped when you finish zoning; a bad delay such as 30x fires nothing and warns on the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delay` | string |  | how long to wait: a whole number of milliseconds, or a number with ms, s, m or h (30s, 1.5s, 2m) |
| `eventName` | string |  | the LavishScript event to fire |
| `payload` | string | `""` | the one argument passed to the event; the first extra word not starting with a dash |
| `-persistent` | switch | `off` | keep the timer across zoning |
| `-key` | switch | `the event name` | -key &lt;k>: the timer's key, case-insensitive |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEvent[5s,MyTimerEvent,hello]
```

### `FireEventEvery`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEventEvery[interval,eventName,repeats,payload,-persistent,-key]`

Fires the LavishScript event eventName every interval, repeats times, always with exactly one argument (the payload, or an empty string); a missing, 0 or negative repeats means forever. Re-arming a pending key replaces it, and unless -persistent is given the timer is dropped when you finish zoning; a bad interval fires nothing and warns on the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interval` | string |  | time between fires: a whole number of milliseconds, or a number with ms, s, m or h; the first fire comes one interval after the call |
| `eventName` | string |  | the LavishScript event to fire |
| `repeats` | int | `forever` | how many times to fire; 0 or less fires until cancelled |
| `payload` | string | `""` | the one argument passed to the event; the first extra word not starting with a dash |
| `-persistent` | switch | `off` | keep the timer across zoning |
| `-key` | switch | `the event name` | -key &lt;k>: the timer's key, case-insensitive |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEventEvery[10s,MyTimerEvent,6,tick]
```

### `Spew`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Spew`

Prints every pending keyed timer to the console, the encounter engine's included: a count line, then one line per timer with its key, event, milliseconds to the next fire, how many times it has fired, and whether it is persistent.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Spew
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn

## Members

### `ChestId`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.ChestId}`

The actor ID of the Exquisite Chest that spawned in this zone, taken from the spawn feed. It goes back to 0 when that chest despawns or you zone.

**Returns:** int64: the chest's actor ID; 0 when there is none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.ChestId}
```

### `DespawnsDispatched`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.DespawnsDispatched}`

The number of despawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded.

**Returns:** int64: despawn events dispatched.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.DespawnsDispatched}
```

### `Dispatched`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Dispatched}`

The total number of spawn and despawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded. It is SpawnsDispatched plus DespawnsDispatched.

**Returns:** int64: spawn plus despawn events dispatched.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Dispatched}
```

### `HasChest`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.HasChest}`

Whether an Exquisite Chest is up in this zone, the same test as ChestId being non-zero.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when ChestId is not 0; FALSE otherwise.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.HasChest}
```

### `IsLive`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.IsLive[id]}`

Whether the actor ID is in the live set: seen spawning (or present when the zone settled) and not yet despawned. The set is wiped when you zone and filled again once the new zone settles, so it can read FALSE for a moment after zoning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | int64 |  | The actor ID to test. |

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when that actor is live; FALSE when it is not, or when no ID is given.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.IsLive[${Target.ID}]}
```

### `LiveCount`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.LiveCount}`

How many actor IDs are in the live set for this zone. It drops to 0 while zoning and refills once the new zone settles.

**Returns:** int: the number of live actors tracked.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.LiveCount}
```

### `OnSpawnDelay`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.OnSpawnDelay}`

How long after an actor spawns the delayed spawn event EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed fires for it (only if it is still live). The default is 1000 ms and the most is 60000; SetOnSpawnDelay changes it for this session only.

**Returns:** int: the delay in milliseconds.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.OnSpawnDelay}
```

### `Received`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Received}`

The total number of actor spawn and despawn events received from the game since the extension loaded. It is a diagnostic counter and is not reset by zoning.

**Returns:** int64: spawn plus despawn events received.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Received}
```

### `SpawnsDispatched`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.SpawnsDispatched}`

The number of spawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded.

**Returns:** int64: spawn events dispatched.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.SpawnsDispatched}
```

### `Subscribers`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Subscribers}`

How many internal listeners are attached to the spawn feed. It counts spawn, despawn and delayed-spawn listeners together.

**Returns:** int: the number of attached listeners.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Subscribers}
```

## Methods

### `DelayStatus`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:DelayStatus`

Prints the delayed spawn event's state to the console: the delay, the per-drain cap, what is waiting and ready, and the counters since the last zone-in.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:DelayStatus
```

### `ResetOnSpawnDelay`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:ResetOnSpawnDelay`

Puts the delay before EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed back to the default of 1000 ms and prints the value to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:ResetOnSpawnDelay
```

### `SetOnSpawnCap`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnCap`

Sets how many due spawns one drain may emit, for this session only, held between 1 and 5000 (0 or a negative is 1), and prints the value in force to the console. A value that is not a number keeps the cap and says so; with no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<k>` | int |  | The per-drain cap, 1 to 5000. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnCap[25]
```

### `SetOnSpawnDelay`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnDelay[<ms>]`

Sets the delay before EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed fires, for this session only (it is not saved), and prints the value in force to the console. More than 60000 ms is held at 60000; a value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is refused with a warning and the delay is unchanged.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<ms>` | int |  | The delay in milliseconds, 0 to 60000. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnDelay[1500]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:Status`

Prints the spawn consumer's counters to the console: spawns and despawns seen, duplicate and unknown ids, the live actor count, the chest id and the router's subscribers and throughput.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:Status
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Targeting.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting

## Members

### `ActiveList`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.ActiveList}`

The name of the saved auto-target list last loaded or saved into the working list, like OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.ListName. Reading it also refreshes the saved-list catalogue for the current zone.

**Returns:** string: the saved-list name; "" when none is loaded or when not in the world.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.ActiveList}
```

### `AssistId`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.AssistId}`

The assist decision as one number, read fresh on each call - the same call as OgreBotAPI.Assist.TargetID. It answers even when the Auto Assist box is off.

**Returns:** int64: greater than 0 is the ID this character would target; 0 when it picks its own target; -1 when its current target should be left alone; NULL when not in the world.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.AssistId}
```

### `Enabled`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.Enabled}`

Whether either targeting engine is switched on: the Auto Assist box or the auto-target box. This is not OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.Enabled, which reads only the auto-target box.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the Auto Assist box or the auto-target box is ticked; FALSE when both are off.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.Enabled}
```

### `InControl`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.InControl}`

Whether this character picks its own target instead of following someone else's - the same call as OgreBotAPI.Assist.InControl. With the Auto Assist box off it reads TRUE.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when this character picks its own target; FALSE when it follows another player, and FALSE when not in the world.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.InControl}
```

### `SavedList`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedList[index]}`

The name of one saved auto-target list for the current zone, counting from 1 in file order, the same as OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.SavedName.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | int |  | Which saved list, counting from 1. 0, or text that is not a number, reads empty. |

**Returns:** string: the saved list's name; "" when index is 0 or past the count, when no index is given, or when not in the world.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedList[1]}
```

### `SavedListCount`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedListCount}`

The number of saved auto-target lists for the current zone, like OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.SavedCount. Unlike that member it reloads the zone's catalogue first when the zone has changed, so it never shows the previous zone.

**Returns:** int: the number of saved lists; 0 when the zone has none or when not in the world.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedListCount}
```

## Methods

### `ClearList`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:ClearList`

Empties the working auto-target list and blanks ActiveList - OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget:Clear without the for-who. Auto-target then falls back to the profile's own AutoTarget entries (nothing to pick if it has none) until a list is loaded or entries are added, and saved lists on disk are not touched.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:ClearList
```

### `LoadList`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:LoadList[<name>]`

Replaces the working auto-target list with the saved list of that name for the current zone (the name is matched ignoring case) - OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget:LoadSaved without the for-who. If the zone has no list by that name, or you are not in the world, nothing changes and nothing is printed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | string |  | The saved list's name. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:LoadList[Trash]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Status`

Prints the assist state to this character's console, the same as `ogre assist`: the Auto Assist, auto-target and direct targeting boxes, the decision and why, the assist anchor, each assist-list entry with their target, and your own target. Prints nothing when not in the world.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Status
```

### `Target`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Target[id]`

Queues a one-time retarget to the actor ID, issued on the next pulse even while OgreBot is paused; it beats auto-target and assist but yields to a target lock or a manual target. It is skipped when that is already your target or is you, and does nothing without an ID.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | int64 |  | The actor ID to target. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Target[${Target.ID}]
```

### `Tick`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Tick`

Runs the assist and auto-target decision now and queues any retarget for the next pulse; it never targets during the call. The bot already does this on its own every 250 ms, and with auto-target on and entries to pick from each call can run a nearby-actor scan, so a script rarely needs it.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Tick
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner

## Methods

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Clear[toon,task]`

Clears error and backoff records and saves them. Last-completed stamps are left alone.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `toon` | string |  | Only this character. Optional: with none, every character. |
| `task` | string |  | Only this task. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Clear[Bob,packpony]
```

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Close`

Closes the Lists window and leaves a run going. :End stops it too.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Close
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:End`

Stops a run and closes the Lists window, the same as `ogre end taskrunner` and the window's X.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:End
```

### `Lists`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Lists`

Prints the configured lists and their characters to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Lists
```

### `Now`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Now`

Scans for due work now rather than at the next interval. Only while the runner is idle.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Now
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Open`

Opens the TaskRunner Lists window, the same as bare `ogre taskrunner`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Open
```

### `Plan`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Plan[list]`

Prints what is due to the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | string |  | Only this list. Optional: with none, the list this session runs. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Plan[daily]
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Reload`

Reads the config again. Refused while a batch is in flight; if the list you are on is gone, the run stops.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Reload
```

### `Run`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Run[list,options]`

Starts this session on one list, the same as `ogre taskrunner run <list>` and `ogre taskrunner -list <list>`. An unknown option, or no list, prints one warning and nothing starts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | string |  | The list's name, after an optional -list or -l; required. |
| `options` | string |  | once or loop, stagger or nostagger, with or without a leading dash, one argument each. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Run[daily,once]
```

### `Start`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Start`

Starts cycling all configured characters. Refused while a batch is in flight, when the config is off, with no characters, or when lists exist and none was named: use :Run then.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Start
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Status`

Prints what the runner is doing to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Status
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Stop`

Stops a run and leaves the window up.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Stop
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.Tour

## Methods

### `Close`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Close`

Closes the New User Tour window, and its intro if that is still playing. The tour is not marked as seen, so it opens by itself again on the next load.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Close
```

### `Done`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Done`

Marks the New User Tour finished: prints 'tour: completed', saves it as seen so it no longer opens on load, and closes the window, then starts the Migration Assistant's automatic run, which copies any OldBot settings files that have no new copy yet and shows a progress window only when something is copied. A call when the tour is not open does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Done
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Open`

Opens the New User Tour, the same as `ogre tour`: a short walkthrough of three window controls (drag to resize, right-click the title bar, Save Position), which also opens by itself on first load until it has been finished or skipped. It hides the InnerSpace console if that is showing and prints 'tour opened', and it does nothing while the tour is already up.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Open
```

### `Skip`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Skip`

Skips the New User Tour: prints 'tour: skipped', saves it as seen so it no longer opens on load, closes the window and, like Tour:Done, starts the Migration Assistant's automatic run of any OldBot settings not yet copied. A call when the tour is not open does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Skip
```

### `Step`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Step[step]`

Called by the tour window when it moves to a new step, and all it does is print 'tour: advanced to step N' to the console. Nothing is saved and the tour window does not change, so a script has no reason to call it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | int | `0` | the step number to print (the tour has steps 1 to 3); text that is not a number prints 0 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Step[2]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh

## Members

### `TMActive`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMActive}`

TRUE while a travel route is running on this character. It reads FALSE while idle, after arriving or giving up, and while a Go is still waiting for a zone to finish loading.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when a route is running; FALSE otherwise

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMActive}
```

### `TMBias`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMBias[kind]}`

The cost multiplier the planner uses for one kind of hop (door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item): 1 is neutral, below 1 prefers it, above 1 avoids it, 0 or less forbids it. Every kind starts at 1.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string |  | the hop kind: door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item |

**Returns:** float: the multiplier for that kind; -1 when the kind is unknown or missing

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMBias[bell]}
```

### `TMCurrentHop`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMCurrentHop}`

A one-line description of the hop in progress: the kind (door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item), the from and to zone short names, and the travel action and destination label when there is one. Empty when no hop is in progress, including after arrival.

**Returns:** string: the current hop's description; empty when there is none

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMCurrentHop}
```

### `TMDataErrors`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrors}`

How many travel data files had a problem at the last load, counting files that were skipped and files that loaded with a warning. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.

**Returns:** int: the number of problem files; 0 when the data loaded cleanly

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrors}
```

### `TMDataErrorText`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrorText}`

The problem report from the last load, one line per file: its path, which layer it came from (default or custom) and the message. Empty when every file loaded cleanly, or until the travel data has loaded.

**Returns:** string: the problem report, one file per line; empty when clean

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrorText}
```

### `TMEdges`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMEdges}`

How many zone-to-zone connections (doors, zone lines, guild hall amenities, travel items and so on) the loaded travel data holds. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.

**Returns:** int: the number of connections in the travel data

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMEdges}
```

### `TMFeatures`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMFeatures}`

One line per account feature the travel data can require (the expansion Friends and Family features), with this character's answer: YES or no, and whether it was scanned or set by you, or unanswered. A no from a scan is checked again after a week, a YES or your own answer is kept, and the lines are read by the travel engine about once a second while you are in the world.

**Returns:** string: one line per account feature

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMFeatures}
```

### `TMGoal`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMGoal}`

The short zone name of the destination of the current or last route, such as antonica. Empty before any route has started.

**Returns:** string: the destination zone short name; empty before the first route

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMGoal}
```

### `TMHop`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHop}`

The number of the hop the route is on, counting from 1. It reads 1 before any route has run and one more than TMHops once the route has arrived.

**Returns:** int: the current hop number, 1-based

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHop}
```

### `TMHops`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHops}`

How many hops the current plan has. After a re-plan this is the hop count of the new plan for the rest of the trip, not the original total.

**Returns:** int: the hop count of the current plan; 0 before any route

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHops}
```

### `TMParty`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMParty}`

For the current or last route: the route id, how many group members it counted, and either "everyone is here" or the names of members not yet in this zone and settled. It is empty before any route has started, and read by the travel engine about once a second while you are in the world.

**Returns:** string: the group status line; empty before the first route

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMParty}
```

### `TMReason`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReason}`

Why the last route stopped, or what its last step reported, such as "stopped by request" or "replaced by a new route". Empty while a route runs normally.

**Returns:** string: the stop reason or last step message; empty when there is none

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReason}
```

### `TMReplans`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReplans}`

How many times the current route has re-planned around a hop that failed. A route gives up after 3 re-plans.

**Returns:** int: the re-plan count for the current or last route

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReplans}
```

### `TMRoute`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMRoute}`

The whole current plan as text, one numbered hop per line in the same form as TMCurrentHop. It still holds the last plan after the route ends.

**Returns:** string: the plan, one hop per line; empty before any route

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMRoute}
```

### `TMStagger`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMStagger}`

The start delay in milliseconds per group member for group travel, so members do not all set off at once. The default is 10000, and 0 means everybody starts at once.

**Returns:** int: milliseconds of start delay per group member

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMStagger}
```

### `TMState`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMState}`

The step the route is on: idle, hop-start, walk, wait-for-group, ride, act, verify, done or failed. It keeps done or failed after a route ends until the next route starts.

**Returns:** string: the current route step name

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMState}
```

### `TMValidate`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMValidate}`

A health check of the loaded travel data, one issue per line. Empty when no issues are found, or until the travel data has loaded.

**Returns:** string: the issues, one per line; empty when there are none

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMValidate}
```

### `TMZones`

`${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMZones}`

How many zones the loaded travel data knows. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.

**Returns:** int: the number of zones in the travel data

```text
echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMZones}
```

## Methods

### `Go`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Go[destination,poi]`

Starts a route like OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh, from your current zone to the destination, walking and using doors, zone lines, bells, spires, druid rings, the fast-travel map, guild hall amenities and travel items in your bags as needed; it replaces a running route, whoever started it, only when the new one can be planned. Problems (no destination, unknown destination with suggestions, current zone not in the travel data, no route) are echoed to the console, a Go made while zoning waits for the zone to settle, and the route moves with OgreBot closed too - TravelMesh:Stop ends it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | string |  | the zone to travel to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case |
| `poi` | string | `none` | optional point of interest in the destination zone to finish at; one the zone data does not list is reported and the trip still goes to the zone |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Go[Antonica,"Druid Rings"]
```

### `GoGroup`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:GoGroup[destination,poi]`

Like OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshGroup: starts your own route as Go does, then sends -TravelMesh for the same destination to the rest of your group through OgreConsole, so each member plans its own route from where it stands, with starts staggered by TMStagger. If your own route cannot be planned the error is echoed and nothing is sent; the other members' copies run as OgreBot routes, so they are stopped with -TravelMeshStop.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | string |  | the zone to travel to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case |
| `poi` | string | `none` | optional point of interest in the destination zone to finish at; one the zone data does not list is reported and the trip still goes to the zone |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:GoGroup[Antonica]
```

### `Preview`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Preview[destination]`

Plans a route from your current zone to the destination and prints it to the console without moving: a summary line with the hop count and rough time in seconds, then one numbered hop per line. An unknown destination prints an "unknown destination" line with suggestions, and no destination prints an error.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | string |  | the zone to plan to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Preview[Antonica]
```

### `Reload`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Reload`

Re-reads the travel data from Ogre/EQ2/Travel/default and your own OgreSave/EQ2/Travel/custom files and echoes a summary of zones, connections, files and errors. Any running route is stopped first, whoever started it; if the first load has not finished within 5 seconds it says so and changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Reload
```

### `ScanFeatures`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:ScanFeatures`

Runs the game's show_account_features command to answer this character's unanswered or expired account features, and echoes a status line. Each feature is scanned at most once per session, a scan also starts by itself when a route is planned, and when nothing is scanned (out of the world included) the line says every feature is already answered.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:ScanFeatures
```

### `SetBias`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetBias[kind,multiplier]`

Sets how much the planner likes one kind of hop: 1 is neutral, below 1 prefers it, above 1 avoids it, 0 or less forbids it, and the new value is echoed. It applies to the next plan and is not saved; a multiplier that is not a number sets the normal bias of 1 and says so.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string |  | the hop kind: door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item; anything else is refused with a console error |
| `multiplier` | float |  | the cost multiplier: 1 neutral, below 1 prefer, above 1 avoid, 0 or less forbid; a word is 1 |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetBias[druid,0.5]
```

### `SetFeature`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetFeature[flag,value]`

Saves your own answer for one account feature for this character in OgreSave/EQ2/Travel/account-features.json; it is permanent and never scanned over, and the answer is echoed. A feature name the travel data does not use is refused with a line naming the ones it does, a blank value prints an error, and a word that is not yes or no leaves the feature as it is and says so.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flag` | string |  | the account feature name as TMFeatures shows it, such as roc_friends_and_family, in any case |
| `value` | bool |  | TRUE, 1, yes or on means this character has the feature; FALSE, 0, no or off means it does not |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetFeature[roc_friends_and_family,TRUE]
```

### `SetStagger`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetStagger[ms]`

Sets the start delay in milliseconds per group member for group travel (0 = everybody at once) and echoes it. A negative number is stored as 0, a value that is not a number counts as 0, and the setting is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | int |  | milliseconds of start delay per group member; 0 starts everybody at once |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetStagger[5000]
```

### `Stop`

`ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Stop[-force]`

Cancels a route started with this object's Go or GoGroup, including one still waiting for a zone to settle. A route someone else started is refused with one line naming the owner and how to stop it, and -force stops it anyway.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-force` | switch |  | stop the route whoever started it |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Stop
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/isxogreeq2/Watcher.md

# ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher

## Methods

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:End`

Turns off both the name watch (Find) and the shiny watch (TrackShiny), closes the Watcher window and prints which of them were on; the off state is saved, so they stay off on the next load. This is what `ogre end watcher` and the window's close button do.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:End
```

### `Find`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:Find[word...]`

Watches for actors by exact name, case not mattering (`ogre find`): given names it replaces the watch list, arms and checks the zone once, then each time a watched name spawns it prints where, broadcasts '&lt;you>: APPEARED: &lt;name>' to your bot sessions and sets an in-game waypoint on it, and it prints when one despawns (these alerts are skipped in a guild hall). A first word that is an option does that instead (-add or -remove &lt;name>, -clear, -list, -on, -off, -scan, -status, -panel opens the Watcher window, -rorr adds the four Renewal of Ro researchers to the names), no words prints the usage, and the list and armed state are saved and restored on the next load.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word...` | string | `none (prints the usage)` | the names to watch (quote a name that has spaces), or one option first followed by its value |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:Find[${Target.Name}]
```

### `TrackShiny`

`ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:TrackShiny[word...]`

Watches for shiny harvest nodes of one colour within 100 units, every 500 ms by default (`ogre trackshiny`): when it finds one it did not just announce, it prints '&lt;colour> shiny!', broadcasts it to your bot sessions and sets an in-game waypoint on it. No word arms it on Purple, a colour name (White, Green, Purple, Red, BlueShimmer, Blue) arms that colour and an unknown one is refused with the list, the options are -off, -status, -colours (or -colors), -interval &lt;ms> (held to 250..30000) and -panel, and the settings are saved and restored on the next load.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word...` | string | `Purple` | a colour to watch for, or one option first followed by its value |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:TrackShiny[Red]
```

# ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset

## Methods

### `Add`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Add[zone]`

Adds one zone to the reset queue and prints how many it holds.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string |  | The zone's name; several words are joined into one name; required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Add["The Feerrott"]
```

### `AddFilter`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:AddFilter[filter]`

Adds every zone the filter picks from the last read to the reset queue and prints how many.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string |  | resettable, noraid or notlocked. Optional: anything else reads as resettable. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:AddFilter[resettable]
```

### `Clear`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Clear`

Empties the reset queue.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Clear
```

### `Dump`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Dump`

Prints the zone table from the last read to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Dump
```

### `End`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:End`

Stops what this tool asked for, drops what it had queued to run, and closes the window, the same as `ogre end zone` and the window's X. A reset that an Instance Controller run or a script asked for carries on.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:End
```

### `Flags`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Flags[flags]`

The flag form, the same as `ogre zone -zone ...`; -all with -force is refused. -h prints the usage.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flags` | string |  | -zone names one zone and takes every word up to the next flag, -force force resets it and spends a charge, -all resets every resettable zone, -allowRaid includes raid zones, -fleet goes to the For Who selection; one argument each; required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Flags[-zone,"The Feerrott"]
```

### `Force`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Force[zone]`

Force resets one zone, which SPENDS one of your limited reset charges and cannot be undone. With no zone it prints one warning and does nothing, and it is refused while a flow runs.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string |  | The zone's name; several words are joined into one name; required. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Force["The Feerrott"]
```

### `Help`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Help`

Prints the `ogre zone` words and flags to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Help
```

### `List`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:List`

Reads the Zone Reuse window again; it opens and closes. Refused while a flow runs.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:List
```

### `Open`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Open`

Opens the Zone Resetter window, which reads the Zone Reuse window, the same as bare `ogre zone`.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Open
```

### `Queue`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Queue`

Prints the reset queue to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Queue
```

### `Reset`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Reset[word]`

Resets the timer of every zone in the queue. Refused while a flow runs.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | string |  | fleet also sends it to the For Who window's selection. Optional. |

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Reset[fleet]
```

### `Status`

`ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Status`

Prints the flow state, zone and queue counts and counters to the console.

```text
ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Status
```
