# ISXOgreX

The core extension: `${ISXOgreX}` and the objects under it.

## ISXOgreX

### Members

#### `Auth`

`${ISXOgreX.Auth}`

The login status object. Read its members: Authenticated, AccessLevel, Username and Status.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.Auth](#isxogrexauth)

**Returns:** ogrexauth: the login status object; as text it reads ISXOgreX.Auth.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Auth.Status}
```

#### `Console`

`${ISXOgreX.Console}`

The Ogre console object. It has no members of its own; call its methods, such as ISXOgreX.Console:Toggle.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.Console](#isxogrexconsole)

**Returns:** ogrexconsole: the console object (methods only); as text it reads ISXOgreX.Console.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Console}
```

#### `Login`

`${ISXOgreX.Login}`

The login box object. ISXOgreX.Login:Show opens the login box, and ISXOgreX.Login:Submit[username,password] saves a login and logs in again with it.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.Login](#isxogrexlogin)

**Returns:** ogrexlogin: the login box object (methods only); as text it reads ISXOgreX.Login.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Login}
```

#### `Options`

`${ISXOgreX.Options}`

The Ogre options window object. Its methods are Open, Save, Close and Ready (fill the open window's fields again).

All of it: [ISXOgreX.Options](#isxogrexoptions)

**Returns:** ogrexoptions: the options window object (methods only); as text it reads ISXOgreX.Options.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Options}
```

#### `Patch`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch}`

The patcher object: its members report the patcher's state and its methods run the patcher's commands. See the ISXOgreX.Patch rows.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.Patch](#isxogrexpatch)

**Returns:** ogrexpatch: the patcher object; as text it reads ISXOgreX.Patch.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch}
```

#### `Release`

`${ISXOgreX.Release}`

The name of the release this PC was last patched to, the same name the What's new page uses. It is empty when this PC has never been patched or the last release had no name.

**Returns:** string: the release name (like 2026.10.16.005); empty when there is none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Release}
```

#### `UI`

`${ISXOgreX.UI}`

The in-game UI object: windows, their values and the UI store. See the ISXOgreX.UI rows for its members and methods.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.UI](#isxogrexui)

**Returns:** ogrexui: the in-game UI object; as text it reads ISXOgreX.UI.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI}
```

#### `Version`

`${ISXOgreX.Version}`

The build date of the loaded core extension. It is not the release name - use Release for that.

**Returns:** string: the core's build date as yyyymmdd.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Version}
```

### Methods

#### `ReloadExtension`

`ISXOgreX:ReloadExtension[reason]`

Reloads this session's core (the game adapter reloads under it) when the core or adapter file on disk is newer than the one this session loaded; otherwise it prints that this session already runs the files on disk. It does nothing while a patch run is in progress on this session, and nothing before the patcher has started.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | `another session on this PC patched` | Text shown in the reload message, saying why the reload was asked for. |

```text
ISXOgreX:ReloadExtension["files updated"]
```

#### `ShowVersion`

`ISXOgreX:ShowVersion`

Prints the release this PC was patched to and the core's build date to the InnerSpace console, with a link to what changed. When this PC was never patched it says so, and when the release has no name it shows the release id instead.

```text
ISXOgreX:ShowVersion
```

## ISXOgreX.Auth

### Members

#### `AccessLevel`

`${ISXOgreX.Auth.AccessLevel}`

The access level name the Ogre server sent for this account at login. Before a login reply arrives it reads a default value.

**Returns:** string: the access level name from the server; a default value before a login reply arrives or when the server sent none.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Auth.AccessLevel}
```

#### `Authenticated`

`${ISXOgreX.Auth.Authenticated}`

Whether this session's login to the Ogre server succeeded. It is FALSE while the login is still waiting for the server.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when the login succeeded; FALSE when it has not started, is waiting, failed, or no login is saved.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Auth.Authenticated}
```

#### `Status`

`${ISXOgreX.Auth.Status}`

Where this session's login stands, as one word.

**Returns:** string: idle (not started), pending (waiting for the server), authenticated, failed, or nocreds (no saved login).

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Auth.Status}
```

#### `Username`

`${ISXOgreX.Auth.Username}`

The account name of the saved login this session logs in with. It is filled from the saved login before the server answers, so use Authenticated to know whether the login succeeded.

**Returns:** string: the saved login's account name; empty when no login is saved.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Auth.Username}
```

## ISXOgreX.Login

### Methods

#### `Show`

`ISXOgreX.Login:Show`

Opens the small Windows login box where you type your Ogre account username and password; if it is already open it is brought to the front instead. Its Login button saves what you typed and logs in, and Cancel just closes it (the Account tab of Ogre Options is the usual place for this - the box is the fallback when that window cannot load).

```text
ISXOgreX.Login:Show
```

#### `Submit`

`ISXOgreX.Login:Submit[username,password]`

Saves the given Ogre account username and password on this PC, closes the login box if it is open and logs in again on the next frame - even when you are already logged in. With either argument missing or blank nothing is saved and one console warning says so.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string |  | Your Ogre account name. |
| `password` | string |  | Your Ogre account password. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Login:Submit["MyOgreAccount","MyOgrePassword"]
```

## ISXOgreX.Options

### Methods

#### `Close`

`ISXOgreX.Options:Close`

Closes the Ogre Options window without saving anything.

```text
ISXOgreX.Options:Close
```

#### `Open`

`ISXOgreX.Options:Open`

Opens the Ogre Options window and fills its fields from the saved settings. If the window is already open it does nothing, so what you typed in it stays (the same as `ogre config`).

```text
ISXOgreX.Options:Open
```

#### `Save`

`ISXOgreX.Options:Save`

Saves the values the Ogre Options window's Save button hands over (this is the call that button makes): UI scale, the console setting, session watch, navmesh downloads and your Ogre login, which tries to log in again if you are not logged in. The window's status line then shows 'Saved.', 'Saved - logging in...' or 'Save FAILED', or 'Save failed (no data)' or 'Save failed (bad JSON)' when nothing usable was handed over.

```text
ISXOgreX.Options:Save
```

## ISXOgreX.Console

### Methods

#### `Clear`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Clear`

Clears the Ogre console's output and the lines it keeps on this session. New lines show as normal afterwards.

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Clear
```

#### `Close`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Close`

Closes the Ogre console window on this session. It stays closed until opened again, even if the UI reloads.

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Close
```

#### `Open`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Open`

Opens the Ogre console window on this session. Opening a console that is already open does nothing.

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Open
```

#### `ReloadSchema`

`ISXOgreX.Console:ReloadSchema[game]`

Reads the console command lists again from disk on this session: the common list, the game's list and any command packs. A missing file just leaves its commands out, and pack problems are shown in the console's Commands tab.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `game` | string | `everquest2` | The game id whose command list to load, such as everquest2 or pantheon. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:ReloadSchema[everquest2]
```

#### `Send`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Send[message,-tab,tab,-rg,group,-cfw,who,-kind,kind]`

Sends message through the uplink to every session in the relay group: a message starting !c or !ci is a command that each session parses, anything else is a chat line. With no arguments it sends the line typed in the console's input box instead.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | `the input box line` | The literal line to send; a leading !c or !ci makes it a command. Leave out every argument to send the input box line. |
| `-tab` | switch | `(none)` | Also show the line in the console tab named by the next argument; may be given more than once. |
| `tab` | string | `(none)` | The console tab name that follows -tab. |
| `-rg` | switch | `(none)` | Send to the relay group named by the next argument instead of the bot's own relay group. |
| `group` | string | `the bot's relay group` | The relay group name that follows -rg. |
| `-cfw` | switch | `(none)` | Give a command a for-who, used by its commands whose own for-who is left as auto. |
| `who` | for-who | `all` | [for-who](ogrebotapi/ForWho.md): this runs only when this character is one it names, for the commands in the line that leave theirs as auto. |
| `-kind` | switch | `(none)` | Show a chat line as a status line of the kind named by the next argument; ignored for a command. |
| `kind` | string | `(none)` | error, warn or system; the line then shows only in its -tab tabs and All, in that kind's colour. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Send["Pulling now",-tab,Raid]
```

#### `Sessions`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Sessions[mode]`

With on or off, turns the uplink's session watch (it says when a session freezes, recovers or closes) on or off until the uplink restarts. With no argument it prints the sessions the uplink has heard from to this session's console; any other word prints the usage.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `(none - print the table)` | on or off to switch the watch; leave it out to print the session table. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Sessions[on]
```

#### `SetOption`

`ISXOgreX.Console:SetOption[key,value]`

Saves one console setting to the console's settings file (the same as the console's settings panel). It does nothing with fewer than two arguments, and an unknown key is ignored with nothing on screen.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | hide_on_load, send_to_irc, show_timestamps, verb_trace, or a colour key starting color_. |
| `value` | string |  | 1 or true (lower case) for on, anything else (TRUE included) for off; for a color_ key, a hex colour of up to six digits. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:SetOption[show_timestamps,1]
```

#### `Toggle`

`ISXOgreX.Console:Toggle`

Opens the Ogre console window when it is closed, and closes it when it is open.

```text
ISXOgreX.Console:Toggle
```

## ISXOgreX.UI

### Members

#### `Get`

`${ISXOgreX.UI.Get[key]}`

Reads the value a UI page stored under `key` with ogreCall('set',key,value); there is one store, shared by every page, and the UI host is loaded first if needed. Returns NULL when the key was never stored, its value is empty, or the UI host is not loaded.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string |  | the store key the page used (case as the page wrote it) |

**Returns:** string: the stored value; NULL when the key is absent, its value is empty, or the UI host is not loaded

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI.Get[radar_cfg]}
```

#### `Value`

`${ISXOgreX.UI.Value[name,id]}`

Reads element `id` of the open window `name` as the page last published it: a checkbox or radio reads TRUE or FALSE, an input or textarea its value (an empty box reads an empty string), any other element its text. NULL when the window is not open or the element never published - only windows opened with ISXOgreX.UI:Open publish, and a read right after your own ISXOgreX.UI:Set waits up to 50 ms for the page to apply it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the window name given to ISXOgreX.UI:Open (case-sensitive) |
| `id` | string |  | the element's HTML id inside that window |

**Returns:** string: the element's published value; NULL when the window is not open or the element never published a value

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI.Value[hello,hello-name]}
```

#### `Window`

`${ISXOgreX.UI.Window[name]}`

Gives the open window `name` - your own, OgreBot's or a help window - as an ogrexuiwindow object (Name, Visible, X, Y, Width, Height) that prints as the window's name. NULL when no window by that name is open, so (exists) answers "is it open"; a window counts as open from the moment OgreUI_Opened fires for it.

All of it: [ISXOgreX.UI.Window](#isxogrexuiwindow)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the window name (case-sensitive) |

**Returns:** ogrexuiwindow: the open window; NULL when no window with that name is open

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI.Window[hello](exists)}
```

### Methods

#### `Close`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Close[name]`

Closes the window `name` - your own or any other open UI window - and OgreUI_Closed fires with reason "closed". Nothing happens when no window by that name is open; a missing name is refused with one console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the window's name (case-sensitive) |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Close[hello]
```

#### `Drain`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Drain`

Runs, right now and in order, the commands UI pages have queued for the script side, stopping after about 1,000 in one call. The extension already does this every frame, so a script rarely needs it.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Drain
```

#### `Eval`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Eval[js]`

Runs the JavaScript js in the UI page, loading the UI host first if needed. Nothing comes back to the script, and without js it is refused with one console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `js` | string |  | the JavaScript to run in the UI page |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Eval["radarSaveNow()"]
```

#### `EvalFile`

`ISXOgreX.UI:EvalFile[path]`

Reads the JavaScript file `path` from disk and runs it in the UI page, loading the UI host first if needed. A file that cannot be read writes a warning to the log file only, not the console, and a missing path is refused with one console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | full path of the .js file to run |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:EvalFile["${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/Scripts/Ogre/Common/OgreUI/common/WindowReset/windowreset.js"]
```

#### `Focus`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Focus[name,id]`

Gives the text field `id` in the open window `name` the keyboard, so keys go to that field and not the game until Escape or a click elsewhere; every call is logged. A hidden window, a missing element or anything that is not a text field is refused (logged only), and leaving out either argument prints a warning to the console.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the open window's name (case-sensitive) |
| `id` | string |  | the HTML id of a text input, textarea or editable element in that window |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Focus[hello,hello-name]
```

#### `Help`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Help`

Opens, in the default web browser, the online documentation page of the window whose Full documentation button was pressed; the window name comes from what the help window stored under help_name. It takes no arguments, and a window with no documentation page only writes a warning to the log file.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Help
```

#### `Host`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Host`

Loads the UI host if it is not loaded yet; it does not open or show anything. Safe to call any number of times.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Host
```

#### `KeyboardDump`

`ISXOgreX.UI:KeyboardDump`

Prints a keyboard report to the console: Shift (as the game and the hardware see it), Caps Lock, Ctrl, Alt, the keys held down, whether the game window is in front, and the UI host's keyboard state. It is meant for pasting into a report about a key that seems stuck.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:KeyboardDump
```

#### `Load`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Load[path]`

Loads the UI host, then replaces the whole UI page with the HTML file path, which takes away the desktop and every window on it: each window closes with OgreUI_Closed reason "reload", as UI:Reload does, and nothing waiting for the desktop runs until a page says it is ready. Without path it is refused with one console warning (ISXOgreX.UI:Host loads the host alone).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | full path of the HTML file to show as the UI page |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Load["${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/Scripts/Ogre/Common/OgreUI/common/Desktop/desktop.html"]
```

#### `Move`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Move[name,x,y]`

Moves the open window `name` (yours or any other) so its top-left corner sits at x,y in desktop pixels - the same numbers the Window object's X and Y read back. The move is not saved, so the window opens at its saved spot next time; anything but two whole numbers prints a warning to the console, and a window that is not open is left alone.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the open window's name (case-sensitive) |
| `x` | int |  | left edge in desktop pixels (a whole number) |
| `y` | int |  | top edge in desktop pixels (a whole number) |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Move[hello,200,150]
```

#### `Open`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Open[name,path,helpPath]`

Opens your own window `name` from one HTML file `path`, with an optional markdown file `helpPath` as the text of the title bar's help (?) button; both files are read when you call it, and the window appears once the UI desktop is up, when OgreUI_Opened fires. If a window by that name is already open only its help text is refreshed, and a file that cannot be read prints a warning to the console and opens nothing; a missing name or path is refused with one console warning.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the window's name, used by every other window call (case-sensitive) |
| `path` | string |  | full path of the HTML file: style, markup and &lt;script> blocks, plus an optional &lt;script type="ogre/window"> block holding the window's options as JSON (title, w, h ...) |
| `helpPath` | string | `"" (no help text)` | full path of a markdown file shown by the title bar's ? button |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Open[hello,"${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/Scripts/Ogre/Common/OgreUI/examples/hello/hello.html","${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/Scripts/Ogre/Common/OgreUI/examples/hello/hello.md"]
```

#### `Reload`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Reload`

Reloads the UI page: every open window goes away at once and OgreUI_Closed fires for each with reason "reload", which is the cue for a script to re-open its own window. The UI host is loaded first if needed; if it cannot load, nothing happens.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Reload
```

#### `SavePref`

`ISXOgreX.UI:SavePref`

Saves a UI page's own preferences: the JSON the page stored under uipref_blob is written into the saved UI state (UIState.json in the Common save folder) under the name it stored in uipref_name, replacing what that name held. Pages call it themselves; it takes no arguments, and missing or invalid values only write a warning to the log file.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:SavePref
```

#### `SaveWindow`

`ISXOgreX.UI:SaveWindow`

Saves one window's position, size, scale and lock settings, read from the blob the page stored under wm_save_blob, into the saved UI state (UIState.json in the Common save folder), replacing what that window had. The window manager calls it from a window's Save Position; it takes no arguments, and a missing or invalid blob only writes a warning to the log file.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:SaveWindow
```

#### `Set`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Set[name,id,value]`

Changes element `id` in the open window `name` as if the user did it: a checkbox or radio is checked for TRUE, 1, on or yes and unchecked for anything else, an input, textarea or dropdown takes the value, any other element shows it as its text, and a form element's change event fires. A missing window, id or value is refused with one console warning (a blank value is a value); nothing happens when the window is not open or no element has that id.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the open window's name (case-sensitive) |
| `id` | string |  | the element's HTML id inside that window |
| `value` | string |  | the new value: TRUE/FALSE for a checkbox or radio, otherwise the text or value to put in |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Set[hello,hello-status,"Said hello"]
```

#### `Size`

`ISXOgreX.UI:Size[name,width,height]`

Sizes the open window `name` (yours or any other) to width by height pixels on screen with its scale applied - the same numbers the Window object's Width and Height read back. The size is not saved, so the window opens at its saved size next time; anything but two whole numbers above 0 prints a warning to the console, and a window that is not open is left alone.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | the open window's name (case-sensitive) |
| `width` | int |  | width in on-screen pixels (a whole number above 0) |
| `height` | int |  | height in on-screen pixels (a whole number above 0) |

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:Size[hello,320,200]
```

#### `WindowResetPanel`

`ISXOgreX.UI:WindowResetPanel`

Opens the Reset UI Windows window, centered on the screen, which lists the open windows and lets the player put each one back at its default spot. It waits for the desktop if that is not up yet, and does nothing if the Reset UI Windows window is already open.

```text
ISXOgreX.UI:WindowResetPanel
```

## ISXOgreX.Patch

### Members

#### `Enabled`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch.Enabled}`

Whether the Ogre patcher may update this PC, as the patcher last read its setting. The setting is read again whenever an update starts or Status runs, so a change shows here after that.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE when patching is on; FALSE when it is off for this PC, its setting cannot be read, or before the patcher has started.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch.Enabled}
```

#### `InProgress`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch.InProgress}`

Whether an update run is going on in this session, including the short wait before the update check at load and a reload queued after an extension was updated. Background navmesh downloads do not count.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while an update run is active in this session; FALSE when none is.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch.InProgress}
```

#### `LastResult`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch.LastResult}`

The one-line result of the last update run on this PC, the same text the run printed after 'patch:' (for example a line starting 'up to date' or 'done - release', which counts the files updated and failed). It is kept in OgreSave/patcher-state.json, so it survives a restart.

**Returns:** string: the last run's result line; "" when no run has finished on this PC or patching was off when the session started.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch.LastResult}
```

#### `ReleaseId`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch.ReleaseId}`

The id of the release the last update run on this PC checked against, kept in OgreSave/patcher-state.json. For the release name players see, use ${ISXOgreX.Release}.

**Returns:** string: the last run's release id; "" when this PC has never been patched or patching was off when the session started.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch.ReleaseId}
```

#### `Tier`

`${ISXOgreX.Patch.Tier}`

The release channel number the update server sent with the release the last update run on this PC checked against, kept with ReleaseId in OgreSave/patcher-state.json.

**Returns:** int: that number; -1 when no update run has recorded one.

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.Patch.Tier}
```

### Methods

#### `Ignore`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:Ignore[op,path]`

Manages the list of files the patcher never writes, kept in OgreSave/patcher-ignore.json, so your own copy of a file is left alone: add or remove a path, or list them. Paths are relative to the InnerSpace folder with forward slashes (backslashes are turned into them), and every change prints a confirmation line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | string | `list` | add, remove or list; leave it out to list. |
| `path` | string | `""` | The file for add or remove, relative to the InnerSpace folder, such as Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/x.json; not used by list. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:Ignore[add,"Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/Commands/everquest2.json"]
```

#### `Mesh`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:Mesh[mode]`

Sets how navmeshes download and applies it at once: all (every zone in the background), ondemand (a zone's mesh when you need it) or off. With no argument it prints the navmesh download summary, and an unknown word prints the usage line.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `""` | all, ondemand or off; leave it out to print the summary instead. |

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:Mesh[ondemand]
```

#### `RevertExt`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:RevertExt`

Puts back the previous ISXOgreX DLL kept after a self-update (the .prev file) and reloads the extension, keeping the replaced one beside it as .reverted. It is refused while a run is in progress, says there is nothing to revert when no .prev exists, and the next update run installs the current release again.

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:RevertExt
```

#### `Status`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:Status`

Prints the patcher's state to the console: whether patching is on, your login state, your file switches, the last release and run, whether this session runs older DLLs than the ones on disk, any run in progress and the navmesh download summary. It changes nothing.

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:Status
```

#### `TestCorrupt`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:TestCorrupt`

A diagnostic switch: each call arms or disarms a one-time fault that flips one byte of the next downloaded file before it is checked, so you can see the check refuse it and keep the old file. It prints ARMED or disarmed and fires on the next update or navmesh download.

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:TestCorrupt
```

#### `Update`

`ISXOgreX.Patch:Update`

Checks for an Ogre update now and installs it: fetches the current release, downloads every changed file, checks each one and swaps them in, reloading the extension if one of its DLLs changed, and afterwards every other session on this PC that runs older files reloads too. It runs in the background, prints 'patch: &lt;result>' when done, and refuses with a console line when a run is already going, patching is off or you are not logged in to Ogre.

```text
ISXOgreX.Patch:Update
```

## ISXOgreX.UI.Window

#### `Visible`

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI.Window[hello].Visible}
```

#### `Width`

The window's on-screen width in pixels with its scale applied, as the page last published it - the number ISXOgreX.UI:Size takes. A hidden window keeps its last on-screen size (0 if it was never shown), and the member reads NULL once the window has closed.

**Returns:** int: on-screen width in pixels; NULL when the window has closed

```text
echo ${ISXOgreX.UI.Window[hello].Width}
```

#### `X`

#### `Y`

**Returns:** int: top edge in desktop pixels; NULL when the window has closed


## ogretimer

### Members

#### `DeciLeft`

`${T.DeciLeft}`

Seconds left before the timer runs out, as text with one decimal, as Object_Timer's DeciLeft: 1500 ms left reads 1.5. It reads 0.0 once the timer has run out or was stopped.

**Returns:** string: seconds left with one decimal; "0.0" when the timer ran out, was stopped or was never set

```text
variable ogretimer T
echo ${T.DeciLeft}
```

#### `MinutesLeft`

`${T.MinutesLeft}`

Whole minutes left before the timer runs out, rounded down, as Object_Timer's MinutesLeft: 119 seconds left reads 1. It reads 0 in the last minute as well as once the timer has run out or was stopped.

**Returns:** int64: whole minutes left (rounded down); 0 when under a minute is left, or the timer ran out, was stopped or was never set

```text
variable ogretimer T
echo ${T.MinutesLeft}
```

#### `Running`

`${T.Running}`

Whether the timer still has time left. A timer set to 0, run out, stopped or never set is not running.

**Returns:** bool: TRUE while TimeLeft is above 0; FALSE when it has run out, was stopped or was never set

```text
variable ogretimer T
echo ${T.Running}
```

#### `SecondsLeft`

`${T.SecondsLeft}`

Whole seconds left before the timer runs out, rounded down, so 1999 ms left reads 1. It reads 0 in the last second as well as once the timer has run out or was stopped.

**Returns:** int64: whole seconds left (rounded down); 0 when under one second is left, or the timer ran out, was stopped or was never set

```text
variable ogretimer T
echo ${T.SecondsLeft}
```

#### `TimeLeft`

`${T.TimeLeft}`

Milliseconds left before the timer runs out - 0 once it has run out, and 0 for a timer that was stopped or never set. Reading the variable itself (${T}) gives the same number, so `if ${T}` means still running.

**Returns:** int64: milliseconds left; 0 when the timer has run out, was stopped or was never set

```text
variable ogretimer T
echo ${T.TimeLeft}
```

### Methods

#### `Dec`

`T:Dec[ms]`

Takes ms milliseconds off the time left - taking off as much as is left (or more) stops the timer, and a timer that is not running stays stopped. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | number |  | milliseconds to take off (fractions are rounded) |

```text
variable ogretimer T
T:Dec[1000]
```

#### `DecMinutes`

`T:DecMinutes[minutes]`

Takes that many minutes off the time left - taking off as much as is left (or more) stops the timer, and a timer that is not running stays stopped. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | number |  | minutes to take off (fractions allowed) |

```text
variable ogretimer T
T:DecMinutes[1]
```

#### `DecSeconds`

`T:DecSeconds[seconds]`

Takes that many seconds off the time left - taking off as much as is left (or more) stops the timer, and a timer that is not running stays stopped. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | number |  | seconds to take off (fractions allowed) |

```text
variable ogretimer T
T:DecSeconds[5]
```

#### `Inc`

`T:Inc[ms]`

Adds ms milliseconds to the time left, and a timer that has run out, was stopped or was never set counts from now instead. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | number |  | milliseconds to add (fractions are rounded) |

```text
variable ogretimer T
T:Inc[2000]
```

#### `IncMinutes`

`T:IncMinutes[minutes]`

Adds that many minutes to the time left, and a timer that has run out, was stopped or was never set counts from now instead. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | number |  | minutes to add (fractions allowed) |

```text

T:IncMinutes[1]
```

#### `IncSeconds`

`T:IncSeconds[seconds]`

Adds that many seconds to the time left, and a timer that has run out, was stopped or was never set counts from now instead. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | number |  | seconds to add (fractions allowed) |

```text

T:IncSeconds[5]
```

#### `Set`

`T:Set[ms]`

Starts the timer so it runs out ms milliseconds from now, replacing any time it had, and Set[0] makes it read as already run out. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | number |  | milliseconds from now until the timer runs out (fractions are rounded) |

```text

```

#### `SetHours`

`T:SetHours[hours]`

Starts the timer so it runs out that many hours from now, replacing any time it had (fractions work). A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hours` | number |  | hours from now until the timer runs out (fractions allowed) |

```text

T:SetHours[1]
```

#### `SetMinimum`

`T:SetMinimum[ms]`

Makes the timer run for at least ms milliseconds from now, and a timer that already has more time left keeps it. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | number |  | the least milliseconds from now the timer should have left |

```text

```

#### `SetMinimumMinutes`

`T:SetMinimumMinutes[minutes]`

Makes the timer run for at least that many minutes from now, and a timer that already has more time left keeps it. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | number |  | the least minutes from now the timer should have left (fractions allowed) |

```text

T:SetMinimumMinutes[2]
```

#### `SetMinimumSeconds`

`T:SetMinimumSeconds[seconds]`

Makes the timer run for at least that many seconds from now, and a timer that already has more time left keeps it. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | number |  | the least seconds from now the timer should have left (fractions allowed) |

```text

```

#### `SetMinutes`

`T:SetMinutes[minutes]`

Starts the timer so it runs out that many minutes from now, replacing any time it had (fractions work). A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | number |  | minutes from now until the timer runs out (fractions allowed) |


#### `SetSeconds`

`T:SetSeconds[seconds]`

Starts the timer so it runs out that many seconds from now, replacing any time it had - fractions work, so SetSeconds[1.5] is 1500 ms. A missing or non-number argument prints a warning and leaves the timer unchanged, and zero or a negative number counts as 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | number |  | seconds from now until the timer runs out (fractions allowed) |

#### `Stop`

`T:Stop`

Stops the timer at once, so TimeLeft reads 0 and Running reads FALSE. It takes no arguments and ignores any it is given.

```text

```

# Commands

What a user types: the `ogre` commands (the in-game Commands panel lists them all) and the console commands (`oc !c` / `oc !ci`).

A console command is sent as `oc !c <command> <who> ...` - typed in the console, put on an MCP button or run from a script. It goes to the sessions on this PC, this one included, and the [for-who](../ogrebotapi/ForWho.md) in `<who>` picks which of them act: `igw:${Me.Name}` is your whole group, `igwbn:${Me.Name}` your group without you. Left out, or `auto`, it uses the For Who window. `oc !ci` does the same as `oc !c`.

- [`ogre` commands](ogre.md) - 94 commands
- [Console commands: ISXOgreX](console-isxogrex.md) - 9 commands
- [Console commands: A-B](console-a-b.md) - 46 commands
- [Console commands: C](console-c.md) - 72 commands
- [Console commands: D-N](console-d-n.md) - 88 commands
- [Console commands: O-R](console-o-r.md) - 65 commands
- [Console commands: S-Z](console-s-z.md) - 83 commands

# `ogre` commands

## `abilitydetails`

`ogre abilitydetails [name or id]`

Show every field your ability export holds for an ability, with a search

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<name or id>` | text | the window opens with nothing picked | An ability's name or ID: a base name picks the rank the bot uses, a rank's full name or an ID picks exactly that rank, and the search box is filled in with it. |

```text
ogre abilitydetails Kick
```

## `account`

`ogre account`

Show this session's account and access level

```text
ogre account
```

## `ae`

`ogre ae`

Also: `ogre abilityefficiency`

Score your abilities as damage / (cast + recovery) into a report file

```text
ogre ae
```

## `afk`

`ogre afk [0|on|off]`

Also: `ogre antiafk`

Keep the session alive (bare = silent; 0 = noisy; off = stop)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | word | bare `ogre afk` turns it on silent | Turn the keepalive on in noisy mode: it prints a line each time it sends its /who all (every 10 to 15 minutes). |
| `on` | word |  | Turn the keepalive on and keep the silent or noisy choice it already has. |
| `off` | word |  | Stop the keepalive (the same as `ogre end afk`); invite accepting is not changed. |
| `invites` | word | off at load | `invites on` or `invites off`: auto-accept group invites from names on your characters list; separate from the keepalive. |

```text
ogre afk off
```

## `analysis`

`ogre analysis [scan|monitor|taps|export|import|end]`

Also: `ogre anal`

Watch actors, record what changes and when, and diff two of them

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scan` | word | bare `ogre analysis` opens the window | Scan the zone's actors; add `<member>=<value>` terms (`<member><<value>` and `<member>><value>` too) to keep only matching ones, none reuses the window's terms or scans everything. |
| `monitor` | word |  | `monitor on\|off\|clear\|list`, or `monitor add <id\|target\|cursor>` / `monitor remove <id>`: pick the actors to watch and record their changes. |
| `taps` | word |  | `taps on` or `taps off`: log the choice and reward windows that appear (any word but off turns them on). |
| `export` | word |  | `export [<name>]`: save what was recorded to a file. |
| `import` | word |  | `import <name\|path>`: load a saved session back in. |
| `end` | word |  | Stop sampling, the taps and any scan, then close the window (the same as `ogre end analysis`). |
| `panel` | word |  | Open the window. |
| `close` | word |  | Close the window only; recording goes on. |
| `status` | word |  | Print what is monitored, the sample count, the scan and the taps. |
| `rate` | word |  | `rate <ms>`: how often monitored actors are sampled, 100 to 10000 ms. |
| `sessions` | word |  | List the saved sessions you can import. |

```text
ogre analysis monitor add target
```

## `bgrender`

`ogre bgrender [on|off|draw <ms>|hz <n>|force on|off|hold <name>|release <name>|clear]`

Skip drawing while this client is in the background (once a second; full drawing when active)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | word | off at load; bare `ogre bgrender` prints the status | Turn background render skipping on. |
| `off` | word |  | Turn it off - full drawing again (the same as `ogre end bgrender`). |
| `draw` | word |  | Set how often a background client still draws a frame, the `<ms>` after it. |
| `<ms>` | number | 1000 | The background draw interval in milliseconds; 0 means never draw in the background. |
| `hz` | word |  | Set the background loop cap, the `<n>` after it. |
| `<n>` | number | 100 | Loops per second while in the background; 0 means no cap. |
| `hold` | word |  | `hold <name>`: keep every frame drawn until that name is released (for scripts that need the screen drawn). |
| `release` | word |  | `release <name>`: drop that hold. |
| `clear` | word |  | Drop every hold. |

```text
ogre bgrender on
```

## `bot`

Load OgreBot (logs &lt;toon> in first if given, on that server and as that class if given)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<toon>` | name | OgreBot loads on the character you are on now | Log this character in first, then load OgreBot. |
| `-s` | flag |  | Log in on the server named next (`-server` works too); needed when the character is on more than one server and none is the default. |
| `<server>` | name | the character's default server | The server for `-s`; `ogre login -?` lists the short forms. |
| `-c` | flag |  | Log in as the class named next (`-class` works too). |
| `<class>` | name | whatever class it was | The class for `-c`. |

```text
ogre bot Mytoon
```

## `buyoverseermissions`

`ogre buyoverseermissions [flags] | stop | status`

Also: `ogre bom`

Buy Overseer missions from the Administrator agent

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-season` | flag | bare = the options on this character's Overseer Buy tab | `-season <n>`: only missions of season 1 to 7 (`-s` works too). |
| `-colour` | flag | any colour | `-colour <name>`: only Blue, Yellow, Purple or Green missions (`-c` / `-color` work too). |
| `-num` | flag | 10 | `-num <n>`: how many different missions to buy (`-n` works too). |
| `-amount` | flag | 10 | `-amount <n>`: how many of each to buy, at most 20 (`-a` works too). |
| `-replenishonly` | flag | off | Only top up missions you already have (`-r` / `-ro` work too). |
| `-noscribe` | flag | scribe is on | Do not scribe the bought missions (`-scribe` turns it back on). |
| `-destroy` | flag | off | Destroy the copies left over after scribing (`-nodestroy` turns it off). |
| `-gettogh` | flag | off | Go to the guild hall when the run finishes (`-gh`; `-nogettogh` / `-nogh` turn it off). |
| `stop` | word |  | Stop a running buy (`abort` works too). |
| `status` | word |  | Print how the buy run is going. |

```text
ogre buyoverseermissions -num 5 -amount 2
```

## `craftgm`

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<range>` | text | bare opens the panel and does nothing else | A level (`131`), a range (`131-135` or `131 135`), or `all`; on its own it opens the panel with the range filled in and scans nothing. |

## `ic`

`ogre ic [status|list|run|check|pause|end|options] | ogre ic -<option>[=off] ...`

Also: `ogre icx`, `ogre instancecontroller`

Open the instance controller - run zones from a queue (doc 28)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | word | bare opens the window | Print the run's state as text. |
| `list` | word |  | `list [<filter>]`: every loaded zone file, or those whose zone or path holds the filter. |
| `run` | word |  | `run <tier> <relative/path.json>`: run that one zone file (not the list); tier is default, test or custom. |
| `check` | word |  | `check [<zone>]`: which files claim the zone (no zone = the one you are in) and whether it is available. |
| `pause` | word |  | Pause the run. |
| `end` | word |  | Close the instance controller out (the same as `ogre end ic` and the window's X). |
| `options` | word |  | `options` lists every option; `options -<option>[=on\|off] ...` sets them. |
| `-<option>` | flag | a bare -option means on | Set any option of the window, e.g. `-loop`, `-haltAtEnd=off`, `-maxwait=30`; several at once. |
| `resume` | word |  | Resume a paused run. |
| `stop` | word |  | End the run (the window's End button). |
| `runlist` | word |  | `runlist [<row>]`: run the queue from the top, or from row `<row>`. |
| `queue` | word |  | `queue` lists it; `queue add <zone name>`, `queue add <tier> <path.json>`, `queue startat <row> <N>` (start that row at step N) or `queue clear`. |
| `wipe` | word |  | Declare a wipe now and start recovering. |
| `reload` | word |  | Re-read the zone files (the window's Reload). |
| `refresh` | word |  | Refresh the zone lock table. |
| `panel` | word |  | Open the window. |

```text
ogre ic -loop -haltAtEnd=off
```

## `im`

`ogre im [-depot -sell -destroy -tse -end] | depot|sell|destroy|tse|restock|trade <args> | chain | status | stop | close`

Also: `ogre inventorymanager`

Inventory manager - the window is the session; runs depot/sell/destroy/tse/restock/trade

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-depot` | flag | bare opens the window | In a chain: deposit to depots. Chain flags run in order: -depot, -sell, -destroy, -tse, -restock, -trade. |
| `-sell` | flag |  | In a chain: sell to the merchant. |
| `-destroy` | flag |  | In a chain: destroy the listed items. |
| `-tse` | flag |  | In a chain: consume items for tradeskill experience. |
| `-end` | flag |  | Close the window once the chain is done. |
| `depot` | word |  | `depot <depot flags>`: deposit into house or guild-hall depots; `ogre im help` lists the flags. |
| `sell` | word |  | Sell; `sell preview\|list\|add\|remove\|status\|stop\|reload` too. |
| `destroy` | word |  | Destroy the list, or `destroy <name>` for one item; `destroy preview\|list\|add\|remove\|status\|stop` too. |
| `tse` | word |  | Consume items for tradeskill experience; `tse -stopafter <n>` stops after that many. |
| `restock` | word |  | `restock [<profile>]` buys up to a profile; `restock list\|show <profile>\|preview\|stop` too. |
| `trade` | word |  | Run the trade queue; `trade add <player> <qty\|all> <item>`, `trade list\|remove <n>\|clear\|preview`. |
| `chain` | word |  | Show what each chain flag does. |
| `status` | word |  | Print what the window and each mode is doing. |
| `stop` | word |  | Stop whatever mode or chain is running. |
| `close` | word |  | Close the window only. |
| `end` | word |  | Stop and close the window (the same as `ogre end im`). |
| `queue` | word |  | `queue <mode>`: run that mode when the current one finishes; `queue` alone shows what waits. |
| `console` | word |  | `console [always\|running\|never\|clear]`: the activity log strip. |
| `settings` | word |  | Print the saved options; `settings bag ...` and `settings tse <option> <value>` change them. |
| `transmute` | word |  | `transmute <name>`: transmute that item. |

## `lag`

`ogre lag [report [s]|dump [s]|on|off|overhead|budget <ms> <ms>|minutes <1-60>|clear|close]`

Every frame of the last few minutes - what it cost and what ran in it; find and open the FPS dips

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report` | word | bare opens the window | Print a report of the last `<s>` seconds: the FPS dips and what caused them. |
| `<s>` | number | 60 for report; everything recorded for dump | How many seconds back report or dump looks. |
| `dump` | word |  | Save the last `<s>` seconds of frames to a file (the save itself costs one frame). |
| `on` | word | on | Record every frame (saved). |
| `off` | word |  | Stop recording; frames already recorded are kept. |
| `overhead` | word |  | Measure and print what the recorder itself costs. |
| `budget` | word | 25 and 33.3 ms | `budget <ms> <ms>`: the two frame budgets the report counts against; the second must be above the first. |
| `minutes` | word | 5 | `minutes <1-60>`: how many minutes of frames are kept; it starts again empty. |
| `clear` | word |  | Throw away the recorded frames. |
| `close` | word |  | Close the window (the same as `ogre end lag`). |

```text
ogre lag report 30
```

## `npccast`

Log what mobs cast (spell name + ability id) to copy or send; watch named mobs' casts - interrupt them or run your own commands

## `pulse`

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|

Watch for a coloured shiny and waypoint it

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<colour>` | name | Purple | Watch the whole zone for shinies of this colour and waypoint them: White, Green, Purple, Red, BlueShimmer or Blue. |
| `-off` | flag |  | Stop watching (also `ogre end trackshiny`). |
| `-colours` | flag |  | List the colours. |
| `-interval` | flag |  | How often to look, in ms (250-30000): `-interval <ms>`. |
| `-status` | flag |  | Show what it is watching for and what it found. |
| `-panel` | flag |  | Open the Watcher window. |

```text
ogre trackshiny Blue
```

## `trade`

Also: `ogre tradeit`

Trade the EXAMINED item to your target (default 12 stacks)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<count>` | number | 12 | How many stacks of the examined item to put in the trade with your target. |

## `travel`

`ogre travel [fast|spire|druid|bell|map|end]`

Also: `ogre travelhelper`

Open the Travel Helper: list a fast-travel, spire, druid-ring or bell map's destinations and send the group to one

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fast` | word |  | Open the window and list the fast-travel destinations. |
| `spire` | word |  | Open the window and list the wizard spire destinations. |
| `druid` | word |  | Open the window and list the druid ring destinations. |
| `bell` | word |  | Open the window and list the bell destinations. |
| `map` | word |  | Open the window and list the destinations of the travel map you have open. |
| `end` | word |  | Stop a list and close the window (the same as `ogre end travel`). |
| `help` | word |  | Show the usage. |

```text
ogre travel spire
```

## `zone`

`ogre zone [force <name>|end]`

Also: `ogre reset`, `ogre zonereset`

Open the zone-reuse resetter (OldBot's `zone` / `reset`)

| Word | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | word |  | Refresh and print the zone table (the Zone Reuse window opens and closes). |
| `force` | word |  | Force-reset one zone, `force <zone name>`; this spends one of your reset charges. |
| `add` | word |  | Add one zone to the reset queue: `add <zone name>`. |
| `addfilter` | word |  | Add many zones to the queue at once: `resettable` (the default), `noraid` or `notlocked`. |
| `queue` | word |  | Show the reset queue. |
| `clear` | word |  | Empty the reset queue. |
| `reset` | word |  | Reset the timers of every zone in the queue. |
| `fleet` | word |  | After `reset`: do it for the characters picked in the For Who window too. |
| `status` | word |  | Show the counters and what it is doing. |
| `end` | word |  | Stop what it was asked to do and close the window (the same as `ogre end zone`). |
| `help` | word |  | Show the usage. |
| `-zone` | flag |  | Reset one zone's timer: `-zone <name>`, every word up to the next flag is the name. |
| `-force` | flag |  | With `-zone`: force-reset it, which spends a charge. |
| `-all` | flag |  | Reset every resettable zone; raid zones are skipped. |
| `-allowraid` | flag |  | With `-all`: include raid zones. |
| `-fleet` | flag |  | Do it for the characters picked in the For Who window too. |

```text
ogre zone add Kralet Penumbra: The Hive Mind
```

# Console commands: A-B

## `-AbilityEmbargo`

`-AbilityEmbargo <who> <abilityid> <duration> <args>`

Also: `-AbilityRotate`

Embargo an ability (its name or id) for N seconds on the toons the for-who names (an ability rotation: the caster tells the others not to cast it).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who embargoes - leave blank to use the For Who window; `all` = every session that hears it. |
| `abilityid` | string |  |  |
| `duration` | string |  |  |
| `args` | rest |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AddEmbargo`

```text
oc !c -AbilityEmbargo all 1234567890 15
```

## `-AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo`

`-AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo <who> <value>`

Clears the embargo on one ability, given by name or id, on the matching characters. A name that cannot be found (including the default Unknown) does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `value` | string | `Unknown` |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearEmbargo`

```text
oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo all 1234567890
```

## `-AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos`

`-AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos <who>`

Clears every ability embargo on the matching characters, so their cast stacks may cast those abilities again. Item embargos are not touched.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearAllEmbargos`

```text
oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos all
```

## `-AbilityTagEmbargo`

`-AbilityTagEmbargo <who> <tagname> <duration> <type> <args>`

Also: `-AbilityTagRotate`, `-AbilityTag`

Holds a cast stack tag on the matching characters for duration seconds: type Embargo (the default) stops entries carrying that embargo tag from casting, and type Allow lets entries that need that allow tag cast. It only takes effect while the Settings tab's Enable Tag Embargo or Enable Tag Allow box is ticked; -m &lt;buff> in the extra arguments ties the tag to a maintained buff, and a missing or 0 duration ends it at once.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `tagname` | string |  |  |
| `duration` | string |  |  |
| `type` | string | `Embargo` |  |
| `args` | rest |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.CastStack:HoldTag`

```text
oc !c -AbilityTagEmbargo all Stifle 20 Embargo
```

`-AbilityTracker_Add <who> <abilityname>`

Adds the named ability to the Ability Tracker watch list (an id is stored as the ability's name) and echoes the result. The name is not checked against the export, one already on the list is not added again, and the change is lost unless you save the profile.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `abilityname` | string |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Abilities:TrackerAdd`

```text
oc !c -AbilityTracker_Add ${Me.Name} "Bulwark of Order"
```

## `-Actor_Click`

`-Actor_Click <who> <actorname> <exactname>`

Double-clicks an actor right away: a number is taken as an actor id, otherwise it picks the nearest interactable actor whose name contains the text (or matches it exactly when exactname is TRUE). Nothing happens when no such actor is found.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `actorname` | string | `asdf1323` |  |
| `exactname` | string | `FALSE` |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Actors:Click`

```text
oc !c -Actor_Click ${Me.Name} "Strange Lever" FALSE
```

## `-Actor_ClickQueued`

`-Actor_ClickQueued <who> <actorname> <exactname>`

Picks the actor the same way as -Actor_Click, but puts the click in the action queue: at its turn it double-clicks the actor and waits for the cast bar (4 seconds by default) before the next queued action. If the actor is gone by then, the click is dropped.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `actorname` | string | `asdf1323` |  |
| `exactname` | string | `FALSE` |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Actors:ClickQueued`

```text
oc !c -Actor_ClickQueued igw:${Me.Name} "Strange Lever" FALSE
```

## `-AddNoOffensiveOn`

`-AddNoOffensiveOn <who> <mobname> <exactmatchonly>`

Adds a mob name to the no-offensive list: while your target matches it, the bot casts no offensive abilities and does not auto-attack. exactmatchonly TRUE (default) needs the exact name, and FALSE matches any name that contains it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `mobname` | string | `DoesNotExist` |  |
| `exactmatchonly` | bool | `TRUE` | TRUE: only a target with exactly this name. FALSE: any target whose name contains it. |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Combat:AddNoOffensive`

```text
oc !c -AddNoOffensiveOn igw:${Me.Name} "${Target.Name}" TRUE
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `toonname` | string |  | The cursed toon |
| `args` | rest |  | Options: -AutoRemove &lt;seconds>, -tag &lt;name> |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestCurse`

```text
oc !c -AutoCurse igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.Name} -AutoRemove 20
```

## `-AutoGroupCure`

`-AutoGroupCure <who> <args>`

Cast the group cure once enough of the group carry a detriment. Kinds: arcane/a, elemental/e, noxious/n, trauma/t (none named = any of the four; each kind is counted on its own). Options: -count &lt;n> (at least n of you and the group, default 1), -AutoRemove &lt;seconds> (watch this long, default 8), -tag &lt;name> (a name -AutoCureRemove can cancel it by). Any other word refuses the request.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `args` | rest |  | Kinds, then options: -count &lt;n>, -AutoRemove &lt;seconds>, -tag &lt;name> |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestGroupWatch`

```text
oc !c -AutoGroupCure igw:${Me.Name} arcane trauma -count 3
```

## `-autohunt`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |


## `-AutoItemCure`

`-AutoItemCure <who> <type>`

Ask the matched toons to cure themselves with a Cure &lt;type> potion from their bags. A potion only cures its drinker, so there is no victim argument - whoever the for-who matches is who drinks. Leave the type blank for whatever they are actually afflicted with.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `type` | string |  | arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma. Blank (or 'any') = whatever is needed, decided when the potion is actually drunk. |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestItem`

```text
oc !c -AutoItemCure igw:${Me.Name} noxious
```

## `-AutoTarget_AddActor`

| `aggroonnonfighteronly` | string | `FALSE` |  |
| `aggroonnotme` | string | `FALSE` |  |

| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `x` | string | `${Me.X}` | X of the flat relative campspot (absolute coordinate, NOT a diff/offset) |
| `y` | string | `${Me.Y}` | Y/height of the flat relative campspot (absolute, not a diff) |
| `z` | string | `${Me.Z}` | Z of the flat relative campspot (absolute, not a diff) |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.CampSpot:SetRelativeLoc`

```text
oc !c -CS_Set_Relative igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.X} ${Me.Y} ${Me.Z}
```

## `-CurePotions_Replenish`

`-CurePotions_Replenish <who> <potion>`

Replenishes cure potions from the depot. Default is all. Other options are: Arcane, Trauma, Noxious, Elemental. All other options will be assumed to be the full name.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `potion` | string | `all` | Optional. Which cure: all, arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma. |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Cures:ReplenishPotions`

```text
oc !c -CurePotions_Replenish igw:${Me.Name} trauma
```

## `-DoHO_Set_Enable`

`-DoHO_Set_Enable <who> <torf> <args>`

TRUE (default) elects this session as the group's HO'er with the options given (-Force, -NoEnable, -NoHoAbilities, -DelayStart, -TimeOut), and FALSE ends the HO run and puts the HO options back. A word that is not TRUE or FALSE changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `torf` | string | `TRUE` |  |
| `args` | rest |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetEnabled`

```text
oc !c -DoHO_Set_Enable ${Me.Name} FALSE
```

## `-DoHO_Setup`

`-DoHO_Setup <who> <args>`

Makes this session the group's HO'er: the others stand down, and it runs Heroic Opportunities until -NumHOsToComplete are done (default 1) or -TimeOut passes (default 25 seconds), then everyone's HO options are put back. Further options are -TargetID, -LeaveWheelOpen, -LeaveStartOpen, -NoModifyOptions and -AllowCastStack.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `args` | rest |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetup`

```text
oc !c -DoHO_Setup ${Me.Name} -TargetID ${Target.ID} -NumHOsToComplete 2
```

## `-LogToonIn`

`-LogToonIn <who> <name> <server> <class>`

Logs a character in on one box: from the login screen, from character select, or from the world on another character (it camps first). Name the box by its InnerSpace session or its character, and at character select or the login screen by the character it last played: oc !c -LogToonIn MyToon MyToon logs MyToon back in after a zone dropped it to character select.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | string |  | The box: its InnerSpace session name or its character's name (at character select, the character it last played). all and groups pick no box. |
| `name` | string |  | The character to log in. It needs a saved login on this PC. |
| `server` | string |  | The server, for a character saved on more than one. Blank uses its default. A short form works: ior, md. |
| `class` | string |  | The class to log in as, like ranger. Blank logs in whatever class it was. |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Session:LogToonIn`

```text
oc !c -LogToonIn ${Me.Name} ${Group[1].Name}
```

## `-MoveToAreaNoTarget`

`-MoveToAreaNoTarget <who> <x> <y> <z> <precision>`

Also: `-Move2AreaNoTarget`

Walks to the given X and Z (Y is ignored) and stops within the precision distance, whether or not the toon has a target. A toon on a campspot stays there until -joustout or -letsgo; nothing moves if X or Z is missing or OgreBot is not open.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `x` | string | `${Me.X}` | X coordinate (paste ${Me.X}), or the name of a point of interest in this zone |
| `y` | float | `${Me.Y}` | Y/height - IGNORED (2D ground move) |
| `z` | float | `${Me.Z}` | Z coordinate (paste ${Me.Z}) |
| `precision` | float | `3` | Arrival precision |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Movement:Move2AreaNoTarget`

```text
oc !c -MoveToAreaNoTarget igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.X} ${Me.Y} ${Me.Z} 3
```

## `-Revive`

`-Revive <who> <option> <exactmatch>`

Presses Revive on the death window, or picks a revive point first.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `option` | string | `0` | Where to revive: 0 = the death window's default Revive button; a row number; or the revive point's name, e.g. Entrance (a point the window does not list = the last revive point it lists, said with the points it has) |
| `exactmatch` | string | `FALSE` | TRUE = the name must equal the revive point's name; FALSE = the point's name contains it |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Session:Revive`

```text
oc !c -Revive igw:${Me.Name} 0 FALSE
```

## `-Set_DisableAllAOEs_AllParams`

`-Set_DisableAllAOEs_AllParams <who> <args>`

TRUE (default) stops AE casting: it ticks the ignore PBAE, encounter nuke and counter-ability boxes, casts your single-target focus ability and cancels your class's AE-proccing buffs, while FALSE unticks the boxes and cancels the focus. -allowcounters keeps counter abilities and buffs, -AllowEncounters leaves the encounter nuke box alone, and -verbose announces each change.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `args` | rest |  |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetAOEsDisabled`

```text
oc !c -Set_DisableAllAOEs_AllParams igw:${Me.Name} TRUE -allowcounters
```

## `-SetCS_BehindNPC`

`-SetCS_BehindNPC <who> <nameorid> <distance> <skipifaggro>`

Moves your camp spot to a point behind an NPC, distance away from it. A blank NPC means your NPC target, and skipifaggro TRUE leaves the camp spot alone while you hold that NPC's aggro.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `nameorid` | string |  | The NPC to position on (a name or an actor id) - leave blank for your NPC target: your target, or your target's target |
| `distance` | string | `3` |  |
| `skipifaggro` | string | `FALSE` |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.CampSpot:SetLocBehindActor`

```text
oc !c -SetCS_BehindNPC igw:${Me.Name} ${Target.ID} 4 FALSE
```

## `-SetCS_InFrontNPC`

| `who` | forwho | `fighter` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |


## `-SetCS_NPC`

`-SetCS_NPC <who> <angle> <nameorid> <distance> <skipifaggro>`

Moves your camp spot to a point at an angle around an NPC, measured from the way it faces: angle 0 is the -SetCS_BehindNPC side and 180 the -SetCS_InFrontNPC side. Unlike those two, the distance also adds the NPC's body size, so the same distance lands further out.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `who` | forwho | `auto` | Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window. |
| `angle` | string | `0` |  |
| `nameorid` | string |  | The NPC to position on (a name or an actor id) - leave blank for your NPC target: your target, or your target's target |
| `distance` | string | `3` |  |
| `skipifaggro` | string | `FALSE` |  |

Runs: `OgreBotAPI.CampSpot:SetLocAtAngleFromActor`

```text
oc !c -SetCS_NPC igw:${Me.Name} 90 ${Target.ID} 5 FALSE
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/developer/api/events.md

# Events

The events the bot fires. Attach an atom to one in your script to react to it.

## ISXOgreX events

### `OgreUI_Closed`

Fires when a window on the Ogre HTML desktop goes away, passing two arguments: the window name, then the reason - "closed" (title-bar X or ISXOgreX.UI:Close) or "reload" (the desktop was reloaded and took the window with it). On a reload every open window fires it, so a script that wants its window back re-opens it from this event.

```text
Event[OgreUI_Closed]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreUI_Hidden`

Fires when an open window on the Ogre HTML desktop changes from visible to hidden, passing one argument, the window name. It fires only on a change, and not when the window is closed (that is OgreUI_Closed).

```text
Event[OgreUI_Hidden]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreUI_Opened`

Fires when a window is created on the Ogre HTML desktop - any window, a script's own (ISXOgreX.UI:Open), OgreBot's or a help window. It passes one argument, the window name.

```text
Event[OgreUI_Opened]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreUI_Shown`

Fires when an open window on the Ogre HTML desktop changes from hidden to visible, passing one argument, the window name. It fires only on a change and not for a window that opens already visible (that is OgreUI_Opened), but a window opened hidden fires it the first time it is shown.

```text
Event[OgreUI_Shown]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

## ISXOgreEQ2 events

### `BalancedSynergy_QueueCasting`

Fires on every box of the group that runs on this PC (the asking box included) when a box's cast stack reaches its Balanced Synergy entry: instead of casting it, that box sends this event to its group with one argument, the delay in seconds (always 10). On each box that receives it the bot itself casts Balanced Synergy after that delay unless "Ignore Balanced Synergy" is ticked or DoHO is running on that box when the delay ends, and a script atom attached here sees the same delay argument.

```text
Event[BalancedSynergy_QueueCasting]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `CampSpotJump_Completed`

Fires on this session when a jump route (OgreBotAPI.Movement:JumpRoute, or one an encounter starts) reaches its end, with two arguments: the result ("succeeded" or "failed") and why ("arrived", "already there", "timed out", "dead", "zoning", "cancelled" or "not above the check height"). A stopped route fires it as failed / cancelled, and a route that is refused at start never fires it.

```text
Event[CampSpotJump_Completed]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreCraft_CraftingStatusUpdate`

Fires on this session as the craft engine starts and ends its work, with one argument: a JSON object holding EventName, CharacterName, Time (unix seconds), Status, the flow flags (Writs / AutoTinkering / LLL / Quest), noMassProduction, craftingType, CraftedCount and CraftCount, plus Index, Error and the active recipe's _recipeName / _recipeID / _quantityToCraft / _quantityCrafted when they apply. Status is one of CraftQueue_Start, CraftQueue_CraftRecipe_Start, CraftQueue_CraftRecipe_End, CraftQueue_Finished, CraftQueue_End (bags full), Writs_Start, Writ_Start (with Writ and TotalWritsToDo), Writ_End, Writs_End, Quest_Start, Quest_End, AutoTinkering_Start, AutoTinkering_End, LLL_Start or LLL_End.

```text
Event[OgreCraft_CraftingStatusUpdate]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreCraft_NavigationRequired`

Fires on this session only when the craft option to manage movement with events (checkbox_craft_useevents) is ticked and craft needs to walk to an out-of-range station, merchant or other craft target, or cannot find it at all; it passes one JSON argument with requestID, action ("move"), category, key, displayName, customNamedPoint, precision, zone, characterName and targetFound, plus targetID, targetName, targetX/Y/Z and targetDistance when the target was found. Craft then waits with no time limit until your script calls ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation (you moved it) or ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation (craft walks itself), and the same JSON stays readable as ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}.

```text
Event[OgreCraft_NavigationRequired]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated`

Fires on this session when a recipe is added to the craft setup queue, its quantity changes, or it is removed, with one JSON argument holding EventName, CharacterName, Time (unix seconds), changeInRecipeQuantity, _recipeName, _recipeID, _quantityToCraft and _quantityCrafted. A removal (including a quantity change that reaches zero) also carries RemoveRecipe with the text "TRUE".

```text
Event[OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingEnded`

Fires on this session when a watched NPC that was casting stops casting that ability, switches to another ability, or leaves the scan, with two arguments: the actor ID and the ability ID that ended. It is part of NPC cast monitoring (watched mobs come from zone data or `ogre npccast watch`, checked every 250 ms within 50 m by default while "NPC Cast Monitoring" is ticked and you are alive), and a cast cut off by zoning or by unticking the box ends silently with no event.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingEnded]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingStarted`

Fires on this session when a watched NPC begins casting, with three arguments: the actor ID, the ability ID it is casting, and the cast time the game reports for it (AbilityCastingTime, as a decimal). Only mobs on the NPC cast monitoring watch list (zone data or `ogre npccast watch`) are checked, every 250 ms within 50 m by default, and only while "NPC Cast Monitoring" is ticked, you are alive and not zoning.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingStarted]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_DoHODisabled`

Fires on this session, with no arguments, every time DoHO is turned off here: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetEnabled with FALSE, the target number of completed HOs reached, the DoHO timeout running out, or the DoHO target dying or going away. Turning off a DoHO that is already off does nothing and fires nothing unless -Force is passed.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_DoHODisabled]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_DoHOEnabled`

Fires on this session, with no arguments, when OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetup or :DoSetEnabled with TRUE primes this box as the HO starter for the first time and it takes over the group's HO options. A re-enable of a box that is already primed, an enable that is already on, or a setup with -NoModifyOptions does not fire it.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_DoHOEnabled]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_GearConditionReport`

Fires on this session after every gear check, with two arguments: the character's name and the condition of the item in the primary slot as a whole percent. A gear check runs from OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckGear and automatically once each time the character dies while OgreBot is loaded; if the item details are not available within 5 seconds the check fails and nothing fires.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_GearConditionReport]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_GroupQueryDone`

Fires on the session that started a group query (${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery[...]} or OgreBotAPI.Comms:GroupQuery) when that query finishes or fails, with two arguments: the query id ("gq:&lt;session>:&lt;n>") and the result as JSON. The same result stays readable with ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Result[id]} for 60 seconds after it finishes.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_GroupQueryDone]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_InGameTell`

Fires on this session each time this character receives an in-game tell, with three arguments in this order: the speaker, the chat target (this character) and the message. It fires only on the receiving session and is not sent to other sessions.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_InGameTell]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_InGameTellSent`

Fires on this session each time this character sends an in-game tell, with three arguments in this order: the speaker (this character), the chat target (who the tell went to) and the message. It fires only on the sending session and is not sent to other sessions.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_InGameTellSent]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_KronoRedemption`

Fires on this session when a Krono redemption started by OgreBotAPI.Inventory:RedeemKrono reports its result, with two arguments: the character's name and TRUE (redeemed) or FALSE (the game said it failed). Nothing fires when there is no Krono to redeem, when no result shows up after 100 checks about a second apart, or when the character dies or leaves the world first.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_KronoRedemption]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnAbilityCast`

Fires on this session the moment the bot sends an ability cast (not when the cast lands), with five arguments: the caster (this character), the ability ID, the ability name, the target's actor ID (0 for none) and the target's name (empty for none); the other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnAbilityCast. A handler that casts from inside this event can nest it at most 8 deep, after which the fire is skipped with a console line.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityCast]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnAbilityCastCompleted`

Fires on this session when an ability the cast stack cast finishes, meaning its cast bar ended or an instant ability went on cooldown, with three arguments: the character's name, the ability ID and the ability name; the other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnAbilityCastCompleted. Items never fire it, and neither does a cast the bot cancelled or saw fail to start, but a cast bar that drops for any other reason (an interrupt, say) counts as finished.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityCastCompleted]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnAbilityReadyTimersUpdate`

Fires on this session about every 500 ms for each enabled ability on the OgreBot Ability Tracker list, whether or not anything changed, with four arguments: the character's name, the ability ID, the ability's short name and its time until ready in seconds (as a decimal). It fires only while the Ability Tracker option is ticked, the list has entries, and the character is in the world; an entry that does not match one of your abilities is skipped.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityReadyTimersUpdate]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded`

Fires on this session when a detrimental with a new icon pair appears on this character, with six arguments: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Your detrimentals are checked about every 500 ms while you are in the world and alive, and a detrimental whose icon changes shows up as a Removed for the old pair and an Added for the new one.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalRemoved`

Fires on this session when a detrimental's icon pair is no longer on this character, with six arguments describing it as last seen: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Checks run about every 500 ms and pause while you are dead, so detrimentals that dropped at death are reported once you are alive again.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalRemoved]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalUpdated`

Fires on this session when a detrimental that is still on this character (same icon pair) changes its increments, Duration or MaxDuration, with six arguments: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Because Duration counts down, expect it for every timed detrimental on about every 500 ms check.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalUpdated]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_OnItemUse`

Fires on this session the moment the bot uses an item (not when the use lands), with four arguments: the user (this character), the item name, the target's actor ID and the target's name; food, drink, potions and other self-used items pass 0 and an empty name for the target. The other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnItemUse.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_OnItemUse]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_SmartLootAssigned`

Fires on the looting session when SmartLoot decides to assign an item to a character, with three arguments: the character's name, the item it counted (the adornment's name when the assign was for an adornment) and that character's new count for it. It fires at decision time, so it still fires if the assign later fails in the loot window.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_SmartLootAssigned]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```

### `OgreEvent_SpewStats`

Fires when OgreBotAPI.Debug:BroadcastStat (or OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewMarked) resolves a value, on the asking session and on the other sessions in its relay group, with one JSON argument holding Character, Command, Label and Value (a faction result also has FactionStanding). Command is the request as typed, such as "-item a frog leg", except the faction, currency and recipe lookups send "Faction", "Currency" or "Recipe", and a bad request prints an error and fires nothing.

```text
Event[OgreEvent_SpewStats]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
```
